    It is not reweighting (the pool changes), not routing (the same route runs
    for every query), and not reranking (the file's own table, §1.2, names rerank
    as the rejected alternative — *"Rerank BM25 top-k (no recall gain)"*).

    **The design property that makes it composable at 14,589 files, and it is
    stated as a constraint rather than a benefit:** SESF *"leaves the underlying
    BM25 index **completely unmodified** — same index, just a different
    query."* **A mechanism that cannot corrupt the index cannot fail in a way
    that requires a rebuild**, and the arena's index is the one artifact that
    cannot be regenerated from source. Combined with **append-never-replace**
    (*"Preserves original IDF weights; expansion only adds recall, never removes
    precision"*) — **a query-side operation that is monotone in the good
    direction and side-effect-free on the index is the rare retrieval change
    that is safe to apply before it is understood.** That is a real reason to
    rank it above designs that score better and mutate state.

    **What it costs, and three of the four are the file's own admissions.**
    (a) **It is not uniform — the file says expansion *dips* on FEVER**, and its
    §4.3 gates accordingly (*"best applied selectively rather than
    unconditionally"*). **A mechanism that helps on 3 of 4 query sets and hurts
    on the fourth needs a gate, which means it inherits the routing problem
    rather than solving it.** (b) **Every LongMemEval-S number in the file is
    projected, not measured** — §3 is titled "Expected Impact Analysis", the
    category table's "CE-QE Expected Gain" column is a column of guesses, and
    "Acc=0.067 → should improve dramatically" is a hope. **Only the BEIR row is
    evidence.** (c) **It has a hard prerequisite the file is candid about: it
    needs a dense leg to have anything to attribute over** (*"Without dense
    retrieval leg, CE-QE has nothing to attribute over"*), so it cannot be the
    first thing built in a lexical-only store. (d) **Its own open-questions table
    concedes the attribution may be noise on the target domain** — MS
    MARCO-trained cross-encoders on dialogue, citing arXiv 2606.04194's finding
    that rerankers *hurt* on OOD conversational queries. **The mechanism's
    central component is the same component the corpus has already recorded as
    degrading out of domain.**

    **Where it lands.** Not as a slot — this area's three slots are about
    *weighting evidence*, and CE-QE is about *constructing the query*, which is
    a different organ. **It is recorded as the arena's strongest measured
    instance of candidate-pool construction, and it raises support for "the fix
    is not the weight" to 5 independent domains** (Area 2's ρ; MEMTIER's
    five-variant null; AgentIR's router capturing the oracle gap; RC-AD's
    across four query sets by one implementation, external and unverified at
    source (§A-3 covers the class).**
  - **TRANCHE 9 — THE CORPUS PROPOSES TO REPLACE THE WEIGHTS WITH A *CONDITIONAL
    TEST*, AND IT IS THE FIRST DESIGN IN 145 FILES THAT OFFERS A THIRD OPTION
    BESIDES REWEIGHTING AND ROUTING.** Two files, read together, supply it.
    `context-aware-drift-detection-conditional-preferences.md` (ORDER line 142,
    read whole) reports **Cobb & Van Looveren, "Context-Aware Drift Detection",
    ICML 2022** (PMLR v162) and its **ADiTT** estimator. The problem it names is
    the one this area's ρ weighting cannot see:

    > *"When the agent sees a session from a different context than historical
    > training data, standard detectors fire false alarms. **The conventional
    > remedy — decreasing detector sensitivity — also suppresses true drift
    > signals like genuine preference reversals.**"*

    **That sentence identifies a false dilemma, and the false dilemma is the
    architecture of every weighted-fusion design in this arena.** A detector has
    one sensitivity knob; turn it down and the false positives fall along with the
    true positives. ADiTT's answer is that the detector had been **estimating the
    wrong conditional**: it tests `P(Y|deployment) ≠ P(Y|historical)` when the
    question is `P(Y|deployment, X=x) ≠ P(Y|historical, X=x)`. **Set membership
    becomes the treatment, context becomes a covariate, and nuisance models
    (propensity and outcome, the same machinery as causal inference) adjust the
    context out before the residual is tested.** Measured, on the paper's own
    domains:

    | Method | FPR (context shift) | TPR (true drift) |
    |---|---|---|
    | MMD (unconditional) | 0.38 | 0.91 |
    | **Context-aware MMD** | **0.07** | **0.89** |
    | KS (unconditional) | 0.42 | 0.93 |
    | **Context-aware KS** | **0.09** | **0.90** |

    **A 5.4× fall in false positives for a 2-point fall in true positives.** That
    is a Pareto move along a curve the arena's own design space has been treating
    as the frontier, and it is achieved *without touching the weights at all*.
    **Support for "the discriminating variable is the regime, not the weight":
    5 independent domains** (Area 2's ρ; MEMTIER's zero-variance null; Open
    Ontologies' constraint-beats-weight result; Fortunate Recall's
    type-conditioned policy; this conditional test).

    **What it costs, stated with the same care the arena applies elsewhere.**
    (a) **The measurements are not agent-memory measurements.** The file says so
    itself, in its own limitations: *"No paper has evaluated context-aware drift
    detection on conversational preference data specifically. The Cobb & Van
    Looveren results are on image classification and tabular data."* The transfer
    to preference distributions is the corpus's inference, not a result.
    (b) **The file then projects the result anyway, and the projection is
    unfounded as stated.** §"Expected Impact" gives a table of Autognosia FPRs
    (~35% unconditional → ~8% context-aware, ~77% reduction) derived by
    *analogy* from the image-classification table, on the reasoning that *"If 38%
    of drift alerts are false positives from context shifts (CBSO research
    indicates context-specific OOD problems in memory retrieval)"* — where
    **"38%" is the paper's CIFAR-scale FPR re-labelled as an Autognosia figure,
    and "CBSO" is cited with no paper ID anywhere in the file.** The 77% is
    therefore **not a prediction the evidence supports; it is the 0.38→0.07 ratio
    copied into a different column.** Filed as a defect (§7 — it would change
    what gets built, because it is the number a capacity plan would be sized
    against) and the *mechanism* is recorded while the *number* is suspended.
    (c) **The framework assumes the context variable is known.** The file's first
    open question: *"The CDM requires specifying context a priori — but what if
    the relevant context is unknown?"* **At 14,589 files the a-priori context
    set is not a design choice, it is the whole tagging problem**, and a context
    the system did not name is a false positive the conditional test cannot
    remove.
  - **AND THE SECOND FILE IN THE BLOCK IS A NEGATIVE RESULT AGAINST LEARNED
    PARAMETERS THAT NOBODY IN THE CORPUS HAS STATED PLAINLY.**
    `context-dependent-lipschitz-constants-k-lambda.md` (ORDER line 144) and
    `continuous-k-lambda-zooming-ts.md` (ORDER line 145) are the corpus's drift
    *hyperparameter* programme: replace FEDD's fixed (k, λ) grid with a
    continuum-armed bandit (Zooming TS, Kleinberg-Slivkins-Upfal STOC 2008;
    CDT, Kang-Hsieh-Lee TMLR 2024) and make the Lipschitz constant a function of
    context. Both are **proposals with no experiments** — §5/§7 of each is
    "Expected Results" and "Hypotheses", `confidence: medium`, and the honest
    framing of 144 is *"The context features … **all correlate with** the local
    Lipschitz constant"* stated as a design premise and never tested.
    **Neither enters a slot, and the reason is the arena's own binding rule
    rather than a judgement call:** both learn their parameters by
    **Thompson-sampling on a reward the system itself computes** — `R(h) =
    F1(FEDD_h(·), ground_truth)` — and 145's own architecture diagram sources
    that ground truth from **human accept/reject feedback on drift alerts.** That
    is not quite a self-measurement loop, because a human is in it, **but it is
    the same shape with a slower clock**, and 144's safety floor
    (`L_predicted ≥ 0.5 × L_global`, *"never more aggressive than global"*) is the
    same instinct as the Arena 1 reachability requirement, reached from a
    different direction. **Recorded in `VERIFICATION.md` rather than as a slot,
    with the R-J2 tension named rather than resolved.**

    **What the pair does contribute is a mechanism claim that belongs to Area 3,
    and it is the fourth independent statement of it.** 145's whole premise is
    that **the reward surface is not uniformly smooth** — flat far from the
    optimum, steep near it, and *"At discontinuities (where a small λ change
    causes detection to fire/not-fire), the gradient is effectively infinite —
    the surface is non-Lipschitz."* **A detector's threshold is a place where the
    landscape has a cliff, and a global Lipschitz bound is the worst case over a
    surface whose worst case is exactly where the system operates.** That is
    Area 3's claim — that the right response to a non-uniform value surface is
    context-dependent scalarization — arriving from hyperparameter tuning rather
    than from multi-objective bandits, and it is consistent with CSTS
    (α(context), higher α when drift is slow) arriving independently in the same
    file. **Support for Area 3 Rank 1's *thesis*: 3 independent sources
    (CSTS's α(context); Open Ontologies' signal-weight insensitivity; this
    non-uniform-smoothness argument). Its grade does not move — the single
    load-bearing unverified claim in Area 3 is still the venue attribution of
    "Park & Farahmand, NeurIPS 2025" and "CSTS, ICPR 2026" (§A-1, §A-2), and
    neither file was read at source.**

    **The fork, stated as a contrast the arena can now act on:**

    | | Rank 1 (to-do-capture hook) | This mechanism (`future_cues`) |
    |---|---|---|
    | Direction | **backward** — harvest from conversation | **forward** — authored at write time |
    | Trigger | pattern-match on agent output | document creation |
    | Cost of recall | pays at capture | pays at write |
    | Coverage | only what was said | only what the author foresaw |
    | Failure | misses unvoiced intentions | **silently absent for everything unforeseen** |
    | Retraction | **no `status` column; table later truncated to 0 bytes** | edit the frontmatter |

    **Why this does not displace Rank 1 but must be recorded beside it.** The
    hook catches intentions the author did not anticipate; the frontmatter cannot,
    by construction. **They fail in opposite directions, which is the strongest
    argument for running both** — and the arena has no slot that says so, because
    an area holds exactly three ranked designs and "run both" is not one.

    **The sharper point is about the retraction column, and it now has a dated
    failure behind it.** Rank 1's write path terminates in a table with no
    `status` column, in a database that was **0 bytes on 2026-09-20** (§ grade
    above). `future_cues` has a retraction operation — **edit the frontmatter** —
    and its backing store is a markdown file inside a versioned corpus with an
    archive. **The mechanism with the weaker capture rate is the one with a
    survivable failure mode.** For an organ whose defining property is that it
    must not lose what it holds, **retractability outranks coverage**, and that
    inverts the arena's implicit ordering, which has treated breadth of capture as
    the thing to maximise. Grade for Rank 1's design stays `UNTESTED` and its
    deployment is now `UNTESTED`; **the comparison is a new observation, not a
    new trial, so no count moves.**

  - **TRANCHE 7 — A FIFTH TRIGGER MECHANISM, AND THE ONLY ONE THAT MAKES THE
    TRIGGER *CHEAP* RATHER THAN *SMART*.** `adaptive-consolidation-triggering-recurrence-utility.md`
    (ORDER line 116, read whole) surveys six trigger families and recommends the
    one this slot does not yet have. **RecMem**
    (`aclanthology.org/2026.findings-acl.1619`) gates the LLM call itself on
    **semantic recurrence**: *"deferring consolidation until ≥N semantically
    similar interactions accumulate (recurrence threshold)"*, with a reported
    **87% token reduction** against eager consolidation. The mechanism is eight
    lines and the file gives them verbatim:

    ```python
    def should_consolidate(new_memory, existing_memories, threshold=3):
        similar = [m for m in existing_memories
                   if cosine_sim(new_memory.embedding, m.embedding) > 0.8]
        if len(similar) < threshold:
            return False  # Skip LLM call, store raw only
        return True      # Proceed with LLM extraction
    ```

    **This is a different kind of trigger from every other one in the area, and
    the difference is what earns it a place.** SleepGate triggers on entropy,
    SLM V3.3 on a forgetting curve, HIMA on interference, CraniMem on utility:
    **all four measure something about the memory to decide whether to process
    it.** RecMem measures something about *whether there is anything to
    consolidate yet* — a **novelty gate, not a value gate.** The store grows
    unprocessed until three mutually-similar items exist, and only then does the
    expensive path run.

    **The distinction matters because it is the only trigger here that is
    *free* when it declines to fire.** Every other trigger in this slot pays its
    measurement cost on every memory and then decides. **RecMem declines 87% of
    the time having spent a cosine similarity and nothing else** — no LLM call, no
    entropy computation, no utility scoring. Per R-J1 cost is not a decision
    axis, and this is not a cost argument: **the structural point is that the
    gate can be evaluated before the expensive machinery is invoked, whereas the
    others are evaluated inside it.**

    **What it costs, stated as the arena's habit requires.** The threshold
    `cosine > 0.8` and `n ≥ 3` are **unstated defaults from the receiving
    system, not derived values** — and the file's own §1 recommends them
    (*"Only consolidate when ≥3 semantically similar interactions accumulate"*)
    without a source for the specific numbers. **A novelty gate is a threshold
    ladder, and this tranche has already produced a live example of a threshold
    ladder with an unreachable rung** (`VERIFICATION.md` I-6.1, `drift_risk > 4`
    on a [0,1] score). **The reachability requirement adopted in Area 1 applies
    here verbatim**, and this is the second slot it touches.

    **A second, sharper cost, and it is one this area's rank-1 has not faced.**
    Deferring consolidation means storing items raw "until three similar items
    accumulate." **For a corpus of *non-recurring* facts — a user's address, a
    one-off decision, a schema change — recurrence never arrives and the raw
    items are consolidated never.** The file acknowledges this obliquely
    (*"Long-running agents with repeated topics"*) and its §6 next-steps do not
    mention it. **A novelty gate needs a floor: a maximum deferral age, after
    which consolidation runs regardless.** Without one, the gate silently becomes
    a policy of never consolidating singletons — which is a forgetting policy
    arrived at through a cost mechanism, and **this arena already has three
    incompatible forgetting policies on record** (Area 11 Rank 1). **Filed as the
    design requirement this trigger earns: a deferral trigger must be bounded by
    age as well as by recurrence.**

    job.** This file is a **survey** — nine sources, all rated, no experiments

  `round84-2026-09-11.md` §4 (**The Missing Knowledge Layer in Cognitive
  Architectures for AI Agents**, arXiv 2604.11364) argues that the two most
  influential agent architectures — **CoALA and JEPA** — have **no Knowledge layer
  with its own persistence semantics**, and that the resulting category error has
  a specific signature: *systems apply Ebbinghaus decay to factual claims, or
  persist everything forever.* Its four-layer decomposition is directly on this
  area's subject:

  | Layer | Persistence semantics | Half-life |
  |---|---|---|
  | **Knowledge** | indefinite **supersession** — persists until contradicted | ∞ |
  | **Memory** | Ebbinghaus decay | 7–693 days |
  | **Wisdom** | **evidence-gated** revision, with provenance | context-dependent |
  | **Intelligence** | ephemeral inference | session |

  **Why this is recorded against the rank-1 slot and not for it:** this design
  says *forgetting is the wrong default for a whole class of content*, and
  "conflict-tag, evict, merge" applied uniformly will decay a fact that should
  only ever have been superseded. It converges with Fortunate Recall (round 83
  §10) and with DynamicMem (round 84 §5) on the same point from a third direction:
  **the discriminating variable is the content type, not the trigger.** That is
  now three independent sources — two proposing type-conditioned policy, one
  reporting a benchmark on which no uniform policy succeeds — and it is the
  strongest convergent finding in this area.
  **The corpus's own eight convergence points are logged because they are the
  shape of the failure:** NornicDB applies 7/69/693-day decay to *all* tiers
  ("forgets permanent facts"); Hindsight persists everything ("remembers what
  should be forgotten"); MemoryBank conflates storage with cognitive
  organisation; the Generative Agents memory stream "lacks a truth-maintenance
  layer"; the BEAM benchmark reports **near-zero contradiction-resolution
  scores.** `UNSUCCESSFUL` for uniform-policy forgetting, in the sense the arena
  means it: tried, in at least two named production systems, and it does not
  work.
  for interference-gated consolidation (SleepGate; SLM V3.3; Microsoft arXiv

    **And the loss list collides with the same file's own format table, which

    the design level, not the claim level**, and the only kind that changes what
    gets built.

    **The requirement this earns is the strongest form of the compression
    caution the arena has recorded: compression is not a size optimisation that
    costs a fixed amount of accuracy, it is a projection onto a subspace, and
    what falls outside the projection cannot be recovered by any reader.** The
    natural build order — compress, then buy the loss back with a better reader
    — is now contradicted by four independent results, and the fourth says *why*
    against the field inventory before it is chosen against the token budget.**
    A store that cannot represent conditionality must not be asked to hold
    conditional claims, no matter how many tokens that saves.

    **A scale consequence the file does not see, stated per R-J5.** Its §7 target
    is *"Token Overhead ≤1.2× baseline"* — a **scalar**. Under per-type format
    selection the index holds **mixed encodings**, so no single ratio describes
    it, and the target becomes unmeasurable exactly when the policy becomes
    non-trivial. **A build that adopts adaptive format selection must report
    overhead as a distribution over formats, not a scalar**, because at 14,589
    files the index-size consequence is the difference between a design that fits
    in context and one that does not — and the failure is invisible until the
    policy is learned and the index is already built.

    **No grade is taken from this file and none should be.** It is a **proposal
    with no experiments** — §7 is "Expected Outcomes", the §4.3 ablation table is
    unrun, and `confidence: 0.85` is asserted on a hypothesis that has not been
    tested (`VERIFICATION.md` I-6.3 covers the same pattern in its sibling file).
    The two reported figures — 98.4% held-out R@5 for MemPalace natural language
    and 84.2% for AAAK — both trace to the **same MemPalace benchmark file**, so
    under the support-count rule they are **one source, not two**, despite being
    presented as a baseline-and-a-regression pair. The corroboration above is
    corroboration of the arena's *compression caution* by a new domain, not of
    any ranked design.

    | Pipeline (same retriever, same rerank) | LongMemEval-S | LoCoMo |
    |---|---|---|
    | Verbatim chunks (512-char) | **67.4%** | **43.9%** |
    | LLM-extracted artifacts | 45.4% | 28.0% |
    | **Gap** | **22.0 pp** | **15.9 pp** |

    **Twenty-two points is not a tuning difference and it is not the largest
    number in the arena — it is the largest gap between two arms of the *same
    experiment*, which is the only comparison where the retriever, the reranker
    and the budget are held constant by construction.** AAAK's 12.4 pp and
    Engram's distractor-removal effect are both cross-system. This one is

    dense-only retrieval, session-level extraction granularity. **The mechanism
    is one sentence and it is the same sentence AAAK arrived at from the

    keep for free… **retrieval accuracy tracks how far the stored

    **So the arena now has four independent losses, and they are losses of four
    different things** — AAAK loses *hedging, conditionality and emotional
    context* (a field inventory); Engram loses *recall to distractors* (a
    selection effect, and it is the one that is recoverable by re-reading raw
    chunks alongside); this loses *verbatim detail per se*; and MEMTIER's
    zero-variance result says a reweighting design loses nothing at all because
    it never changes anything. **The four do not compose into a single
    percentage and the arena should not average them.** What they do compose
    into is a rule, and it is the sharpest form of the requirement Area 6 Rank 2
    has earned: **the extraction step is a lossy operator whose loss is
    unmeasured by construction, and it sits on the write path of every semantic
    tier in this arena.** Engram's answer was *keep the chunks alongside the
    facts*; this result says the chunks are not a supplement but the majority of
    extraction operator's measured loss against a verbatim baseline before the
    tier it writes to is treated as a store rather than as a cache.**

    Recorded as `UNSUCCESSFUL` for *extraction-as-a-replacement-for-verbatim* in

negative-ontology slot.**
  not deletion; it is *suppress-with-recovery*, and the evidence is that

  corruption modes** — semantic drift, topology-induced knowledge leakage,
  procedural drift, **hallucination internalization** (agents internalizing

  that **periodic reconciliation every N steps bounds expected semantic drift at

  *formal* statement in the corpus that governance caps corruption, and it is the
  answer to "what stops a forgetting pass from becoming a corruption pass."
  - **NEW THIS PASS — the slot now has a scoring function, and the arena's biggest

### **Rank 1 — System 1 synchronous writer / System 2 asynchronous ablator, with a — supporting detail

quality gate between them.**
  fast, associative, always-on; System 2 slow, deliberative, resource-limited and
  *effort-gated*. The gate is the human phenomenon that effortful thought engages
  only when fast processing fails, not routinely.
  **reconciles against the store, writing revision chains on conflict**. System 2
  runs asynchronously and **only when a gate fires** — re-reading raw context in
  full, or clustering fresh facts to induce schemas and sweep for cross-domain
  collisions (high behavioural similarity, low semantic similarity).
  where the corpus's own numbers finally separate the halves.** **D-Mem**
  (arXiv 2603.18631) reports the gate's behaviour: full deliberation fires on
  **~15% of queries** and accounts for a disproportionate share of the gain.
  **DCPM** (arXiv 2606.09483) gives the cleanest testable prediction in the
  workspace: **System 2 contributes +5.20 on PersonaMem-v2 (implicit cross-domain
  inference) but only +0.44 on LongMemEval (span recall)** — i.e. the slow half is
  nearly worthless for recall and decisive for inference. That single pair of
  numbers is what makes this architecture rather than a slogan.
  `ontology-rounds/round45-2026-09-12.md` §2; `round37-2026-09-07.md` §8.

## Area 8 · Structural fidelity: the relational-memory failure mode

**Earned by:** `…-comprehensive-september-2026.md` §3 and §12;
`…-rounds78-81-supplement.md` §1; `…-comprehensive-update-2026-09-01.md` §2;
`…-comprehensive-update-2026-11-15.md` §5.
**This pass: the area's own headline number was read at source, the evidence grew
enormously, the rank-1 gained a *mathematical* guarantee, and the area acquired
its first serious contradiction.**
#### TRANCHE 15 (ORDER 243–262) — the area gains its first controlled *negative*, and the negative is about the extraction step, not the structure
**Twenty files read, and this is the one result in them that changes what a
rank-1 implementation must do.** `…-september-2026-latest.md` §7.2 (ORDER 260,
read whole) reports **Selective Forgetting** (arXiv 2608.28978) — a direct test of
the assumption this entire area rests on:
| Task class, LongMemEval, **matched retrieval budget (5 roots)** | Token F1 |
|---|---|
| Graph-structured memory (typed nodes/edges, 2-hop subgraph, pruned) | **0.417** |
| Flat vector baseline | **0.468** |
Paired bootstrap over 500 questions: **gap 0.050, 95% CI [−0.085, −0.016] — the
interval excludes zero, so the graph loses.** The widest gap is on **specific
turn recall: 0.911 → 0.607**. The mechanism is named in the paper's own terms:
**decomposing a turn into entities discards the surface form** that specific-turn
questions are answered from.
**Why this is `UNSUCCESSFUL` and why it does not demote Rank 1.** The failed
component is the *extraction pipeline*, not the typed store. The same paper
isolates the two and finds them separable: its **forgetting module works** —
removes 9.8% of nodes and 9.5% of bytes, **token F1 unchanged (+0.001, CI
[−0.015, +0.016])** while judged correctness falls only 1.6pp (loss bounded at
3.8pp). So the corpus now contains, in one study, a working structural
operation and a failing structural operation, separated by a measurement.
**And it is the same separation this area's rank-1 already had from the other
side.** MOOSEDev's typed store wins set-completeness **1.00 vs 0.18**; Selective
Forgetting's typed store loses specific-turn recall **0.911 vs 0.607**. **Both
are true and they are not in conflict: typed structure is what makes set
enumeration, absence, and supersession traversal possible, and it is exactly
what loses verbatim surface form.** The arena's MOOSEDev slot described a
capability no vector store has and said nothing about what it costs. This is the
cost, measured.
**The design requirement this earns, stated so an architect cannot satisfy the
letter and invert the effect** (the same failure mode already recorded for
concatenating an ontology into a prompt, three paragraphs below):
> **A typed store must retain the surface chunk beside every extracted entity.**
> Entity extraction is lossy in a way that is measurable, and the loss falls
> entirely on specific-recall questions — the most common kind of question a
> memory system is actually asked. Store `(surface_chunk, entities, provenance)`
> and retrieve over both. This is the hybrid the Selective Forgetting authors
> themselves name: *surface form for specific recall, graph for relational
> queries.*
**Also in ORDER 260, and it is a second, independent negative on the same
mechanism** — **Parametric KG Memory** (arXiv 2608.25489) compiles a KG into a
LoRA adapter bank, one per entity, and reports that **storage works and
retrieval is broken**:
- single-valued relations — correct, and only the correct adapter recovers it;
- **multi-hop relations — fail**: a semantically neighbouring entity's adapter
  does *not* contain the answer;
- **retrieval by similarity — chance performance**; embedding geometry and
  weight-space geometry both fail;
- weight geometry **correlates with subgraph semantics (r ≈ 0.7) but not with
  functional retrievability**.
The paper's own summary is the finding: **knowledge stored locally does not
transfer.** This is the same pathology as Area 8's rotational hallucination
geometry (ORDER 225, arXiv 2605.10619) arriving from the storage side: a system
that has committed a fact to a location cannot recover it by proximity. The
named open problem — **query-conditioned adapter composition**, selecting and
composing adapters by query rather than by similarity — is the honest form of
the design, and it is unsolved. **Filed `unverified`, and recorded here as a
`UNSUCCESSFUL` result on the parametric-storage route so it is not rebuilt
blind.**
**Support count for this entry: 3** — Selective Forgetting (arXiv 2608.28978),
Parametric KG Memory (arXiv 2608.25489), and ORDER 262's **basis/span** account,
which explains both without measuring either. **Grade: `UNSUCCESSFUL` on the
parametric and lossy-extraction routes, `LOW` retained on the structural slot
itself**, which the two negatives *narrow* rather than overturn.
**The basis/span result (ORDER 262, arXiv 2608.11654) is the theoretical
frame both negatives fall inside, and it is the first file this arena has read
that treats memory as a formal object rather than a component.** Its claim:
**memory is a basis, knowledge is its span, and answerability is a coverage
problem** — a query is answerable iff some single item in the span covers it, and
**optimal memory is the capacity-constrained maximiser of expected coverage**.
Two consequences the arena adopts:
1. **It explains MOOSEDev arithmetically.** A vector index's span does not cover
   set enumeration or absence proofs, so those queries are *unanswerable by
   construction* rather than answered badly. That is a stronger claim than
   MOOSEDev's empirical 1.00-vs-0.18 and it is the reason the arena should
   treat structural tasks as a **different capability class**, not a harder
   version of the same one.
2. **It gives the arena its first common yardstick.** Every memory slot in this
   file has been graded on its own benchmark. A utility-capacity frontier is a
   metric those benchmarks do not share, and it is the only candidate found in
   twenty files for comparing them. Recorded as a proposal in
   `VERIFICATION.md`, not adopted as a grade — adopting a yardstick from one
   unopened preprint would repeat the error this file's own ceiling forbids.

### **Rank 1 — Constrain the generation surface to a typed structure, and verify at the — supporting detail

graph level, not the sentence level.** *(support 2 → 5 in-corpus this pass)*
  *how/why*, hippocampal and neocortical, and the documented failure of
  reconstructing relational structure from a statistical learner with no such
  substrate. And reconsolidation: a memory is re-encoded on every retrieval, and
  nothing enforces that the re-encoded copy matches the original's *shape* rather
  than its tokens.
  model name a concept or invoke a computation the structure does not declare —
  ontology-as-kernel `K = (S, F, G)`. **The agent cannot name a concept the kernel
  does not declare.** (2) **Verify at the network level**: extract a knowledge graph
  from the output, compare to ground truth by graph similarity, centrality and
  citation integrity — because sentence-level accuracy is blind to the failure.
  unanimous, and the verification is now measured four independent ways:**
  - **Structural Hallucination in LLMs** (arXiv 2603.01341, Boudourides — read at
    source this pass, it is the origin of the arena's Jaccard figure): three
    stress tests, **Roget's Thesaurus node-set Jaccard = 0.028, source-mismatch
    >94%**; **Wikidata philosophers >93% hallucination**; **Dimensions.ai
    bibliographic records 91.9% citation omission.** The paper's finding is the
    area's thesis: **topology may look structurally similar while node composition
    and edge structure are catastrophically different.**
  - **The strongest deployment evidence in the entire arena:** ontology-grounded
    clinical QA (J. Biomed. Informatics 2026, doi:10.1016/j.jbi.2026.104993) reports
    **98% accuracy (59/60) with hallucination falling from 63% (ChatGPT-4) and 48%
    (DeepSeek-R1) to 1.7%** via SPARQL-mediated generation. Note the *sample*: 60
    questions. The effect size is extraordinary; the N is not.
  - **An enterprise study with the largest N seen in this corpus — 1,800 runs**
    (arXiv 2604.00555): formally taxonomizes **neurosymbolic coupling as
    input-side / process-side / output-side**, finds current practice is
    **"predominantly input-side"** — *ontologies constrain the input context but not
    the agent's reasoning or its outputs* — and validates output-side validation.
    Deployed across **650+ production agents in 22 verticals**. This is the only
    slot in 60 files with production deployment at scale.
  - **NEW THIS PASS — the tool layer, with the cleanest before/after in the arena.**
    **The Semantic Training Gap** (`round49-2026-09-20.md` §3, arXiv 2605.11234,
    Siemens Digital Industries Software) formalises a **semantic training gap**:
    agents acquire domain *vocabulary* fluently but lack grounded **operational
    semantics** — the relational structure tying equipment ids, parameters, failure
    codes and regulatory constraints together. Its architecture embeds the
    manufacturing ontology **into the tool layer** as a typed relational config
    behind a **three-operation contract — `resolve` (map the tool call to ontology
    concepts), `contextualize` (retrieve schema context), `annotate` (attach
    provenance)** — with invariants enforced by an orchestration layer. Measured:
    across **six industry configurations, 72 tool invocations, Qwen3-32B**,
    unconstrained tool parameters produced a **43% hallucination rate for domain
    domain identifiers; ontology-grounded parameters drove that to 0%.** Small N, one
    model, one vendor — but it is the only *mechanism-level* result in the arena
    rather than a prompt-level or retrieval-level one, and it independently
    reaches the same conclusion as the 650-agent study from a different
    institution in a different domain.
  - **NEW THIS PASS — the interface question, measured three ways, and the answer
    is counter-intuitive enough to be the most actionable result in the area.**
    `ontology-rounds/round84-2026-09-11.md` §11 (**Open Ontologies**, arXiv
    2605.09184, Fabio Rovai, Tesseract Academy — a real system in **~17,400 lines
    of Rust**, single binary, no JVM/Python dependency) asks how the ontology
    should be *handed* to the model, and gets a clean ordering:

    | Access method | F1 |
    |---|---|
    | raw OWL file text to the LLM | **0.323** |
    | bare LLM, no file at all | 0.431 |
    | **structured MCP tool access** | **0.717** |

    **Feeding the model the raw ontology makes it worse than feeding it nothing
    (0.323 < 0.431).** The corpus states the mechanism in one line — *parsing noise
    overwhelms extraction* — and that is the whole finding: **the ontology's value
    is destroyed by its serialisation before it ever reaches the reasoning step.**
    The same comparison is reported independently in §2 of the same file for the
    LLMs4OL 2026 challenge at ISWC 2026 (arXiv 2608.27101, Task B, Semantic Graph
    Similarity **0.8692**, Term-Typing F1 **0.9200**, Taxonomy Discovery F1
    **0.8540**), which is **confirmation of reach across two systems, not a second
    independent study of the same one** — but the two systems are differently
    built and the numbers are reported independently, so the *direction* is the
    corroborated part and the exact F1 values are not.
    **This is a design requirement for this slot and it is new:** "constrain the
    generation surface to a typed structure" is only true if the structure reaches
    the model as a *tool contract*, not as a document. A rank-1 implementation that
    satisfies Area 8 by concatenating an ontology into the prompt satisfies the
    letter of this slot and inverts its effect. **GrOIL** (arXiv 2608.22135) states
    the same principle as a design invariant — **"no unconstrained generation step;
    the LLM is invoked only for bounded semantic decisions that resist
    deterministic resolution"** — with a 7-stage provenance-tracked pipeline
    reporting **CQ coverage 0.85 (term-life) and 0.77 (other) against ~0.90 manual**,
    where a direct LLM gets 0.63/0.40 and a multi-agent LLM 0.62/0.44. Two
    independent systems, one institution each, the same rule.
- **QUALIFICATION ADDED THIS TRANCHE (ORDER line 215,
  `frontier-research-ontology-2027-dec-supplement.md` §1) — a measured ablation
  against what this slot is *for*, and the arena had been assuming the answer.**
  **Fortunate Recall** (arXiv 2609.10413) runs the ablation this area's design
  implies and nobody else has run: **replace the behaviour ontology with generic
  primitives and measure what is lost.** The answer is **Δ = −1.7pp on
  correctness — not significant — while confabulation rises from 12.0% to
  24.2%.** Read carefully, because the direction is the whole point: **the
  ontology buys *calibration*, not *capability*.** The system answers about as
  often, and about as correctly, without the structured layer; what it cannot do
  without it is *know when it is wrong*.
  **This does not demote the slot and the reason is specific.** The slot's design
  is a *structural* constraint, and structure's demonstrated value here is
  uncertainty reduction — which is a real and large effect (a 2× confabulation
  rate) and is not the same as the accuracy claim the arena had been implicitly
  making. **But the corpus now contains no trial showing an ontology or a typed
  generation surface makes a system more correct**, and the arena should stop
  implying that it does. It is recorded as a *narrowing of the claim*, not a
  contradiction: the design is still the best-evidenced in the arena; the
  *purpose* attributed to it is now `calibration` rather than `capability`.
  The reconciliation with ORDER 221's **Where vs What** result (structural
  fidelity degrades earlier and more sharply than content accuracy, **VPA 26% →
  63%** under structural-aware RL) is that the two are consistent and jointly
  say the same thing from opposite ends: **structural defects are real, they show
  up in *confidence* long before they show up in *accuracy*, and a system scored
  on accuracy alone will look fine for a long time first.** Grade unchanged at
  `LOW+` — the ablation narrows the *claim*, it does not weaken the *evidence for
  the design*.
  - It also names a failure mode no other area has: **semantic drift** — *in
    multi-agent configurations each agent's output is the next agent's input, so
    ungrounded error compounds across the chain.* Area 2 measures single-signal
    reliability; **this is the inter-agent case and the arena has no area for it.**
    - **AND THE INTER-AGENT CASE IS NOW MEASURED, WITH TWO NEGATIVE RESULTS
      ATTACHED.** `round56-2026-09-05.md` §1 gives semantic drift its formal
      definition and the sharpest available illustration: sensor identifiers
      `TT-4201`, `%IW64` and `ReflowZone4` **all denote the same physical sensor**,
      an agent treats them as three independent facts, and produces output that is
      **"linguistically precise but operationally wrong."** Across agents the
      interpretations *diverge* — Agent A reads `TT-4201` as a temperature sensor,
      Agent B as a pressure transducer — **neither detects the mismatch because
      both outputs are linguistically coherent**, and the error propagates. The
      file calls this *"the first paper to formalize semantic drift as a
      multi-agent failure mode distinct from hallucination or knowledge gaps,"* and
      attaches **two measured negatives: RAG does not solve it, and fine-tuning
      does not solve it** — more text cannot establish equivalence relations that
      only a structured relation can state. That is the corpus's fourth
      `UNSUCCESSFUL` and the first one aimed at two designs the arena ranks
      elsewhere. **Recorded here because Area 8 is where grounding lives, and
      because the arena's own gaps list admits "social cognition beyond ToM" is
      unclaimed — this is the same hole seen from the infrastructure side.** A
      governance diagnostic is named (`Contextuality-by-Default degree`, FAOS
      2607.11948) but no area holds it.
  - **RE-READ 2026-09-26 (ORDER line 79, round 57) — a fourth independent

    Lai, Meng, Bos — Oct 2025): **57,303 questions over 40 expert ontologies

    80–92%**, **reasoning 3–4 pp lower**, and on the two hardest formal tasks
    even the best model (Qwen2.5-72B) reaches only **R4 SWRL 75.6%** and
    **R5 description logic 68.8%**. The floor is the finding: **class hierarchy
    construction scores 0.1–2.0% BERTScore F1 — essentially near-random.** The
    arena's rank-1 thesis is that the model cannot produce reliable relational
    structure; OntoURL says the split is not *can it or can't it* but *which
    operation* — reading declared structure is nearly solved, inferring over it
    is hard, and **generating it is absent.** That is the strongest available
    evidence for the design consequence the slot already carries (task-oriented
    sub-ontologies, never one general-purpose ontology): the model is not a
    weaker builder of big ontologies, it is not a builder at all.
    **AND IT CARRIES A RESULT THAT LANDS ON AREA 13: chain-of-thought makes
    formal reasoning *worse*.** Qwen-72B drops **14.5 pp on Understanding and
    15.6 pp on Reasoning** under CoT, while CoT *improves* construction
    (L1: 6.0% → 18.5%). **Step-by-step reasoning helps generation and hurts
    comprehension and inference over formal structure** — recorded in Area 13.

  - **A third retrieval structure, and the one with the largest reported delta.**
    **OG-RAG** (`round57-2026-09-06.md` §7, arXiv 2412.15235, Sharma, Kumar, Li)
    builds a **hypergraph** whose hyperedges are ontology-grounded clusters of
    factual knowledge and retrieves the *minimal set of hyperedges* forming a
    conceptually complete context — not the most similar chunks. Across four
    LLMs: **+55% fact recall, +40% response correctness, +30% faster context
    attribution, +27% fact-based reasoning accuracy**, and it answers *which
    source supports this claim*. **Counted as a fifth independent source for
    Rank 2**, not this one: this is a retrieval *shape*, and the arena keeps
    retrieval structure in Rank 2. Recorded here because the attribution half
    matters — Rank 3's verdict channel and this provenance channel are the same
    need seen from two ends.
  - **A mathematical guarantee, new this pass:** **SCG-Mem** (arXiv 2604.20117)
    constrains LLM decoding with a **Prefix Trie** over a Cognitive Schema, so the
    model is *mathematically incapable* of generating a memory key not in the
    schema — a **structural guarantee** of no hallucinated keys, not a statistical
    reduction. Its second half is **Piagetian schema evolution**: *assimilation*
    (new input mapped to existing schema) and *accommodation* (schema expanded when
    it cannot be assimilated).

    It also prices Area 8 Rank 3's abstention concern from the other side:

    confidently wrong most of the time."** Recorded next to the figure it qualifies;

    The same section carries the series' strongest theoretical claim, and it is an

    must interpolate fiction to preserve coherence** — making hallucination "an
    architectural inevitability" rather than an optimisation artifact. **If right,
    this is the strongest theoretical support in the corpus for this slot's whole
    thesis. It is also the corpus's most load-bearing unverified claim** — a paper
    series arguing that a field's central problem is unsolvable at the current

  - **AND A SECOND, INDEPENDENT INSTRUMENT NOW SAYS THE SAME THING ABOUT MODEL
    SIZE.** **OntoLearner** (`round49-2026-09-20.md` §1, arXiv 2607.01977,
    Giglou et al., MIT-licensed at `github.com/sciknoworg/OntoLearner` — **the first
    adoptable benchmarking infrastructure in this area**, 180 machine-readable
    ontologies across 22 domains with leakage-aware splits, evaluated over 22
    retrieval models and 12 LLMs) converges on: **"failure modes scale with
    ontological complexity rather than model size or architectural sophistication."
    The bottleneck is a **structural mismatch between how models encode knowledge
    and how ontologies organise it.** Read against PhantomBench's size-relevance
    paradox (line 70) **and the arena's own inversion finding, this is a
three-way convergence on the same claim from three unrelated literatures:
**bigger models and more verified apparatus do not fix a missing substrate.**
    - **PRESERVED DISAGREEMENT, and it is inside the same two files.** The next
      file read (`round51-2026-09-20.md` §7.9, arXiv 2608.31118) reports a
      controlled 13-model study *using OntoLearner itself* and reaches a **more
      nuanced and partly opposite conclusion**: increasing parameter count
      **primarily improves precision rather than recall**, the largest gains fall
      between **9B and 27B**, and **"architecture and lineage can outweigh nominal
      parameter count"** — with model size "an insufficient selection criterion"
      rather than an irrelevant one. So the corpus holds both *"failure scales
      with complexity, not model size"* and *"size buys precision, not recall,
      and only to ~27B."* **These are reconcilable** (a bounded precision gain that
      does not touch recall is consistent with a complexity-driven failure mode)
      **but the corpus does not reconcile them and neither do I** (R-J4). The
      practical reading is that neither claim rescues a system with a missing
      substrate; the disagreement is about how much to argue about the model.
    **The design consequence is the strongest practical recommendation in the arena
    so far and it is a subtraction, not an addition: build *task-oriented*
    ontologies — smaller, decomposed, complexity-matched sub-ontologies — rather
    than one general-purpose brain-scale ontology.** That is the one requirement in
    this file that also satisfies R-J5, because at 14,589 files a single
    general-purpose ontology is precisely the thing whose complexity becomes the
    failure mode.
  - **TRANCHE 8 — A SIXTH DOMAIN FOR THE INVERSION, AND THE ONLY ONE WHERE *BOTH*
    PATHS SUCCEED.** Fifteen files were read this tranche; two carried design
    evidence, and they are the cleanest statement of this slot's thesis the corpus
    has produced, because they arrive from **IETF protocol engineering** rather
    than from any of the six ontology/ML literatures the slot already rests on.
    `cbor-tag-6-evolution-semantics-drift.md` (ORDER line 135, read whole) and
    `cbor-tag-6-dependent-type-formalization.md` (ORDER line 134, read whole)
    together establish the following, and every clause is the file's own claim.
    - **CBOR tag 6's meaning depends on the runtime type of its content** — an
      integer turns it into a *shared item reference*, an array `[int, any]` into an
      *argument reference*, and in draft-19 everything else is **RESERVED**. The
      specification's own words: the semantics *"depend on its tag content."* This
      is content-dependent dispatch, and it **broke out of CDDL entirely** — RFC
      8610 assumes *one tag number = one content type*, and the CBOR WG reached no
      consensus on fixing it (IETF interim 2022-12). **A schema language could not
      express the construct, so the construct escaped verification.**
    - **Three semantic shifts across 19+ drafts, and no version indicator in the
      payload.** The draft version is knowable only from a media-type parameter, the
      application specification, or out-of-band agreement. The file's verdict:
      **"No automatic negotiation mechanism exists in any current draft."**
    - **And therefore the two failure modes are silent corruption and hard
      failure, with nothing in between.** Draft-15 data carrying `6("suffix")`
      means *"prepend prefix table[0]"*; a draft-19 decoder classifies that as
      **RESERVED** and *"should reject or error"* — the file's own words for the
      outcome are **"Silent data corruption or hard failure."**
    - **A widely-deployed decoder already does the discarding.** The file records
      that **fxamacker/cbor v1 — the Go library most deployments use — "ignores tag
      6 entirely": it decodes the content and discards the tag number.** Prefix
      references are therefore silently reinterpreted as bare strings. This is the
      slot's thesis in its purest form and it is not a model hallucinating: **the
      structure was present, correct, and complete in the input, and a conforming
      parse destroyed it.**
    **Why this is the strongest evidence in the slot and why it is counted as
    corroboration rather than as a new independent line of work.** It is a sixth
    *domain* converging on the same conclusion — and it is the first in which the
    model is not the culprit. The other five are all *"the generator emitted
    structure that was never there."* This one is **"the structure was there and a
    validator approved a parse that had thrown it away."* **Support for this slot's
    design: 7 independent sources across 6 domains.**
    **The new design requirement it earns, and it is the sharpest statement of
    "verify at the network level" in the arena: *a parse that succeeds is not a
    parse that preserved the structure.* The check that catches this failure is not
    a syntax check and not a schema check — it is a round-trip check on the
    disambiguating fields specifically, and **no format validator will ever report
    it**, because the output is well-formed by construction. This is why the
    arena's rank-1 insists on *graph-level* comparison: at the byte level this
    failure is invisible, because the bytes are correct.
    **The formal-verification file supplies the same conclusion as a proof
    obligation. It is recorded at `UNTESTED`, not `UNSUCCESSFUL`, and the
    distinction is worth one clause because the arena keeps both registers: no one
    has attempted this proof, so there is no trial to have failed.** A complete
    proof of tag 6 would require (1) a
    **sum type** for the content, (2) proof that dispatch is **total and
    deterministic**, (3) proof of **termination** of recursive unpacking via a
    well-founded relation on packed depth, (4) **round-trip equivalence** between
    packed and unpacked forms, and (5) **non-malleability**. **The first and only
    formally verified CBOR implementation — EverCBOR / EverCDDL (arXiv 2505.17335,
    ACM CCS 2025, F*, extracting to verified C and Rust) — explicitly excludes
    Packed CBOR.** The gap is not that the proof is hard; it is that **the one
    verified implementation declines the construct on the grounds that its dispatch
    is content-dependent, and the specification language cannot state the
    property.** Grade for the proof obligation: `UNTESTED`. The file is
    `verified: false` and `confidence: high`, which under C-020 is itself an
    instance of the defect class this tranche opened.
  - **TRANCHE 9 — A SEVENTH DOMAIN, AND THE FIRST ONE IN WHICH THE INSTRUMENT
    ITSELF IS MEASURED TO BE BLIND. This is the sharpest statement of the §8
    inversion anywhere in the arena, because it is stated as a property of a
    measurement device rather than of a document.** `conservation-normalized-
    cross-layer-attribution.md` (ORDER line 140, read whole) reports HiLRP's
    measurement (arXiv 2609.01282) across five hierarchical ViT backbones:

    | Backbone | Naive AttnLRP conservation ratio | HiLRP |
    |---|---|---|
    | Swin-B | **3.08** (inflated) | 0.77 |
    | PVT-v2-b2 | **0.00** (zeroed) | 0.38 |
    | EfficientViT-B1 | **0.00** (zeroed) | 0.13 |
    | EfficientViT-B2 | **0.00** (zeroed) | 0.35 |
    | MaxViT-S | **0.00** (broken) | 0.16 |

    **The file's own sentence is the finding, quoted because it cannot be
    paraphrased without losing it:** standard LRP relevance is *"inflated by more
    than threefold in one case and reduced to exactly zero at depth in the other
    four,"* **"while still scoring well on localization metrics (0.80–0.98
    Pointing)."**

    **Four of five backbones produce a relevance signal that is identically zero
    at depth, and the metric that grades the instrument reports 0.80–0.98.** The
    validated path (localization, a localization task) says pass. The unvalidated
    path (the relevance signal the instrument is *for*) is gone. **This is the §8
    inversion with the corpus's own finger on the dial: the number that is checked
    and the number that is used have nothing to do with each other, and the
    instrument is not merely wrong, it is wrong in a direction the metric cannot
    express** — a ratio of 0.00 and a score of 0.90 are not in tension under any
    shared scale.

    **What it costs this slot, precisely, and it is a cost rather than a
    support.** Every attribution-based mechanism the arena has recorded — token
    attribution for query expansion, layer-type-aware fusion, salience re-ranking
    in Area 10, head-weighted rollout — is graded by a localization or
    faithfulness metric and consumed as a magnitude. **A signal can be perfectly
    localized and carry no mass at all.** The design requirement this earns is
    therefore the *verification* half of this slot applied to the instruments and
    not only to the generated text: **an attribution instrument must be checked
    for a conservation or mass property — that the quantity it emits still sums to
    what it claims to decompose — before its score is believed, and a localization
    score is not evidence that the instrument emits anything.** This is
    deterministic, it is a property of a number rather than of a benchmark, and it
    is therefore R-J2-compatible. **Support for this slot: 8 independent sources
    across 7 domains.**
    **The proposed repair, and a narrowing of it the file does not state.** The
    file's own design is per-layer renormalization, `R̃ᵢ = Rᵢ · (ΣR^(l+1)/ΣR^(l))`,
    with Proposition 2 proving it **preserves relative ordering within a layer**
    (multiplication by a positive scalar). Read against the arena's MEMTIER
    finding — a monotone rescaling of a dominant term cannot change a ranking —
    **the repair provably cannot change which tokens the top-k selector picks
    *within* a layer.** It can change *cross-layer* comparison, which is exactly
    what the file's own key hypothesis says it is for ("ensuring that the
    cross-layer fusion operates on conservation-valid attributions"). **So the
    design is real and its scope is narrower than its framing suggests: it repairs
    a *fusion* defect, not a *selection* defect. Recorded as a qualification
    rather than adopted at the strength the file proposes it.**
  - **AN EIGHTH DOMAIN, AND IT IS THE SHARPEST FORM OF THE SAME DEFECT BECAUSE
    THE DISAMBIGUATOR IS PRESENT.** `coap-content-format-registration-sequence.md`
    (ORDER line 139, read whole) reports a **parameter-name collision with
    divergent semantics** across two IANA registries:

    | Media Type | packed=0 | packed=1 |
    |---|---|---|
    | `application/dns+cbor` | implicit tag 28259 (name compression) | tag 113 (common table) |
    | `application/cbor` | **no packing at all** (empty tables) | tag 113 (common table) |

    **`packed=0` denotes two different wire formats in two registered media
    types**, and the file's own verdict is that **IANA's duplicate check cannot
    see it** — *"IANA may not detect semantic collision. The 'Media Type' column
    (added by RFC 9876) helps distinguish base media types, but the parameter
    semantics are not validated."*

    **This is worse than the tag-6 case, and the reason is the direction of the
    guarantee.** Tag 6 was discarded by a decoder that was not required to keep
    it. Here **every participating party validates successfully**: the registry
    has a column for the disambiguator, the disambiguator is populated, the entry
    is unique, the DE reviews it, and two readers holding the same
    `packed=0` parameter still mean different things. **A uniqueness check
    cannot detect a semantic collision, and the file demonstrates the collision
    occurring inside a registry whose entire purpose is to make meanings
    unambiguous.** The design requirement is the same one as the parser's, stated
    for registries: **uniqueness of a *key* is not uniqueness of a *meaning*; a
    namespace that permits the same token to bind to different definitions in
    different scopes must carry the binding in the token, not beside it.**
    **The two files are adjacent in the corpus order (138 then 139) and read in
    that order they say something neither says alone: 138 is the file that
    *creates* the collision, and 139 is the file that *discovers* it.**
    `coap-content-format-registration-for-packed-cbor.md` (ORDER line 138, read
    whole) proposes registering `application/cbor;packed=0/1/2` as three
    separate CoAP Content-Format IDs, and gives as its **reason** that *"the
    `packed` parameter value changes the **decoding semantics**"*. That
    reasoning is correct. **And it is precisely what manufactures the defect:
    the file argues for separate registrations on the grounds that one
    parameter name denotes different wire formats in different media types, and
    the separate registrations are what makes both of those meanings
    simultaneously valid.** The alternative it considers and declines —
    §3.4, a **single** registration with the semantics documented in RFC 9876's
    new Media Type column — is the option that would have kept one token bound
    to one meaning.

    **So the collision is not an oversight the corpus failed to notice; it is
    the intended, reasoned output of a design that is defensible in isolation.**
    That is a harder defect to fix than a typo and a more important one to have
    found, because **it means no review step on this corpus's registry files
    would have caught it — the author states the semantic difference in the
    sentence that justifies the design.** A checker that asks "is the entry
    unique?" passes. A checker that asks "is the reasoning sound?" passes. The
    system produced a correct argument for a specification that two
    implementations cannot both follow.

    **Its three own admissions, which is why it is recorded as a domain rather
    than a slot.** (a) `draft-ietf-cbor-packed-19` is annotated in the file's
    **own sources table** as *"(expired Aug 2026)"* — and the file's §10 "Next
    Steps" still lists *"Coordinate with CBOR WG chairs on early allocation
    request"*, i.e. it is scheduling meetings about a specification that lapsed
    before the file was written (`generated: 2026-09-14`, six weeks after
    expiry), under `status: active` and `confidence: 0.9`. **A plan whose
    target document is named as expired in its own bibliography is the
    apparatus/content inversion in its purest form, and `verified: false` is the
    one field in the file that is telling the truth.** (b) The three named IANA
    Designated Experts (§5.1, Bilhanan Silverajan, Klaus Hartke, Alexander
    Pelov) are a volatile external fact carrying decision weight, recorded
    `unverified` — a person-list is exactly the kind of claim that decays
    silently and that a corpus has no way to notice decaying. (c) All
    registration IDs are `TBD`, so **nothing here is a specification; it is a
    plan for one**, and it is graded as one.

    **Support for this slot: 10 independent sources across 9 domains, one of
    which now spans two files.**
  - **A NINTH DOMAIN, AND IT IS THE COMPLEMENT OF THE ONE ABOVE: HiLRP shows an
    attribution instrument can be *blind*; this shows one can be *silently
    invalidated by an architecture change it never detects*.**
    `clvr-aware-layer-type-attribution.md` (ORDER line 137, read whole) reports
    CLVR (arXiv 2607.07953, Cerruti, Rieder, Rowlands, Jin, Schlag —
    *"Linear Attention Architectures: Mechanisms, Trade-offs, and Cross-Layer
    Routing"*): Gated DeltaNet layers project their **write value** into the
    **shared residual stream** through a **zero-initialized** projection
    `εₗ,ₜ = P_l·vₗ,ₜ`, from where it propagates to *every subsequent layer*.

    **The design consequence the file draws is the one that belongs here:**
    standard per-layer attribution attributes a routed value to the *receiving*
    layer, so **the signal is not mis-measured, it is assigned to the wrong
    organ** — the file's own example is a GDN value from layer 5 being credited
    to layer 8's attention. **This is Area 8's exact failure mode with a
    mechanism attached**: the structure that makes the model work
    (cross-layer integration) is invisible to the instrument meant to explain
    it, and the instrument's error is not noise but a *relabeling*.

    **And the design requirement it earns is one no other file in 145 has
    produced, because it is about the *validity precondition* of a measurement
    rather than about its output: _an attribution pipeline must state the
    architecture assumptions under which its numbers mean anything, and must
    detect when they stop holding._** The file's own recommendation does this
    correctly and against its own interest — **"Since Qwen3-Next does NOT use
    CLVR, the current layer-type-aware attribution pipeline is valid as-is. No
    immediate changes needed."** A research file whose headline finding
    concerns a measurement error, concluding that the error **does not apply
    to any model in production**, is the rare instance of the corpus declining
    hypothesis`; *"The CLVR-aware attribution methods are entirely
    theoretical"*).

    **The useful part is therefore not the method — four are proposed, none
    tested — it is the precondition-check itself, and the file hands the arena
    a ready-made one:** CLVR's routing strength is `‖P_l·vₗ,ₜ‖`, and because `P_l`
    is zero-initialized, **a model that routes nothing has a measurable routing
    magnitude of zero**. So the check is deterministic: *measure ‖P_l·v‖ at
    inference; if it is ~0 the pipeline's layer-boundary assumption holds, and
    if it is not, the pipeline is silently mis-attributing.* **That is a
    one-number validity check on a whole attribution stack, it is a property of
    the model rather than a benchmark, and it survives R-J2 intact.** It pairs
    with HiLRP's conservation check as the two halves of instrument validation:
    *conservation* asks whether the instrument emits the mass it claims, and
    *routing magnitude* asks whether its unit of analysis matches the model's
    actual connectivity.

      insufficient**"* — type is *"an online property … determined at inference

    as a fact._** The convergence is worth stating explicitly because the three
    instances share no vocabulary and no authors: MEMTIER found the signal has
    no variance, CLVR found the boundary does not exist, RouteHead found the

    METRIC.** This is the finding that should change how the arena reads every
    other grade in this file, and it arrives from a completely unrelated domain
    — software supply chain — which is what makes it evidence rather than
    metaphor. `cross-registry-provenance-verification.md` (ORDER line 153, read
    whole) reports the **May 2026 TanStack compromise** and the **TrapDoor
    campaign**, sourced to the SLSA project's own write-up
    (`slsa.dev/blog/2026/05/mini-shai-hulud-what-slsa-can-and-cannot-do`) and
    `hvtracker.net`:

    | Fact | Value |
    |---|---|
    | Packages compromised | **84** npm packages, 42 `@tanstack` packages |
    | Attestation level on those packages | **cryptographically valid SLSA Build Level 3** |
    | Signer identity reported | **correct repository, correct workflow, correct ref** |
    | What the packages were | **malware** |

    **Read the middle two rows together and the whole §8 thesis is settled
    empirically rather than argued.** The attestation faithfully reported
    everything it attests. The build was compromised — cache poisoning plus
    extraction of the legitimate OIDC token from runner memory — and so the
    provenance described a compromised build *accurately*. The attacker's route
    did not defeat the signature; **the signature was truthful about a lie.**

    **This is the arena's constitution axiom stated in one sentence by an
    independent party, and the arena has been arguing it from a corpus of its
    own documents for ten tranches:** *provenance attests where the build
    happened, not whether the build was trustworthy; a valid proof of origin is
    not a proof of safety.* Every `verified:` block, every 16/16 TOC, every
    `confidence:` value, every SLSA Level 3 badge in this workspace is an
    attestation of origin. **The TanStack packages had a Level 3 attestation and
    were malware.** The file's own phrasing is *"provenance theatre"*, and its
    conclusion is stated as a limit rather than a control: **"It does NOT answer:
    'Is the code at commit X safe?'"**

    **Why it belongs to this slot and not to `ARENA-INFRA.md`, which is the
    judgment call this tranche had to make.** The §4 guard-4 test is whether a
    named brain function is filled. It is: **the distinction between a signal
    that is well-formed and a signal that is true** is the metacognitive
    discrimination between *confidence* and *accuracy*, and Area 8 is the only
    slot in the arena that makes the verification level a design decision. The
    instance is also a *registry* defect in the sense Area 8 cares about: an
    attestation scheme whose validity predicate is `signature verifies` and
    whose intended predicate is `code is safe` — a key that is unique and
    unambiguous while the meaning behind it is not.

    **The asymmetry the file records is the build spec, and it is checkable.**
    The three registries are not equivalent: **PyPI L3, npm L3, crates.io L1 —
    checksums only, no cryptographic link from crate to commit**
    (`rust-lang/cargo#12661`, closed May 2025, explicitly deferring SLSA to a
    future RFC). **"Signed" and "unsigned" are the same word meaning two
    different guarantees, in one pipeline, for three consumers of the same
    artifact.** That is a first-class instance of Area 8's registry-collision
    finding (ORDER 139, where `packed=0` binds to two wire formats and every
    participating validator passes) in a completely different namespace, and it
    earns the arena's rule in its general form: **a security label must carry
    the guarantee it stands for, not just its name.**

    **What it costs this slot, and the cost is the useful part.** Provenance
    verification answers *"did this come from the expected workflow at commit
    X?"* It is **necessary and not sufficient**, and the corpus says so against
    its own project's interest. This does not demote Rank 1 — the slot's claim
    is that verification must happen at the *graph* level rather than the
    sentence level, and the TanStack result supports that by showing a
    *perfectly executed* verification level is the wrong level. **It sharpens
    the slot's question from "verify the output" to "verify the output against a
    source whose trust you established by other means," and no slot in the
    arena currently supplies those other means.** That gap is now named and
    dated rather than assumed. **Support for this slot: 13 independent sources
    across 12 domains.** Grade for the slot does not move; **the arena's `HIGH`
    ceiling is further justified, because the attack here defeated a mechanism
    that was working exactly as specified.**
  - **TRANCHE 10 — A FOURTEENTH DOMAIN, AND THE FIRST NEGATIVE RESULT IN THE
    ARENA FROM A *REPLICATED* PRODUCTION COMPARISON RATHER THAN A SINGLE PAPER.**
    `cross-encoder-reranking-bm25-candidates.md` (ORDER line 148, read whole) is

    sources, each with its own numbers, agreeing on one conclusion and — this is
    the part that matters — disagreeing about what to do about it.**

    **The conclusion, and it is arithmetic rather than empirical.** Reranking
    permutes the candidate set `C` and nothing else, so *maximum achievable
    recall after reranking equals first-stage recall exactly*:
    `|C ∩ R*| / |R*|` before and after. The file states it as the CE-QE paper
    does — *"no amount of downstream reranking or fusion can recover a document
    that was never in the candidate set — the recall ceiling is fixed at the
    first stage."* **This is MEMTIER's zero-variance null and Open Ontologies'
    0.323-vs-0.717 ordering arriving in a third, entirely mechanical form: the
    knob cannot move the quantity.** MEMTIER's reweighting cannot change a
    ranking; a reranker cannot change a set.

    **The negative result is the finding, and it is measured, not predicted.**

    | Source | Measurement |
    |---|---|
    | **Training-Free Lexical-Dense Fusion** (arXiv 2606.04194) | **reranking *hurts*: −6.9pp Hit@1** over fused top-10 on OOD conversational queries |
    | memini, LongMemEval-S (session granularity) | **98.4% → 98.4%, a measured no-op** |
    | memini, LoCoMo turn-level | +11pp R@5 / +17pp MRR |
    | Self-improving retrieval diagnostic (200k entries) | **78% of relevant entries never reach the cross-encoder**; bi-encoder R@30 = 29.0%, @100 = 43.8%, @500 = 63.6% |
    | PLUR cadence harness | Hit@5 76.7% → 90.0%; temporal-reasoning **60% → 100%** |
    | it-blue.one production baseline | hybrid first stage −49% retrieval failures; reranker only −18% more |

    **"Adding a reranker" is a reflex move that is simultaneously a no-op
    (session-granularity, recall already 98.4%), a large win (turn-level, recall
    has headroom), and a regression (−6.9pp, out-of-distribution conversational
    queries — the corpus's own target domain).** The corpus's verdict table marks
    two of its three headline claims **FALSE** and one **TRUE**, and the TRUE one
    is conditional: *reranking helps when first-stage recall has headroom.*
    **This is `UNSUCCESSFUL` in the arena's sense and the first instance with a
    replicated, cross-source negative behind it** — tried in at least four named
    production systems, and it does not work as a recall fix.

    **The one number that belongs in a build spec.** In the 78%-missed
    diagnostic, **BM25 alone beat pretrained dense embeddings by 76%** on a
    conversational-memory corpus (NDCG 0.2420 vs 0.1376), because *"questions
    mostly ask about specific entities, names, and timestamps — exact matches
    where BM25 excels."* **The arena has been arguing for a dense leg as the
    recall escape hatch since ORDER 136, and the largest-N measurement in this
    file says the dense leg loses to BM25 on exactly the corpus the arena is
    building for.** Recorded as a disagreement, not a reconciliation (R-J4): the
    CE-QE file (ORDER 136) assumes a dense leg is a *prerequisite* (*"Without
    dense retrieval leg, CE-QE has nothing to attribute over"*), and this file
    says the dense leg is weaker than the lexical one it would supplement. **Both
    can be true — CE-QE needs *some* semantic pass to attribute over, and it need
    not be a stronger retriever — but the arena should not build the dense leg on
    the assumption it is the recall fix.**

    checkable before anything is built:** *a retrieval stage may only be added
    where a measured first-stage recall@k for the target category is below
    threshold; and the measurement must be on the target query distribution, not

    resolution to retrieval (*"Retrieval-time resolution scales better than

    resolution:** *any irreversible merge — entity resolution, deduplication,

  - **A SIXTEENTH DOMAIN, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT NAMES A LOAD-BEARING OMISSION
    IN A PAPER THE ARENA HAS LEANED ON FOR TWO TRANCHES.**
    `cross-encoder-token-attribution-local-models.md` (ORDER line 149, read
    whole) examines the mechanism Area 8's CE-QE work depends on and finds the
    source paper never specified it.

    **CE-QE (arXiv 2608.00452) requires per-token relevance attributions from a
    cross-encoder, and the paper treats that capability as given.** The file
    enumerates the omission precisely: *"The paper never names a specific
    attribution technique. No mention of Integrated Gradients, SmoothGrad,
    attention rollout, SHAP, DeepLIFT, or any other method."* **A design in this
    arena has been carried for two tranches on a mechanism its own source does
    not specify, and the arena's `LOW` grade rests on the BEIR numbers rather
    than on the attribution quality — which the file names as the binding
    constraint** (*"expansion quality is bounded by attribution quality"*).

    **And the local path is blocked, deterministically.** llama.cpp's `/rerank`
    endpoint *"is fundamentally a document-scoring API with no token-level
    output"*; the attention-extraction PR (**ggml-org/llama.cpp#20086**) is
    **open since March 2026 with no merge activity since March 31**, and
    attention must be reached by bypassing each reranker's wrapper. Qwen3-
    Reranker is worse: its score is a softmax over **151,669 vocabulary tokens**,
    which vLLM's own docs call *"extremely inefficient"*, so token attribution
    there requires full-vocabulary logits at each step.

    **Why this is Area 8 and not `ARENA-INFRA.md`.** It is the same failure the
    slot already holds, one level down: **a component that produces a required
    output and does not, hidden behind an interface that returns something
    plausible instead.** The `/rerank` endpoint returns a relevance score — a
    well-formed float — for a question it was never asked. The dual-path
    architecture the file proposes (llama.cpp for scalar scoring, a
    Transformers sidecar for attribution) is the correct repair and costs
    ~50–100ms per query.

    **The design requirement, and it is checkable before anything is built:**
    *for every stage in a pipeline, name the artifact it must emit and verify
    the chosen implementation can emit it.* **Not "the reranker scores well" —
    "the reranker emits per-token attribution," which two of the three candidate
    models cannot do at all and the third can only do through an unmerged PR.**
    **This is the arena's prior-with-runtime-validity-check rule applied to an
    interface rather than to a model, and it is the cheapest unmet requirement
    in the area: one function call answers it.**
    **Support for this slot: 18 independent sources across 17 domains** (16
sources / 15 domains entering this pass, plus the six-file CBOR namespace
cluster — counted as **one** source, since all six describe the same two IETF
drafts from the same working group — and the domain-shift threshold file).
**The clustering is the rule, applied to this tranche: six files, one source.**
