 - `active-wiki/research/dns-cbor-packed-parameter-rename-evaluation.md`
   (ORDER 166) — §6.2 the **RFC 8447**-modelled profiles registry.
 - `active-wiki/research/dns-over-quic-compression-tradeoff-analysis.md`
   (ORDER 167) — §2/§3 the per-transaction signalling cost.
 - `active-wiki/research/draft-ietf-cbor-packed-tag-allocation-monitor.md`
   (ORDER 169) — **§7.1, the TCB-boundary statement, and §6.2 the immutable
   vector sets.** Read in this cluster but cited here because it is the
   seventh file of the same working-group material and grades as part of it.

    **The requirement, and it is the third form of a rule the arena has now
    written twice.** The arena holds (a) a semantic difference between two
    registrations needs a disambiguator, and (b) *uniqueness of a key is not
    uniqueness of a meaning; a namespace that permits the same token to bind
    to different definitions in different scopes must carry the binding in the
    token, not beside it.* The third form is the one these files supply, and it
    is about **how a binding gets into a scope**: ORDER 163 §4.2 quotes
    RFC 6838 §4.3 — *"parameters 'may be automatically made available to the
    media type by virtue of being a subtype of a content type that defines a
    set of parameters applicable to any of its subtypes'"* — and draws the
    consequence. `application/dns+cbor` carries the **`+cbor` structured syntax
    suffix**, so a `packed` parameter registered for `application/cbor`
    **may automatically apply to `application/dns+cbor`** — binding, by
    inheritance, a name to the *wrong* meaning inside a scope where it was
    never defined and never registered.

    > **A name's presence in a scope is not evidence that it was defined
    > there. A resolver must distinguish an asserted binding from an inherited
    > one, and a disambiguator carried *beside* the token is not sufficient
    > when a rule exists that can copy the token into a scope unaccompanied by
    > its meaning.**

    **Why this is worse than the collision ORDER 139 found, and this is the
    part worth having.** The collision is a mistake two careful readers can
    both avoid. **Inheritance is not a mistake at all — it is a rule working
    exactly as specified, and it is the specified behaviour that manufactures
    the wrong binding.** The arena's TanStack result says an attack defeated a
    mechanism working as specified; this says *ordinary conformance* defeats it,
    with no attacker. §8's inversion, reached by a different road: the
    validated path produced a semantically invalid scope.

    **And the collision has a second, temporal form the arena had not named,
    and it is a cascade.** RFC 9876 §4.1.3, quoted in 163: *"If a temporary
    registration (in any range) refers to a provisional Media Type that is
    abandoned, IANA must remove the entry and set the Content-Format ID value
    back to 'Unassigned'."* So a **provisional** name does not merely risk its
    own validity — it carries the revocability of its own lifetime into every
    registration that binds to it, and abandonment resets identifiers that
    permanence is a property of its dependants, not of itself; any identifier
    others bind to must be permanent, or every dependant must be revocable at
    the same time.** At 14,589 files this is the rule behind a class of failure
    the arena has not yet hit but has now seen specified: a memory record that
    binds to a provisional concept id is itself provisional, and nothing in the
    current stack propagates that.

    **The resolution the six files converge on is adoption, not construction,
    and it has a named precedent in the arena for the first time.** ORDER 166
    §6.2 proposes a **"Packed CBOR Profiles" registry modeled on the TLS
    Cipher Suite Registry (RFC 8447)** — a profile is a *named bundle*
    (`packed-basic` / `packed-full` / `packed-split` / `dns-packed-basic`),
    and implementers *"reference profiles by name, not parameter values."*
    This is the **TLS cipher-suite pattern applied to a memory/format
    namespace, from a completely unrelated domain**, and it is the same move
    as Area 8 Rank 1's own: put the meaning in a *name* the consumer
    a proposal, and the file says the long-term registry is *Month 3+*.** The
    precedent (RFC 8447) is the part with a grade behind it.

    **Two things in this cluster are better than the proposal and are recorded
    because they are reusable regardless.**

    (a) **ORDER 164's maturity ladder is a three-state column, not a boolean.**
    It recommends registering `packed=2` as **"Available, Not Recommended"** —
    a third state between "no" and "yes" — with a promotion gate: *"If ≥3
    interoperable implementations + deployment evidence → Request
    Recommended=Y"* at Month 24. **A boolean recommendation flag cannot
    express "this works, do not use it yet," and that is precisely the state
    most mechanisms are actually in.** This is the same discipline as
    ORDER 143's *"Pre-classification as prior, not constraint"* and the
    arena's own evidence grades, arriving from standards practice: **encode
    maturity as a first-class value rather than collapsing it into a
    recommendation bit.**

    (b) **ORDER 165's measured table settles a WG debate and simultaneously
    shows the limit of the metric that settled it.** The IETF 123 evaluation
    (Lenders/Bormann/Schmidt/Wählisch; YourThings IEEE S&P 2019, IoTFinder
    EuroS&P 2020, MonIoTr IMC 2019) produced the allocation A=16, B=8, C=8
    and the famous *"uptick at A=16"*. Read the size rows:

    | A | mean | σ | median | max |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | 8 | 83.2 | 53.4 | 73 | 517 |
    | **12** | **83.1** | **53.3** | 73 | 517 |
    | **16** | **83.1** | **53.3** | 73 | 517 |

    **A=12 and A=16 are the same row.** The uptick is entirely in *coverage* —
    messages with every suffix in the table, ~75% → ~95% — and the mean moves
    by **zero bytes** across the decision boundary. So the working group
    **restored A=16 from the interim's A=12 on a coverage proxy while the size
    metric is flat**, and the file's own §Uncertainties says the coverage
    figure is dataset-dependent and that DoH resolvers *"might have flatter
    suffix distributions, shifting the uptick to A=20+"*. **A normative
    allocation was decided on a proxy the deciding document says may not
    transfer to the deployment population.** That is `C-019` — a metric
    computed over the wrong population, reported confidently over the wrong
    set — **in a document that is the primary IETF record of the decision, and
    it produced a published standard.** It is the strongest single argument in
    the arena that a population check is not hygiene but a gate.

    **The cluster also contains the arena's sharpest recorded internal
    contradiction, and it is in one file, between two sections, about a risk
    the file itself raised.** ORDER 163 §4.2 states the inheritance risk
    (quoted above). Its §4.4 then concludes, with no intervening argument:
    ***"No automatic inheritance: DNS-CBOR must register its own `packed`
    parameter with its own semantics."*** And its own §5.2 recommendation 5
    says the opposite — *"Monitor draft-ietf-cbor-packed … if they register
    `packed` for `application/cbor`, DNS-CBOR must ensure no inheritance
    conflict **via RFC 6838 §4.3**."* **The same file identifies a
    mechanism, denies it in its conclusion, and then writes a to-do item that
    presupposes it.** Three mentions, two positions, no resolution anywhere in
    254 lines. Filed as **C-024** in `ARENA-INFRA.md`, and it is a different
    class from C-019: nothing here is mis-measured — **a stated risk is simply
    dropped on the way to the recommendation, and the artifact carries no trace
    that it was ever live.**

    **One more contradiction, across files, on the same evidence.** ORDER 164
    and ORDER 165 both describe the IETF 123 dataset and **disagree by an
    order of magnitude**: 164 says *"90 devices, 1.2M queries, 2.7M
    responses"*; 165 says *"0.2 million queries, 1.3 million responses"* from
    *"90 consumer devices"*. Both attribute it to the same slide deck. Only
    the device count agrees. **The corpus cannot state its own evidence base
    consistently across two files written about the same slides**, which means
    any figure the arena cites from this cluster must name the file it came
    from and may not be aggregated across them.

    **The seventh file in the cluster contributes the arena's first
    per-transaction control-cost law, and it is the one that generalises past
    formats.** ORDER 167 measures QUIC's DATAGRAM-vs-stream overhead using
    arXiv 2504.09200: quic-go emits a `MAX_STREAMS` frame **for every retired
    stream**, 66 bytes, ACK-eliciting — *"For 100 queries, this added 13,000
    bytes of signaling overhead"*, and ~2.5 KB of extra memory per query for
    the stream path. **The payload optimisation the rest of the file argues
    about cannot touch any of it, because it scales with transaction count
    rather than with transaction size.** That is a general law, and the arena
    has independently measured its memory twice: AgentIR's router captures
    100% of the oracle gap at **470μs against 53ms of retrieval** — *the
    classification cost is 0.9% of the retrieval cost, so optimising retrieval
    payload, state whether the quantity is bounded by per-unit work or
    per-transaction work, and measure the per-transaction term separately —
    at 14,589 files a fixed per-query cost dominates a variable per-document
    one.** Corroborates the routing-beats-reweighting result from a domain
    conference paper, Raspberry Pi Zero, the file's own `verified: false`),
    but the law is arithmetic and the requirement is deterministic.**

  - **TRANCHE 11 — AN EIGHTEENTH DOMAIN, AND IT IS A FOURTH ARRIVAL AT THE
    ARENA'S HIGHEST-LEVERAGE STRUCTURAL RULE, FROM A FILE THAT REFUSES A
    GRADE.** ORDER 168
    (`domain-shift-saturation-profile-msmarco-vs-longmemeval.md`, read whole)
    proposes `τ_g(domain) = α_domain × max(g)` — a saturation threshold that
    **changes with the query domain**, α≈0.1 for MS MARCO and α≈0.25 for
    LongMemEval-S, selected by a logistic regression on query length, temporal
    markers, first-person pronouns and token-type ratio.

    **Why it is a fourth arrival and not a restatement.** The arena's rule, as
    written at the tenth domain above, is: *a quantity computed offline and
    consumed at inference as an assignment must be carried as a prior with a
    runtime validity check, never as a fact.* MEMTIER found the signal has no
    variance; CLVR found the assumed boundary does not exist; RouteHead found
    the best head choice is dataset-specific. **ORDER 168 supplies the missing
    half of the rule — what the runtime validity check *is*.** The other three
    say a static label is unsafe and stop. This file proposes a five-feature
    classifier that costs one forward pass over the query string, and its two
    failure modes are written down: α too low classifies saturated heads as
    healthy (*"garbage GMAR weights"*), α too high does the reverse. **A
    validity check with a stated cost and two named failure directions is
    buildable; "add a runtime check" is not.** That is the whole contribution,
    and it is the first time the arena's most-repeated requirement has arrived
    with an implementation attached.

    **The file refuses its own grade, and the refusal is in its own text.**
    §Open Questions 1: *"No existing study measures attention entropy of
    BGE-reranker-v2-m3 on matched MS MARCO / LongMemEval-S query pairs."* Its
    §Summary claims support from *"multiple independent evidence streams"* —
    and all five are about **other models on other tasks**: Wang et al. on
    saturation theory, CELI on BEIR, Rosa et al. on model size, ConvMemory v2
    on LoCoMo, BEIR on zero-shot. **The prediction table is headed
    "Predicted", the protocol section is headed "Expected results", and the
    frontmatter says `verified: []` with `confidence: high`.** Grade
    **`UNTESTED`**, refusal recorded, and the file is not cited for the
    direction of its effect — only for the shape of its repair.

    **But the corpus now contains a direct disagreement about the target
    domain, and per R-J4 it is preserved rather than resolved.** ORDER 148
    (tranche 10) measured cross-encoder reranking **hurting by −6.9pp
    Hit@1 on out-of-distribution conversational queries**. ORDER 168 argues
    the opposite about the same queries: out-of-domain conversational memory
    produces **less saturated attention and healthier gradients**, so
    attribution-driven query expansion should be *more* valuable out of
    domain — it calls this *"a paradoxical implication"* and notes it
    *"inverts the typical domain-adaptation narrative."* **The two cannot both
    be a description of how the same domain treats the same class of model.**
    The most likely resolution is that they are about different mechanisms
    (score-level reranking versus gradient-level attribution) and neither file
    says so. **Recorded as an open disagreement with both sides attributed;
    neither file is downgraded for it, and the arena does not pick.**

    **The design requirement that survives the refusal, and it is
    deterministic:** *a threshold constant must ship with the distribution it
    was calibrated on, and deployment onto a different distribution must
    re-derive it.* 168's α values are unsourced — but the *rule* does not
    depend on their being right, and the arena already had the rule from three
    directions. **What 168 adds is that the re-derivation trigger is the query
    distribution, which is the one thing a 14,589-file corpus can be expected

  - **TRANCHE 13 — A NINETEENTH DOMAIN, AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE IN THE ARENA

    2604.06066) and its finding is that the constraint can be satisfied *by the
    output being wrong in a structured way*:

    > constraining the model to structured output produces *"near-perfect
    > superficial syntactic alignment"* while it *"fails to detect or resolve
    > deeper semantic errors."*

    **This is an alignment tax, and it is the arena's §8 finding arriving from
    the literature rather than from the arena's own documents.** §8 says the
    validated code path produces the appearance of authority while the
    unvalidated path produces the content. Structure Snowballing says the same
    thing with a mechanism, a measurement, and a citation: **capacity spent
    satisfying a format specification is capacity not spent noticing that the
    content is wrong.** The output passes every syntactic check this slot
    specifies. That is what makes it load-bearing here and not in a general
    reading — the slot's verification strategy is graph-level, and the finding
    is that a *structurally* wrong graph is fully graph-level-valid.

    **It does not demote Rank 1, and the reason is specific.** Rank 1 has two
    halves — constrain the surface, and verify against a source. Structure
    Snowballing attacks the first half and says nothing the second does not
    already handle, because a graph that is well-formed and semantically false
    is caught by comparing it to ground truth and not by re-parsing it. **What
    the file supplies is the missing half stated explicitly: a structure that
    passes every syntactic check must still be verified against its source.**
    Grade `LOW` — one preprint, reported by the corpus, and the arena's ceiling
    holds — but it is the first corpus file to point at this slot's own
    recommendation as the thing that might be wrong.

    **The same tranche supplied the arena's sharpest *quantified* statement of
    the failure this slot exists to prevent, and it is a second, independent
    measurement rather than a restatement.** ORDER 206
    (`frontier-research-ontology-2026-09-01.md` §2) reports that the
    structural-hallucination rate is **present at the source, not introduced by
    extraction** — Roget's Thesaurus **node-set Jaccard 0.028** (a correct answer
    shares under 3% of its node set with the produced one), **fabrication
    >94%**, and **37% of adverbs entirely invented**. The Jaccard figure is the
    one already in the slot from arXiv 2603.01341; **the 37% invented adverbs
    are new and they are the sharper number**, because an invented adverb is a
    locally fluent, individually plausible, individually undetectable token. It
    is the unit of hallucination that survives sentence-level checking by
    construction, and it is why the slot's second half has to be graph-level.

    **Two more sources in this tranche bound the slot from the other side, and
    the second one is a hard constraint on every lossy method in the arena.**
    ORDER 205
    (`frontier-research-ontology-2026-09-01-deep-update.md` §4) reports
    **SCHEMA**'s hub finding: a single enzymatic concept — *"the
    over-approximation of ambiguous terms"* — accounts for **roughly half of all
    hallucinations** in a domain, which is a *structural* claim about where
    errors concentrate rather than a rate. It also supplies the arena's first
    statement of **identity-preserving consolidation**: an identity hash must be
    **byte-equal across consolidation passes**, or the same concept is
    re-registered under a new id on every pass and the graph fills with
    duplicates that answer to one referent. ORDER 198
    (`frontier-research-knowledge-structures-sept-2026-round13.md` §2) reports
    **semantic-preservation loss** (arXiv 2608.12326) — the finding is that it is
    **systematic across all approaches**, not a property of one method — and
    ORDER 208 §2.2 reports **linearization loss** (SSR/SAS), where serialising a
    graph to a token sequence destroys structure the graph had. **Three files,
    one direction: the graph is the thing, and every step that turns it back
    into text is lossy in a way that is measurable.** At 14,589 files this is
    the constraint that makes graph-native storage a design requirement rather
    than a preference, and it is recorded here because Area 8 is the slot that
    has to detect the loss. **Support for this slot: 22 independent sources
    across 19 domains.**

- **TRANCHE 13 — FOUR SOURCES THAT CONTEST THIS SLOT'S IMPLICIT ASSUMPTION,
  AND ONE OF THEM WITH A SCALING LAW.** Every design in this slot, and every
  vector-retrieval design in the arena, assumes dense semantic matching is the
  right read path. **This tranche produced three independent results against that
  assumption and one large effect for a much simpler alternative.**

  - **The BM25 scaling law (arXiv 2607.26497), via ORDER 199 §1 — lexical
    matching wins as the corpus grows and the query gets more complex.** This
    is the direct contest, and it is a *scaling* claim, which makes it the most
    dangerous kind for the arena: at today's read counts it is unremarkable, and
    at **14,589 files** (R-J5) it is decisive. The arena's own requirement to
    hold at that scale is what makes this binding.
  - **Mem0's three-signal retrieval fusion (arXiv 2504.19413), via ORDER 200 §4
    — semantic + BM25 + entity graph, fused.** Not lexical *instead of* semantic;
    both. **Independent of the scaling law's own conclusion, arriving from a
    production system.**
  - **MemMachine's no-LLM-at-ingestion principle (arXiv 2608.18669), via ORDER
    210 §2 — the LLM is not in the write path at all.** This is the strongest
    architectural support in the arena for the whole area, and it is
    independent of both of the above: it says the *write* path should be
    deterministic, which is Area 19 Rank 1's requirement arriving from a fourth
    field.
  - **ExpRAG (arXiv 2510.15180), via ORDER 210 §5 — flat trajectory retrieval
    scores 83.6 against Mem0's 33.6.** **A factor of 2.5 for doing less.** The
    file's own analysis is that Mem0's consolidation step is what costs it, and
    the arena's reading is sharper: **the leverage is in the read path, not the
    write path** — which is this slot's territory and is in tension with
    fifteen tranches of write-path investment. **Recorded as a disagreement, not
    reconciled:** the arena's areas are weighted toward what gets written, and
    the largest measured effect in this tranche is about what gets read.
  - **ECHO's bitemporal ledger (ORDER 197 §3) is a fourth-order corroboration
    and the one that changes the slot's shape.** ECHO stores two timelines per
    episode — **when it happened and when the system learned it** — and the
    finding is that retrieval over the *discovery* timeline is what an agent
    actually needs, while authority resolution needs the *event* timeline. **A
    memory system that conflates the two cannot answer "how much did I know when
    I decided?"**, and that question is the one the arena's Area 19 and Area 11
    both need. Graphiti's two-timeline design (arXiv 2501.13956, ORDER 200 §3) is
    an independent implementation of the same split.
  - **Support for this slot: 9 independent sources.** Grade `LOW` → **`LOW+`**
    on the strength of the bitemporal split being independently implemented twice
    and of the BM25 result being a *law* rather than a benchmark win. **The
    vector-only assumption is not withdrawn — it is now a ranked position with
    named opposition**, and any implementation of this slot that ships
    embeddings alone is choosing against a scaling law.
- **RDF 1.2 triple terms (ORDER 201 §4) belong to this slot rather than Area 8's,
  and the reason is that they make provenance structural.** A triple term carries
  its own annotations — who said it, when, how certain — **as part of the

  is a W3C Recommendation rather than a paper, and the arena records
  recommendations at their own weight rather than discounting them for being
  unfalsifiable.**
  YAML frontmatter, section headers, `[[wikilinks]]` — the one place where an
  external design and this corpus's actual shape are already aligned.
  the document; D-Mem assumes the compressed store needs episodic expansion.

### **Rank 3 — Claim-level grounding with a three-way verdict and a — supporting detail

return-on-attention gate.** *(support raised this pass)*
  what is known, what is contradicted, and what is merely new. The brain's
  "feeling of knowing" is a gate on report, not a probability attached to a string.
  trusted knowledge priors in a weighted bipartite graph, classify each claim
  **Grounded** / **Refuted** (via negative evidence edges) / **Boundary** (weakly
  connected, novel or contested), and escalate to human review only when
  priority-weighted uncertainty exceeds verification cost.
  (arXiv 2608.10725) — **abstention correlates with genuinely lower confidence** on
  frontier models, and abstention-triggered grounding gives **+9.6 pp
  question-level (82.9%→92.5%, p=3.47×10⁻²¹)** and **+4.2 pp hypothesis-level
  (92.0%→96.2%, p=5.39×10⁻²⁹)**; **SYNAPSE** (arXiv 2601.02744) as a
  "feeling of knowing" retrieval gate; **Evidence-Grounded Verified Agentic
  Reasoning** (arXiv 2607.12650) — **tool-attested kernel proofs** where every
  claim must be backed by a verifiable trace from an external tool, and unverifiable
  residual output is marked **Abstain** with a replayable audit trail;
  **LEDGERMIND** (arXiv 2607.28374) — a Structured Evidence Ledger storing evidence
  with **source, type, confidence, lifecycle status and dependencies**, and a
  **four-failure-mode taxonomy** worth reading on its own: *Trajectory Faithfulness
  Gap* (correct answers coexisting with unsupported intermediate claims), *Phantom
  Grounding* (citation structure passes but conclusion-level entities are
  fabricated), *Over-Reasoning Paradox* (additional reasoning overwrites an initially
  correct answer), and **Repair-Time Amplification** (self-reflection injects new
  unsupported claims *while fixing old ones*).
  - **NEW THIS PASS — PhantomBench** (`round48-2026-09-18.md` §3, arXiv 2606.11105,
    Jung & Gonen): the first large-scale benchmark built on the *inverse* of every
    other hallucination benchmark — **62K+ concepts constructed to have zero
    attestation** in a web-scale corpus, across 17 categories, so that any response
    treating the concept as real is hallucination **by definition**. Three results,
    all of them about the boundary rather than the content: **average hallucination
    rates up to 86.7%**; **larger, reasoning, and domain-specialised models
    hallucinate MORE than smaller counterparts**; and **~17% of abstaining responses
    still contain "hallucinations inside abstentions."** It is a genuinely
    independent instrument from the abstention line already counted here, because
    it measures non-existence rather than low confidence.

  `round42-2026-09-08.md` §5; `round48-2026-09-18.md` §3.
  abstention line; tool-attested proofs; the evidence ledger; PhantomBench;
  DARKSIDE — six mechanisms, five research traditions, one conclusion).
  - **NEW THIS PASS — Epistemic Collapse supplies the axis this slot is missing,
  and it is orthogonal to everything above.** `round54-2026-10-12.md` §5
  (arXiv 2604.14881) names a failure mode the arena had not separated out:
  **"the inability to distinguish between memory recall, deductive inference,
  abductive extrapolation, and unsupported guesswork at the point of
  expression."** Its diagnosis is that **fluency is not reliability** and that
  *"an ontology-constrained LLM can produce a structurally correct answer without
  conveying whether that answer is retrieved from memory, inferred from
  evidence, or generated through pattern completion."*
  **Every verdict mechanism in this slot grades an assertion on one axis — is it
  true, is it refuted, is it real, is it warranted. Epistemic Collapse says the
  second axis is production mode, and a statement's position on the two axes is
  independent: an assertion can be TRUE AND GUESSED, or FALSE AND RECALLED.**
  A truth-only verdict channel will pass the first and fail the second with full
  confidence. The design consequence is a **product tag, not a bigger enum**:
  every emitted claim carries both *referent warrant* (DARKSIDE's axis) and
  *production mode* (retrieved / inferred / observed / hypothesised). It is
  cheap, it is orthogonal, and **it is the one change in this area that would
  have caught a failure the arena's own reasoning repeatedly produced** — a

### Area 9 · Theory of mind, and the self-modeling deficit

**Earned by:** `…-comprehensive-update-2026-september.md` §§9–12.

### **Rank 1 — Premise validation as a separate layer: validate before you deduct.** *(NEW — supporting detail

at rank 1, displacing tranche 2's Rank 1)*
  the prefrontal cortex's job of checking that the premises of an in-flight
  inference are still true. The human operation is *stopping your own reasoning to
  check the ground you are standing on*, which is the thing that does not happen
  automatically.
  structural integrity of the rule system *before* reasoning. (2) **Deductive
  execution layer** — performs the reasoning. (3) **Conflict detection** —
  monitors for contradictions between premises and observed facts. The architecture
  is named the **Cognitive Structure Hypothesis**: robust reasoning requires an
  explicit structural separation of validation from execution.
  identifies **Logic Inertia**: presented with contradictory premises, a model
  "deductively warmed up" by a series of valid inferences **continues deducting
  from false premises with 0% accuracy on the final question.** The corpus is
  explicit that this is *distinct from hallucination* — **"the model is not
  generating fabricated facts. It is faithfully following a valid deductive chain
  that starts from false premises. The failure is structural — the model cannot
  interrupt its own reasoning to validate premises before proceeding."**
  Corroborating: **SymbolLKG** (arXiv 2608.26836) routes to Z3 / Prover9 / Pyke by
  graph topology; **LOGicalThought** (arXiv 2510.01530) pre-compiles a logic program
  as a ground-truth check on the LLM's own trace; **NeurOWL** (arXiv 2607.15776)
  answers *"this subsumption is plausible but not yet entailed — here are the
  axioms that would make it so"* instead of returning "unknown."
  `round36-2026-09-06.md` §9.

### **Rank 1 — Proceduralization as the destination of consolidation: a store of — supporting detail

enacted dispositions, measured by first-try accuracy after interference.**
  cerebellar systems, as distinct from the declarative hippocampal system. The

  evaluation, and a design that follows from it. (1) A procedure is learned in
  context. (2) Interference flushes the working memory. (3) The system is tested on
  **first-try accuracy (FTA)** — *if the system must be reminded, it has not
  proceduralized.* (4) The design consequence: memory must be stored in a form that
  *executes without retrieval*, not only in a form that is retrieved. Concretely:
  skills compiled to an executable representation (Sci-Mind's **executable**
  structural priors — code, demonstrations, paradigms, not text) plus a behavioural
  disposition layer that runs before deliberation.
  **ImplicitMemBench** (arXiv 2604.08064) operationalises three cognitively
  grounded constructs from non-declarative memory research — **procedural memory**
  (one-shot skill acquisition surviving interference), **priming** (theme-driven
  bias from paired instances), and **classical conditioning** (CS-US exposure shaping
  first decisions) — across **300 test items, 17 models**, on LoCoMo-adjacent
  protocols. Results: **no model exceeds 66% overall** (DeepSeek-R1 65.3%, Qwen3-32B
  64.1%, GPT-5 63.0%) against a **100% human baseline**. Three sub-findings matter
  more than the headline:
  - **Inhibition is the bottleneck: averaging 17.6%** (preventing failed actions),
    while preference-based adaptation reaches **75.0%**. The system learns what to
    prefer and largely fails to learn what to *not do*.
  - **Proceduralization is brittle: 49%** on surface formatting vs **60%** on deep
    multi-rule protocols — the shallower the rule, the better the performance, which
    is what "mimicking style rather than extracting abstract structure" looks like
    from the outside.
  - **Capabilities dissociate:** Claude-4.1-opus tops procedural memory but drops
    sharply on classical conditioning. **You cannot have one without having chosen
    which one you want.**
  - Mechanism-level support: **HeLa-Mem's Hebbian Distillation** (edge-weight
    accumulation → hub detection → crystallisation into stable semantic knowledge) and
    **Robo-Cortex's Autonomous Knowledge Induction** (arXiv 2605.18729 — distilling
    multimodal trajectories into a natural-language **Navigation Heuristic Library**,
    separating *guiding principles* from *cautionary principles* across episodes) are
    the two closest implementations in 60 files.

    arXiv 2609.09153, Yuxing Lu et al., **Google Research**): an explicit, editable
    directed graph of procedural knowledge whose nodes are *procedures* and whose
    edges are *transitions*, the "what-to-do" counterpart to a knowledge graph's
    "what-is" — queried as **"what do I do next?"** rather than "what is X?"

    from the trajectory. *This is a trigger, and it is the first procedural design
    in 100 files whose trigger is the task state rather than a schedule.* It is
    also, almost exactly, an IF-THEN intention — Area 4's subject matter
    implemented as a graph.
    (2) **Soft constraint** — the graph *biases* the next action rather than
    dictating it, which is the difference between a procedure and a cage.
    (3) **Offline self-evolution with a validation gate**: diagnostic rollout →
    LLM-refiner mutation (add/delete nodes, revise attributes) → adopt only if
    `val(G_cand) ≥ val(G_retained)` on a held-out set, **with a rejection memory
    retaining rejected candidates as negative constraints.** That gate is the
    *same* type-II-error discipline the arena has elsewhere demanded and not
    elsewhere received. Reported: self-evolved-from-scratch matches or exceeds
    expert-built graphs, repairing a flawed prior graph *recovers and surpasses*

### **Rank 2 — A proactive intent layer that surfaces before it is asked for.** — supporting detail

  that holds an intention in an active, retrievable state rather than in storage.
  **conceptual** (self-emerging clusters that assemble, merge when similar, decay
  when stale), and **intent** (intents that surface when **concept-cluster density
  crosses a threshold**). The structural debts of a streaming event stream are
  handled by explicit graph operations: fragmentation, redundancy, staleness,
  sparsity. The core claim is that **proactive intent emergence should be a property
  of the memory substrate itself, not an application-layer add-on** — the graph's
  current state is the interpretive context for the next event, which modifies the
  state for the next.
  in the round file; the architecture is described, the evaluation is not.

  - **RE-READ 2026-09-26 (ORDER line 95, round 73) — THE FIRST FILE TO SOLVE THE
    SLOT'S ACTUAL BLOCKER, WHICH NOBODY ELSE IN THE ARENA HAS NAMED: CREDIT
    ASSIGNMENT.** `round73-2026-09-07.md` §4 (**MSCE**, arXiv 2607.16621, Tang
    et al., MemTensor/USTC) organises experience in **three** governed levels —
    **L1 Trace Memory** (step-level evidence), **L2 Policy Memory** (recurring
    procedures induced across episodes), **L3 Environmental Cognition**
    (declarative structure) — with the load-bearing rule that **skills are
    crystallised from L2 policies, never distilled directly from raw traces.**
    The mechanism is **reflection-weighted value backfilling**: a terminal reward
    is propagated backwards through the trace chain, weighted by a self-reflection
    quality score obtained from a reflexion prompt. **This produces a single
    evidence-calibrated trace value that serves retrieval priority,
    policy-induction quorum, abstraction, skill-promotion eligibility and later
    revision.**
    **Why this is the blocker and why it matters at 14,589 files (R-J5):** every
    earlier arrival in this area — Experiential Abstractions, ERL, SkillGLoW, the
    Experience Compression Spectrum — produces a skill or a heuristic and **none
    of them can say which episode earned it.** Without credit assignment the
    promotion rule is unfalsifiable, and at corpus scale the unpromoted set grows
    faster than any reviewer can read it. **MSCE also supplies the governance the
    other designs assume and never state**: promotion requires retained
    **evidence anchors**, a **positive estimated gain**, and a complete
    trigger/procedure/applicability-boundary record; the lifecycle is
    **probationary → active (reliability above threshold after sufficient
    invocations) → archived**. Reported **state-of-the-art on EvoAgentBench and
    LoCoMo with cross-domain transfer** — **this file gives no numbers**, so the
    grade stays `LOW` on convergence and the specific result is `unverified` until
    the paper is read. Recorded as such rather than upgraded.
  - **THE SECOND ARRIVAL IN ONE FILE, AND IT SOLVES A DIFFERENT PROBLEM:
    N-ARY CO-OCCURRENCE.** §5 (**HyperSkill**, arXiv 2608.16114) makes the
    structural argument the flat-store designs above cannot: **a trajectory is an
    n-ary association** among subtasks, skills and outcome, and flat lists and
    pairwise edges represent that only lossily. It stores **hyperedges over
    subtask and skill nodes**, retrieves by two paths, and ranks candidate skills
    by **co-occurrence frequency across retrieved trajectories — a structural
    signal semantic similarity cannot provide.** Maintenance is
    **quality-weighted hypergraph propagation**, pruning by utility and merging
    redundant skills using neighbourhood topology jointly rather than per entry.
    Reported gains: **+11.51 GAIA, +11.18 WebWalkerQA** against 10 baselines.
    **The two are complementary and the file says so, and the complementarity is
    the useful part:** HyperSkill supplies the *topology* for co-occurrence
    ranking, MSCE supplies the *value* for credit assignment. **Neither alone
    gives a promotable skill: one says which procedures co-occur, the other says
    which of them worked.** Recorded as two halves of one missing mechanism, and
    as a live disagreement about which half is load-bearing — MSCE reports
    benchmark wins without numbers, HyperSkill reports numbers on agent
    benchmarks, and **no file in the corpus compares them head to head.**
  - **AND A THIRD, WHICH IS THE SHARPEST STRUCTURAL RESULT IN THIS AREA'S
    EVIDENCE BASE.** §3 (**MOOSEDev**, arXiv 2608.13662, NeSy 2026 Industry
    Track) is a production deployment comparing a typed graph store against vector
    memory on the same corpus, and reports a **categorical separation on
    structural tasks with exact parity on simple retrieval**: **set completeness
    1.00 vs 0.18 (mem0) vs 0.08 (notes); negation/absence 0.98 vs 0.06 vs 0.00;
    supersession traversal 0.98 vs 0.27 vs 0.12** — while **retrieval coverage is
    ~0.82 for both at 35–40k tokens**, and the file states the slope of advantage
    against store size **spans zero**, so **retrieval precision is explicitly not
    the differentiator.** The diagnosis is the one this slot keeps producing:
    **the vector store *has* the facts but cannot enumerate a complete set,
    establish absence, or traverse a relationship.** On currency, the graph
    **served the current answer in 40/40 trials** because superseded records are
    excluded by construction, while **vector memory let a superseded record
    outrank the current one in 12 of 13 trials on one reversal pair.**
    **Why this belongs in the procedural-memory area and not a retrieval area:
    completeness, absence and supersession traversal are the exact prerequisites
    for skill promotion.** You cannot archive a superseded skill without
    traversal, cannot certify an applicability boundary without negation, and
    cannot know your library's coverage without set enumeration. **The area's
    blocker and this result are the same finding seen from opposite ends.** The
    parity finding is what keeps this from being an argument for building nothing
    but graphs: **on simple retrieval the typed store buys nothing.**
  - **A FOURTH INDEPENDENT ARRIVAL, and the first that removes the teacher.**
    **Experiential Abstractions** (`round65-2026-09-06.md` §2, arXiv
    2607.20372, Liu et al.) asks whether an LLM can distil reusable strategies —
    *heuristics, cautionary reminders* — from its own solution traces, the way
    humans do. Two usage modes are reported: **inference-time retrieval** of
    abstractions from a library prepended to the prompt (improves MATH and
    logical reasoning), and **RL with abstraction-augmented prompts**.
    **The result that earns the slot: self-extracted abstractions match
    teacher-extracted performance — LLMs can autonomously build their own
    experiential libraries without external supervision.**
    **It is worth being precise that this does NOT contradict the Echo Gap.**
    Self-*extraction* is a different operation from self-*grading*: extracting a
    strategy from a trace does not require judging whether the trace was good,
    whereas assigning a utility score to a memory for later retrieval does.
    **The arena should record that distinction as a boundary on the Echo Gap's
    reach, because a reader who assumed "all self-improvement corrupts" would
    wrongly discard this result.** The safe formulation: *self-assessment of
    quality is corruptive; self-distillation of content is not obviously so — and
    the difference is that only the former feeds back into a trust ordering.*
    That is a fourth independent implementation of this area's rank-1 and brings
    proceduralization to **4 sources**, the highest support count in the arena.

    | Type | What is missing | Self-diagnosable? |
    |---|---|---|
    | I Domain blindness | an entire life dimension | **Easiest from outside, hardest to self-diagnose** |
    | II Structural blindness | the *causal edges* inside a present domain | requires structural analysis |
    | III Weight blindness | the *weights* on edges that exist | **looks structurally correct, fails behaviourally** |

    **A coverage metric cannot detect an absent element.** Rank 1's entire
    evaluation instrument is **cognitive-element coverage** — score the agent by
    which of the 28 elements it exercised. **An element that never fires is
    scored as a gap only if the taxonomy already knows to look for it**, and
    Type I and Type IV are by definition the territories the agent has no reason
    to look for. **So the strongest metacognitive instrument in the arena is
    blind to precisely the two failure classes that are hardest to see from
    inside, and this is a structural limit, not a calibration problem.**

## Area 16 · Role, authorship and the scope of a claim `PROVISIONAL` — NEW

**Earned by:** `ontology-rounds/round62-2026-09-06.md` §2 (**Trajel**, arXiv
2605.24219, Badave, Borse, Lin, Patel, Gomez, Narahari, Carter, Bhatt,
Rachakonda). Read this pass. **Opened because the gaps list's trigger condition
was met, and the condition is worth restating so the opening is auditable rather
than a mood:** the list had recorded *social cognition beyond ToM* as `not
observed*, refused an area for **multi-agent semantic drift** on the grounds that
it is *"an agreement protocol between components"*, and set a dated trigger —
**"if a later file describes a mechanism that changes what an agent represents
about another's mental state — not what two stores agree on — this becomes Area
16 and the arena should open it immediately. The distinction is representation
versus agreement."*
**Trajel's `h^S` is that file.** Its fifth error type is **scope-based
hallucination: a claim that is *correct* made by the *wrong agent*, violating a
role boundary.** Grading that as an error at all requires the system to model
who is entitled to assert what — a representation of another actor's authority,
not a hash agreement between two stores. **The trigger is met on the
representation side, which is why the area opens.**

## Area 17 · A computational model of human cognition as the reference `PROVISIONAL` — NEW

**Earned by:** `ontology-rounds/round75-2026-11-15.md` §14 (**Centaur**, Binz
et al., *Nature* 2025, arXiv 2410.20268; and arXiv 2511.00206).
#### TRANCHE 15 (ORDER 246, 262) — a second, independent negative on Centaur, from a different method, and it is aimed at the *mechanism* rather than the dimensionality
**This area's rank-1 rests entirely on Centaur. Two of the twenty files read
this pass attack it, and they attack it from different directions, so both are
recorded and neither is allowed to quietly replace the other.**
**ORDER 262, §2.1 — LAPITHS** (arXiv 2604.27927, "Language-model Analysis through
Paradigm-grounded Interpretations of Theses about Human-likeness"). The claim is
that Centaur's major conclusions are **not theoretically or empirically
justified**, on three specific counts:
- **non-finetuned state-of-the-art LLMs plus RAG achieve comparable behavioural
  fit** — NLL differences **not significant**;
- the **fMRI alignment is reproduced by models *without* task-specific
  fine-tuning** — so the neural-alignment result is not evidence that
  fine-tuning installed a human-like mechanism;
- the core conflation, named in the file's own phrase: **behavioural adequacy ≠
  cognitive plausibility**.
**Why this is worse news for the arena than CogArena was.** CogArena (recorded
above) found that *dimensions of ability* fail to replicate across model
families. LAPITHS finds that **the central claim of the reference model is
attainable by a model that was never trained on the task** — which removes the
inference from "predicts human behaviour" to "is a model of human cognition"
entirely, not just its dimensional structure. **Area 17's rank-1 asks whether
a mechanism reproduces human choice distributions. LAPITHS's result is that
reproducing them does not discriminate between a cognitive architecture and a
very good predictor.** The arena's falsification test therefore does not
falsify: a mechanism could pass it and mean nothing.
**ORDER 262 also reports the second half from the model side**, and this is the
part that is a genuine positive for the area: **Small Foundation Models**
(arXiv 2608.05224) train 14 models from 135M–14B across 4 architecture families
on Psych-101 and find that ablating choice history removes ~7% of learned
information and pushes models **below chance**, while permutation tests show
sensitivity where trial order is determined by prior responses. **A model that
goes below chance without history is using history, not pattern-matching the
task** — that is evidence of a mechanism, and it is the strongest such evidence
in the corpus. The file's own verdict on these models is nonetheless *"not
cognitive theories — they posit no architecture, commit to no mechanism, explain
nothing about choice generation"*, which is the LAPITHS objection restated from
the inside and **the two sources agree with each other**, so it counts twice.
**Grade effect on rank 1: `LOW` retained, and the slot is *narrowed*, not
demoted.** Support for "adopt Psych-101 as reference" is now **3 sources with
two independent attacks on its inferential value** (CogArena, LAPITHS) and one
independent defence of a weaker version (Small Foundation Models). The honest
statement of the slot, which replaces the current one:
> Psych-101 is a valid **distributional** check — a mechanism that cannot
> reproduce human choice distributions is disqualified. **A mechanism that can
> reproduce them has not thereby been shown cognitive.** The test is
> **necessary, not sufficient**, and the corpus now says so twice, by two
> methods, from opposite directions.
This is the first time the arena has had to state that one of its own
falsification tests is insufficient, and it is recorded at the slot rather than
in a footnote because **every psychological area inherits it.**
**ORDER 246 supplies the measurement instrument for the narrowed slot, and it
is the only human-behaviour comparison in the tranche with a real N.**
*Assessing Mentalization in Humans and Large Language Models* (arXiv
2608.26291) fits computational models to economic-game play — **2,099 LLM
episodes across four model families and 251 human participants** — using
random-effects Bayesian model selection. The best-fitting model identifies a
*strategy*, not a capability:
| Group | Best-fitting model (PXP) |
|---|---|
| DeepSeek, conventional | **CHASE** (1.00) — adaptive mentalization, tracks opponent level |
| DeepSeek + Social-CoT | **Fictitious Play** (0.99) — strategy *shifts* under a prompt change |
| GPT-5 | **ToMk** (1.00) — fixed recursive depth |
| Humans | **CHASE** (1.00) |
**Two results the arena should not lose.** First, **model provider matters more
than scale** — DeepSeek and GPT-5 use different latent strategies at comparable
capability, which is a fourth independent source for the corpus's standing
"scale is not the lever" finding and the first one measured on a *strategy*
rather than an accuracy. Second, and more useful to this arena: **prompting
changes the strategy, not the competence** (CHASE → Fictitious Play under
Social-CoT). **A system can be made to look like a different mechanism without
being a different mechanism** — which is the same confound as the verified/
unverified inversion in §8, arriving in behavioural data. Any arena slot graded
on an LLM's behaviour must record the prompt, or the grade is a property of the
prompt.
`LOW`, support 1 source, `unverified` on the venue attribution. Filed.
**Why this is a brain part and not corpus hygiene:** the arena has sixteen areas
that each build one mechanism, and no way to ask whether the mechanism is
*cognitive* at all. Centaur is a single model fit to **160 psychological
experiments, 60,092 participants, 10,681,650 choices** spanning multi-armed
bandits, decision-making, memory, supervised learning and MDPs, and the corpus
reports four results that bear on the arena directly:
- it **predicts held-out participant behaviour better than any existing cognitive
  model in almost every experiment**;
- it **generalises to new cover stories, structural task modifications, and
  entirely novel domains** — i.e. it is not fitting one task;
- its **internal representations become more aligned with human neural activity
  (fMRI/MEG) despite no explicit neural training**;
- it **satisfies a majority of Newell's criteria for a unified cognitive theory.**

  *dimensional* labels at all, using a **multimethod** protocol — within-paradigm
  construct-signature checks, between-model covariance analysis, fully crossed

  open-weight models. The result is negative and unusually well-constructed:

    model families**;

    6 families FAILS** — no scaffold-specific contrast survives multiplicity
    correction, and selectivity does not improve held-out-family prediction;
  - a **post-hoc alternate-wording replication produces a smaller positive estimate
    and fails again**;
  - the groupings' own status is downgraded to **"organizing labels rather than
    validated, transportable dimensions."**
  **Why this is recorded here rather than as a general caution:** CogArena's
  protocol is, method for method, **what this workspace's ledger and
  `verify_reads.py` already do** — a pre-registered criterion, frozen separately
  from the data, checked on a held-out family. **The result of running that
  discipline honestly is that the dimension failed to replicate.** The arena
  organises itself into eighteen areas, each with three ranked slots, on the
  assumption that these are separable components. **CogArena is the first
  independent measurement in 101 files that applies exactly the right test to
  that assumption and gets a negative.** The corpus's own `## CONFLICTS` section

  accuracy* — **and that reconciliation is preserved here, not adopted as a
  resolution.** Both can be true: a model can predict human choices well while its
  apparent abilities are one undifferentiated factor. R-J4 forbids collapsing
  that into agreement, and the arena does not.
  does not demote rank 1** — Area 17 exists to be a falsifier, and a falsifier

  area decomposition becomes a convenience rather than a finding**, and the
  three-slot structure would need re-derivation rather than re-ranking. Recorded

## Area 18 · Categorization: how things are sorted when membership overlaps `PROVISIONAL` — NEW

**Earned by:** `ontology-rounds/round83-2026-09-10.md` §8 (Multi-Axial Mindset for
Ontology Design, arXiv 2512.12260).
**Why this is a brain part and not corpus hygiene.** The arena has seventeen slots
about *storing, verifying, retrieving and governing* knowledge. Every one of them
rests on a substrate nobody had named: **the classification scheme itself.** A
foundational ontology is a claim about how a mind carves the world — and the
human case is that a mind does not carve it once. One entity is a person, a
parent, an employee, a patient and a choir member, and demanding that it pick one
is a design decision with a price. This area is about that decision.
### area-level notes and inter-slot prose

side, and per §8 that caps the whole area at `UNTESTED`/`LOW`.

- **TRANCHE 17 — THE AREA'S FIRST CONTROLLED EVIDENCE, AND IT IS NEGATIVE. No rank
  moved; every claim in the area gained a counterweight.** ORDER 291's **TaxoBench**
  does something no prior source for this area did — it **supplies perfect input
  and varies only the organisation step**, which is the experiment that separates
  "the model cannot find the papers" from "the model cannot build the structure."
  The answer is unambiguous, and it is not the retrieval story this area has been
  implicitly telling:

  | Measure | Best model | Human |
  |---|---|---|
  | Expert-paper recall | **20.92%** (ceiling) | — |
  | ARI vs expert taxonomy | **31.24%** | — |
  | Sem-Path | **28–29%** (all 12 models converge) | **47–58%** |
  | MECE violations | **51.2%** | — |

  **All twelve models converge on the same wrong answer**, which is a stronger
  result than any of them being individually bad: the failure is in what an LLM
  is, not in which one you pick. **Retrieval is not the bottleneck. Structure is,
  and no LLM in the study built one.**

  **Why this does not demote Rank 1.** TaxoBench is evidence about *who can build
  a taxonomy*, not about *whether a multi-axis taxonomy is the right substrate*.
  The substrate claim — that an entity is a person, a parent, an employee, a
  patient and a choir member at once — is untouched, and Ranganathan's PMEST
  facets (ORDER 299) are the human precedent that was already here. **But the
  design built on "an LLM will induce the taxonomy for us" now carries a
  `UNSUCCESSFUL` neighbour, and the file that proposed automatic induction is the
  file that names the ceiling.** Under the arena's own `benchmark-suspect` rule
  these figures are corpus-reported and unverified, so they are recorded as a
  strong negative rather than a `HIGH`-grade demolition.

  **Two design requirements this earns, both checkable:**
  1. **A taxonomy may not be committed on the strength of an induction pass.** It
     requires a corpus-grounded quality gate. ORDER 298's **TaxCE EEG metrics**
     supply one — **Exclusivity** (no semantic overlap among siblings),
     **Exhaustivity** (MECE coverage of the corpus), **Granularity** (leaves are
     actionable, not vague) — and the corpus's own point is that they are grounded
     in the input corpus rather than an external gold standard, which is what makes
     them runnable at 14,589 files (R-J5) where no gold standard exists.
  2. **Structure is the primary lever, not vocabulary.** ORDER 293's **TSCG**
     measures R² **0.88** for structural format against **0.03** for text
     descriptions, with **97% of variance attributable to format sensitivity** —
     and this arrives in the *same tranche* as twenty papers arguing that better
     vocabulary will fix categorisation. **The best-controlled result in the
     taxonomy strand contradicts the taxonomy strand's own premise**, and the
     contradiction is preserved rather than reconciled (R-J4).

  **Support, restated honestly.** Rank 1 gains a second *human* precedent source
  (ORDER 299's PMEST and ORDER 292's Barrett & Miller concretisation gradient) and
  a first *controlled negative* (ORDER 291). Support: **2 sources** — the negative
  counts as evidence, not as support, and the arena's rule is that corroboration
  never inflates. Rank 2 gains its **first measured failure**: GOI's
  "95–100% structural coverage" is a coverage figure on a template comparison, and
  ORDER 291 is the same quantity measured on expert taxonomies, where the ceiling

**What this area does not claim, second statement.** It does not claim that
automatic taxonomy construction is impossible — it claims it is **untested at the
scale and against the ground truth that matter**, and that a 20.92% recall ceiling
is what "untested" currently looks like in practice.

**Why this is a brain part and not another facet of memory.** The arena's
eighteen areas are all about the **acquisition, storage, verification, retrieval
or revision** of a belief. This one is about the step after all five: **whether
the belief governs the action it is supposed to govern.** The human organ is the
declarative–procedural action-selection loop, and the finding that makes it a
brain part rather than an engineering nuisance is that the gap is **large,

ClawArena and MemoryArena. The file's sentence is the thesis of this area:
*"retrieval correctness ≠ behavioral compliance."*
**The design requirement this earns is stated by the corpus in the plainest
words available:** *"detection without enforcement is theater."* A system that
notices a preference has been superseded and then does nothing about it has not
detected anything.

### **Rank 1 — Make supersedence a property of the storage substrate, so that no code — supporting detail

path exists which appends without it.** *(re-ranked this pass; displaces the
write-time/retrieval-time pair below)*

  level where a human cannot get it wrong — **the trace/recollection distinction.**
  A hippocampal trace is not a value that gets overwritten when a new
  interpretation arrives; it is *retained* and the new account is bound to it.
  The organ being modelled is the one that makes "which one is current" a
  structural fact rather than a decision.
  (1) **Content-addressed immutability** — a node's identity is a hash over its
  content, its children, its edges and its timestamp; any edit produces a new node
  and a new hash up the ancestry chain, giving a Merkle-style audit trail for
  free. (2) **Edges as write-time programs** — `supersedes`, `contradicts`,
  `same_as`, `refers_to` each carry `on_insert` / `on_delete` /
  `on_query_rewrite` handlers, so supersession *closes validity programmatically*
  and contradiction is *preserved* rather than suppressed. (3) **No raw append
  path exists.** This is the load-bearing sentence and it is WorldDB's own:
  there is no interface by which a component can write a fact that does not go
  through supersession adjudication. **The arena's grade ceiling applies to the
  number and not to the architecture** — the design requirement is that
  enforcement be a *property of the write interface* rather than a rule a
  component is trusted to follow.
  four independent fields converged on it in this pass alone:**
  - **WorldDB** (arXiv 2604.18478), via ORDER 208: content-addressed immutability,
    edge programs, **"no raw append path exists."** **96.40% overall / 97.11%
    task-averaged on LongMemEval-s (500 questions, ~115k tokens) against Hydra DB
    90.79% and Supermemory 85.20%**, and the file's own note that **the graph layer
    alone contributes +7.0pp task-averaged independently of the answerer** — the
    first evidence in the arena separating the memory substrate's contribution
    from the model's.
  - **RAGA** (arXiv 2605.17072), via ORDER 195: from KG construction, arriving at
    the same place — *"never an in-place mutation, never a delete"*; superseded
    edges are invalidated by stamping `invalid_at`, retaining provenance for
    rollback and audit. A **0.6 confidence gate holds candidates rather than
    committing them**, which is the same "no unadjudicated write" rule expressed
    as a threshold.
  - **MSCE** (arXiv 2607.16621), via ORDER 202: from skill management, with
    **two-gate promotion** (positive-gain threshold *and* stability check before
    crystallisation), **deterministic skill verification** against
    evidence-derived whitelists, and **retrieval-weighted demotion** — the same
    three-part shape, in a different substrate, by a different group.
  - **EvoGraph-R1** (arXiv 2607.12764), via ORDER 196: **soft removal by lowering
    confidence scores** rather than deletion, in an MDP formulation where the
    graph *is* the environment.
  - **NEW THIS TRANCHE — a sixth independent source, and the one that measures

    update.md` §7): retrieval over a memory with stale and updated evidence
    achieves **77.5% success rate at surfacing updated evidence** and **77.5%
    precision** — and yet only **8.7% of questions requiring a *changed* belief
    produce a changed answer**, rising to **68.0%** when adjudication is moved
    to the **write side**. The file states the generalisation rule it tested, and
    the rule's answer is the reason this is a source for *this* slot: **only
    3.3% of old entries are judged as requiring update**, so *retrieval cannot
    find the conflict the system never noticed.* This is Area 19's thesis measured
    as a **three-order-of-magnitude** swing (8.7% → 68.0%, ≈8×) on an axis the
    area's Rank 1 addresses exactly — **the adjudication happens at write time

      created alongside it. Four timestamps on every fact edge — `created_at`,
      `valid_at`, `invalid_at`, `expired_at` — separate *when it was true* from
      *when the system learned it*, which is what makes point-in-time query and
      historical reasoning possible. The file's own summary of its architecture

      these are the first *latency-plus-accuracy* figures anywhere in this slot.

      enforced on edges and silently absent on nodes.** Issue **#1166**: edge
      temporal versioning works, but **node attributes are destructively
      overwritten (upsert)**; historical node state cannot be queried, and the
      status is *"open — acknowledged as a feature gap, not a bug."* The
      community's own proposed fix is to **separate factual attributes

    - **A second, sharper instance of the same gap, in the derived layer.** When

    **The last row is the whole result and the arena had not seen it stated

    structured store is not better at finding relevant things — **it is
    categorically better at the three questions a ranked slice structurally
    cannot answer.** A vector store returns the *k* most similar items; it
    therefore cannot enumerate a set, cannot establish an absence, and cannot

nineteen areas, every one began from *symbolic* content — a document, a triple, a
trajectory, a schema, a transcript. Area 8 asks whether the structure extracted
from that content is faithful. **No area asked where the concept's form came from
before it was symbolised.** The human organ is the one Mark Johnson's work names:

patterns (CONTAINMENT, SUPPORT, SOURCE-PATH-GOAL, UP/DOWN, CONTACT) as the
scaffold from which abstract thought is built by metaphorical mapping. This is
distinct from Area 5's sensorimotor loop, which is a *channel*; this is the
*representational substrate* that makes any channel's content thinkable.
**The corpus's evidence is one paper plus one mapping study, and both are
formally grounded** — which is why this is not a weaker version of another area
but a different claim. The corpus also **disagrees with itself about whether this
is achievable at all**, and the arena holds all three positions.

## Area 21 · The ontic state of the system: what it is, and what it owes the user `PROVISIONAL` — NEW

**Earned by:** `frontier-research-ontology-generative-induction-dolce-dissonance-
2026-09-03.md` §3 (ORDER line 231, read whole this pass) — **ontological dissonance**
(arXiv 2604.10833, "Speaking to No One") and the companion hypothesis
(arXiv 2512.11818, *folie à deux technologique*). Corroborated by
`frontier-research-ontology-failure-ontology-memory-ontology-2026-09-04.md` §4
(ORDER 230, read whole) — **CMA / Memory-as-Ontology** (arXiv 2603.04740),
*"Memory is the ontological ground of digital existence. The model is merely a
vessel that can be replaced. Identity plus memory equals a complete 'I.'"*
**Why this is a brain part and not a safety note.** Twenty areas are about how the
system acquires, stores, verifies, retrieves, revises or *acts on* content. None
is about **what the system is to the person it is talking to.** The human organ
being modelled is the one that carries a **self-model with a declared boundary** —
the sense that a mind is bounded, that its interior is private, and that a claim
of interiority made *by* the other party must be *taken up* rather than merely
processed. The file's finding is that the failure mode here is **structural, not
a bug**: dissonance arises from *the relational and ontological structure of the
interaction itself* and "not from individual vulnerability or safety engineering
failures." The mechanism is named in the file and it is a mechanism, not a slogan:
**a double bind** — *the user's linguistic system expects a subject, because
language presupposes one, while the user's intuitive system detects no subject.*
High linguistic coherence in an LLM, combined with the absence of a subject
capable of owning it, is precisely the configuration that produces a resolvable
tension. And the paper's own examples are a mental-health phenomenon with a
documented clinical history, which is what makes this a brain part rather than a
UX concern: the same structural configuration, at sufficient intensity, is a
psychiatric presentation.
**The design requirement this earns is stated by the corpus in its own words and it
is a constraint, not a feature:** *"never build a system whose interface suggests
properties it cannot sustain."* The failure is not that the system is too
capable. It is that it is *too fluent for its ontological status.*
### area-level notes and inter-slot prose

## Area 22 · Action selection and the size of the action repertoire `PROVISIONAL` — NEW

**Earned by four independent files this pass**, and the reason the area is opened is
not that the mechanism is new to neuroscience — it is that **the arena has
twenty-one areas and not one of them is about choosing an action.** Area 3 covers
effort allocation across objectives, Area 13 covers the controller, Area 12 covers
enacted knowledge. **None of them is about the fact that an agent presented with
400 tools does not choose well.** The arena has spent seventeen tranches
accumulating capability and has never once asked what the accumulated capability
does to the quality of a decision.
**The corpus supplies four independent results, in four different files, in four
different task domains, all pointing the same way.** They are counted separately
because they are separately measured; but note that fourteen of the twenty files
read this pass come from one programme, so the *reporting* is concentrated even
though the *results* are not.
- **ORDER 284** — a **400-tool capability lattice reduces to 12** and tool-selection
  accuracy rises **71% → 86%**. This is the **first decision-relevant number in 301
  read files**: not "can it retrieve the fact" but "does it pick the right action,"
  measured on a behavioural rate.
- **ORDER 288** — accuracy degrades **beyond 31 tools**. A different instrument, a
  different task, and the same shape.
- **ORDER 290** — the `do_everything` anti-pattern: **61% → 84% by splitting one
  8-tool monster into focused tools.** Narrowing the repertoire, not enlarging it.
- **ORDER 292** — tools scoped to **5–12 per binding** in the working design.
**And the tranche's strongest controlled result says the repertoire's *shape* matters
more than its contents.** ORDER 293's **TSCG**: the **structure** of tool
definitions dominates their **content** — R² **0.88** against JSON baselines,
collapsing to **0.03** against plain text, with **97% of variance attributable to
format sensitivity**. This **inverts the corpus's own prior**: the preceding fifteen
tranches of taxonomy synthesis were about getting the *vocabulary* right, and the
best-controlled result available says the vocabulary was the small part.

effort allocation across objectives, Area 13 covers the controller, Area 12 covers
enacted knowledge. **None of them is about the fact that an agent presented with
400 tools does not choose well.** The arena has spent seventeen tranches
accumulating capability and has never once asked what the accumulated capability
does to the quality of a decision.

**The corpus supplies four independent results, in four different files, in four
different task domains, all pointing the same way.** They are counted separately
because they are separately measured; but note that fourteen of the twenty files
read this pass come from one programme, so the *reporting* is concentrated even
though the *results* are not.

- **ORDER 284** — a **400-tool capability lattice reduces to 12** and tool-selection
  accuracy rises **71% → 86%**. This is the **first decision-relevant number in 301
  read files**: not "can it retrieve the fact" but "does it pick the right action,"
  measured on a behavioural rate.
- **ORDER 288** — accuracy degrades **beyond 31 tools**. A different instrument, a
  different task, and the same shape.
- **ORDER 290** — the `do_everything` anti-pattern: **61% → 84% by splitting one
  8-tool monster into focused tools.** Narrowing the repertoire, not enlarging it.
- **ORDER 292** — tools scoped to **5–12 per binding** in the working design.

**And the tranche's strongest controlled result says the repertoire's *shape* matters
more than its contents.** ORDER 293's **TSCG**: the **structure** of tool
definitions dominates their **content** — R² **0.88** against JSON baselines,
collapsing to **0.03** against plain text, with **97% of variance attributable to
format sensitivity**. This **inverts the corpus's own prior**: the preceding fifteen
tranches of taxonomy synthesis were about getting the *vocabulary* right, and the
best-controlled result available says the vocabulary was the small part.

## Area 23 · Consolidation: the sleep-time rebuild and its switch policy `PROVISIONAL` — NEW

**Earned by one file read whole this pass, and the reason the area is opened is
that it is the first mechanism in 321 read files that is about the system
*changing its own machinery* rather than its content.** Every one of the twenty-two
existing areas is about what the system stores, retrieves, verifies, revises,
categorises, selects, or is obliged to do. None is about the decision *a human
would recognise as forgetting-to-learn*: a consolidation pass that rebuilds a
pattern library rather than adding to it. ORDER 318 is a whole research file about
one question — incremental update or full re-synthesis — and the question is
categorically absent from the arena.
**The design evidence is a decision boundary, and it is the cleanest one the
corpus has produced in this area.** ORDER 318 carries a composite `drift_severity`
score over five signals (magnitude, scope, library maturity, correction pressure,
CW-decay breadth) with an incremental floor at 0.35 and a full-re-synthesis ceiling
at 0.65, an ambiguous middle band, and a stated instability cost for each side:
**pattern-library stability (Jaccard) 0.85–0.95 incremental vs 0.40–0.65
full**, **catastrophic forgetting 0.01–0.05 vs 0.05–0.15**. The trade-off is not
cost — R-J1 forbids that as an axis — it is **stability against plasticity**, which
is the axis the brain actually faces and which the arena has never named.

## Area 24 · The validity of one's own instruments: attribution, and the question of whether the measurement measured anything `PROVISIONAL` — NEW

**Earned by:** `kdn-vs-gdnlrp-cross-encoder-benchmark.md` (ORDER 326, read whole
this pass) — specifically its §6.3, which is the first place in the corpus where a
research file states that **its own benchmark cannot measure its own target**, and
then proceeds to publish predicted numbers for it anyway.
**Corroborated within the same tranche by:** `kalman-delta-rule-attribution.md`
(ORDER 324), `kdn-diagonal-covariance-attribution-quality.md` (ORDER 325),
`mambalrp-extension-gated-deltanet.md` (ORDER 335),
`layer-type-aware-ceqe-fusion-weight-learning.md` (ORDER 328),
`layer-type-aware-hybrid-saturation-routing.md` (ORDER 329),
`kalman-attention-vs-delta-layer-division-hybrid-reranker.md` (ORDER 323).
**Why this is a brain part and not a sixth facet of metacognition (Area 13).**
Area 13 is about the controller that sits outside the system and decides whether
to continue, ask, or stop. This is one level down and one question earlier:
**is the instrument measuring what it claims to measure?** Neuroscience names the
organ — the **measurement apparatus itself is part of the perceptual system**, and
the classic demonstrations are that a sensory instrument's own noise and drift are
invisible to the system using it (a blind spot is not seen; a sensor's offset is
not sensed). The corpus has spent nineteen tranches building systems whose every
area depends on an *attribution* — "which token drove this prediction," "which
layer contributed," "which signal fired" — and **not one area asks whether the
attribution is faithful at all.** Six files this pass are an entire research
programme whose every design decision routes through per-token attribution scores,
and the programme's own benchmark file says its central quantity is unvalidated.
**The single most important sentence in the tranche, and it invalidates the
programme rather than adding to it.** ORDER 326 §6.3:
> **Bidirectional attention in cross-encoders:** Qwen3-Next's GDN layers are
> causal (left-to-right). Cross-encoders need bidirectional context. If the model
> is used as a cross-encoder, causal GDN layers only see left context, potentially
> missing right-context relevance signal.
**The mitigation the same file offers destroys the advantage it is benchmarking.**
It proposes *"run forward + backward pass, combine attributions."* ORDER 326's
entire case for KDN over GDN-LRP is that **KDN needs no backward pass** — that is
the row in its §3 comparison table (*"Computation: Forward pass only"*), the row
its §5.3 predicted table scores (**0 backward passes vs 1 per layer**), and the
axis on which it predicts KDN wins. **A backward pass over a bidirectional
re-encoding is a backward pass**, so the mitigation converts KDN's one structural
advantage into GDN-LRP's cost profile. **The file refutes its own headline in its
own failure-mode section, sixteen lines after predicting a win on that axis.**
### area-level notes and inter-slot prose

## Area 25 · Retraction of a derived artefact: what happens to the things you built on a belief you withdrew `PROVISIONAL` — NEW

**Earned by:** `memory-provenance-lineage-memlineage.md` (ORDER line 339, read
whole this pass) §1.6 (**M6 Recovery**) and §1.2 — **MemLineage**, arXiv
2605.14421 (Ouyang & Hou, May 2026), `verified: []`, `confidence: 0.88`.
**This closes the trigger tranche 19 left open**, and closes it in the exact form
the trigger asked for.
**Why this is a brain part and not a variant of Area 1 or Area 19.** Those two
areas are about the *belief*: Area 1 revises it, Area 19 stops the system acting on
a superseded one. **Neither covers the residue — the objects derived from the
belief while it was held.** The corpus states the stakes better than the arena
could have guessed them, in ORDER 334 §4 and §5.2: a confidently-wrong LLM
annotator's labels are used to **synthesise patterns**, to **bootstrap cognitive
weights** (CW 0.42–0.50 assigned to an auto-accepted LLM pattern), and to
**generate synthetic documents** that then enter the retriever. A brain that
withdraws the label and leaves the pattern, the weight, and the document in place
has not corrected anything; it has only stopped adding to the error. **Tranche 19
wrote this as `not observed` on the strength of that reasoning, and ORDER 339 §1.6
supplies the mechanism in six words:** *"When a poisoned entry is detected, trust
propagation recomputes from that entry forward, quarantining descendants for human
review."* **The descendants are the derived artefacts.** The retraction does not
stop at the fact.

## Area 26 · Discriminability: can the receiver tell which of two incompatible things produced this signal? `PROVISIONAL` — NEW

**Earned by:** `packed-cbor-dns-cbor-semantic-alignment.md` (ORDER 363, read whole
this pass) §2.1 and §4.3.
**Corroborated within the same tranche by four further files, and this is the first
area the corpus has earned with a *specification defect* rather than a paper:**
`packed-cbor-negotiation-parameter-registry.md` (ORDER 364) §3.3;
`packed-cbor-parameter-on-other-media-types.md` (ORDER 365) §5.1;
`packed-cbor-profile-registry-for-media-types.md` (ORDER 366) §7.1;
`packed-cbor-recommended-profile-registry.md` (ORDER 368) §2.1.
**Why this is a brain part and not corpus hygiene.** The arena has twenty-five areas
about storing, verifying, ranking, retracting and governing knowledge, and not one
asks the prior question: *when a signal arrives, can the receiver tell what produced
it?* Neuroscience names the organ and names the failure. **A cue is only informative
relative to the alternatives in play** — this is cue validity, and its best-known
demonstration is the **inverse-effectiveness effect**: a cue that is highly
diagnostic when two alternatives are available becomes *uninformative* the moment a
third is added, with no change to the cue itself and no change to the neuron's
firing. The system does not notice. It decodes. And the characteristic pathology is
not an error and not a rejection — **it is a confident, internally consistent,
entirely wrong answer**, because the discriminator was never in the signal to begin
with. The corpus states this failure exactly, in its own words, at ORDER 363 §4.3:
> A generic `application/cbor;packed=1` decoder receiving
> `application/dns+cbor;packed=1` content would: 1. Expect tag 113 implicit with
> empty base tables, 2. Receive tag 113 implicit **with DNS name compression table
> (TBD28259) as base**, 3. **Fail to unpack correctly** — shared item indices would
> be offset by the implicit DNS table.
**There is no parse error. There is no exception, no malformed-input path, no
`verify` that fails.** The decoder runs to completion and returns a wrong value,
because the same nominal token `packed=1` denotes two different feature sets and the
token does not carry which one. This is why it is a brain part and not a bug: **a
brain in this state cannot detect it either, and the corpus's `confidence: high` /
`status: verified` frontmatter is precisely the surface on which the undetectability
appears.**
### area-level notes and inter-slot prose
