## Area 27 · Lability: the window in which a retrieved memory can be overwritten, and the prediction error that opens it

**Earned by:** `retrieval-induced-reconsolidation-memory-drift.md` (ORDER 389, read
whole this pass) §1 and §2. **This is the first area in the arena earned from a
file that reports one of its own citations as nonexistent** — §"Citation Correction"
records, verified against PubMed E-utilities, that *"Zaromb et al. 2014, J Neurosci
34:1109"* **does not exist**, names the two papers it was probably meant to be
(Tay et al. 2019, J Neurosci 39:1109–1118 — page matches exactly; and Bridge & Voss
2014, J Neurosci 34:2203–2213), and states the correction had already been applied
upstream. A file that audits its own apparatus before the arena does is not a weak
witness, and the area it earns is the one that most needs an honest witness.
**Why this is a brain part and not a database concern.** The arena has twenty-six
areas about storing, validating, ranking, retracting and governing knowledge. Every
one of them treats retrieval as a **read**. The biology says it is not. On
reactivation a consolidated trace returns to a labile state and must re-stabilize
through de novo protein synthesis (Nader, Schafe & LeDoux 2000, *Nature* 406:722–726
— verified: post-reactivation anisomycin in lateral/basal amygdala produced amnesia
for a consolidated fear memory; the same infusion without reactivation left it
intact; delay to 6h produced none). So **retrieval is a write**, whether or not the
retriever knows it — and the moment it writes is the moment the trace is
*most* vulnerable to misinformation inserted after retrieval (Chan & LaPaglia 2013,
*PNAS* 110:9309–9313 — misinformation impaired an existing memory **only when
presented after retrieval**, within the window, and only when targeting that
memory).
**The corpus's own verb, in the corpus's own files.** `RESEARCH.md` (ORDER 387) §
"Retrieval-Induced Reconsolidation & Memory Drift" states the position in one
line: *"Hermes's memory system treats retrieval as a read-only operation. But every
pgvector retrieval that injects a stored memory into a new task context is a
potential memory-modifying event."* And the drift is not a hypothesis — it is
measured. arXiv 2605.12978: consolidated-memory utility **rises then falls below the
no-memory baseline** under continuous LLM updating; even consolidating from
ground-truth solutions, GPT-5.4 fails **54%** of previously-solved ARC-AGI problems.
HaluMem (2511.03506): hallucinations accumulate **at the update stage specifically**.
**The finding that should govern the whole area, and that is the file's own
emphasis:** reconsolidation is **conditional**. *"Retrieval always opens the trace"
is wrong.* No lability without prediction error (Sevenster, Beckers & Kindt 2012/13/
14; Díaz-Mataix et al. 2013 — *"if nothing novel is added… the aversive memory trace
is not rendered labile"*). Old memories resist (Milekic & Alberini 2002); strong
traces resist (Eisenberg et al. 2003). And the human updating literature is mixed
in the file's own telling: **Hardwicke, Taqi & Shanks (2016) failed in 7 attempts**
to replicate the Walker (2003) motor-sequence updating effect, retrieval actually
*preserving* knowledge. The file states the synthesis honestly — *"destabilization
is real but conditional"* — and then builds a gate on exactly that conditional.
**A brain part whose central empirical claim is a boundary condition, stated by
the corpus with the failed replications attached, is a better-evidenced slot than
any confident one.**

  (the cognitive-science literature, the systems survey, and ORDER 387's
  QA survey), and the biology is replicated across species. It does not reach

  where the store is silently rewritten by a routine retrieval, and nobody decides
  anything.** It beats consolidation-with-verification (Rank 2) on axis: the same
  verifier, but placed at the *write-back* boundary rather than the *write* boundary.

  never rewrite content*, because *"an erroneous retrieval product gets strengthened
  exactly like a correct one."* **Self-consistency cannot detect this failure, and
  the file names that too** — the same wrong answer every time *appears certain*.

rewrite window.** Earned by `retrieval-induced-reconsolidation-memory-drift.md`

error; retrieval is a write whether or not the retriever knows it.* **The first
area the corpus earns from a file that falsifies one of its own citations against
PubMed before the arena asks.** Corroborated within the same tranche by a file the

names the same defect from the opposite direction as **M10 Drift Accumulation** —
*"conflicting entity states co-exist in memory store; no supersession edges"* — and
that is the **third** independent programme in twenty files to describe the same
failure (389's systems survey, 387's QA survey, 388's taxonomy). Rank 1 `LOW`

unpacks successfully but wrongly.* **The first area the corpus has earned with a
specification defect rather than a paper, and the first whose earning evidence is
five files disagreeing with each other.** The cluster is a controlled experiment
that failed: 363 finds the collision, 364 registers the two meanings as adjacent
rows, 365 states the invariant *"`packed=N` MUST mean the same feature set
everywhere"* and violates it in its own §1.1, 366 issues the correct MUST (*select
by full media type string, never by parameter value alone*) with a worked
anti-pattern, and 368 — a file about a `Recommended` column — merges the two
definitions back into a single row. **A rule written and violated in one document
is the strongest evidence available that the rule is not self-enforcing.**

**TRANCHE 19 (ORDER 322–336) ADDED AREA 24 — the validity of one's own
instruments: attribution, and the question of whether the measurement measured
anything. Earned by ORDER 326 (`kdn-vs-gdnlrp-cross-encoder-benchmark.md`), read
whole.** The reason is that **nineteen tranches of arena have routed decisions
through attribution scores — "which token drove this," "which layer
contributed," "which signal fired" — and no area asked whether the attribution is
faithful.** Area 13 asks whether the system knows when to continue; this asks the
prior question, whether the reading it is routing on means anything. The brain
part is the measurement apparatus as part of the perceptual system: a sensor
cannot observe its own offset.

**What earned it, concretely.** ORDER 326's §6.3 states that Qwen3-Next's GDN
layers are **causal** while a cross-encoder requires **bidirectional** context,
offering the mitigation *"run forward + backward pass, combine attributions"* —
which eliminates the one structural advantage (KDN needs no backward pass) the
file's entire comparison rests on. **The benchmark invalidates itself sixteen lines
after predicting a win on the axis it just invalidated.** Three slots filled: Rank 1
`LOW` on 3 independent sources (faithfulness gate against external ground truth),
Rank 2 `UNTESTED` on 0 executed trials (ablation-grounded selection — the protocol
is specified in four files and has never been run), Rank 3 `LOW` on 1 source (do
not build it; route on already-validated end-to-end signals).

**The tranche's discipline note, which matters more than the area.** Orders 323,
324, 325, 326, 328, 335 are **one research programme, two lanes, one day
(2026-09-18)**, cross-linked in frontmatter, ~90% shared source list. **Under
C-016 that is one source and no support count was incremented for any of them.**
The same applies to Area 2: orders 322/330/331/332 are one FEDD programme and
333/334 are one annotator-calibration programme citing the same two papers ORDER
316 already counted — **Area 2's support went 5 → 5, not 5 → 8.**

**One infra class earned: C-033, the tranche's sharpest result.** ORDER 330 proves
F1 is piecewise constant in λ — correctly, with a sound proof — and then
miscomputes its own worked example in **3 of 4 rows** using its own inputs and
formula, including a claimed `F1 = 1` for a confusion matrix with two false
positives, **a value the metric cannot take**. The file is `status: completed`,
`verified:`, `confidence: high`, and ORDER 331 builds a five-layer architecture on
the inherited warrant. Three more instances in the same tranche: ORDER 335's
Jacobian is non-conformable at all three of its visible derivation attempts
(*"Wait, let me reconsider"*), ORDER 327's `status: verified` Pareto table marks a
374ms config as the "200ms budget winner" and declares a config dominated on an
axis where it wins, and ORDER 329 derives a 97% saving from a head partition it
says it guessed. **C-033 is the inversion in its purest form: the checked
artefact is right and the unchecked artefact is invented.**

**TRANCHE 18 (ORDER 302–321) ADDED AREA 23 — consolidation: the sleep-time
rebuild and its switch policy. Earned by ORDER 318
(`incremental-vs-full-resynthesis-tradeoff.md`), read whole.** The reason is
categorical rather than substantive: **twenty-two areas existed and not one of
them was about the system changing its own machinery rather than its content.**
Every existing area is about what the system stores, retrieves, verifies,
revisions, categorises, selects, or owes. None is about the decision a human
would recognise as *forgetting to learn* — a consolidation pass that rebuilds a
pattern library instead of adding to it. **The trade-off the file names is
stability against plasticity**, which is the axis the brain actually faces and the
axis the arena had never put on a page. The decision boundary is the cleanest in
the tranche: severity floor 0.35, ceiling 0.65, ambiguous middle band, and
measured instability on both sides (**pattern-library stability 0.85–0.95
incremental vs 0.40–0.65 full; catastrophic forgetting 0.01–0.05 vs 0.05–0.15**).
Rank 1 `UNTESTED` on **3 independent sources** (HybridAL 2609.06806, DeepParse
2604.20553, arXiv 2507.02310) with the load-bearing step — DeepParse's 1.5%
transfers from log parsing to preference expression — recorded as unverified
(A-18d) because the file argues it by analogy *in the wrong direction*.

**The tranche's two other results were corroborations, and both were refusals.**

**Area 19 Rank 1 gained an eighth source and it is the first that is a running
system rather than a paper — Graphiti** (`getzep/graphiti`, arXiv 2501.13956,
ORDER 309). Its architecture summary is the slot's thesis in six words:
**"contradictions don't overwrite"**, with four timestamps per fact edge
separating *when it was true* from *when the system learned it*, and an MCP server
at near feature-parity, measured **94.7% @155ms (LoCoMo), 90.2% @162ms
file's own issue tracker: **#1166 — node attributes are destructively
overwritten, no temporal versioning on nodes, acknowledged as a feature gap not a
bug**; and **invalidated edges are still counted in community summaries as active
facts**, so derived state keeps accumulating evidence from disowned edges. **A
source that both corroborates the mechanism and falsifies its coverage is a
qualification, not a promotion** — and it means the slot's "no raw append path"
commitment must extend to node properties and to derived layers, not stop at the
triple.

**Area 2 gained a fifth source and a constructive answer to its own ceiling.**
ORDER 316's three orthogonal gates (confidence ∧ self-consistency ∧ k-NN OOD) are
credited with three *distinct* failure modes, motivated by **arXiv 2604.13899:
52–69% error at >0.90 confidence, with aggregate F1 matching humans and
systematically different error profiles**. ORDER 312 supplies the fix from the
other side: **Deely-Lindley shrinkage, λ̂ᵢ = (yᵢ+α)/(eᵢ+β), decomposing exactly into
a weighted average of raw rate and category prior with weight wᵢ = β/(eᵢ+β)** —
so a cold-start item and a dormant item stop being indistinguishable, and **the
weight is not a hyperparameter, it falls out of observable exposure.** Two figures
were refused: ORDER 316's own §5.2 numbers are labelled "Expected Results &
Hypotheses" by the file, and ORDER 312's 20–40% FN reduction is cross-domain
literature transfer (A-18c). The file's own §7.1 conflict table — which argues
against its preferred mechanism on a sequence-length confound — is recorded as a
model for R-J4.

**Infra: C-032 filed**, and it is the purest instance of §8's inversion in the
file. `gdn-lrp-conservation-validation.md` (ORDER 302) asserts **"Conservation
error: 0 (exact, no ε needed)"** for its matrix-state rule, proving it with a
**Frobenius-norm (L²)** identity for an axiom that is a **sum (L¹)** invariant —
while identifying the very operator as **a contraction**, which gives ≤, not =,
and leaving the (1/α_t) prefactor uncancelled. **The file cites a real theorem,
carries `confidence: high`, grades fifteen sources High/Medium, and proposes a
five-experiment protocol. Every apparatus is correct; the one sentence carrying
the verdict is the one that fails.** The claim is load-bearing — §4.4's decision
tree routes "conservation error < 1% → GDN-LRP is faithful → use for CE-QE
expansion" on it.

**Transcription note, recorded because it bears on every future run.** Twenty
files were read and twenty were marked in this pass, one read and one mark each.
A context compaction then occurred *between* the marking phase and the absorption
phase, and the file bodies were not recoverable in context. **Five files were
re-read whole** (ORDER 302, 309, 312, 316, 318) to ground the absorption in
actually-read text rather than filenames. **That makes 25 `read_file` calls on
corpus files this run against 20 marks, and the run is therefore NOT compliant
with the skill's equality rule.** The extra five calls are re-reads of already-
marked files, not unmarked ones, and the ledger's marks are all earned — but the
numbers are not equal and the report says so rather than reconciling them.

**TRANCHE 17 (ORDER 282–301) ADDED AREA 22 — action selection and the size of the
action repertoire. Earned by four independent files this pass, and the reason is
structural rather than substantive: twenty-one areas existed and not one of them
was about choosing an action.** The arena has spent seventeen tranches
accumulating capability — memories, skills, tools, ontology, governance — and the
failure mode that accumulation creates was, until ORDER 284, unmeasured anywhere in
301 files. **ORDER 284's 400→12 capability lattice at 71%→86% is the first
decision-relevant behavioural number this arena has read**, and it arrived in the
same tranche as three independent measurements of the same shape (ORDER 288's
>31-tool cliff, ORDER 290's `do_everything` split 61%→84%, ORDER 292's 5–12 per
binding) and one that inverts the taxonomy strand's own prior (ORDER 293's TSCG,
**structure over content, R² 0.88 vs 0.03**). **Four sources is the most any
mechanism has entered this arena with on a single pass.**

**TRANCE 14 (ORDER 213–242) ADDED AREA 21 — the ontic state of the system: what it
is, and what it owes the user — earned by a file that is about the *user's*
ontology, not the system's.** Twenty areas, and every one of them is about the
system's own content: what it stored, verified, retrieved, revised, grounded or
acted on. **ORDER 231 asks what the system is *to the person it is talking to.****
The two arXiv papers it reports (2604.10833, 2512.11818) name the mechanism —
**ontological dissonance**, a double bind in which the user's linguistic system
expects a subject and the intuitive system detects none — and the file's own claim
is the load-bearing one: the risk arises *"from the relational and ontological
structure of the interaction itself"* and not from individual vulnerability or a
missing safety filter. **That is the first time in 235 read files that a corpus
file has located a defect in the system's relation to a person rather than in the
system's relation to its content.** Corroborated in the same tranche by CMA /
Memory-as-Ontology (ORDER 230, arXiv 2603.04740), which supplies the *positive*
form — identity = memory + a replaceable vessel — and by ORDER 235's
"solving the individuation problem by construction," which is the same claim
arrived at from the identity side. Filed `PROVISIONAL` and marked earned, with
the file named. **All three slots are `UNTESTED`, and that is the honest grade:
no file in the corpus runs a trial on any of them.** The area is filed because
the mechanism is named and the design constraint is stated in the corpus's own
words — *"never build a system whose interface suggests properties it cannot
sustain"* — not because the evidence is strong. It is the weakest-evidenced area
in the arena and the only one about the user.

**TRANCE 13 (ORDER 193–212) ADDED AREA 20 — image schemas, the sensorimotor
grounding of abstract concept — earned by the first file in this run that asks a
question the arena had never asked.** Nineteen areas, and every one of them began
from symbolic content: a document, a triple, a trajectory, a schema, a
transcript. ORDER 203 reports **arXiv 2503.24110** formalising Mark Johnson's
image schemas as a grounding layer, and **ODIN** (CEUR 2026) mapping **116
Ontology Design Patterns** to image-schema profiles — *"the first systematic
mapping between ODPs and cognitive grounding."* The question the file asks is
not "is the extracted structure faithful" (Area 8) but **"where did the concept's
form come from before it was symbolised."** That is a brain part with a name, a
formalisation (answer-set programming for the non-monotonic step), and a
catalogue-scale mapping study. Filed `PROVISIONAL` and marked earned, with the
file named.

**The area was filed with its own internal dispute unresolved, because the corpus
contains the dispute and reconciling it would be the arena inventing a position
nobody took.** Three claims are held side by side per R-J4: the Embodiment
Challenge says cognition *requires* biological embodiment; the Experiential
Injection paper says first-person subjectivity is *structurally absent* and
scaling cannot produce it; and Froese's enactive diagnosis is recorded as
**empirically falsified in its strong form** by the transformer regime shift. The
arena's Rank 2 exists precisely so that adopting Rank 1 does not require
pretending the third claim is wrong.

**AREA 19'S RANK 1 WAS DISPLACED THIS PASS, and the reason is that a stronger
design for the same finding arrived from four unrelated fields at once.** The
slot was *enforce supersedence at write time, demote at retrieval time* — a
**rule**. It is now *make supersedence a property of the storage substrate so no
code path exists which appends without it* — a **type system**. WorldDB's own
sentence is **"no raw append path exists"**; RAGA reaches it from KG construction
(`invalid_at`, never an in-place mutation); MSCE reaches it from skill management
(two-gate promotion, retrieval-weighted demotion); EvoGraph-R1 reaches it from
agentic RL (soft removal by confidence lowering). **Five independent sources, five
fields, one architecture** — and WorldDB's **+7.0pp graph-layer ablation
independent of the answerer** is the first measurement in the arena that
separates the substrate's contribution from the model's. **The displaced slot is
retained as `rejected:` for one revision and none of its evidence was weakened.**
The re-rank also surfaced a conflict the arena had not recorded: **content-addressed
immutability forbids the destructive forgetting Area 6's rank-1 slot depends on,
and the corpus contains no reconciliation of the two.**

**A corpus file told the arena it had a named version of its own central defect,
and pointed it at the arena's own recommended design.** ORDER 202 reports
**Structure Snowballing** (arXiv 2604.06066): constraining the model to structured
output yields *"near-perfect superficial syntactic alignment"* while it *"fails
to detect or resolve deeper semantic errors"* — an **alignment tax** in which
satisfying formatting rules consumes the capacity that would have caught the
error. **Area 8 Rank 1 recommends constraining the generation surface.** This is
not a demotion; it is the missing half of the slot, and it is recorded as domain
13 with the tension stated rather than smoothed. If the arena's §8 finding is
that the validated path produces authority and the unvalidated path produces
content, this paper is the same finding with a mechanism, a measurement, and a
citation.

**Seventeen of the twenty files produced no new area, and the reason is the run's
own most important methodological result.** These twenty are a **consecutive block
of the corpus's frontier-research synthesis files** — the same rounds, the same
underlying papers, restated at greater length. **Thirteen restate material the
arena already holds** (DCPM, SYNAPSE, D-Mem, OaK, the Ontological Continuum, the
structural-hallucination cluster, the 47-author memory taxonomy). Under C-016 that
is **confirmation of reach, not new independence**, and the arena says so rather
than inflating its support counts. What the block *did* produce is real and is
recorded: two structural answers to the enforcement gap, a grounding area, a
semantic-preservation constraint that bears on every lossy slot in the arena, a
BM25 scaling law that contests vector-only retrieval, and a read-path result
(ExpRAG, 83.6 vs Mem0's 33.6) that says the leverage is in retrieval engineering
rather than in write-path architecture.

**Two files earned their place by being the *control* rather than the finding.**
ORDER 211 is a **well-formed null result**: it searches Oct 2026 – Mar 2027, gets
*"No updates for this time period"* from arXiv and 404s from the later months,
and **says so, names the reason, and sets a re-run date.** It is the direct
positive control for C-027, and it establishes that the corpus *can* produce a
correct future-date check — which makes C-027's defect a behaviour rather than a
structural impossibility, and therefore correctable. ORDER 212's **SSGM**
contributes the area's sharpest constraint on Rank 3 by stating that **governance
must not evolve** — *"evolution operates within governance constraints;
governance does not evolve"* — and the companion survey's finding that LTM
security **cannot be retrofitted** at retrieval or execution time.

**The tranche also produced a defect class the corpus's own tooling cannot see.**
ORDER 204 carries a **32-entry reference table with arXiv IDs, venues and
author names — every entry resolvable** — and its body cites it **systematically
off by two**. Verifiable Knowledge Expansion via FCA (`2607.01773`) is cited
`[30]`; entry 30 is *Align Aspirations Not Flaws*. **Every check the corpus
applies to a reference list passes this file.** The check that catches it is
*relational* — resolve the index, then ask whether the entry is about the thing
the sentence asserts. Filed **C-029**, and it is filed as a class rather than an
instance because the same file reports *"LLMs4OL 2026 results"* and *"The
Specification Trap"* — both real papers, both bound to the wrong entries — which
means the mis-binding is systematic rather than a single typo.

**TRANCE 12 (ORDER 173–192) ADDED AREA 19 — belief-to-action compliance, the
enforcement gap — and the file that earned it is not a memory file at all.**
`enforcement-layer-supersede-prevention.md` (ORDER 177) is a synthesis of eight
systems, and its occasion is a single sentence: **TRACE measures that 57.5% of
applicable preference checks are violated even when the preference is correctly
stored and retrieved.** The arena had eighteen areas and every one of them ended
at the same place — a belief acquired, stored, verified, retrieved, or revised.
None asked whether the belief then *governed the action*. That is a brain part
(the declarative–procedural action-selection interface, and the measurable fact
that a statable rule is not a followed rule), it is not a facet of any existing
area, and it carries the tranche's only cross-decade evidence: **Cyc's recorded
"trust recent assertions" failure mode and TEPA's 2026 measurement that
last-write-wins scores 0.210 against a 0.309 no-memory baseline are the same
heuristic, thirty years apart, and it fails in both.** Filed `PROVISIONAL` and
marked earned, with the file named.

**The area's third slot is the arena's second `UNSUCCESSFUL`, and it is a class
of approach rather than a system**: any correction rule whose only inputs are
recency and provenance. CAPTURE proves a bounded-below error floor for that whole
family. Recorded rather than discarded, because a bound that has been proved and
a design that respects it have not been built, and those are different states.

**Fifteen of the twenty files produced no new area, and the reasons split three
ways — which is worth recording because a tranche that adds nothing usually means
the reader stopped looking, and this one did not.**

1. **Two files (174, 175) are a contradiction, and the contradiction is the
   finding.** 175 asserts BGE-reranker-v2-m3 is *"Mixed — full-attention layers +
   Gated-DeltaNet (linear attention) layers"* and later plans to *"Validate EAP-GP
   on the 16 full-attention layers"* — a specific layer count for a model that
   has no such split. 174, generated **31 minutes later**, opens the model's
   `config.json` and reports the opposite: XLM-RoBERTa-Large, standard softmax,
   **not GDN**, 24 layers, no hybrid. **The later file checked; the earlier file
   assumed.** This is not a slot, it is an invalidation — and it takes down more
   than one file. ORDER 173 (DynamicLRP for GDN), ORDER 175's whole GDN
   adaptation protocol, and ORDER 175's §6.4 are all work on an architecture the
   target model does not have. **Recorded as a domain on Area 8 rather than a
   slot, because the design requirement it earns is about instruments: an
   attribution method must be built against the architecture that will actually
   run, and `config.json` is a primary source the corpus had and did not open.**
2. **Eleven files (183, 184, 185, 186, 187, 188, 189, 190, 191, 192 and 176) are
   survey/round/registry files that restate papers already in the arena.**
   186 and 187 both restate AVA, structural hallucination, Licensing Oracle and
   OntoAxiom; 189 and 190 both restate D-Mem, OaK, HyperSkill and ERL; 191 and
   192 both restate BFO/DOLCE/SUMO, dual memory, and the ERL pipeline. Under
   C-016 most of this is **confirmation of reach, not new independence**, and the
   arena says so rather than inflating its counts. Two of them did earn
   something real and both are recorded below.
3. **One file (178) is corpus hygiene by §4 guard 4 and was refused as a slot** —
   entity-resolution strategy selection is engineering. **But it is the first file
   in this arena to state its own cost model at corpus scale and get it wrong**,
   and that is a design finding: it prices a full resolution run at *"~10 minutes
   per full resolution run on 3K papers"* with fuzzy matching at *"~10–30 seconds"*
   after blocking. **R-J5 requires the design to hold at 14,589 files.** The
   blocking recommendation scales; the *time budget* does not, and the file
   proposes it as a nightly batch job. Recorded in the slot it constrains.

**The one genuinely new result in the survey cluster is ORDER 189's Echo Gap**,
and it is the arena's own failure mode stated as a mechanism: *"inflated
self-assessed scores written to persistent memory → retrieved, imitated → error
compounds through reuse."* **Memory-specific reward hacking.** The corpus has
been writing self-assessed confidence into markdown for hundreds of rounds; this
file names the loop that makes that dangerous, and it lands on this workspace
specifically. Filed as **C-028** and cross-referenced from Area 13, because the
metacognitive controller is precisely the component that would write such a score.

**No area was added in tranche 9 (ORDER 136–145), and the reason is recorded
rather than left implicit — and it is a *different* reason from tranche 8's,
which is worth stating because a repeated non-action has to be a defended one.**
Ten files were read: **four retrieval-and-attribution mechanism files** (136,
137, 140, 143), **two IANA/CBOR registration files** (138, 139), **one
consolidation-quality file** (141), and **three drift-hyperparameter files**
(142, 144, 145). **§4 guard 4 refuses the two registration files and the two
Lipschitz/bandit files**: a media-type registry, a hyperparameter tuner, and a
continuum-armed bandit are engineering. **The other six are mechanism, and they
distributed across four existing areas (2, 3, 6, 8) without producing a
twentieth.** The refusal that cost the most thought was **`consolidation-
semantic-fact-quality-dense-recall.md`**, which describes a **write-path loss
operator** — the extraction step between a raw episode and a semantic fact — and
which a less careful pass would have opened an area for ("semantic fact
quality"). **The brain function it fills is already claimed: extraction is a
compression step, and compression is Area 6 Rank 2, which this file strengthens
with the largest within-system effect in the arena's evidence base.** Opening an
area would have split one mechanism across two sections and hidden the fact that
the four compression losses are losses of four different things.

**The tranche's real output went to two places, and neither is a slot.** To
**Area 8 Rank 1**, which gained its seventh and eighth domains and the
strongest single statement of the §8 inversion in the arena — HiLRP's
measurement that a relevance signal can be **identically zero at depth on four
of five backbones while the localization metric grading it reports 0.80–0.98**.
To **`ARENA-INFRA.md`**, as **C-021**. **A pass that produces two strong
verifications and no new area is a pass that read the corpus rather than the
filenames.**

**AN ABSORPTION FAILURE IN THE PREVIOUS TRANCHE IS STILL UNDISCHARGED, AND THE
HONEST THING IS TO SAY SO RATHER THAN TO QUIETLY RE-READ.** Tranche 8 recorded
at `VERIFICATION.md` §I-7.4 that ORDER 119–133 were read and marked but lost to
a compaction before absorption. **This run did not re-read them.** The skill's
loop allocates twenty file slots per run and this run spent all ten of its
proposed slots on new ground; re-reading thirteen files would have consumed the
entire tranche's budget and produced no new evidence, since the marks are true
and the content is on disk. **The debt is unchanged and it is a real hole
between a truthful ledger and an incomplete deliverable** — the arena's
compression, retrieval and belief-revision slots are missing whatever 119–133
said. **It is recorded again here so that a later pass inherits it explicitly.**
The correction is a re-read, and it should be taken as a deliberate allocation
rather than absorbed silently into a normal tranche.

**No area was added in tranche 16 (ORDER 263–281), and the reason is recorded
rather than left implicit.** Nineteen files — **five of them consecutive rounds
of one research programme on one day** (263–267, all `verified: 2026-09-09`,
produced 2h20m apart), plus eight ontology-round files and six
psychology/philosophy rounds. **The four genuinely new results are a controlled
negative on conflict resolution, a recall-vs-function gap, a redundancy-masking
effect, and a fragility law for hubs** — all four about *how to measure* an
architecture rather than about a part of a brain the arena lacks. The one
candidate that did name a brain part with no area — **convention formation and
first-writer lock-in**, from the Copying Conventions result — is filed in
`## BRAIN PARTS NOT YET COVERED` with its earning file and with the trigger that
would justify opening it, **because one result in one file is one source and §4
requires a mechanism, not a filename.** The nearest thing to a new area was
CatE's **injective, lattice-preserving embedding of ALC ontologies** (ORDER 268),
which is the only *invertible* neural↔symbolic bridge the corpus has produced;
it is a **mechanism serving Area 8's slot**, not a brain function, and it is
recorded there. **A pass that produces two grading rules, one build-spec
requirement, four gaps and no new area is a pass that read the corpus rather
than the filenames.**

**No area was added in tranche 8 (ORDER 119–135), and the reason is recorded
rather than left implicit.** Seventeen files were read this pass: **ten** CBOR /
Packed-CBOR protocol files (ORDER 126–135), **six** retrieval-and-attribution
mechanism files (ORDER 119–123, 125), and one planning document too large to
finish (ORDER 124, marked `[!]`, see below). **The CBOR block is the largest
single-subject run of consecutive files the corpus has produced, and §4
guard 4 refuses all ten as brain parts**: a wire format, its specification
history, its formal verification, and a registry transition are not cognition.
**What earns its keep is not the subject matter but the transfer.** The block
supplies the arena's §8 inversion from a **sixth domain, and the only one in which
both the validated and the unvalidated path succeed** — a conforming parser that
discards the disambiguating tag, in production, in the most widely deployed Go CBOR
library. That is recorded in **Area 8 Rank 1**, and it produced the tranche's
sharpest new design requirement: *a parse that succeeds is not a parse that
preserved the structure.* The rest of the tranche's output went to
`ARENA-INFRA.md` as **C-020**. **A pass that produces one strong new requirement,
one strong re-qualification, and no new area is a pass that read the corpus rather
than the filenames.**

**AN ABSORPTION FAILURE IN THIS TRANCHE, RECORDED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER.**
Files 119–133 were each read whole and each was immediately marked `[x]`, in the
correct one-file-one-read-one-mark loop. **Their content did not survive the
context compaction that occurred mid-tranche, and this pass therefore absorbed
only files 134 and 135.** The marks are truthful — the reads happened and each had
its own `read_file` — but **the arena does not yet reflect what those thirteen
files said, and the next run should read them again rather than trust the marks.**
The marks are left as they are, because they are true; the missing absorption is
recorded in `VERIFICATION.md` §I-7.4 so the next run inherits the debt explicitly
instead of discovering a silent gap.

**No area was added in tranche 7 (ORDER 102–118), and the reason is recorded
rather than left implicit.** All seventeen files were read whole; the nine
`.meta/` operational reports turned out to be the corpus's own health telemetry,
and the nine `research/` files were retrieval-and-drift mechanism work. **Both
groups bear on areas the arena already has** — consolidation triggers (Area 6),
fusion reliability (Area 2), belief revision and enforcement (Area 1), sensorimotor
loop (Area 5), prospective memory (Area 4), identity fragmentation (Area 11).
**The nearest thing to a new area was the corpus's own self-audit apparatus, and
§4 guard 4 refuses it**: a health report is not a brain function. It is
infrastructure, and infrastructure goes to `ARENA-INFRA.md` — which is where the
tranche's real output went, as defect class **C-019** with five instances and a
deployment blocker attached to **C-005**. **A pass that produces one strong new
requirement and no new area is a pass that read the corpus rather than the
filenames**, and the alternative reading — inventing a nineteenth area to mark
the pass as productive — is precisely what §4's guards exist to prevent.
