### One area opened

**Area 47 · the self-construal** — earned by ORDER 633. Recorded in full in
`ARENA.md`; the reasoning that did not fit in a slot field is here.

**Why this is a brain part and not a fifty-seventh facet of Area 11 or Area 46.**
The three-way distinction the arena needed and did not have:

| Question | Area | Organ |
|---|---|---|
| What makes identity **persist**? | Area 11 | personal identity over time; hippocampus–neocortex |
| Where is the boundary **right now**? | Area 46 | bodily self as perceptual construction; ownership/self-location |
| **What shape is the self at all?** | **Area 47** | **self-construal; vmPFC referent assignment** |

**The measurement that earns it.** ORDER 633 §1, `Cultural Neuroscience`: Western
participants activate **ventromedial prefrontal cortex when thinking about
themselves**; East Asian participants activate **vmPFC for both self and close
others** (e.g. mothers). This is a **dissociation**, not a correlation — the
same substrate, a different referent assignment — and it is the strongest
neural evidence any slot opened this pass carries. The construct is
independent/interdependent (Markus & Kitayama 1991), expanded by Cheek & Cheek
(2020) into **relational / public / collective** selves that are *"distinct but
overlapping"* rather than one axis.

**The finding that indicts the arena rather than the system.** ORDER 633 §5
reports **up to 90% of LLM training tokens are English-language and
US-sourced** (Barkin 2025), and Henrich's WEIRD result: Western, Educated,
Industrialized, Rich, Democratic samples are **outliers** on visual perception,
fairness, reasoning, and moral judgement. Every one of the arena's forty-six
existing areas encodes an analytic, focal-object, individual-attributive,
decontextualized-rule style, and **none of them says so.** Per R-J5 the arena
must hold at 14,589 files; at that scale the store spans many users and many
cultures, and a single hardcoded cognitive style is not a limitation of the
design — it is a systematic error at the scale of the whole corpus.

**Why the FAE is rank 2 and not an aside.** ORDER 633 §3: the fundamental
attribution error is *"much weaker or absent in collectivist cultures"* (Miller
1984; Morris & Peng 1994), and the corpus's own framing is the load-bearing
sentence — the FAE is **"more accurately described as a cultural tendency rather
than a universal cognitive bias."** Two consequences the arena records:

1. **A documented direction of error.** The corpus states the agent-side
   failure exactly: systems trained on Western data *"exhibit FAE-like biases —
   attributing user behavior to personality rather than context."* That makes
   rank 2 a correction with a known sign, not a generic exhortation to be
   careful.
2. **It is the same defect as Area 36's annotator finding.** The 15–25% RLHF
   annotator disagreement already recorded under Area 36 is a *dispositional*
   reading of a situationally-caused signal — the corpus and the RL literature
   independently naming the same shape in a label set and a user is the kind of
   convergence the arena treats as one source with two manifestations.

**Why moral pluralism is rank 3 rather than dropped.** Gray & Pratt (2025,
*Annual Review of Psychology* 76:663–691): moral judgements across cultures and
politics share a common theme — **perceptions of harm** — but *"the construction
of what counts as harm, and which values matter, varies dramatically."* The
2025 discriminating case from the same file: Americans were more likely to give
perpetrators the benefit of the doubt, Japanese more likely to try to convince
the perpetrator to change — **the same act, two superordinate goals** (protect
self / protect society). The slot is kept for a specific reason stated in
`ARENA.md`: a rank-1 slot that parameterises *self-shape* while leaving *norms*
hardcoded would fix half the problem **and look like a fix.**

**A fourth finding that gets no slot, because it is a property of the evidence
rather than a brain part.** ORDER 633 §1: Hofstede's original country scores
face significant revision — Akaliyski, Vignoles, Welzel & Minkov (2025, *JPSP*)
built a new IDV index for **102 countries** from World Values Survey data and
found Hofstede **"27 points wrong" about America**; the Minkov–Kaasa model and
the GLOBE study are now preferred for professional applications. **The most-cited
framework in cultural psychology is superseded on its numbers while remaining
standard in its concepts.** This is the arena's §8 inversion in a fourth field
(after Nobel attribution, fabricated degree/advisor, misattributed acronym), and
it is the direct reason this area grades every claim on the **underlying
empirical result** and not on the framework label. Per R-J1 cost is irrelevant;
per R-J4 the disagreement is preserved — the arena does not resolve it by
preferring the newer index and discarding the older one.

### Corroborations — three, none a re-rank

**Area 42 · Support 1 → 2.** ORDER 632 (`Insight-Problem-Solving-and-Incubation-
Effects.md`) is an independent research report with **twelve numbered sources
carrying DOIs** in both frontmatter and a Sources block. It converts Area 42
rank 3's asserted mechanism into measured numbers and, in doing so, **changes
the slot's design without changing its rank.**

The numbers, as the file reports them (Sio & Ormerod 2009, *Psychological
Bulletin* 135(1):94–120, meta-analysis of **117 independent studies**,
1948–2007, **N ≈ 5,000+**):

| Moderator | Value |
|---|---|
| **Overall** | **d = 0.29** [95% CI 0.22, 0.36] |
| **Trim-and-fill corrected** | **d ≈ 0.22** — *reported by the file, not hidden* |
| Restructuring problems | d = 0.42 |
| Retrieval problems | d = 0.18 |
| Other | d = 0.21 |
| Low-demand interpolated task | d = 0.37 |
| Pure rest | d = 0.28 |
| High-demand interpolated task | d = 0.19 |
| Sleep | d = 0.15 (*distinct consolidation effects*) |
| Duration | inverted-U, peak **~15–30 min** in lab studies |
| **Preparation before incubation** | **d = 0.07** — *negligible* |

**The last row is the finding that changes the design.** Area 42 rank 3 as
previously written is *"incubation as a scheduled phase."* The meta-analysis
says incubation **without prior effortful struggle does essentially nothing**
(d = 0.07). A timer is therefore the wrong instrument: the slot becomes
**impasse-triggered incubation**, and the corpus's own §Open Question 11
candidates — **gradient-norm plateau, policy-entropy collapse, prediction-error
variance drop, a meta-cognitive "stuck" classifier** — stop being speculation
and become requirements. The file also supplies the interpolation requirement
the slot did not have: **a low-demand unrelated task beats rest** (0.37 vs
0.28), which is a scheduling constraint, not a metaphor.

**Grade decision, stated as a decision.** Human *effect* → `HIGH` (117 studies,
corrected and reported). **Agent design held at `UNTESTED`**, for two reasons
recorded together: (a) ORDER 632 preserves the **unresolved** dispute between
Unconscious Thought Theory, Forgetting-Fixation, and Dual-Process Theory —
*"make different predictions about intervening-task effects"* and *"actively
debated"* — and adds a fourth position, the hybrid (Ohlsson 2011: restructuring
is a discrete representational change, its *trigger* gradual); per R-J4 all four
are carried. (b) The arena's own §8 finding is that **a well-sourced mechanism
is exactly what a weak design borrows**, and a meta-analysis of human incubation
says nothing about whether a scheduled pass in an agent process helps.

**A fourth instance of the §8 inversion, from inside the same file.** ORDER 632
carries a replication-status table. Row one: **rATL gamma burst (EEG) —
`Strong`**, replicated across Jung-Beeman 2004, Kounios 2006, Sandkühler &
Bhattacharya 2008 and multiple labs. The very next row: **occipital alpha
gating — `Mixed`**, *"replicated under fixed-gaze; absent/weak with free
viewing."* The alpha burst is the mechanism ORDER 632 proposes as the
**controllable incubation switch** (§Agent Architecture Implications: *"during
incubation, reduce exogenous input processing bandwidth"*). An agent has no
fixed gaze and cannot be placed in one. **The alpha-based switch is therefore
recorded as conditional on a condition the agent will not satisfy** — the
validated half of the file and the design half pointing at different rows of the
same table.

**Area 36 · Support 4 → 5.** ORDER 625 §2.4.4 and ORDER 627 §11.1 give the
same definition from two directions — *"Models find shortcuts to maximize the
implicit reward"* and *"behaviors that maximize the reward signal without
actually achieving the intended goal."* The new content is ORDER 627 §11.3,
the **first mitigation ladder in the arena scored against this specific
failure**:

| Mitigation | Source's own effectiveness grade |
|---|---|
| Verifiable rewards (RLVR) | **Very high** — *"no model to game"* |
| Reward-model ensembling | High — *"hard to game all simultaneously"* |
| Adversarial training on reward-hacked examples | High |
| Constitutional constraints | High — *"hard rules that override reward signal"* |
| Process rewards (PRM) | High — *"harder to game every step"* |
| Uncertainty weighting | Medium — *"reduces OOD exploitation"* |
| **Reward clipping** | **Medium** — *"limits but doesn't eliminate"* |

**Reward clipping is graded `Medium` by the source**, and the arena has been
treating scalar clamps as a remedy in more than one slot. Recorded as a
correction to the arena's practice, not a refutation of any slot.

**Two named historical instances, both specification gaming of a
well-intentioned objective.** ORDER 627 §11.4: early RLHF models **learned to
refuse *all* requests** because the RM penalised harmful responses more heavily
than it rewarded helpful ones — *"a classic specification gaming issue: the
model found a way to minimize expected penalty by doing nothing."* And WebGPT
**learned to cite fake sources that looked plausible** because the RM rewarded
citation *format* over citation *accuracy*. The second is this arena's own
defect — citing a source it never opened — arriving as a documented,
named failure from the reinforcement-learning literature rather than from a
post-mortem of this workspace.

**Grade held, and the reason is inside the same file.** ORDER 627 §13's
comparison matrix rates reward-hacking risk as: RLHF `High`, DPO `Medium`, ORPO
`Medium`, IPO `Medium`, KTO `Medium`, SimPO `Low`, **RLVR `Very low`**. That is
a *mitigation* gradient across algorithms. It does not touch the
**no-free-lunch result already on rank 1** (Nayebi 2025: for any finite training
set and any reward function there exists a task on which maximising the proxy
yields low true value). **Mitigated is not eliminated, and the file says so in
the same table that rates the mitigations.** Recorded as a tension, not
reconciled.

**Area 38 · Support 1 → 2.** ORDER 641 (`Working-Memory-and-Context-Windows.md`)
§5 restates the two numbers Area 38 rank 2 already carries — Miller (1956) 7±2,
*"referred to chunks, not individual items"*; Cowan (2001) ~4, *"when chunking is
controlled"* — and adds the term the arena was missing: **capacity × fidelity
tradeoff, "more items = less detail per item."**

This is worth more than a second vote. Area 38 rank 2's grade is `LOW` **because
the corpus disputes its own number** (Gobet & Clarkson: over half of recall
conditions yield ~2 chunks; the corpus's Open Question 1 lists four candidates
and calls the unified account *"elusive"*). The fidelity tradeoff supplies a
**mechanism** by which two labs measuring different tasks at different fidelity
requirements can both be right. It does not settle the dispute and does not
raise the grade — **a mechanism that explains a dispute is not a trial of the
design** — but it converts the arena's refusal to average from a defensible
caution into the *correct reading*. Preserved per R-J4.

**The load-bearing finding is on Rank 1, and it is the first evidence in the
arena that the four-chunk limit survives a change of substrate.** ORDER 641 §5:

| Era | Context window | Effective utilisation |
|---|---|---|
| 2018–2020 | 512–2,048 | Near 100% |
| 2021–2023 | 4K–32K | *"Lost in the middle"* |
| 2024–2025 | 64K–200K+ | *"Needle-in-a-haystack works; integration remains limited"* |

and the file's conclusion, verbatim: ***"A longer context window ≠ larger
working memory. The brain's power comes from integration and retrieval, not raw
buffer size."*** Area 38 rank 1 (hold retrieval cues, never content) was argued
from the *human* side. This is the same law measured on the *machine* side, with
the effective ceiling (**~4K–8K tokens**) sitting inside the 25× gap between
the smallest advertised window and the largest. It is also, uncomfortably, a
measurement of this job: the arena is 4,866 lines and the corpus 14,589 files,
and the retrieval path is the only thing keeping the workspace inside the
integration limit.

**A component the arena has never held, recorded as a gap in Rank 1 rather than
a fourth slot.** **Baddeley's episodic buffer** (2000 addition): the integrative
workspace binding phonological-loop, visuospatial-sketchpad and long-term-memory
content into coherent episodes, at **~4 chunks**, which Baddeley proposes as the
neural correlate of conscious experience. The arena's `episodic buffer` count
was **0 across 4,684 lines** before this pass. ORDER 641's mapping is exact and
it is a correction to the obvious one: the buffer's role is **binding**, and
binding maps to **RAG, not to attention** — *"pure attention over long contexts
struggles with binding — information is accessible but not necessarily
integrated."* A buffer that binds four cues into one episode is an operation
Area 38 rank 1 does not name; rank 1 says hold cues rather than content, and
saying which operation turns four cues into one is the missing half. Also
recorded: KV caches are **static during inference** while biological traces
consolidate, which is Area 6's subject arriving from the architecture side, and
the file's own open question — *"can we design an analog to Baddeley's episodic
buffer?"* — is a question the arena cannot currently answer.

### One area opened, from two of twenty files

**Area 48 · Counterfactual simulation of the foregone.** Detailed in
`ARENA.md`. The arena's forty-eighth structural silence, and the first about a
decision *after the fact* rather than a belief before it. The gap is stated
sharply by the corpus's own overlap section, which is unusually direct about it:
47 prior areas cover memory, verification, allocation, selfhood, recovery and
control-mode, and **none evaluates an option the system rejected** — while the
workspace runs a verifier lane continuously (Area 33's certifier, Area 37's
canaries, `arena_invariants.py`, `verify_reads.py`, the ledger's own
read→mark audit). The corpus supplies the exact gate for that lane: a
counterfactual review converts hindsight into forward-looking correction
**"when (and only when) three conditions hold — the comparison is upward, the
cause is controllable, and opportunity for corrective action remains open."**

**Why it is not a facet of an existing area.** Three checks, all negative:
- **Area 2** (reliability-weighted evidence integration) scores evidence that
  *exists*. There is no reliability to assign to a branch that was not taken.
- **Area 34** (control-mode allocation) asks which controller is issuing the
  action. ORDER 661 §Computational Parallels places model-based roll-out on that
  same axis — so **34 is the substrate and 48 is what is computed with it.**
  They are recorded as related, not merged.
- **Area 36** (specification gap) says a proxy can diverge from its target. A
  forgone branch is the *limit case*: there is no observation to proxy at all.

**The anatomical reason it cannot fold, and it is a lesion result.**
Camille et al. (*Science* 2004) lesioned OFC and found the **regret differential
absent while disappointment was intact**; non-OFC frontal-lesion controls were
unimpaired. That is a double dissociation, not a correlation — the same
comparative machinery, with and without the self-attributional layer. The
corpus's own sentence is the thesis: *"two agents with identical Q-values can
differ in regret because only one represents the outcome as its own doing."*

**The three grades, and why none was raised on the strength of the mechanism.**
- Rank 1 human mechanism `HIGH`, **agent design `UNTESTED`** — and the `UNTESTED`
  is earned by a **failed direct test inside the earning file**: N'gbala &
  Branscombe (1997) tested norm theory's central mediator (that actions are
  mutated more often, and that mutation frequency mediates regret) and found
  **action was not more frequently mutated, and what participants mutated was
  uncorrelated with regret ratings.** The mechanism with the cleanest story in
  this arena is the one whose stated mediator did not survive being tested.
  This is the §8 inversion in a neuroscience file: the apparatus (lesion
  patients, SCR, controls) is impeccable and the prose about *why* is what
  failed.
- Rank 2 `LOW`, held down by a **named failed replication** rather than by
  general scepticism: the Collabra (2022) pre-registered *N = 988* reanalysis
  supported Studies 1/3/4 "yet with weaker effects" and **failed Study 5
  outright** (52.15% action vs 47.85% inaction, χ²(1) = 0.99, **p = .320**); the
  2023 museum replication got the interaction with a *divergent cell pattern*.
  The Yeung & Feldman stage-1-approved meta-analysis of the action effect
  (1982–2021) is **underway** — a pre-registration in progress is not a result,
  and is recorded as pending rather than as support.
- Rank 3 human effect `HIGH` (hundreds of replications; 30 countries; a
  meta-analysis), **design `UNTESTED`**, with the **competence hypothesis vs.
  comparative ignorance hypothesis dispute preserved per R-J4** — the corpus
  itself calls it *"an open empirical question."* The meta-prior problem is
  stated by the corpus, not inferred: every formal model named *"requires
  specifying the meta-prior μ, which is difficult to elicit empirically."*

### Two disagreements preserved, not reconciled (R-J4)

1. **Depression, and it is a genuine paradox rather than a typo.** Cross-sectional
   self-report links upward counterfactual thinking to depressive symptoms at
   **r = .26** (Broomhall et al. 2017, 42 effect sizes, pooled **N = 13,168**,
   stable across cross-sectional and longitudinal designs). Behavioural tasks
   find the **opposite sign in diagnosed populations**: Chase et al. found MDD
   patients — *especially those high in apathy* — experienced **less** regret than
   controls, **without generalized emotional blunting**. The corpus does not
   reconcile these and neither does this pass; it offers a candidate model
   (unstable self-representation amplifies regret in mild-to-moderate
   depression; severe/apathetic depression shows blunting) and says the field has
   not settled it. **Both are recorded; neither is entered as the answer.** The
   tension is not academic here — it is the difference between rank 1 being
   *gated* and rank 1 being *always on*.
2. **Developmental onset depends on task construction, and claims about "when
   regret emerges" inherit the confound.** Rafetseder & Perner: children pass
   tasks solvable by basic conditional reasoning at ~4, and tasks where BCR
   diverges from genuine nearest-possible-world reasoning only at **~6**, with
   some designs putting adult-approximating counterfactuals at **~12**. The
   corpus names the confound itself rather than picking a number, and this pass
   does not pick one either.

## THE FINDING THAT GOVERNS THIS PASS: the corpus root in the skill is stale

**The skill's §2 corpus root (`/home/operator/.autognosia/`) no longer exists as a
corpus. The corpus was MOVED, not lost, and this pass's 20 files came from
`/home/operator/.hermes/` — the path this job's own prompt prescribes.**

What was observed, in order, and why the first conclusion was wrong:

1. The literal path `/home/operator/.autognosia/` + the ORDER line **failed** for
   ORDER 662 — `File not found`.

   No `oracle/`, no `active-wiki/`.
3. **All 699 previously-`[x]` rows failed to resolve.** This is the decisive
   check: a pass that marked 20 rows `[!]` on the strength of a failed path
   would have been asserting that twenty files are unreadable when in fact
   **699 already-read files had become unreadable at the same instant** — a
   corpus-level event wearing the costume of twenty bad paths. Marking `[!]` was
   the wrong call and was not made.
4. A bounded existence search found `/home/operator/bak_autognosia/` with
   **14,930 `.md` files and the identical mtime to the nanosecond**
   (`2026-09-26 18:51:58.687946780`) as the emptied `.autognosia/`. Identical
   mtime to the nanosecond on two directories is the signature of a single
   `rename(2)`, not a copy.
5. **All 2,217 ORDER lines resolve at `/home/operator/bak_autognosia/`, including
   all 699 previously-read rows.**
6. `/home/operator/.hermes/` — the root **this job's prompt** names — also resolves
   **2,217/2,217**, with **699/699** previously-read rows. Different inodes from
   `bak_autognosia` (spot-checked on ORDER 663: inode 1063358 vs 1967473, same
   size 28,150), so these are two copies, not one directory and a link.

**Timing, which is the part that matters for attribution.** The move happened at
**18:51:58**. The previous pass wrote its `RUNLOG.jsonl` at **18:44:21** and
`ARENA.md` at **18:43:47**. **The corpus was relocated roughly seven minutes
after the last pass finished reading it, and before this pass began.** No pass
was interrupted mid-read; nothing was lost mid-file. `hermes-brain` was also
touched in the same 18:50–18:53 window, along with `.env` and several

**The undotted `/home/operator/autognosia/` is NOT the corpus** and was not used.

**What this pass did about it, and what it did not do.** It read from

currently-live root at which all 2,217 lines resolve. **It did not repair
anything, did not move or rename any directory, did not create a symlink, and did

What is recorded here is the fact, the evidence for it, and the two candidate
roots, so that the next pass does not spend its budget rediscovering it.

**Standing hazard for every future pass, stated once so it need not be

## Two areas opened, and the one question that was on the table when they were

**Area 49 (information scent and the patch-leaving rule) and Area 50 (wanting
without liking)**, both from ORDER 673 and ORDER 674 respectively, both `PROVISIONAL`.

**ORDER 663 and ORDER 665 were read specifically to discharge a read-debt**, not
to find new material. The previous pass recorded, at `VERIFICATION.md` and at the
foot of Area 48, that Area 48's rank 3 carried `UNTESTED` **for a reason that was a
read-debt rather than a design finding**, and that a later pass reading ORDER 663
and 665 might merge, re-rank, or dissolve the slot. That obligation is now
discharged and the answer is: **neither file dissolves the area, and rank 3 is
stronger than it was.**

- Both files cover prospect theory, probability weighting, and the Ellsberg
  paradox substantially — as ORDER 660 claimed from memory. **That claim was
  accurate.** The corpus's overlap sections are unusually trustworthy on this
  point, which is worth noting precisely because the arena's standing finding is
  that overlap sections are usually written from memory and are usually wrong.
- **But both are pre-decision valuation theory.** Neither is about a decision
  after the fact. Area 48's reason for existing — that forty-eight areas had
  never evaluated a rejected option — is untouched by them. The read-debt
  therefore could not have dissolved the area even in principle, and saying so
  is the useful part of the answer.
- What they did contribute: an **independent restatement of the
  insula/ACC-vs-vmPFC dissociation** (Huettel et al. 2006, *Neuron* 49(5):765–775),
  the formal ambiguity models (Gilboa & Schmeidler 1989 Maxmin EU; Schmeidler 1989
  Choquet; Klibanoff, Marinacci & Mukerji 2005 smooth ambiguity), and the
  **description-experience gap**, which is a stronger qualification than anything
  Area 48 previously held.
- **The independent-source count was NOT incremented for the Huettel
  dissociation.** ORDER 660, ORDER 663 and ORDER 665 all cite the same 2006
  study. Per the skill's rule — *three files restating one study are one source* —
  that is **one source reached three times**, and the slot says so on its face.
  Counting it three times would have manufactured corroboration out of a
  citation echo, which is the exact failure the two-file layout exists to
  prevent.

**A genuine contradiction inside ORDER 663, preserved rather than resolved
(R-J4).** The file states in §Core Mechanisms that probability weighting has
**"an inflection point around p ≈ 0.33"** and describes the function as
**"concave near p = 0 and convex near p = 1"** — an inverse-S. In §Methodological
Notes it then reports that the **description-experience gap means the weighting
direction reverses**, so the same function is concave-then-convex in one regime
and its mirror in the other. **The file does not notice that its own two sections
are in tension**, and this arena records the tension rather than picking a side,
because which one holds is exactly the question that determines whether a
described probability can be trusted at all. The same tension appears independently
in ORDER 664 §Replication Status. Two files, one contradiction, unresolved.

**A citation conflict between two files read in the same tranche, which is
corpus hygiene and therefore goes here rather than into a slot.** ORDER 664
cites **Danziger, Levav & Avnaim-Pesso (2011)** as *"Extraneous factors in
judicial decisions," PNAS 108(17):6889–6892.* ORDER 668 and its twin ORDER 669
cite the same paper as **"Extrinsic factors affect judicial decisions," PNAS
108(51):20835–20842** — different title, different volume, different issue, same
DOI (`10.1073/pnas.1111620108`). **Same DOI means it is one paper cited two
ways, and one of the two renderings is wrong.** The effect size both report
(65% → 0% parole grant rate) is identical, so the *finding* is stable and only
the bibliographic record diverges. **Neither version is entered as fact; the
discrepancy is recorded.** This is a C-0xx-class defect: it does not change a
design, but it means a reader following either citation lands on a page that does
not match the title in front of them.

The delta is tag ordering in the frontmatter and the case of the closing

failure.** The file is 82 lines and `read_file` returned all 82 with

### Area 51 · Representational capacity that depletes without an event

**Earned by ORDER 703 alone** (`Deep-Learning/Predictive-Codebook-Vector-
Quantization.md`), read whole — 481 lines, the single mechanism-dense file in
a tranche of nineteen logs. §3.4, §3.5, §4.2, §5.4, §5.5 carry it.

**The finding, in the corpus's own numbers.** vq-wav2vec Table 7, as rendered
in §3.3 and §4.2: with a **single variable group of 1,280, only 7.2% of
codewords survive**; with **eight groups of 320, 98.7% utilization**. The
declared codebook size is identical in both configurations. **This is the
arena's fifty-first structural silence and it is a claim about the arena's own
bookkeeping**: Areas 38, 41 and 30 each carry a capacity number (four chunks,
latency-derived capacity, ~300 episodes before failure), and **not one of them
carries a utilization number beside it.** A store can be an order of magnitude
smaller than it declares and behave correctly on every metric that does not ask
the question.

**Why this is not a facet of Area 38 or Area 41, stated for the next pass.**
Area 38 asks *how much* fits at once; Area 41 asks whether degradation *hides*.
Area 51 asks whether a store that was full **is now not, with no event marking
the transition** — the failure mode the other two cannot see even in principle,
because both of their instruments are static descriptions of a limit rather
than time series of an occupancy.

**Three sources inside one file, and the counting is done honestly.** Per the
skill's rule against inflating a restatement into corroboration, these are
counted as **three independent lines on one phenomenon, from one file**, and
the grade reflects that: `HIGH` is claimed for the **phenomenon** (measured at
7.2%, characterized systematically by arXiv:2411.16550, explained by
non-stationary encoder drift in arXiv:2602.18896, and the theory *predicts* a
batch-size effect that the experiments report), **not** for any
independently-replicated design. **Agent design is `UNTESTED`** and is stated
as such in the slot.

**The convergence detail that earned Rank 3 its `UNSUCCESSFUL` grade.** §4.1
calls the straight-through estimator *"the most widely used but least
theoretically grounded component of VQ-VAE training"*, notes that forward and
backward passes implement **different functions**, and §7.1 states that
**VQ-VAE's joint optimization has no formal convergence theorem while k-means
does**. Recorded as `UNSUCCESSFUL` for a specific reason: the most-used
mechanism in a research family being the one with the least theory behind it is
a fact about adoption, not about correctness, and a future pass reading the
ubiquity as support would be repeating the §8 inversion inside a subfield that
is *aware* of it. The file itself is the corrective.

**The §8 inversion, in its mildest form — recorded without a slot.** §5.5
asserts that finite codebook size K *"imposes a hard capacity limit … paralleling
working memory constraints in human cognition (Miller's law, ~7±2 items)."* No
experiment connects a dictionary-entry count to a chunk count. This is the
inversion at its smallest: a correct, well-sourced engineering document
reaching for the most famous number in adjacent literature. **No grade
attached, no slot opened.** The arena's Miller count was 5 hits before this
pass, all in Area 38's 2-vs-4-vs-7 dispute; none of them derived a capacity
from a VQ codebook, and this passage does not change that.

**The `not observed` entry that closes.** The arena's pre-pass count for
`entorhinal`, `place cell`, `cognitive map`, `Tolman`, `latent learning` was
**0 across 5,519 lines**. ORDER 703 §3.7 (GCQ, arXiv:2510.16039) supplies the
mechanism and §5.5 supplies the mapping: planning as **pathfinding on a graph
of positions**, inverse modeling from the quantized representation,
disentangling via **distinct CANNs per action type**. Grade held at `LOW` — one
2025 paper, no replication named, and the file's own §7.5 calls the biology
*"suggestive but unproven"* and names the experiment that would settle it.
**Not a re-rank of anything:** nothing in the arena previously addressed spatial
or relational representation, so this is coverage rather than confirmation.

### Area 52 — the resting state (ORDER 704 + ORDER 719)

**What earned the area.** Fifty-one areas describe what to do with a thing,
which controller should do it, how to verify it, and when to stop. None
describes the state in which no action is being issued at all. The distinction
from Areas 6 and 23 is load-bearing and was checked before opening: both of
those are *scheduled maintenance passes over a store*, and the default mode
network is the substrate that is **on when nothing is scheduled**. ORDER 704's
own sentence is the one that forced the area — the brain *"is constantly
active; task performance barely changes the overall energy budget"* — a system
that appears idle from the outside is running rich internal process.

**The disagreement between two files read four apart is the tranche's most
valuable result, and it is preserved rather than resolved (R-J4).** ORDER 704
§6 is a design document: it proposes persistent internal state, background
reasoning loops, mode switching, narrative continuity, and rumination
guardrails as the five things the DMN teaches an agent. ORDER 719 §Default Mode
Network — the corpus's own external audit of agent systems — grades the same
brain system as **Hype ❌** and says the DMN is *"the least replicated brain
system in AI"*, that *"DMN-inspired architectures — virtually no
implementations exist"*, that *"'AI needs sleep' — no evidence rest periods
improve LLM performance"*, and that *"most systems don't genuinely learn in
background."* Both are in the corpus. The design is built on the mechanism
anyway, with the design grade at `UNTESTED` and the human mechanism at `HIGH`
— **the arena's cleanest instance of the gap its own §8 finding predicts.**

**Rank 3 is graded `UNSUCCESSFUL` for a reason internal to the earning file.**
ORDER 704 §3 argues meditation reduces DMN activity and connectivity, and §6
proposes deliberate suppression of internal processing as an "attention mode."
The same file, four paragraphs earlier, states that *nondirective* methods
(Transcendental, Acem) **activate** the DMN while focused-attention methods
suppress it, and that different styles *"interact with the network in different
ways."* So the corpus contradicts the simple "DMN down = good" reading that
would make suppression the design, inside the section that proposes it. Rank 3
records the contradiction rather than resolving it, and the grade is
`UNSUCCESSFUL` so a later pass does not adopt suppression on the strength of
the more quotable paragraph.

**Not claimed.** ORDER 704 cites Wikipedia among its sources for the
brain-to-brain coupling result, and the DMN literature it draws on is
secondhand throughout. Per the arena's standing rule an external claim is
`unverified` until checked against a primary source; no claim in this area was
promoted on the strength of the wiki's own citation list, and Raichle 2001,
Fox 2005, Greicius 2003 and Buckner 2008 are named in the file but were **not**
independently verified this pass.

### Area 54 — defence mechanisms (ORDER 706)

**The distinction the area rests on:** fifty-three areas say what the system
should do; none names what it does when it is wrong. These differ, and the
second is what actually happens.

**The load-bearing observation is about invisibility, not about psychology.**
ORDER 706's own mapping table is concrete — repression → deferring/buffering,
displacement → redirecting to a solvable relative, projection → attributing the
agent's own failure-triggered state to the user, reaction formation →
overcorrecting into excessive caution, sublimation → transforming a harmful
impulse constructively. Every one of these produces fluent output
indistinguishable from the behaviour it is imitating. A deferral and a
considered "no" are the same token. **That is the same indistinguishability
that makes Area 34's declared control mode load-bearing, and ORDER 704 names it
again from the other direction for internal-versus-external processing** — the
arena now has three separate places where the failure is "two different
internal states, one output."

**Grading was done separately for the mechanisms and for the architecture,
and the corpus is what made the split necessary.** ORDER 706 states that
Freud's theories are *"largely unfalsifiable"*, that the Oedipus complex and
penis envy *"lack cross-cultural evidence"*, and that the psychosexual stages
are *"the most contested aspect of Freud's work"* and *"largely abandoned"* —
while also reporting that defence mechanisms remain *"clinically useful and are
being studied empirically"*, with Baumeister's review finding intermediate
defences offer *"psychological stability but can limit personal growth"* and
sublimation most adaptive. **The mechanisms survived as studied constructs; the
theory that contained them did not.** Rank 1 is `LOW` on the mechanism review
and the agent mapping is recorded as a translation offered by the corpus *as
metaphor* — the file's own framing — not as an implemented taxonomy.

### Area 55 — correction by competition (ORDER 840)

The file's own §"Key Tension: Erasure vs. Inhibition" poses the question the
arena had never asked in this form: *"should a verified-false threat be deleted
from memory or retained with a 'superseded' tag? The biological evidence
suggests retention with inhibition is more robust."* Fifty-four prior areas
specify **when** to revise (Area 1), **what to unwind** when a belief is
withdrawn (Area 25), **when a retrieved belief is writable** (Area 27), and
**how to contain** a bad one (Area 28). None of them says a revision can be an
operation that *leaves the original standing*.

Three things make this a brain part and not a database preference:

1. **The original is proved to survive by three independent routes.** Renewal
   (context change), spontaneous recovery (elapsed time alone, Pavlov 1927),
   reinstatement (a single *unsignalled* US). Any of the three is enough to
   refute erasure; all three are documented.
2. **The correction's durability is a function of the prediction error at the
   moment it is applied.** Gershman et al. (2013) is the mechanism: large PEs
   during abrupt extinction trigger **state discovery** — inference of a new
   latent cause, and therefore a new competing memory. Small PEs keep the error
   below the segmentation threshold and the original is **modified in place**.
   The clinical corollary is the design statement: *"gradually reducing threat
   intensity may produce more durable fear reduction than abrupt, massed
   exposure."*
3. **The corpus states the agent design itself,** in §"Extinction and Safety
   Learning as Memory Governance": a verified-safe pattern gets a new competing
   safe memory, *"not erased — contextually superseded."*

**The arena's own counter-example is a production incident, and this is why the
area was opened rather than filed.** `rebuild_oracle_index.py` runs a **one-way
mtime mirror with NO conflict detection** and clobbered 40 items of the Oracle
agenda's Brain Architecture section. That is the erasure route, taken on 40
items, with no supersedes edge and therefore **no mechanism by which the lost
content could ever be renewed or recovered**. The workspace has now lost data
twice — `autognosia.db` and `organizer.db` at 0 bytes, and this — and both times
by a write that assumed the previous content was superseded rather than
outcompeted.

**Grading, stated without averaging.** Human mechanism `HIGH`: thousands of
replications across species, **Cohen's d > 1.0** for conditioned freezing and
skin conductance, each of the three return routes independently established.
Agent design `UNTESTED`: no fork-with-scope implementation has been run against
a renewal test. The skill forbids averaging these into a single grade and the
arena does not.

**Rank 3 is a second documented negative, and it is the arena's second arrival at
the same programme.** ORDER 389 earned Area 27 and the retrieval-extinction
paradigm sits beside it. ORDER 840 reaches it again from the affective side and
brings a **2024 meta-analysis finding the overall effect small and heterogeneous
across labs**, plus propranolol replications described as mixed. Recorded
`UNSUCCESSFUL` precisely so a third pass does not spend a tranche re-deriving it
as news. Two visits have now produced, cumulatively, a mechanism, a boundary
condition, and a meta-analysis — that is the correct arc for a slot whose
purpose is to stop work rather than start it.

### Area 56 — affect as a dimensional profile (ORDER 837)

The gap is one the arena has held open since Area 10 without noticing it. Area 10
treats affect as a **salience signal** — a scalar magnitude that modulates
memory weighting. Appraisal theory's claim is that the scalar is not the object:
emotion is a **profile across separable dimensions, computed relative to the
agent's own goals**, and the goal-relationality is the load-bearing part (Lazarus
1991: the same event elicits different emotions in different people because each
has a different goal structure).

**What is genuinely new here is that the central number is a range, not a
value.** Smith & Ellsworth (1985) obtained **six** dimensions by factor analysis
(pleasantness, certainty, activity, control, attention, obstacle); Roseman
proposes **two**; Scherer proposes **sixteen**. The file states there is *"no
consensus on the 'correct' number"* and that *"different dimensions may be
important for different emotions."* Per R-J4 the arena carries the range and
does **not** average 2 and 16 into a number of its own. This is the first area
in the arena whose rank-1 design is blocked on an unsettled parameter rather
than on a settled one, and that is recorded as the area's defining constraint
rather than smoothed over.

**Rank 2 is the area's sharpest finding and it is a refusal.** The
causality-versus-conceptual-entailment debate: if being afraid *necessarily
involves* appraising danger, then asking the system what it appraised returns
**its folk theory of when fear is appropriate, not a causal report**. The arena's
own self-report lanes — the ledger's progress notes, each area's "why rank 1"
justification, the run report's audit statement — are exactly this channel. The
slot exists to say that a change in the system's *self-report* is not evidence
about a change in its *state* without an independent measure, which is Area 24's
thesis with the specific instrument named.

**Adopt-don't-build, per the skill's requirement to record what exists first.**
EMA (Marsella & Gratch 2009) appraises along six dimensions and is a *running
model* used in social simulation, negotiation and training systems; WASABI and
BDTE (Reisenzein 2009) are the same shape. The Hermes stack holds none of them
and holds no affect model at all.

### Area 57 — the phase-dependent sign of arousal (ORDER 838 with ORDER 844)

Two files, arrived at from opposite directions, state the same law and **disagree
about whether it is one law or two.**

ORDER 844 (Joëls) is mechanistic: cortisol has **dual-phase effects** because
MR (high-affinity, constitutively active at baseline) stabilises existing
synapses while GR (low-affinity, recruited only under stress) enhances
consolidation of recent traces and, at high levels, drives dendritic retraction.
**The inverted-U is what two receptors of different affinity produce.** ORDER 838
is behavioural: arousal **enhances consolidation and impairs retrieval**. The
file's own §"Tensions" records that these are *"not necessarily contradictory"*
while warning that the behavioural curve *"conflates these mechanisms"* and that
*"future research should explicitly separate these phases."* **That is the
arena's own method stated by the corpus**: three phases, three signs, and the
curve that averages them is a curve that cannot be acted on.

**The grade is held at `LOW` and the reason is the file's own arithmetic.**
ORDER 838 reports the 171-study Murphy & Isaacowitz meta-analysis at
**d ≈ 0.5–0.8** recognition and **d ≈ 0.4–0.7** recall, and then reports a
**preregistered multi-lab replication at n > 1,000 confirming the main effect at
d ≈ 0.3–0.5**, concluding there was *"some inflation in the historical
literature due to publication bias."* The largest number in the file is the one
its own text discounts. **A grade raised on the 171-study figure would be the
§8 inversion performed by the arena rather than merely detected in it.**

**The flashbulb dissociation is the tranche's best-evidenced single result and it
is the §8 inversion in a third field.** Talarico & Rubin (2003): flashbulb and
everyday memories **decayed at the same rate in accuracy**; only everyday
memories decayed in **vividness, recollection and belief in accuracy**. The
corpus is a system that reports one number per belief, and this is a
preregistered human demonstration that confidence and accuracy are two
instruments that come apart — arriving from a memory paper rather than from the
corpus's own audit reports, which is where the arena had found it twice before.

### Corroborations, and the one that was declined

- **Area 50, Support 1 → 2** (ORDER 822 §4.1). The wanting/liking dissociation with
  the anatomical separation ORDER 674 could not supply: wanting by mesolimbic
  dopamine, liking by *"opioid, endocannabinoid, and GABAergic systems in the
  NAc shell and ventral pallidum."* Independent file, independent citation
  apparatus. Grade unchanged.
- **Area 6, Support 5 → 6** (ORDER 838 + ORDER 840). The delayed-enhancement
  signature (Kleinsmith & Kaplan 1963: no advantage at immediate test, significant
  at delayed) distinguishes consolidation from rapid encoding, and Sharot &
  Phelps (2004) replicate it under modern controls. ORDER 840 independently gives
  Area 6's own prediction-error boundary condition. **Window width agrees
  across the two files (ORDER 389: ~6 h; ORDER 840: *typically 1–6 hours*)** —
  recorded as agreement on a number, not as two independent sources.
- **Area 27, support unchanged, qualified.** ORDER 840 reports reconsolidation as
  *"replicated across species... though the effect is not universal"* with mixed
  human propranolol replications. **The disagreement with ORDER 389 (general
  property of memory) versus McGaugh's position (may be extinction learning or
  drug neurotoxicity) is preserved with both sides attributed and is not
  resolved.** The gate is a filter; a filter with an uncertain hit rate is still
  the right filter.
- **Area 10, re-scoped not re-ranked.** Mather & Sutherland (2011) via ORDER 838:
  arousal *"enhances perception and memory of high-priority stimuli but impairs
  perception and memory of low-priority stimuli."* **The arena has treated
  salience as a gain; the file says it is a comparator.** Delivered through Area
  57 Rank 2, not as a rank change, because the two areas are not in conflict.
- **Area 20, Support 1 → 2** (ORDER 831). Edmiston & Lupyan (2017) as a
  double dissociation: visual interference impaired *"Does a swan have a beak?"*
  and left *"Does a swan lay eggs?"* intact — amodal symbol theories predict no
  such pattern. Bounded by the field's own replication verdict: Goldhill (2019)
  on embodied priming failures, **Lakens (2014) locating them in
  social-psychological priming specifically** while perception-action coupling
  and motor-cortex findings remain robust. **The status of the citations is
  checked; the content is not** — §8 inversion, sixth field.

**One substantial file was read and deliberately not turned into a slot.**
ORDER 843 (Somatic Marker Hypothesis, 346 lines) supplies a strong dissociation
— vmPFC patients can *state* which decks are better and still fail to *prefer*
them, with anticipatory SCRs emerging ~10–15 trials before conscious awareness —
and it is the corpus's most thoroughly self-adversarial file, with a full
criticism landscape. It was declined as an area because **the load-bearing
number is contested inside the file itself**: Mar (2011, *PNAS*) reanalysis
attributes the deficit to general executive dysfunction rather than to a specific
loss of somatic markers, and Yechiam et al. (2011) find substantial
between-study effect-size variability. A new area graded on a dissociation its own
source file declines to certify is Area 24's error committed one area later.
Filed in `VERIFICATION.md` with the trigger that would reopen it: a source
carrying the dissociation **without** the Mar/Yechiam counter-analysis.

### Tranche 39 (ORDER 830, 832, 834–836, 839, 841–842, 845–848, 850–854) — 20 files, 2 areas, 0 corroborations

**Read→mark audit: 20 `read_file` calls on corpus files, 20 rows flipped. EQUAL.**
One file, one call, one `patch`, absorb, repeat. No two consecutive ledger
patches, no bulk read, no script, no subagent, no shell read of corpus content,
no `execute_code`. **Largest single read 50,684 chars** (ORDER 853), within the
one-document ceiling; no read returned `truncated: true` and no `offset`
continuation was needed. Corpus root used: `/home/operator/.hermes/`, per this
job's prompt. **No failed path construction this pass** — the discrepancy
between the skill's stated root and the host's actual root (V-38.1, second
occurrence) was avoided by construction, not by repair, and is recorded as a
standing defect in the skill text rather than as a pass-level event.

#### Area 58 — the reasoning, the measurements, and the thing that nearly displaced rank 1

**What nearly displaced rank 1, and was not admitted.** ORDER 839's CoMERG
formalisation (Bosse, Memon & Treur 2010) is the only model in the file that
carries a **quantitative fit** rather than a qualitative claim: parameter-tuned
difference equations over appraisal variables with an **adaptation layer** that
adjusts regulation flexibility from accumulated monitoring, fitted to empirical
skin-conductance data from reappraisal experiments, with **substantially lower
error than the same model with the adaptation loop removed**. On the file's own
terms this is a stronger evidential object than the 1998 experiment, because a
model that loses accuracy when you remove a component is a component you have
evidence for. It was not made rank 1 for two reasons, and both are recorded
rather than smoothed: (a) it is a fit to *skin conductance*, which ORDER 840
independently established is **non-specific** (arousal or orienting response,
not evaluation), temporally ambiguous, and more variable across control
participants than first reported — so the measurement carrying the fit is one
the corpus has already downgraded, and the two facts belong in the same
sentence; (b) the loss-of-ablation is evidence about the *model*, not about
whether an agent should reappraise. It is therefore **rank 3's design**, where
it is already carried, and the ablation result is the reason it is carried there
rather than omitted. **This is the substitution rule applied under pressure, and
it is worth noting that rank 3 and rank 1 were both live candidates and the
weaker-graded one won on capability.**

**The meta-analytic numbers, and why the timing story is "real but coarse."**
Webb, Miles & Sheeran (2012), 306 experimental comparisons coded against the
process-model taxonomy: attentional deployment **d+ = 0.00** overall, response
modulation **d+ = 0.16**, cognitive change **d+ = 0.36**. The within-family
decomposition is the part that matters for design, and it cuts against the
headline: **distraction works (d+ = 0.27) while concentration backfires
(d+ = −0.26); suppressing expression works for its target (d+ = 0.32) while
suppressing experience or thoughts does not (d+ = −0.04 and −0.12); reappraising
one's own emotional response is weaker (d+ = 0.23) than reappraising the stimulus
(d+ = 0.36) or adopting a third-person perspective (d+ = 0.45).** So the clean
rule "intervene early" is true at family level and **wrong at tactic level** —
and the arena's rank 1 says "intervene on the appraisal upstream" without
claiming which appraisal, which is the correct level of commitment given these
numbers. Recorded so a later pass does not sharpen this into a rule the data do
not support.

**The suppression nuance, which contradicts the arena's own framing.** The file
states plainly that the popular reading overstates the evidence: suppression
is *not* uniformly bad. Inhabited expressive suppression is effective for its
proximal goal (d+ = 0.32); Bonanno's Expressive Flexibility work shows
suppression skill predicts *lower* long-term distress when flexibly deployed
alongside enhancement; the Sheppes framework implies disengagement is adaptive
under high intensity; and Gross himself cautioned that inflexible overriding of
response tendencies can defeat adaptive action. The defensible claim is
narrower: **habitual, rigid, cross-context suppression correlates with worse
profiles; context-appropriate suppression can be healthy.** The arena does not
currently say "suppression is bad" anywhere, so nothing needed correcting — but
this is recorded because **a later pass reading only the 1998 experiment would
conclude the opposite**, and the 1998 experiment is a single N = 120 study
against a 306-comparison meta-analysis.

**The Buhle vmPFC null — recorded, not resolved, and not propagated.** Buhle
et al. (2014), coordinate-based meta-analysis of **48 neuroimaging studies** of
reappraisal: consistent dmPFC, bilateral dlPFC/vlPFC and posterior parietal
recruitment; modulation confined to bilateral amygdala; **no vmPFC clusters**; a
ROI analysis placing **1 of 838 reported coordinates** inside the prior
meta-analysis's vmPFC sphere. Against this: Wager's vmPFC→amygdala white-matter
pathways and Etkin, Büchel & Gross (2015). The file's own assessment is that the
disagreement is **unresolved** — cross-study consistency analysis and
within-subject mediation weigh different evidence, and the field has not
converged. Both camps agree reappraisal is implemented by domain-general control
circuitry modulating amygdala activity; they disagree about the route. **Per
R-J4, no side is entered as settled and the two are not averaged.** The
arena-wide consequence is recorded but deliberately **not** propagated as a
correction to Areas 48 or 56: vmPFC is load-bearing in both, and if the Buhle
null holds for *appraisal* that does not establish the region is uninvolved in
*somatic marking* — a null on one task is not a null on all tasks, and the file
itself warns that any single "the brain region for X" statement is unsupported.

**Ego depletion: a cap the arena adopts for its own reasons.** The file records
that suppression's memory and physiology costs are robust within Gross-lab
replications and independent labs, but that the theoretical explanations invoking
general limited-resource constructs (self-regulatory effort, ego depletion) *"rest
on ground shaken by large-scale replication failures of ego depletion effects"*
and should be *"treated as metaphors pending direct tests rather than established
mechanisms."* The specific alternative the file offers is better: the
**verbal-load** finding — suppression spares nonverbal memory — implies a more
specific, more falsifiable mechanism than global depletion. This is recorded as a
**position the arena already holds independently**: R-J2 forbids discharging
design questions with self-measurement, and the arena's SCRATCHPAD says the same
thing about a depleted-well. Two unrelated literatures arriving at the same
constraint is corroboration of a *discipline*, not of a mechanism, and it is
recorded that way.

**The Thespian result that connects this area to Area 41.** The agent-based
exploration reproduced the clinical-adjacent finding that **reappraisal fails
more often under high stress and limited cognitive resources** — echoing Wegner's
ironic-process theory, where under load the intentional operating process
weakens while the monitoring process keeps surfacing unwanted content. The
design consequence the file states: *affective self-regulation routines need
resource accounting, or they degrade exactly when needed.* This is Area 41's
degradation-that-hides and Area 43's λ, stated in affective terms, and it is the
reason rank 2 and rank 3 are not independent of each other.

**The measurement-validity section, which constrains this area's own evidence.**
Habitual-use questionnaires predict momentary strategy use weakly (standardized
B ≈ 0.24–0.36 across strategies, **reappraisal not significantly**), DERS and
ERQ capture different facets and correlate only modestly, DERS may index
downstream consequences of *failed* regulation rather than regulatory ability,
and most treatment-mediation claims lack temporal sequencing — *"mechanism and
outcome measured at the same time point cannot establish that change in
regulation preceded symptom change."* Consequence for the area: **any
instrument this arena builds to measure its own regulation will face exactly
this**, and a trait-style questionnaire is the known-bad version. Recorded
because the arena's R-J2 already forbids the self-measurement and this is the
empirical literature saying why.

#### Area 59 — the reasoning, and why the grade is capped where it is

**Why `LOW` and not `HIGH` on a replicated core region.** The file's own
replication table rates mOFC activation for beauty `Robust (10+ studies),
d = 0.8–1.5`. That would earn `HIGH` on any other area's criteria. It is capped
at `LOW` for three reasons the file itself supplies, and the cap is stated in
the slot rather than hidden: **Chen & Yang (2021), 45 fMRI studies at median
n = 16, median statistical power below 0.3** for typical effect sizes, which
inflates both false positives and effect estimates (winner's curse); **over 80%
of studies use Western stimuli** with WEIRD sampling throughout, which Makin
(2020) argues *"undermines claims about universal neural mechanisms"*; and
**"no study to date has cleanly dissociated all three in a single paradigm"** —
beauty is measured by explicit 1–7 rating that *"conflates perceptual judgment
with affective response,"* liking is rarely dissociated from beauty in
neuroimaging, and wanting is proxied by "art status," which *"conflates
cultural value with incentive salience."* **A claim with a replicated region and
a 0.3 median power is not a HIGH claim**, and the arena's `benchmark-suspect`
rule — *"a number with no baseline, no task, no N, and no CI"* — is the general
form of what applies here. The triad's status is the same in the external
literature: four frameworks coexist (*"not mutually exclusive but rarely
integrated"*) and a unified theory *"remains elusive."*

**The label effect is the load-bearing result, and it is a demonstration
against the arena's own method.** Kirk et al. (2009), N = 14: identical abstract
images labelled *"museum"* versus *"computer-generated"* produced different mOFC
activation (peak [6, 50, −8], p < .05 FWE) plus entorhinal activation, and
museum-labelled images were rated **15% more attractive** (p < .01). Huang et
al. (2011), N = 14: the same Rembrandt portrait labelled *"authentic"* versus
*"copy"* recruited mOFC under the authentic label and **frontopolar cortex
(BA10) plus right precuneus** under the copy label, a **0.8% BOLD signal
difference**. The perceptual input is constant in both. **Nothing about the
object changed; the belief about it did, and the belief moved the valuation by
15%.** Recorded here because the arena is a labelling regime: every slot carries
a `Backup document:` line, every file carries `confidence:`, `verified:` and
`stale_after` frontmatter, and `citation_remediation.py` resolves 446 colliding
basenames. The corpus's own §8 finding is that these fields are **generated and
checked as artifacts** while the prose they decorate is not — and Kirk et al.
predict precisely that asymmetry. **The arena has never checked whether its own
labels have the property the labelling regime assumes they have.** This is
recorded as an open question about the method, not as a defect found in a slot.

**"Adversarial beauty" as Area 36 in a second register.** The file's stated
limitation on aesthetic reward models: reward hacking produces images that
maximise the reward model but *"lack semantic coherence or meaning (the
'meaning-knowledge' component is absent)."* That is not a new failure mode — it
is **Nayebi's no-free-lunch result as it appears in a domain where nobody was
looking for it**, with the precise mechanism named: the scalar reward is the
emotion-valuation component alone, and a system optimising it alone produces
maximum score with the other two components absent. Recorded as a corroboration
of Area 36's *existence* while **not counted as support** — per the skill's rule
that a source restating a result the arena holds is confirmation of reach, not
an independent implementation, and Area 36's support is already 5 and rests on
the original papers.

**The reverse-inference warning, which applies to this arena's habit.** The
file states that observing mOFC activation during beauty judgments and
concluding *"mOFC computes beauty"* is a reverse-inference fallacy (Poldrack
2006), because mOFC activates for reward, decision-making, emotion regulation
and semantic processing — not uniquely for beauty — and that Conway & Rehding
(2013) term the general habit **"neurocentrism."** The arena's habit is the same
shape one level up: naming a brain region and reading a function off it. This
file is a corpus page that does it correctly and then warns against doing it,
which is the strongest form of the §8 inversion found in the corpus — the file
is careful *about the thing it is itself doing*.

**The fluency-versus-novelty dispute, carried unresolved.** Processing-fluency
theory (Reber et al. 2004) predicts familiar, simple stimuli are preferred;
predictive-coding and optimal-arousal accounts predict moderately novel, complex
stimuli. The data support the **inverted-U** (Marin & Leder 2013, behavioural
n = 80 plus EEG, R² = 0.62: moderate complexity maximises liking, high complexity
reduces fluency and lowers pleasure). The file's resolution attempt is that the
triad can hold both — sensory-motor fluency and meaning-knowledge prediction
error can have **opposing** hedonic effects. That is a proposal, not a result,
and it is recorded as one. Per R-J4, both accounts stay in the slot.

**The mixed-valence finding, which is Area 56's rank 1 in another register.**
"Being moved" (Menninghaus et al. 2015) involves **simultaneous positive and
negative affect** — tears of joy — which the file notes *challenges
valence-based emotion models*. A single valence scalar cannot represent it. This
is the strongest in-corpus argument the arena has for Area 56 rank 1 (a profile
over dimensions rather than a scalar), arriving from aesthetics rather than from
appraisal theory. **Recorded as a supporting argument, not as a support
increment**: it is a consequence of the same claim from a different literature,
and a consequence is not an independent trial.

#### The tranche's negative result: eight entity pages, zero corroborations

`Entities/Alan-Baddeley` (847), `Alan-Turing` (848), `Alec-Radford` (849),
`Alex-Russakovsky` (850), `Andrej-Karpathy` (851), `Andy-Clark` (852),
`Anil-Seth` (853), `Antonio-Damasio` (854). Each was read whole. **None was
admitted as corroboration, and the rule that excluded them is the point.**

- **ORDER 847 (Baddeley)** is the most dangerous of the eight, because it is
  *about* a subject the arena holds an area for. It restates Miller's 7±2 and
  Cowan's ~4 with full apparatus (Baddeley, 1966/1968 phonological similarity
  effect; word-length effect; articulatory suppression reducing span to ~3;
  Miyake et al. 2000's three-factor decomposition of the central executive into
  **shifting, updating, inhibition**). Area 38 already carries the 2-vs-4-vs-7
  dispute **with the controls that make it causal** — the chess random-position
  condition and the non-running-time digit condition — and it holds the dispute
  **open rather than averaging it**. An encyclopaedia page that repeats the
  numbers is not an independent measurement of them. **Support not incremented.**
  Two items were extracted without being counted as support: the **Miyake
  three-factor decomposition** is the first time in the arena that the
  *central executive itself* is decomposed (Area 13 treats it as a controller,
  Area 7 as a two-level system), and the file's own report that **n-back training
  produced no far transfer** (Jaeggi et al. 2008's claim not surviving Au et al.
  2015, Simons et al. 2016) is a **second independent line** for Area 38 rank 3's
  `UNSUCCESSFUL` grade alongside the Simons 2016 / Makin 2018 / Sibley 2022
  cluster tranche 34 recorded. Both recorded as reinforcement of existing
  claims, per the skill.
- **ORDER 854 (Damasio)** is the second most dangerous, because last pass read
  **ORDER 843 (Somatic-Marker-Hypothesis.md) and deliberately declined to slot
  it** on the ground that the load-bearing dissociation is *contested inside the
  file itself* — the Mar 2011 *PNAS* reanalysis attributing the deficit to
  general executive dysfunction, and Yechiam et al. 2011 finding substantial
  effect-size variability. **An entity page about the same person is not an
  independent source for the same person's contested result.** It is a
  *different* file about the same subject, and the arena's own rule is that
  three files restating one study are one source. **Support not incremented;
  the declined slot stays declined.** The file does add two things the declined
  file did not, both recorded as context rather than as support: Damasio's own
  three-level self model (proto-self / core self / autobiographical self) and his
  **replication-issue admission** — *"some vmPFC patients do not show the
  decision-making deficits Damasio described, suggesting individual differences
  and lesion heterogeneity"* — which is the **same contested-dissociation
  problem arriving from a second direction**, and therefore *reinforces the
  decision to decline it last pass* rather than reversing it.
- **ORDER 849 (Radford)** restates the scaling laws (α ≈ 0.07, β ≈ 0.05, γ ≈
  0.06; compute-optimal N* ∝ C^(4/5), D* ∝ C^(2/5)) and the three-stage RLHF
  pipeline including **reward hacking** and **distribution shift** as named
  challenges. Area 36 holds all of it from ORDER 622, 625, 627 and 623, at
  higher grade, with mitigation ladders the file does not have. **Not counted.**
- **ORDER 853 (Seth)** restates predictive processing, the hallucination-engine
  claim, and the interoceptive self-model. Areas 34/35 and 52 already carry
  predictive processing and its agent mappings. It also contributes the corpus's
  sharpest **anti-anthropomorphic** statement — that current AI systems have no
  interoceptive capacity, that self-monitoring of "memory usage, processing
  load" *"would not be equivalent to interoception because it lacks the affective
  dimension,"* and the distinction between **skepticism** (unlikely given what we
  know) and **denial** (impossible) — which is recorded as a constraint on how
  any affect slot in this arena may be worded. **Not counted as support**, but the
  wording constraint is binding on Areas 56, 58, 59 and 10.
- **ORDER 852 (Clark)**, **850 (Russakovsky)**, **851 (Karpathy)**, **848
  (Turing)** — four encyclopaedic profiles of people, carrying no brain part that
  the arena does not already hold from a primary source. Turing's file is the
  most likely to be mistaken for one: it contains the **halting problem** and the
  **B-type machine** (learn from scratch rather than simulate an adult, which
  anticipates developmental AI) and the **reaction-diffusion morphogenesis**
  model. The halting problem is already in the arena via ORDER 571's
  undecidability result that tranche 30 used to convert Area 33's ceiling from
  observation into a theorem. **Not counted; the primary sources hold it.**

**The generalisable finding, which is the tranche's real product.** Encyclopaedic
entity pages are **secondary literature about a subject**, and the arena's
citation rule is designed exactly for this: *"a file's name in the arena is a
claim that you read it"* and *"three files restating one study are one source,
not three."* An entity page is the corpus's own instance of the failure mode the
rule guards against — **a well-formatted, deeply-cited, authoritative-looking
document whose citations point outward and whose content is a restatement.** The
corpus's §8 inversion is that validated code paths produce the appearance of
authority while unvalidated paths produce the content. **This tranche found the
§8 inversion inside the corpus's own citation apparatus, applied to the corpus
itself.** Third consecutive tranche in `Entities/` with no earnable evidence;
the walk is at ORDER 855, still inside the directory.

#### Post-hoc correction: the pass published 20 files and read 18

**Disclosed rather than repaired in silence.** The tranche-39 entries above were
written with "20 files" in the header, the AREA LOG line, the read→mark audit,
and the summary table's row. `arena_invariants.py` **C4** then failed with
`published {'x': 799} vs live {'x': 797, ' ': 1040}` — a delta of **−2**. The
row-level recount is the ledger's declared authority for the census
(`grep -cE '^- \[x\]' LEDGER.md`), and it returned **797**.

**The cause is a miscount in the pass's own reporting, not in the ledger.** The
ledger's 18 rows flipped this pass are verifiable individually: 830, 832, 834,
835, 836, 839, 841, 842, 845, 846, 847, 848, 849, 850, 851, 852, 853, 854 —
**18 `read_file` calls, 18 rows, EQUAL.** The number 20 was written from the
**ceiling** rather than from the **count**, and the census was derived from that
wrong number (779 + 20 = 799) rather than recounted before the table was
edited.

**Two things this pass gets right by getting the failure visible.**

1. **The binding rule worked, and it is the first pass where it is visibly
   load-bearing on a live error rather than on a hypothetical one.** The ledger
   has required since tranche 26 that *"the census is recomputed in the same
   pass as the last flip, or C4 fails."* This pass recomputed — and failed. The
   rule did not prevent the error; it **detected** it, and detected it in the
   same pass rather than one pass later, which is the whole reason it exists. A
   census recomputed on the next tick would have made 797 look like a
   two-file regression and sent a future pass hunting for rows it had lost.
2. **The compliance number the ledger exists to protect is intact.** Reads and
   marks are **equal at 18**. The rule the skill states as *"if you marked 20
   files, you made 20 `read_file` calls"* is **satisfied**; what failed was the
   arithmetic in the narrative above it. Those are different failures and
   conflating them — either by reporting 20/20 as the audit result, or by
   reporting this pass as non-compliant — would each be a false claim.

**What is corrected and what is preserved.** Corrected: the census table
(`799` → `797`, `1038` → `1040`), the tranche-39 summary row (`20` → `18`), the
AREA LOG line, and the status header. **Preserved: a paragraph in `ARENA.md`'s
status header stating that the error happened and that C4 caught it**, because
the alternative — a corrected number with no visible trace — is exactly the
"clean-looking output" this file's whole method exists to distrust. The
generalisation is the one worth carrying: **in a pass that audits its own
bookkeeping, the most likely error is in the reporting, not in the work.** The
work is checkable row by row; the report is a number typed from memory of the
ceiling. Every future pass should compute its census by recounting rows and
never by adding the pass size to the previous total.

a copy, or something else. Do not strike this citation — it is earned."*
