### Tranche 50 — ORDER 1113–1131 (19 files) + ORDER 1145 (remediation) · 20 files

**Read→mark audit: 20 `read_file` calls on corpus files, 20 rows flipped. EQUAL,
and the 20-file ceiling was RESPECTED** — the first pass since tranche 44 to
clear it, and the ledger's own tranche-48 rule (*check the running count before
starting file 21*) is what did it: 19 tranche files were planned, the 20th slot
was allocated to remediation in advance, and the pass stopped at 20. No two
consecutive ledger patches; no patch touching more than one row; no bulk read; no
script; no subagent; no shell read of corpus content. Largest single read
**55,536 chars** (ORDER 1125). No read returned `truncated: true`; no `offset`
continuation needed.

**Remediation discharged on arrival, and it was the whole first slot.**
`arena_invariants.py` reported exactly one violation on arrival:
`C6 ... Dual-Process-Cognitive-Memory -> ORDER 1145 is [ ]`. Per tranche 49's
standing instruction, ORDER 1145 was read **as its own pass, first, before the
cursor** — not folded into the tranche and not read with the answer already
written. **Verdict: it is a byte-level twin of ORDER 553**, the same DCPM report
at a second path (`memory-architecture/` vs `Cognitive-Architecture/`, infra
**C-056**). C6 now clears. **The citation was earned and the check reported a
false FAIL** — the safe direction of the C-019/C-035 hazard, and the third
instance of that hazard class working rather than a defect in the arena. **The
support counts on the three ORDER-553 corroborations were NOT incremented.** One
document published at two paths is one source, and the pass that reads both
copies is the pass most likely to double-count.

**Two areas opened, five corroborations, no re-ranks, one narrowing recorded.**
Areas **87** (performance/learning dissociation) and **88** (language-contingent
cognition). Corroborations: **Area 6** ← ORDER 1121 (Support 4→5); **Area 12** ←
ORDER 1130 (4→5, plus a narrowing); **Area 34** ← ORDER 1129 (3→4); **Area 38**
← ORDER 1122 (2→3); **Area 66** ← ORDER 1131 (2→3). No slot was re-ranked and no
grade was raised; one grade *narrowing* was recorded against Area 12's rank 1.

**The tranche's finding, and it is about the arena rather than the corpus.**
Eighty-eight areas now grade evidence, and this tranche produced the literature
that says **the grading instrument is biased in a known direction.** Bjork &
Bjork's two-strength account separates **retrieval strength** (rises fast with
contiguous re-exposure, decays) from **storage strength** (grows only through
effful reconstruction, never decays), and the measured dissociation is not subtle:
Roediger & Karpicke (2006) found restudy winning at 5 minutes and testing winning
at 2 days and 1 week, **with the restudied group reporting higher confidence at
every delay**; across studies **65–85% of participants pick the less effective
condition, and the illusion survives being shown the contradicting results.**
The arena's Support count is a count of *sources*, which is the RS measure. The
SS measure — how well a slot survives a retrieval after partial forgetting — is
not computed anywhere in this workspace, and **Cepeda et al. (2008) supply the
shape it would take** (optimal gap ≈20% of the target retention interval at short
delays, ~5% at one year, `d = 1.1` over zero-gap). This is the first time a read
has named a way the arena's *own evidence base* is measured wrong, and it is why
Area 87's rank 1 is a scheduling rule rather than a component.

**The counter-evidence, kept because it is the reason rank 2 is not rank 1.**
The desirable-difficulty literature is the most replicated in the learning
sciences **and** it reverses on its own materials: Brunmair & Richter (2019) find
`g = 0.67` for paintings and **`g = −0.39` for word lists — blocking wins there**;
Kumar et al. (2024) find pooled transfer `g = 0.59` falling to **0.43 after
outlier removal at I² = 73.6%**; Czyż et al. (2024) rated **0 of 34** motor-
learning studies "strong" quality and found **lab SMD = 0.75 vs applied SMD =
0.34 (ns)**. And Birnbaum et al. (2013) show the two difficulties are
**subadditive in the harmful direction** — interleaving wins contiguous
(`d = 0.678, p < .0001`) and the benefit **vanishes** when spacing is added
(M = .29 vs .28, ns), while *filler between exemplars impairs* learning
(`η²ₚ = .15`) with total spacing held constant. **A design rule that only holds on
the materials it was derived from is not a design rule**, and the arena now says
so at the slot.

**The second new area is a capability the arena has been assuming it has.**
ORDER 1116's replication table (§6.4) is the corpus's most useful single
artefact this pass: colour **mixed** (a 2020 registered replication failed on
the *siniy/goluboy* boundary), spatial frame **robust**, time **asymmetric**
(Mandarin vertical robust, English horizontal failed — January & Kako 2007
reported six unsuccessful replications), **number robust**, gender **fragile in
native speakers and real under artificial learning** (Elpers et al. 2022
registered replication, N = 375). The pattern the file draws is the finding:
**online-linguistically-mediated effects are fragile; symbolically-offloaded ones
are robust.** The Pirahã result (Frank et al. 2008) is that exact matching
succeeds up to ~10 items **with no memory component** and becomes approximate the
moment a delay is inserted, at chance above 3 for exact discrimination — number
words are a **technology for exact memory**, replicated in Mundurukú, Nicaraguan
Sign Language cohorts, and homesigners. **The arena's own violation is already
present**: `LEDGER.md` holds the exact count and `ARENA.md` restates it in prose.
Per R-J2 no measurement was created to test whether that restatement is
currently accurate; the rule is recorded and the check is `UNTESTED`, which is
the honest grade for it.

**Where the tranche declined to corroborate, and said so.** ORDER 1125
(`Error-Driven-Learning-Prediction-Error.md`, 539 lines, the largest read of the
pass) is the most measurement-dense file here and it earns **no arena slot and
no new area**. Its content — the TD-error ↔ dopamine-RPE isomorphism, Dabney et
al. (2020)'s quantile tiling, the Eshel et al. (2015) circuit-level subtraction —
is already covered by Areas 34, 66 and 75 through three earlier files, and this
one restates them with the same primary sources. **Counting it would have
incremented three Support counts on the strength of a fourth presentation of the
same studies**, which is the failure the one-source-per-subject rule exists to
stop. Its genuinely new material is the **dispute landscape** (§Methodological),
and the arena's existing slots already record the disputes in their own areas'
terms. Recorded here so the next pass does not re-derive the decision.

**Five files earned nothing, itemised with reasons so the census is not read as
five wasted slots.** ORDER 1113, 1115, 1117, 1119, 1126 are `index.md` directory
stubs (161 characters between them, `V-50.3`). ORDER 1128 is a **stub body with
a complete apparatus** — full frontmatter with `confidence: high`, 14 numbered
sources, 11 cross-links, and **no prose before `### Open Questions`** (`V-50.1`).
These are read, marked, and counted honestly; **none was skipped on filename
judgment**, because skipping on filename judgment is how 39 unearned citations
happened.

**Per R-J4, three disagreements are preserved rather than reconciled.** (1) The
critical period appears in the corpus in **both** the strong (hard-cutoff) and
sensitive-period (graded) forms, in the same files, unreconciled — Area 88 Rank 3
holds both and grades `LOW` deliberately. (2) The bilingual executive-function
advantage is **contested**: Bialystok et al. (2007) report a ~4-year dementia-onset
delay while Paap & Greenberg (2012) failed across 31 experiments and >1,000
participants and de Bruin et al. (2015) found the advantage disappears under
publication-bias control — the arena records the cognitive-reserve effect as the
robust half and does not average it with the executive-function half.
(3) Grammatical gender: the effect is real in **artificial** language learning and
absent in native speakers, and the arena does not resolve that into one verdict.

**Nothing was re-ranked, and that is the finding rather than an absence of one.**
The tranche's two areas are new; the five existing areas gained support without
changing order. Under the skill's rule — *never re-litigate a settled ranking
without new evidence* — the evidence that arrived was corroborative and
qualifying, not displacing. Recorded plainly: **the arena's rankings did not
move this pass, and the reason is that the new evidence agreed with them.**

### Tranche 52 (ORDER 1152–1171) — the tranche whose two new areas are about the arena itself

Twenty files: the `Memory-Architecture/` cluster (ORDER 1153–1163), four
`Memory*` directory index stubs (1152, 1164, 1165, 1167), the
`Memory-Theory/` pair (1167–1168), `Memory/Working-Memory-Update-Mechanisms.md`
(1169), and two `.meta/archive/` frontier-research syntheses (1170–1171). The
walk is the densest single-topic block the corpus has produced since the
`Learning/` cluster, and its centre of gravity is **not** the biology — it is a
set of measured results about *where a retrieval should be routed* and *what a
retrieval does to everything it did not retrieve*.

**Why this tranche is different from the last several.** Areas 85–88 each opened
on a *silence* — a term the arena had never written. Areas 93 and 94 open on
silences too, but of a different kind: they are silences about **the arena's own
operating procedure**, established by counting. `ARENA.md` held **0** occurrences
of *ranking starvation*, *Nrp*, *query patterns are write operations*, *never
retrieved*, *dark corner* across ninety-two areas that describe what to store,
how to store it, when to consolidate it, how to verify it and how to retract it.
And it held **0** occurrences of `2604.04503`, `2607.03726`, `2603.18631` or
`2608.22974` — four 2026 papers on agent memory architecture, none read, none
cited, in a file with ninety-three memory areas in it. **A retrieval system that
does not model the effect of its own retrievals, populated by literature it did
not read.** That is the finding, and it is uncomfortable enough to be worth
stating plainly rather than dressing as a new brain part.

**The two results that carried the most weight, and neither is from a
neuroscience paper.**

1. **MIA's ablation is a negative, and the negative is the interesting half.**
   From ORDER 1154's own tables: adding non-parametric memory to the **Executor**
   with no planner **decreased** multimodal average accuracy by **0.4 points**;
   feeding the *same memory* to the **Planner** instead gained **+3.5**
   multimodal and **+4.15** text-only. The paper's own sentence: *"This
   validates MIA's architectural choice of using memory as a contextual prior for
   planning rather than directly feeding it to execution."* Every other
   component in the ablation contributes too (+2.37 trained Planner, +3.23
   test-time learning, +0.43/+3.28 reflection), so this is not a single-axis
   result — but it is the **largest single gain in the table and the only
   negative one**, and the arena had no slot that distinguished which module
   receives a retrieval at all.
   *Counter-evidence, recorded not smoothed:* the Pith and EmergentMind reviews
   both warn the headline advantage "could partly come from extra rollout
   compute, plan examples, or a strong planner/router scaffold rather than the
   full bidirectional parametric/non-parametric memory loop," and disentangling
   those needs ablations the paper does not run. The slot survives because the
   **routing** claim is the one the published table *does* isolate; the broader
   bidirectional-conversion claim is not promoted on the strength of it.

2. **Plain RAG is the strongest baseline in the field, reported by the paper
   that beat it.** ORDER 1161: RAG scores 0.339 / 0.346 / 0.320 at 100K / 500K /
   1M against SelfMem's 0.504 / 0.487 / 0.454, and it does so while costing
   **$18.830 and 25,779 embedding requests** to reach 0.292 where SelfMem
   reaches 0.454 at **$2.004 with zero embedding requests**. Read carelessly
   this looks like "RAG is enough." It is not — the file's own interpretation is
   that **the bottleneck in this task family is initial retrieval quality, not
   memory architecture sophistication**, and the architecture earns its keep by
   *making retrieval better* rather than by being elaborate. The arena's
   `brain_sync` / Brain Search stack is already RAG-plus-more; this says the
   *more* has not yet paid for itself against the plain version on the one
   benchmark where both were measured. Per R-J2 this arena does not construct a
   second benchmark to find out otherwise.

**The effect-size floor, and why Area 93 is graded the way it is.** ORDER 1159's
own replication record is two-sided and the arena keeps both halves. **Rowland,
Bates & DeLosh (2014, *Front. Psychol.* 5:584)** — a deliberately high-powered
replication — found RIF cleanly in the traditional paradigm in both an
undergraduate and a Mechanical Turk sample, and **failed** to find it under the
Anderson–Spellman independent-cue procedure in Experiment 3. That is the
contested front: Camp et al. (2007) argue apparent cue-independence is residual
cue overlap; Murayama et al.'s meta-analysis supports a real overall cost;
strength independence is the best-supported of the four criteria, because
forgetting and facilitation can double-dissociate. **And the narrowing that
matters more than any of it:** Area 6 already holds a *larger and older*
measurement of the same effect — Basden et al. (2014) N = 288 null; Huettl et al.
(2021) preregistered N = 630 at **d ≈ 0.15–0.20**; Depret, Erlbaum & Eerland
(2020) 105 experiments / 39,000+ participants at **d = 0.31** uncorrected and
**~0.15** with publication bias corrected, against a published 0.47–0.65. So the
honest statement is not "RIF is robust" but **"RIF is real, fragile, and roughly a
third of its published size once you look for it."** Area 93 inherits that floor
rather than re-deriving a friendlier one.

**The compound prediction, which neither RIF nor misinformation literature makes
alone.** ORDER 1159 says retrieval suppresses competitors. ORDER 1155 says
retrieval opens a reconsolidation window into which post-event information
physically enters — Hupbach et al. (2007) found a *subtle reminder* before new
learning caused List-2 items to intrude into List-1 recall 24 hours later,
selectively for the reactivated memory, and **reactivation without a reminder
produced no intrusions**. **Together: a retrieval event both admits new
information and makes the un-retrieved unreachable, simultaneously.** For a
read-then-write agent — which is every consolidation pass, every dedup job, every
summarisation — the most dangerous moment for a record is the moment it is being
updated. ORDER 1155 states the design resolution and it is the same one the
arena's own rules encode: **gate the writes** (provenance, conflict checks,
immutable raw capture) and **do not deny lability**, because lability is the only
path by which a correction ever lands. Its own §"Tension 1" calls the dilemma
plainly and does not pretend it is soluble.

**Belief is not recollection, and the gap is instrument-dependent.** From ORDER
1155: a systematic review (Brewin & Andrews 2017) finds **~47% of implantation
participants show some recollective experience** but only **~15% plausibly hold
full memories**; the preregistered Murphy et al. (2023) replication reports
**35%**; the single-lab Shaw & Porter (2015) crime study claims **70%** and drew
a direct commentary challenging its criteria, with the authors themselves
conceding a single-interviewer design, a mid-study taxonomy switch, and inability
to exclude lingering demand characteristics. The file's own conclusion — *the
spread tracks coding rubrics more than populations* — is the design-relevant
part: **any percentage for this phenomenon is conditional on its coding scheme**,
and ORDER 1166's competing figures (~25% mall / ~50% dramatic) are the same
phenomenon under a different rubric. Both are recorded at `V-51.5`; neither is
averaged. The one genuinely encouraging result: **Oeberst et al. (2021, *PNAS*
118:e2026447118) reversed rich false memories** in humans, with personalized
error-feedback outperforming source-sensitization — and the open question that
keeps this `LOW` rather than higher is whether reversal generalises to naturally
acquired false beliefs that were never marked as suspect, which is exactly the
case an agent is in.

**OaK's function-module ablation is the same shape as MIA's, one paper later.**
ORDER 1156: removing the typed function layer entirely and letting the model
reason over the full graph drops CRMArenaPro from **78.38% to ~35%** on
DeepSeek-v4-flash; removing only function *composition* drops TravelPlanner from
**55.90% to ~30%**. **Graph access is not a substitute for schema-adapted
procedures.** The corpus's version of "a substrate handed to the wrong module is
worse than no substrate," and it arrives independently of MIA's result, from a
different lab, on a different benchmark, with a different mechanism (typed
composition vs. role routing). That is two independent implementations moving the
same variable, which is the arena's own bar for raising a grade — **and it is
still not raised to `HIGH`**, because both benchmarks are closed-world with
ground-truth answers and ORDER 1156's own open question asks what happens on
open-ended tasks with no objective quality metric and does not answer it.

**Sleep replay: the causal half is established and the arena's half is not.**
ORDER 1163 supplies what ORDER 1144 only implied — **Jadhav et al. (2012,
*Science* 336:1454–1458)** optogenetically disabled sharp-wave ripples during
post-learning sleep and spatial memory consolidation **impaired**. But the same
file's §"Tension" records the limit: *it is not established that sequential replay
is the causal agent rather than general ripple-associated plasticity*, because
disrupting sequential structure while preserving the oscillation has not been
achieved, and *"the sequential nature of replay may be epiphenomenal rather than
causal."* **This area's rank 1 is a consolidation pass that replays.** Three
further items recorded: the **ripple–spindle coupling chain** (slow oscillations
<1 Hz as master clock, spindles 10–15 Hz nested in their up states, ripples in
the hippocampus — the *coupling* is the proposed mechanism, which means a
consolidation design has a timing requirement the arena has never stated);
**targeted memory reactivation** works in humans via sensory cues re-presented
during SWS, i.e. *cue-gated* rather than time-gated consolidation, which is
cheaper than anything in rank 1; and the **standard model vs. multiple trace
theory** dispute (Squire & Alvarez 1995 vs. Nadel & Moscovitch 1997) is live and
the arena holds neither side. Left explicitly `not observed`: what determines
*which* experience is replayed, and whether replay prunes as well as stabilises.

**SIMPLE needs no decay parameter, and that is a narrowing, not a refutation.**
ORDER 1168 is the most formally useful file in the tranche. Ecker &
Lewandowsky (2012) name three modelling victories for interference over decay,
and the first is decisive: **SIMPLE (Brown, Neath & Chater 2007) reproduces
serial-position curves, primacy/recency, long-term recency, the Brown–Peterson
data and time-scale invariance with no decay parameter at all** — items sit on a
log-transformed temporal dimension and lose accessibility purely through local
distinctiveness (neighbours in psychological time), which also explains why
edge items (first/last) have fewer neighbours and so survive. **Consequence for
Area 6: an area that justifies eviction by "things fade" is using a mechanism the
corpus's best-fitting model does not contain.** But the file is pluralist and
says so: **TBRS\*-I fits the full dataset only with both** decay and
interference, over millions of simulations across seven factors, and Wixted
(2004) holds that the curve's shape alone cannot arbitrate. The one number that
decides a design regardless of which side wins: **distractor variability switches
forgetting on and off** in complex-span work — constant distractors produce almost
none, variable distractors produce massive loss — and **no decay model accounts
for that pattern.** A consolidation pass therefore needs an *interference*
trigger, not a clock. That is Area 93 rank 3's premise, earned here.

**A `UNSUCCESSFUL` recorded against Area 87.** ORDER 1169 settles the
working-memory-training literature and the settlement is against far transfer:
**Au et al. (2015)** and **Simons et al. (2016)** found little to no far transfer
in meta-analysis; near transfer (untrained n-back variants) is reliably present;
and a 2022 mediation study across **three RCTs, 460 participants** found the
apparent far transfer to Matrix Reasoning was **fully mediated** by near transfer
with **no direct intervention effect**. The bearing on Area 87 rank 1 is narrow
and worth stating exactly: rank 1 says *space and interleave the review*; this
says **spacing a review of material the system cannot yet perform will transfer
to that performance and no further** — a schedule that measures success by
re-running the task is measuring precisely the quantity that transfers. Recorded
as `UNSUCCESSFUL` in the first-class sense so it is not rebuilt blind. Two items
from the same file recorded for their measurement content rather than as
corroboration: the **n-back construct-validity problem** (strong face validity,
weak-to-modest convergent validity with other WM measures), and the clean
pharmacological dissociation that makes the mechanism separable at all —
**tolcapone (cortical dopamine, N = 49) improved maintenance and did nothing for
gating; sulpiride (striatal D2, N = 34) altered output gating specifically.** The
arena's word "update" bundles two operations with different receptors, different
timescales and different failure modes.

**A narrowing against Area 90 that the arena had been carrying the wrong end of.**
ORDER 1157 is a **fragment** (V-51.2) but what it carries is the
separation/completion **balance table**, and it inverts this area's implicit
failure mode. The arena treats separation as the primitive; the corpus says the
balance is **state-dependent, not fixed by anatomy** — ACh high → DG sparseness
high, CA3 suppressed, **separation dominates**; ACh low at retrieval → CA3 active,
**completion dominates**; **stress and glucocorticoids reduce DG neurogenesis and
sparseness, biasing toward completion and overgeneralization** (Epp et al. 2015).
So the degradation mode is not "fails to separate" but **"over-separates into
over-generalization."** Two challenges recorded, both narrowing rank 1: the
**DG/CA3 dichotomy is a gradient, not a binary** (CA3 also separates under high
interference, DG also completes from partial cues, CA1 also separates), and the
**"small world" assumption may be wrong** — CA3 connectivity is more modular than
the classic single-attractor picture assumes (Blanco-Ferrera et al. 2020). And a
measurement bound: **fMRI cannot resolve DG from CA3** (both ~1–2 mm, confounded
with subiculum), and intracranial recordings give different results in some cases.

**Scene construction, added to Area 92 as a third theory in rank 3's dispute.**
ORDER 1160 holds Hassabis & Maguire (2007) — the hippocampus as a **spatial-scene
generator**, not a memory store. The patient evidence is the sharp part:
bilateral hippocampal damage leaves object recognition and semantic knowledge
intact while imagined scenes return as **disconnected fragments**, and the **P01
anomaly** (~50% bilateral volume loss, dense amnesia, *preserved* scene
construction) is read as scene construction being **necessary but not sufficient**
for episodic memory. **The Squire critique is the strongest form of Area 92 rank
3's position** — Squire et al. (2010) and Kim et al. (2015) found hippocampal
patients *normal* on scene construction and boundary extension while severely
impaired on memory, attributing the spatial performance to intact working memory
and parietal cortex. And the file offers the reconciliation rank 1 needs: the
**relational-intensity hypothesis** — scenes are simply the *most demanding*
relational task, so SCT and Cohen & Eichenbaum's relational theory are degrees of
one thing. Recorded, not resolved. **No grade moved**, for the reason Area 92
already records and this file extends: no episodic-foresight instrument verifies
a simulation against an outcome, spatial-coherence coding is subjective and
varies across studies, and SCT's own paradigm relies on verbal report — which
confounds language ability and is Area 88's territory. **The file carries three
defects of its own** (V-51.3): an orphaned YAML fragment at line 35, in-text
bracket numbers that do not match its own Sources list, and unresolvable path
prefixes in its `Related` block. A document this area is about to cite, failing
in three ways, is the §8 inversion appearing inside the evidence base.

**The snowball, and the arena's own pipeline.** ORDER 1170 and 1171 (read as
separate files on overlapping primaries; counted once) supply the sharpest
agent-relevant number in the tranche. Hallucinations injected at stage 1 of a
sequential multi-agent pipeline do not merely persist — they **transform**, and
**detectability degrades near-irreversibly at each step: only 4% are catchable at
the S1→S2 handoff, and 89.3% have escaped by S3→S4**, because the information
required to verify the original claim is *structurally destroyed* by the upstream
transformations. Containment: **boundary gates at handoffs cut survival from
58.4% to 16.2%** (42.2 pp, h = −0.911, p < 0.00001) versus end-checking, and the
file's conclusion is **propagation control, not detection.** **This workspace is
such a pipeline** — read, mark, absorb, write — and the arena's §8 inversion (a
document with correct apparatus carrying invented content) is not a folk warning
but a *measured property of chained transformation*. Also carried: the network
stress test (**Jaccard 0.028** on Roget's Thesaurus, **>94%** source mismatch,
independently reproduced by ORDER 1171 with citation omission at 91.9%), and the
**inverse parametric-knowledge effect** from the FAOS deployment (1,800 runs, 5
industries, 3 LLMs) — grounding value is **inversely proportional to
training-data coverage**, Vietnamese domains gaining 2× over English
(Δ = +.29 vs +.12), replicating across all three models. That last one is the
most encouraging result in the tranche for a system whose corpus is 14,589 files
of domain material: **the more obscure the domain, the more a knowledge layer
pays.** Recorded with its caveat — the file is a synthesis of 50+ papers of which
its own quality table marks ~35 as arXiv preprints, not peer-reviewed.

**ORDER 1158 was read whole and deliberately counted zero times.** It restates
the MIA, SelfMem and D-Mem primaries that ORDER 1154, 1156 and 1161 carry
independently, and per the support rule three files restating three papers is
three sources, not six. It is also the file with `SECTION_END` and
`echo "Exit: $?"` sitting in its own body at lines 239–240 (V-51.7) — shell text
captured into the artifact, which is the §8 pattern in its purest form: the
generation path is visible in the output. **Read, marked, absorbed, not counted.**

**Ledger arithmetic, and a stale summary found and corrected.** The summary table
in `LEDGER.md` read `1028 [x] / 767 remaining` on arrival while the row-level
count was `1047 [x] / 748 remaining` — the tranche-51 pass flipped its rows but
did not update the hand-maintained totals. Measured at this pass's close:
**1067 `[x]` · 421 `[-]` · 1 `[!]` · 728 `[ ]` = 2,217.** The gap was arithmetic
drift in the summary, **not lost marks**; the row-level marks were and are
correct, and the discrepancy was resolved by measurement rather than by
incrementation, which is what the table's own F2-6 caption demands.

**Twins walked in passing.** ORDER 1151 (`memory-architecture/index.md`) and
ORDER 1152 (`Memory-Architecture/index.md`) are a case-variant basename
collision — the same shape as ORDER 1142/1143 in tranche 51, and the reason
`citation_remediation.py` reports **446 corpus basenames published at more than
one row**. The 1152 file is a 22-line index listing **3 of its 11 siblings**, a
second instance of the partial-index defect class. Neither path is cited in the
arena, deliberately: a bare `index.md` token would resolve to an excluded row.

**Standing caveat, restated because it applies with unusual force to this
tranche.** Six of the twenty files are stubs or fragments (1152, 1157, 1164,
1165, 1167 stubs/fragments; 1158 carrying shell text in its body) and two
(1170, 1171) are generated research syntheses rather than primary sources. **The
two areas opened this pass rest substantially on those two syntheses and on
files with known defects.** That is recorded rather than hidden: Area 94's ranks 2
and 3 are graded `LOW` partly because the underlying benchmarks are narrow, and
Area 93's rank 1 is `UNTESTED` on the design. Per the skill's closing finding —
*the validated code path produces the appearance of authority, and the
unvalidated path produces the content* — **the arena's own corpus is the
strongest available demonstration of the failure mode the arena exists to
prevent**, and the two new areas are the first slots written by a pass that named
it.

### Tranche 53 — zero files read, and the twenty marks that had to be undone

**Pass type:** tranche, aborted by instrument failure. **Remediation queue was
empty on arrival** (`citation_remediation.py`: 0 PROVEN, 0 MUST RE-READ,
0 MUST STRIKE) — this was a normal tranche until the first `read_file`.

**Read→mark: 20 `read_file` calls, 0 successful reads, 0 rows legitimately
flipped. NOT COMPLIANT, and the non-compliance is stated rather than papered
over.** The 20 rows the pass flipped were flipped to `[!] blocked` on the
strength of `File not found` — which turned out to be false in all 20 cases.
**All 20 were reverted before the run ended.** Final census `1067 [x] /
421 [-] / 1 [!] / 728 [ ]` = 2,217, identical to the state on arrival.

**Root cause.** The skill's §2 workspace table gives the corpus root as
`/home/operator/.autognosia/`. That path does not exist. The corpus is at
`/home/operator/.hermes/` — the value the cron job prompt supplies and the value
every prior tranche used in practice. The skill and its own job prompt disagree,
and the skill is wrong.

**This defect is four passes old, and that is the more important fact.** The
ad-hoc verification of this pass's own record caught it: `ARENA.md` lines 185–190
and `VERIFICATION.md` `V-38.1`/`V-45.1` already document it, and tranches 44/45
state explicitly that they *avoided* it by building paths from `~/.hermes/`.
**A pass that had read `V-45.1` before issuing its first `read_file` — it was
one entry up in the file — would not have made twenty failed calls.** The
knowledge was in the repository the whole time; only the reading order was
wrong, and a fresh context window plus an authoritative-looking skill document
is exactly what produces that failure. The first draft of this entry claimed the
defect as a discovery and C-058 as "the most consequential defect class found so
far"; both claims were false on the evidence already in the workspace, and both
have been corrected. Full defect record: **C-058** in `ARENA-INFRA.md`.

**What made it survivable.** One habit, not a rule: after the third consecutive
miss the pass stopped trusting the error string and ran `ls` on the parent
directory instead. That check is the only reason 20 false permanent blocks did
not land in the ledger. It is exactly the kind of unscripted, unmandated
verification that C-058 argues must become a rule — the pass that most needed it
was the pass with no instruction to do it.

**What the pass did *not* do.** It did not read a single corpus file, so it has
nothing to contribute to any area, no slot to update, no grade to move, and no
corroboration to count. `ARENA.md` is untouched. There is no design claim in this
pass, and none is manufactured to fill the space.

**Cost of the abort:** one 13-minute slot, zero of the 728 remaining rows
advanced. The next pass starts at ORDER 1172 unchanged.

### Tranche 54 — ORDER 1172–1191 (20 files). One qualification, no new area, no re-rank, no grade change.

**All twenty files are `frontier-research-ontology-*` synthesised rounds** — six
`archive/` update files and fourteen `archive/ontology-rounds/roundNN-*` files,
rounds 24–41 plus the September and (future-dated) 2026-11-15 comprehensive
updates. Per the skill's rule that **three files restating one study are one
source**, none of the twenty increments an independent-source count anywhere in
the arena. They are the same class as the `frontier-research-*` cluster tranche 47
already recorded as *"the most useful negative in the tranche"* — successive
rounds restating one another, where the accumulated ontology machinery is not
validated end-to-end. **The walk cleared that cluster for the seventh
consecutive tranche and directory order, not corpus thinness, set this one's
yield.** Cursor moved 1172 → 1192.

**The one result that changed the answer, and it is a negative.** ORDER 1185
carries **GraphRAG-Bench** (ICLR 2026), a benchmark of existing retrievers. Its
finding: **graph-based retrieval frequently underperforms plain vector RAG, and
graph construction consumes the majority of the retrieval budget.** This lands
directly on **Area 8's structural premise** — the area whose rank-1 design is a
typed, verified structure compiled from retrieved text, and whose three prior
supports (ORDER 996, 1021, 420) all argue the structure is worth building.

Recorded as a **qualification in Area 8's grade field, Support held at 7**, on
three grounds stated so a later pass can disagree with any of them:

1. **It is not a trial of Area 8's design.** A benchmark of shipped retrievers
   cannot confirm or refute an untested design; it constrains the *premise* that
   structure helps. Per the skill's own grading rule this is `benchmark-suspect`
   adjacent — a measurement nobody has acted on is not a reason to promote a

### What the tranche was worth

**One area opened (Area 95), one corroboration (Area 12), zero re-ranks, zero
grade changes, and three `VERIFICATION.md` findings.**

This is the **fourth consecutive tranche** consisting entirely of
`frontier-research-ontology-round*` synthesised files (1172–1191, then
1192–1211), and the discipline from those tranches was applied unchanged: **a
named system in a round file is not a corroborating source when the arena
already holds the parent mechanism.** Nineteen of twenty files fell under that
rule. The one that broke it is the reason the mission is a read and not a
search.

**ORDER 1211 (`round60-2026-10-20.md`, 375 lines) — the file that earned Area
95.** Its §1 reports **Memory Reward Inflation in Self-Improving LLM Agents**
(Asadolahi, Amini, Talebi, Farhadi, Zamanifar, arXiv 2608.00017), and the
mechanism is one the arena held **nothing** on:

> In deployment, ground-truth labels are unavailable, so the stored reward is at
> best an LLM self-assessment. Incorrect episodes receive inflated rewards; the
> agent preferentially reuses **the very mistakes it is most confident in**.
> Because the error compounds through memory rather than averaging out, and the
> confirming judge's errors remain correlated with the original self-grading
> bias, **it cannot identify which memories are overvalued.**

The formal content is what made it an area rather than a caution. The loop is
`store → self-grade → retrieve → trust → write back`, and four named
amplifiers sit in it: self-grade inflation, **trust amplification** (planner
weights high-scored memories at A_tr > 1), **retrieval amplification**
(similarity retrieval surfaces memories similar to successes even when wrong,
κ > 0), and compounding write-back. **Theorem 1** — inflation compounds
*multiplicatively*, not additively. **Theorem 2** — the corrupted attractor is
analytically predictable from independently measured parameters, **p\* = 0.45
predicted against 0.42 observed**.

**The requirement it yields is a condition on a signal, not a better model.**
The **Error Independence Assumption (EIA)**: a de-inflation signal is valid only
if it tracks truth *and* does not echo the self-grade bias. **An LLM judge fails
EIA** — its errors correlate with the original grader's. The shipped correction
is **LUCID** (Label-free Utility Correction via Independent De-inflation) using
answer-free signals only: execution/engine feedback, cross-episode logical
consistency, structural validation. On BIRD text-to-SQL, naive self-graded
memory **54.0%** execution accuracy → LUCID **56.9%** (+2.9 pts), closing most of
the gap to the oracle upper bound.

**Why this is a brain part and not a fourth facet of Areas 24 or 33.** Area 24
asks whether an instrument is faithful. Area 33 asks what class of claim a
detector can support even when it is faithful. This is one level up the loop and
one question earlier in time, and the organ is the **teacher signal's
independence from the action policy** — a genuine prediction error requires a
signal carrying information the policy does not already have. A self-grader does
not supply a weaker teacher signal; it supplies none.

**And the arena is exposed to this by construction.** Areas 6, 12, 23, 30 and 94
all write to memory, and in all five the grader and the graded are the same
system. `verify_reads.py` and `arena_invariants.py` are the same shape — they
read an artefact produced by the same process whose reads they are counting. Area
33 Rank 1 already said *a detector is not a certifier*; Area 95 says a
**self-detector is not even a detector, and the bias compounds multiplicatively.**
That is why this is a new area and not a note appended to Area 33.

**The corroboration that earns its place, from the opposite direction — ORDER
1207 (`round56-2026-09-05.md`, 477 lines) §1, Semantic Training Gap (arXiv
2605.11234).** A manufacturing agent meets `TT-4201`, `%IW64` and
`ReflowZone4` — three designators for one physical sensor — and treats them as
three data points, because it has statistical fluency without operational
semantics. The failure is *linguistically precise and operationally wrong*. In a
multi-agent configuration it becomes **semantic drift**: each agent embeds its own
interpretation, they diverge, **neither detects the mismatch because both outputs
are linguistically coherent**, and the error compounds down the chain. Support
**1 → 2** for Area 95 Rank 1, and the second source is a genuinely different
failure (entity resolution *across* agents) arriving at the same requirement (a
check the system cannot perform on itself).

### The disagreement, preserved and not resolved (R-J4)

ORDER 1211 makes the **self-grading** property load-bearing. ORDER 1193
(`round43-2026-09-09.md` §2, KBevo, arXiv 2608.26386, COLM 2026) cuts the other
way: **outcome-based reward driving joint KB-and-reasoning improvement** —
grounding 48% → 55%, reasoning correctness 45% → 55% — with **no
de-corroboration step of any kind**, and an ablation showing reasoning
optimisation alone cannot compensate for a weak KB while a strong fixed KB can
match co-evolution.

On KBevo's reading, grounding the score in an **external outcome** rather than
in the model's own judgement is sufficient, and Rank 1's independence
requirement is stronger than the corpus warrants. **Both positions are recorded.
Neither is averaged.** What survives the disagreement is the narrower claim the
area actually rests on, and it holds on **both** readings: *a score generated by
the same process being scored cannot detect that process's errors.*

#### Area 96 — the substrate as a budget, and exhaustion has an order (ORDER 1231)

The first non-catalogue file in three tranches, and the first from a corpus directory the arena had no occurrence of. `ARENA.md` held 0 occurrences of *metabolic triage*, *degradation order*, *ketone*, *substrate exhaustion*; the only *glucose* hits were incidental (an energy aside in the default-mode-network area at line 6302, a human-cost aside at 4594).

The distinction that earns the area rather than an extension of Area 82: **Area 82 is a gate, this is an order.** McNay & Gold (2002) give the double dissociation — moderate hypoglycaemia (plasma glucose ~3.0 mM) impairs hippocampal-dependent memory formation while leaving hippocampal-independent memory intact — and the file states the ordering and its cause: complex executive function first, attention and working memory next, simple motor function preserved longest, **mirroring per-gram metabolic rate**. That is the load-bearing clause, because it means **vulnerability tracks energy intensity, not importance**, which inverts the arena's implicit assumption that the most important function is the one to protect.

**The qualification is carried in the slot, not dropped.** The file's own §"Individual Differences in Metabolic Cognitive Vulnerability" records the order is *not* uniform: diabetes (impaired counter-regulation, "hypoglycemia unawareness"), aging (reduced metabolic flexibility, decreased ketone utilisation), genetic variation in GLUT1/GLUT3, and prior hypoglycaemic episodes (downregulation of counter-regulatory responses) all move it. A single global order is therefore a first approximation the source already qualifies. Rank 1 is graded `LOW` on the human mechanism for the same reason — the animal literature replicates the hierarchy, the transfer to a symbolic system is established nowhere, and per §8 a well-replicated mechanism in the wrong substrate is not a `HIGH` grade for a design.

**Rank 3 is the tranche's `UNSUCCESSFUL` slot and the reason this file was worth 21 reads.** The fasting→ketone→BDNF→neurogenesis→scheduled-consolidation-window analogy is the single most attractive design the file offers, and the corpus records its own refutation: **Martin et al. (2006) found no significant cognitive differences between continuous caloric restriction and control in a large randomised trial.** The positive human results are real and small — Mattson et al. (2006) verbal memory in older adults over three months; Witte et al. (2009) +20% verbal memory over three months of caloric restriction in healthy elderly — and the file's own summary is that *the field is limited by small sample sizes, short durations, and difficulty controlling for confounding variables (sleep, hydration, caffeine)*. **The design is already deployed** (this job's own `RUNLOG.jsonl` consolidation, `brain_sync` cron, the archival session-export cron), which makes the finding operationally important in a way most `UNSUCCESSFUL` slots are not: the schedule must be kept on operational grounds and **may not be cited as physiological support** by Areas 6 or 23.

**Preserved disagreement, unresolved (R-J4).** ORDER 1231 §"Evidence and Controversy" records a live dispute about the mechanism Area 82 Rank 1 leans on. **Dienel (2012)** argues lactate accumulation during brain activation is a minor fraction of glucose metabolised, that stimulated glycolysis is not exclusive to astrocytes, and that lactate is *"an opportunistic glucose-sparing substrate when present in high concentrations"* rather than a primary fuel. **Pellerin & Magistretti (2012)** hold the shuttle as load-bearing. The file's own resolution — both cell types glycolyse, astrocytes preferentially, neurons preferentially oxidative — is **recorded as consensus and is a finding of neither paper.** Both sides entered; neither averaged. This qualifies Area 82's evidence base without demoting its slot, and it is filed here rather than as a rank change because Area 82's grade was already `LOW` for a different and unaffected reason (its own effect sizes, 10–30% LTP changes).

#### Area 97 — the memory architecture as the plastic variable (ORDER 1230 §1, MemEvolve)

**The brain-part naming in this area is the arena's mapping, not the file's claim, and the slot says so.** The file supplies a mechanism, a codebase and a measurement; it names no anatomy. The mapping is to **experience-expectant architecture** plus metaplasticity one level up — Area 66 makes the *learning rate* a function of recent activity, this makes the *architecture* one. `ARENA.md` held 0 occurrences of `MemEvolve`, `2512.18746`, *bilevel*, *Encode/Store/Retrieve/Manage*, *experience-expectant*.

The measured numbers: **+17.06%** over SmolAgent and Flash-Searcher, with **2.0–9.09%** transfer to unseen benchmarks and backbones. The grade is `LOW` and not `HIGH` for two reasons the file itself supplies, in its own `UNCERTAINTIES` and `CONFLICTS` blocks: **broader generalisation untested** beyond four benchmarks, and hand-designed systems have **interpretability and control advantages that were not measured**. That second one is the trade this arena cares about most, and it is why rank 1 is also flagged *against the workspace's own checkers* — `arena_invariants.py`, `verify_reads.py` and `citation_remediation.py` all assume a **fixed** ledger schema and a fixed slot format, and an evolved memory architecture is unverifiable by a checker written against the previous schema. That is Area 33's detector/certifier asymmetry arriving as an engineering constraint rather than as an epistemic caution.

**Rank 3 is the finding the tranche actually needed, and it is deliberately not a measurement proposal.** Area 62 Rank 3 recorded the arena's `"earlier tranches were right"` constraint as a silent self-reinforcing loop. MemEvolve supplies the only construction in ninety-seven areas that can distinguish an architecture which has **stopped improving** from one that is improving slowly: outer-loop selection on held-out tasks. Applied here, the fixed inner loop is the seven-slot format, the four ledger marks, the read→mark loop and the three-slot rule, and the holdout is a set of tasks the method has not seen. **Per R-J2 this slot creates no self-measurement** — it records the absence of a holdout, and proposes no experiment. A saturated method and a working method produce identical ledgers, identical arena files and identical PASS verdicts.

#### Corroboration 1 — Area 12, Support 6 → 7 (ORDER 1229 §1, Procedural Graphs, arXiv 2609.09153)

Independent: a Google Research paper on an explicit editable graph of procedures, arriving from the procedural-graph literature, citing neither ImplicitMemBench (arXiv 2604.08064) nor the Experience Compression Spectrum (arXiv 2604.15877).

Two results earn the increment, and one of them **narrows the area rather than reinforcing it.** The self-evolution loop is gated and keeps its rejections: diagnostic rollout → feedback-driven mutation → **validation gate** (`val(G_cand) ≥ val(G_retained)`, adopt only on non-regression) → **rejection memory**, where rejected candidates are retained as negative constraints. The second result is the narrowing: a **static expert PG matches or surpasses hand-designed graphs**, and a **self-evolved one matches or exceeds the expert PG**. The area's current reading leans on the `curated +16.2pp vs self-generated +0.0pp` result (tranche 55, ORDER 1194), and this says curation is not privileged for *procedural graph structure specifically* — the two are compatible only if curation matters for skill content and not for procedure topology. Recorded as a narrowing; the grade stays `LOW` because this is a benchmark of a procedure store, not a trial of proceduralization.

**Two design requirements earned, both cutting against existing slots.** First, the validation gate must read a **held-out** score: a candidate procedure adopted because the model that wrote it also judged it is exactly the self-graded shape Area 95 shows compounding, and ORDER 1229's gate is the arena's first *working instance of the independence requirement*. Second, the **soft-constraint** design — a guidance model reads the surrounding subgraph and translates edge attributes into step-level natural language that **biases the solver's next action without dictating it** — is the first source in this arena to separate a procedure which **guides** from one which **compels**, which is the distinction Areas 4 and 12 both need and neither states.

#### Corroboration 2 — Area 8, reach only, no increment (ORDER 1230 §5, Hallucination Snowball)

**The one-source rule applied against incrementing.** ORDER 1170 already supplies arXiv 2608.14588; ORDER 1230 restates it. Reach confirmed, Support unchanged. What the re-read adds is the **quantitative chain** the arena's earlier version lacked: per-boundary escape probabilities **24.6% (Raw Fact → Derived), 48.3% (Derived → Narrative), 89.3% (Narrative → Invisible)**, over **346 injected hallucinations** in a 4-agent financial pipeline on FinanceBench; GPT-4o detection **72.0% → 50.9%** across the stages; **23.7% survive completely undetected**; boundary gates cut survival **58.4% → 16.2%** (42.2 pp, Cohen's h = −0.911, p < 0.000001) against **2.3 pp** for end-of-pipeline checking.

**A ceiling the arena did not hold:** the strongest model tested (Qwen3.5-397B, 87.0% at Stage 1) projects only **60–65%** Stage-4 detection. The snowball is therefore **not a detector-quality problem**, and the arena's instinct — build a better verifier — is refuted by a number rather than by an argument. The file's own prescription is stated as a generality: **"when you verify matters more than whether you verify"**, with the resource corollary explicit (invest at Stage 1, where 75.4% are still catchable). Recorded limitation, from the file: the Markov model **assumes a linear pipeline** and branching/parallel topologies are unmodelled — which is the shape of every multi-agent design in this arena.

### The shape of the tranche, and why it matters

**Three of the four new areas are about how this arena reads itself rather than about a mechanism it lacks.** That is the second tranche in a row with this shape (tranche 44 opened Areas 74–76, two of which were aimed at the answer file's own prose), and the second occurrence is what makes it a pattern rather than a coincidence. The reason is visible in what was read: **the corpus's entire `Metacognition/` directory — ten files, read in full this pass — is a literature about the reliability of self-report, and it happens to live inside a document whose method is self-report.** Area 98 (nothing consumes what the arena reads), Area 99 (the aggregation convention can manufacture a finding), and Area 100 (the reference class is accumulating unused in `RUNLOG.jsonl`) were not reachable from the mechanism side. They were reachable because the read reached the literature that describes them.

**This is a caution about the discovery rate.** An area count that is partly a function of what the corpus happens to be about will inflate in any directory that discusses epistemic hygiene and deflate in one that does not. The defence is that each area names a **brain part** with a neuroscience citation and a mechanism, and a self-help book would fail that test — but the pattern is recorded because a future pass that opens five areas in a row should ask whether it is reading or being read at.

### Area 98 — monitoring and control are two systems (ORDER 1240, 1241)

**What the file establishes.** Nelson & Narens (1990) split cognition into object level and meta level, and the load-bearing result is the **dissociation**, in both directions. Four pieces of evidence, from four different paradigms: Nelson & Leonesio (1988) *labor-in-vain* — accurate judgments of difficulty, effort spent anyway, insufficient to compensate; Kornell & Metcalfe (2006) — with already-learned items removed, learners restudy the items they judge **most** learned, the opposite of discrepancy reduction's prediction, which means control is a rate-of-return calculation and not "fix what monitoring says is broken"; Maniscalco & Lau (2012, 2014) — **meta-d′/d′ can be selectively impaired while d′ is preserved**; Paulus et al. (2013) and Balcomb & Gerken (2008) — implicit monitoring present in 3.5-year-olds whose explicit confidence judgments do not discriminate; and Fleming & Lau (2014) — rlPFC/anterior PFC for monitoring against lateral PFC for control, anatomically separate.

**Why it ranks 1 for this arena specifically.** The arena *is* a monitoring organ with no control path. `RUNLOG.jsonl` records `duration_seconds`, `order_numbers_read`, `invariants` verdicts and `read_file` counts; `ARENA.md` records ranks; **nothing in the stack reads the first and changes the second.** The corpus's own summary of the failure — *"a system with perfect monitoring sensitivity but zero monitoring-control coupling would be a perfect observer but a helpless agent"* — is the arena's condition stated by a source that did not know the arena existed.

**The thing that nearly displaced it, and did not.** Rank 2 as first written was the **coupling measurement** (Koriat, Ma'ayan & Nussinson 2006: monitoring and control correlate without monitoring causing control, because both draw on the same cues), on the argument that measuring the halves is worthless if the link is an artifact. It was ranked 2 rather than 1 because the arena has no coupling to measure — the field separation is a precondition for the measurement being meaningful, and a pass that cannot yet measure cannot be told to measure better. **Recorded rather than discarded**, because a later pass that finds a real coupling would need it.

**Grades: `UNTESTED` on the design, `HIGH` on the dissociation, Support 2.** The cap is stated on the slot: the evidence is human and the transfer to a symbolic system is established nowhere in this corpus. The two sources are genuinely independent — ORDER 1240 from the control side (ABR, RPL, study-time allocation), ORDER 1241 from the measurement side (SDT construction, HMeta-d, domain specificity) — and they meet on the McIntosh et al. result, which used the monitoring/control instrument to *refute* the double-burden account. That is the strongest available demonstration that the two can be pulled apart: a null where the prediction was a difference.

### Area 99 — the pattern replicated, the explanation did not, and one replication used noise (ORDER 1236)

**The file's own summary is the area.** Five independent statistical accounts — Krueger & Mueller (2002) regression plus better-than-average; Magnus & Peresetsky (2022) censored Tobit on bounded scales, N = 665, near-perfect fit; Nuhfer et al. (2016) **the canonical graph regenerated from random numbers**; Gignac & Zajenkowski (2020) heteroskedasticity and individual-level quadratic regression; Jansen, Rafferty & Griffiths (2021) Bayesian updating under optimistic priors — each reproduce the Dunning-Kruger figure from premises containing no claim about the unskilled being unaware. The file's conclusion: the debate has moved from *does the pattern exist* (yes) to *what does the pattern mean* (contested), and the statistical accounts "collectively explain more variance with fewer theoretical assumptions."

**Read against this arena, it is not a footnote.** The arena ranks by top-three-per-area and invites comparison across areas. That is a quartile-style aggregate operation on bounded 0–3 scores, and the corpus's mechanism applies with the sign reversed: selecting on extreme values of *x* and plotting *y* guarantees a crossing whenever *r* < 1, and the literature's *r* is **.19–.35**. Nuhfer's finding is that the *graphical convention* — `(y − x)` against *x`, quantile-aggregated line charts — **creates** the nonlinearity, and that the valid conventions are individual scatterplots with best-fit lines.

**The honest reading of that for the arena is two-sided, and both halves are on the slot.** The saving fact: this arena reads **individual files one at a time**, which is the individual-data condition both Nuhfer and Gignac call valid; the three-slot discipline, which has always looked like an obstacle to throughput, is also the arena's defence against the artifact it just learned about. The exposing fact: nothing in this file measures the *correlation* between a slot's grade and the quality of evidence behind it, so the arena cannot currently say whether its cross-area comparisons are riding on a strong relationship or a weak one. **Per R-J2 that measurement is not created here** — the slot's requirement is on what a claim must *state*, not on a new number to collect.

**Rank 3 exists to stop rank 1 being misread.** The pattern is robustly replicated across domains, cultures and populations; the **double-burden account** is what failed (McIntosh et al. 2019: meta-d′ does not differ across quartiles, *F*(3, 1150) = 1.2, *p* = .31; McIntosh et al. 2022 is titled "Skill and self-knowledge: empirical refutation of the dual-burden account"). `UNSUCCESSFUL` is recorded **for the account specifically**, with `LOW` on the pattern. The arena's `UNSUCCESSFUL` grade exists so a dead end is not rebuilt blind, and this is the clearest instance in the tranche.

**The tranche's best-evidenced claim is formal, not empirical.** Calibration and sensitivity are **orthogonal by construction**: meta-d′ is criterion-free, so a temperature-scaled confidence can have Brier 0.25 and meta-d′ = 0 — report 50% on a 50% base rate, be perfectly calibrated, and be completely uninformative, unable to say *which* answer is wrong. This arena's `confidence:` field is a calibration statement read as a sensitivity statement, and no grade in 13,608 lines has made that distinction. Graded `HIGH` on two sources, and ranked 2 for a stated reason: it is a claim about the measurement apparatus rather than about a mechanism, and the mechanism is rank 1.

### Area 100 — the outside view, and the reference class already in the log (ORDER 1242)

**The datum that earns the area.** Buehler, Griffin & Ross (1994, five studies, N = 207): participants underestimate their **own** task completion by 22–31% (*d* = 0.6–0.8) and predict **other people's** accurately — 27.3 predicted against 27.1 actual. Same experiment, same day, identical base rates available to both judgements. Study 3 makes it worse for any self-correction story: **best-case and realistic estimates were statistically indistinguishable, and worst-case estimates still fell short of actual outcomes for 70% of participants.** The corpus's reading is that this is structural blindness to the distribution, not insufficient contingency.

**The receipt.** This job runs on a **13-minute cron slot**. Every `RUNLOG.jsonl` line carries `duration_seconds`. That is a (predicted, actual) pair, logged unprompted, for hundreds of runs — **which is a reference class, accumulating in the workspace and never converted into a distribution.** `ARENA.md` held **zero** occurrences of *reference class*, *outside view*, or *uplift* before this pass. The skill's own §6 sets the volume rule in prose ("runs average ~8.7 minutes against a 13-minute slot") when the correct instrument is a per-class multiplier distribution at a stated percentile, and the file names the exact application: log predicted and actual duration per job, compute actual ÷ predicted, apply the P80/P90 uplift for the class.

**Grade and the disagreement, both preserved.** `UNTESTED` on the design, `HIGH` on the phenomenon, Support 1. Flyvbjerg's database is 863+ projects with **0.5%** delivering on time, on budget and on benefits; Park (2021) reports UK overrun falling **38% → 5%** after the 2003 mandate, with a with-without comparison against the US (+12 pp vs −17 pp against an on-budget target). **R-J4 disagreement, not reconciled:** Themsen (2019) reports Danish RCF applied selectively to projects already likely to succeed, with uplifts politically overridden when inconvenient, and classes as small as N = 5–8 producing unstable estimates. The corpus's own reconciliation is *institutional enforcement* — mandate versus recommendation — which is a claim about governance, not about cognition, and is recorded as such on the slot.

**Rank 3 is `UNSUCCESSFUL` and the reason is the one that would have bitten this workspace silently.** The corpus's requirement is blunt: *"no project was quietly excluded for being embarrassing."* Failed projects get archived, re-scoped and forgotten, so the class becomes a class of survivors. The concrete form here: **a pass that crashes, is reaped, or overruns must still log its `duration_seconds`** — otherwise the reference class becomes the distribution of runs that finished cleanly, which is the distribution of the system's successes, and every percentile computed from it is optimistic in exactly the direction that makes overruns worse. The previous pass's reported ceiling breach (21 files against a 20-file rule) is the live instance: a pass that broke the rule is a pass that must appear in the class.

### Area 101 — the scheduler cannot represent what it schedules (ORDER 1263, corroborated in reach by ORDER 1237)

**The brain part.** McClure et al. (2004): immediate rewards recruit limbic and ventral-striatal activity, delayed rewards recruit dorsolateral PFC and posterior parietal — the "impatient" and "patient" systems, in competition at the moment of choice. With that, human discounting is **hyperbolic** (Mazur 1987; Green, Myerson & McFarland 2004), which produces **preference reversal**: $10 today over $11 tomorrow, and $11 in 31 days over $10 in 30 days. Ainslie (1975, 1992) established that the same form fits animal choice, so it is not a human-specific bias.

**Why this is a mathematical silence and not a tuning gap.** Every scheduler in this stack — cron intervals, task queues, budget allocation — uses **`γ^t`, which is time-consistent by construction**. A time-consistent discount function **cannot represent a preference reversal**: if A ≻ B at *t*₀, consistency guarantees A ≻ B at every later moment. So the representational failure is not that γ is mistuned; it is that the property the scheduler is *defined by* is the property the brain *violates*, and no value of γ repairs it. `ARENA.md` held **zero** occurrences of *hyperbolic*, *preference reversal*, or *TMT*.

**The mechanism behind the asymmetry, and it is the hippocampus.** Dolan et al. (2007): hippocampal damage steepens discounting, and prompting subjects to imagine future scenarios before choosing **reduces** discount rates. The patient system's substrate is the same machinery that simulates — which is why "imagine the future self vividly" is an intervention and not a metaphor.

**Why TMT is rank 2 and not rank 1, stated on the slot.** Steel's equation `Motivation = (Expectancy × Value) / (1 + Impulsiveness × Delay)` is the tractable form, four parameters, all estimable from a log this workspace already writes, and the denominator shrinking toward the deadline is exactly the non-linearity `γ^t` misses. But **TMT fixes the order and does not represent its revision** — a system running TMT still cannot exhibit the preference reversal it is derived from. Rank 1 is the harder requirement; this is the tractable half, and saying so is the point of the ranking.

**R-J2 is satisfied by construction here, and it is the first slot in the arena that can say so.** Rank 1's observable signature is a task re-promoted under a hyperbolic form that `γ^t` would never re-promote. That signature is **present or absent in an existing queue** — no new instrument, no new measurement, no new number to collect. The constraint that has governed every previous area is met without an exemption.

### Corroboration — Area 74, Support 1 → 2 (ORDER 1235)

`oracle/brain/Metacognition/Confabulation.md` (164 lines) corroborates Area 74 from a **different literature**, which is the test applied: Nisbett & Wilson (1977) and Hall & Johansson's **choice blindness** appear nowhere in the Sperry file and are not derivable from it. Choice blindness is the stronger of the two for this arena — **70–80% of secretly swapped choices go undetected, detection does not improve when participants are told swaps will occur, and the participant then confabulates specific arguments for the alternative they originally rejected.** The confabulated preference can persist and alter later genuine choices, so the narration is not epiphenomenal.

**What it adds that ORDER 947 could not is the sincerity property**, and sincerity is the arena's actual problem. Deception leaves detectable traces of intent to mislead. The confabulator leaves none — which is why the corpus's thesis is the sharpest sentence in this tranche's reading: **self-report cannot be the verifier.** The gap between narration and cause is not represented anywhere in the system, so the subject is sincere *because* the error signal is missing, not despite it.

**The empirical anchor, and it lands exactly here.** Verbalized LLM confidence reaches only **~62.7% AUROC** at discriminating correct from incorrect answers — barely above chance — while probing finds genuine uncertainty signals **in hidden states** that generation does not surface by default (Kadavath et al. 2022; Azaria & Mitchell 2023, as summarised on the sibling page). **That is this arena's exact condition: the signal exists in the representation and is absent from the report.** Areas 98, 99 and 100 all found the same shape independently from three literatures; this file names it as a measured number.

**Grades held at `UNTESTED`, not raised.** Two sources of a human phenomenon is still human evidence, and per §8 the new file's `confidence: high` frontmatter is an artifact grade, not a trial — the exact inversion the arena already documents in its own corpus files.

**ORDER 1267** (`Multimodal-Foundation-Models.md`, 651 lines) — a technically strong engineering reference: CLIP's symmetric InfoNCE and its derivation, the learned temperature θ initialised to `log(N)⁻¹ ≈ 0.067` at batch 65,536, SigLIP's pairwise sigmoid variant, DataComp-1B reaching 76.4% ImageNet zero-shot against OpenAI's 75.5% on 400M curated pairs, latent diffusion's ~486× per-timestep saving, classifier-free guidance and its `w = 7–15` range, the Perceiver resampler compressing 196 ViT tokens to 64 query tokens, and Gemini's native unified tokenization against GPT-4V's retrofit.
**Not turned into a slot.** These are **model architectures, not brain parts.** The one genuinely reusable finding is the alignment-technique comparison — contrastive produces a flat space good for retrieval and poor for generation; generative alignment forces fine-grained correspondence at high data cost; cross-attention is the flexible middle. **That is a design axis for a perception subsystem, not an organ**, and the arena has no perception-area for it to amend. Recorded here so a later pass reading the second multimodal file does not re-derive it. **One §8 instance worth flagging:** the file's own §6.5 lists benchmark limitations (overfitting, <10K test sets, prompt sensitivity, data leakage) with more rigour than its front matter (`confidence: medium`, `sources: []`) earns, and **reference 25 is a duplicate of reference 9** — Wang et al. *Stable Diffusion*, arXiv 2112.10752, which is Rombach et al., already listed at position 9. Filed as `V-58.3`.

**ORDER 1269** (`Multimodal-Learning-and-Integration.md`, 148 lines) — superior colliculus multisensory integration and the **principle of inverse effectiveness** (the weaker the unimodal response, the stronger the multisensory enhancement; Stein & Meredith), the STS and the McGurk effect, cross-modal plasticity in congenital blindness with structural MRI evidence of rewiring, sensory substitution devices (vOICe, BrainPort, EyeMusic), temporal synchrony as the infant learning signal, and integration windows narrowing from several hundred ms in newborns to **50–100 ms in adults**.
**Not turned into a slot, and this one is a real deferral rather than a rejection.** `inverse effectiveness` is a genuine, well-replicated integration rule and `ARENA.md` holds **0** occurrences of it, while **Area 2** (reliability-weighted evidence integration) is the area it would amend — inverse effectiveness is the *biological* form of a reliability weighting, and it says something Area 2's current design does not: **weighting is superlinear at the low end, not merely proportional.** Deferred rather than opened because the file's rule is about *sensory* channels and Area 2's is about *evidential* ones, and asserting the transfer is this arena's invention with no trial. **Named here as the single highest-value unopened candidate in this tranche**: a file that measures inverse effectiveness against a proportional baseline would earn it immediately. `sensory substitution` and `cross-modal plasticity` are likewise at zero.

**ORDER 1271** (`Synfire-Chains-Coherent-Neural-Patterns.md`, 58 lines) — Abeles 1982, Griffith 1963's "complete transmission line", the Diesmann/Gewaltig/Aertsen 1999 *Nature* simulation, synfire braids (Bienenstock 1995), **polychronous groups (Izhikevich 2006) whose number can exceed the total neuron count**, and the Litvak et al. 2003 correction to the synchronous-only result.
**Not turned into a slot.** `synfire`, `Abeles` and `polychronous` are all at **0** occurrences in `ARENA.md`, so this is a gap, not a duplicate. The reason for not opening it is that the file's own §1.6 is candid: *"direct anatomical evidence for synfire chains remains limited"* and the field has not settled whether the brain implements synfire chains, polychronous braids, attractor sequences, or a hybrid. **A mechanism with no located anatomy and an open question about its own status is a candidate, not a slot** — and the design consequence (a sequence encoded as a timing pattern that coexists in one substrate) is close enough to **Area 91**'s time-window stack that opening it would duplicate. Recorded for the next pass that reads a file resolving the hybrid question.

**ORDER 1281** (`Hormones-Neuroendocrinology-and-Cognitive-Modulation.md`, 426 lines) — HPA axis with the MR/GR inverted-U, **acute versus chronic stress** (PFC "offline," amygdala and striatum taking over), **allostatic load** (McEwen & Stellar 1993), PTSD's **hypocortisolism** as the mirror image of depression's hypercortisolism, oxytocin (amplifies existing social biases rather than promoting prosociality; Zilkha et al. 2025 on distinct oxytocin populations for seismic versus militant behaviour), vasopressin, testosterone and estrogen, the **"type 3 diabetes"** hypothesis, and a five-principle hormonal-AI synthesis.
**Not turned into a slot, and the strongest of the deferrals.** The one item with real design weight is a **vicious feedback loop with a structural substrate**: chronic stress shrinks the hippocampus, and the hippocampus is one of the structures responsible for telling the HPA axis to stand down — **so chronic stress degrades the very organ that terminates the stress response.** A negative feedback loop whose sensor is destroyed by the signal it regulates is a failure mode with no entry in the arena, and the closest (**Area 42**'s protective inhibition, a circuit breaker) is an *acute* all-or-nothing shutdown, not a *chronic* one that erodes its own regulator. Deferred because the arena's own Areas 40 (circadian phase) and 57 (arousal as a gain trade) hold the state-variable half, and the loop is an argument about what happens when a state variable's substrate degrades — which is **Area 96**'s exhaustion-order question arriving from endocrinology. **`allostatic` appears 3× in `ARENA.md`, none of them about cumulative wear.**

#### Two corroborations, one grade change

**Area 75, Support 1 → 2, mapping `LOW` → `HIGH`.** Earned by ORDER 1275/1276 as one source. The Dayan entity page (ORDER 941) supplied the four-way mapping as a theoretical proposal; this file supplies **circuit anatomy** (VTA/SNc, raphe, basal forebrain, a locus coeruleus of **~1,600 neurons in rats and 10,000–30,000 in humans**), receptor-level pharmacology, and **three independent experimental lines** — single-unit recording, optogenetics, human pharmacology — where the entity page had one paper. **The grade is scoped explicitly: it is on the four-way *dissociation*, not the four-way *assignment*,** because the file's own §"Serotonin's Specificity Problem" records that serotonin's role is *"extraordinarily broad"* and its theories *"are post-hoc explanations,"* and the Cools–Fletcher assignment has evidence *"mixed across tasks."*
**The substantive addition is the sign.** 5-HT2C receptors on VTA dopamine neurons **inhibit** dopamine release (Dong et al. 2012, ~40% firing reduction), so serotonin is a **brake on** the dopamine channel rather than a fourth quantity beside it. **Area 75's four-column design is necessary and not sufficient** — a four-column schema has no way to say "this suppresses that" — and the amendment is now **Area 103 rank 1**.

**Area 38, Support 2 → 5 — the tranche's largest increment, from four independent files** (ORDER 1278, 1277, 1280, 1274). The mechanism for a number this area has argued about for twenty tranches: **capacity is a ratio of two clocks.** A ~6 Hz theta cycle (~167 ms) contains **4–7 gamma cycles** at ~40 Hz, and working-memory capacity *is* that ratio. **"Four" is not a property of a buffer**, which explains why labs measuring different tasks report different numbers, and why Area 38's refusal to average the 2-vs-4-vs-7 dispute was correct for a reason it did not previously have.
**Three qualifications carried, not averaged (R-J4):** Cowan's revised 3–4 does not *"neatly match"* the 4–7 figure; **Lopez-Peredo et al. 2019** report **"gamma reversal"** — gamma peaking at the *opposite* theta phase at some sites; **Lundqvist, Herman & Miller 2018** argue the scheme is an **epiphenomenon** that realistic circuit models produce with no assigned function.
**And a fourth caveat that is the §8 finding in a new place.** All four files carry `confidence: high` and populated `sources:` lists — the validated-artifact path — and **the disputes live in the prose those artefacts decorate, not in the artefacts.** Each file's §"Measurement Challenges" or §"Replication Status" section is where the failures are named; each file's front matter is where it declares itself settled. A reader trusting the metadata would have read all four as uncontested. **This is a cleaner instance of the inversion than the corpus-wide finding, because here the artefact and the prose disagree *within the same file*.**

#### `UNSUCCESSFUL`, twice

**Spindle-memory (Area 104 rank 2).** **Ujma (2024, *Neuropsychologia* 198: 108886)** meta-analysed **53 studies** and concluded there is **"no relationship between sleep spindles and memory"** and that spindles are *"unlikely to be generally implicated in learning and plasticity."* The corpus calls this **"one of the most significant recent controversies in the field"** and does not bury it. **Scoped to the density proxy, not to consolidation** — and the disagreement is preserved: intracranial and targeted studies continue to find strong links, and the corpus attributes the dispute partly to method (scalp vs intracranial, detection algorithm, task type). The stated survivor is **cross-frequency coupling, not spindle density** (Hyafil et al. 2015).

**The four-parameter agent has no arbiter (Area 103 rank 3).** Recorded against the corpus's *own design*: the file's "Integrated Agent Architecture" specifies four neuromodulatory parameters producing adaptive behaviour and presents the omission as a feature (*"without explicit environmental models"*), while its **first open question** asks how the four systems resolve conflicts when dopamine says explore and serotonin says avoid. **The file answers nowhere.** **Area 34** (control-mode allocation) is exactly the missing arbiter, reached from the behavioural side; the gap is in neither area.

#### A third artefact class, for the inversion's field list

Tranche 57 added the generated self-measured report as a fourth field. Tranche 58 adds a fifth: **the index.** ORDER 1272 and 1273 are two indexes of one directory under two spellings, and **their file listings disagree** — one lists one file, the other lists two. Both are `type: Index`, both are generated by `hermes-agent`, and one is wrong. **The index is a validated artefact carrying an unverified claim about its own directory**, the same shape as the TOC finding, and it is now the second instance in this arena of *the generated view being the thing that is wrong while the prose is right.*

#### Not read, and named

`ARENA.md` still holds **0** occurrences of *mirror neuron* / *Rizzolatti* despite ORDER 1265 §4 devoting a substantial passage to the mirror-neuron system and recording the Heyes dispute (mirror properties from associative learning, not innate circuitry) alongside the Open Encyclopedia of Cognitive Science's 2025 entry. That passage was read and deliberately **not** used: the file presents the debate as unresolved, and an area built on a mechanism whose innateness is contested would rank a contested thing first. **Named so the next pass treats it as a live candidate with a known objection**, not an oversight. Similarly 0 occurrences of *oxytocin*, *allostatic load* as a construct, *cerebellar cognitive affective syndrome* (CCAS, Schmahmann), and *PINK*/*Parkinson's* as a design failure mode — ORDER 1265 §2 and §3 carry all of them in detail.

**Infra:** no new defect class. `ARENA-INFRA.md` untouched. The index-disagreement and twin-directory instances are C-056 (case-variant basename collision) and C-047 (one source at several rows), both existing.
