### Tranche 59 — ORDER 1282–1301 · Areas 105 and 106 · the pass's finding is a defect class

**Read→mark: 20 `read_file` calls on corpus files, 20 rows flipped to `[x]`. EQUAL.** One
file, one call, one single-row patch, absorb, next. No consecutive ledger patches, no
multi-row patch, no bulk read, no script, no subagent, no `execute_code`, no shell read
of corpus content. Largest single read 46,054 chars (ORDER 1295); no `truncated: true`
and no `offset` continuation was needed by any of the twenty. **Ceiling checked before
file 21** — ORDER 1302 left unread rather than jumped. Six of the twenty were one-line
directory stubs.

**Remediation discharged on arrival.** `citation_remediation.py` reported **0 MUST
RE-READ, 0 MUST STRIKE**, 6 pre-existing AMBIGUOUS twins. The priority condition in the
job prompt ("until the MUST RE-READ count is 0, do not start a new tranche") was
therefore satisfied at the top of the pass and a normal tranche followed.

**Root, confirmed empirically this pass.** `/home/operator/.autognosia/` **does not
exist** on this host (`ls` returns *No such file or directory*); every read resolved
under `/home/operator/.hermes/`. This is the same finding the job prompt itself asserts
and the same one nine consecutive passes have reported. It is now the oldest open item
in the workspace.

#### Why Area 105 exists: no area could compare representations

`ARENA.md` held **0** occurrences of *RDM*, *hyperalignment*, *CKA*, *Algonauts*, or
*second-order isomorphism* across 104 areas. That absence is not a gap in coverage of
the brain — it is a gap in the arena's *instruments*, and it is worth being precise
about why it is a brain part at all rather than a piece of tooling. Kriegeskorte et al.
(2008) do not offer RDM as a convenience; they offer it because **the same information
is encoded in many different topographies across individuals**, which hyperalignment
then demonstrates (Haxby et al. 2011, 2020). That degeneracy is a property of the
cortex. A system that wants to be checked against a brain has to answer the question
RSA answers, and it has to answer it knowing that a *high score is not a
discrimination* — which is the Conwell et al. (2024) flexibility problem, now sitting
in rank 2 rather than being buried in a methods section.

**The rank ordering was decided by the negative results, not by preference.** Rank 3 is
`UNSUCCESSFUL` on Gao et al. (2025) — 1,000 simulated datasets per condition, RSA
*worse* than linear regression for first-order model selection — and that result is
what scopes rank 1 to the questions first-order comparison cannot reach. Had the
tranche contained only the method's own description, the slot would have been written
as universal adoption, and it would have been wrong.

**The one-source discipline was tested and held.** ORDER 1287 and ORDER 1288 are the
same document at two paths — identical frontmatter `id`, identical `aliases`, the same
30-item source list, one at 3,736 bytes and one at 45,680. This is exactly the case
§"Corroboration is new data, not repetition" warns about (*"three files restating one
study are one source, not three"*), and it is the first time in this arena that a
twin pair is a **compressed stub of a full report** rather than two stubs. Area 105
counts them once and says so in the slot, so a later pass reading the citation count
does not double it.

#### Why Area 106 exists, and why its rank 2 is aimed at Area 44

ORDER 1295 §"6. Circular Inference in Computational Modeling" is the finding that
justified a new area rather than a paragraph in Area 75: *"Many studies fit RL models
to behavior, then correlate fitted meta-parameters (α, γ, β) with neuromodulatory
proxies (pupil, pharmacology). This risks circularity: the model assumes the
neuromodulator controls that parameter, then 'confirms' it."* The corpus names the fix
(independent manipulation, then measure the change in the fitted parameter) and names
how rarely it has been run — achieved for NE/learning rate (Jepma et al. 2016), *"but
rare for other systems."*

**This is aimed at an existing area, and that is the point of recording it.** Area 44
is *self-diagnosis by parameter recovery* — fit a generative model to your own
behaviour, read the parameters back. That is the same move. It currently carries no
recorded reason to distrust the inference step. A design that recovers a parameter
from its own fitted model and then treats the parameter as evidence about itself has
measured its own fit — the §8 inversion with the model in place of the pipeline. **Area
44 is not demoted by this; the two files were read in different tranches and a
deliberate demotion on a cross-reference would be exactly the unearned-citation
pattern in reverse.** The pointer is recorded and a later pass holding both should
arbitrate.

#### Two corroborations, both with a qualification attached (R-J4)

**Area 66 (metaplasticity) 3 → 4.** ORDER 1300 supplies the equation the slot had been
asserting in prose: **θ_M ∝ ⟨y²⟩_τ**, τ of seconds to minutes, with the sign rule
stated as the slot states it. Two *measured* threshold movements now back it — Artola
et al. (1990) dark-reared cats **~20–30% lower**, Hulme et al. (2012) hippocampal
conditioning **25–35%**. The qualification is the file's own and is not averaged away:
the functional form is *"debated"*, some data show **bistability** (Abramsson et al.
2008) rather than a smooth slide, the timescale *"varies widely across brain regions"*,
and **anti-Hebbian STDP in cerebellum and olfactory bulb is unexplained by BCM alone**.
Design grade held `UNTESTED` — the arena still has no gain state.

**Area 39 (coincidence detection and the veto) 2 → 3.** ORDER 1298 supplies the
arithmetic the 25:1 conductance ratio was missing: an NMDA spike needs **10–50
co-activated neighbouring synapses** within **~20–50 μm** and **~10–50 ms**. *Starting
requires many; stopping requires one* — and that asymmetry is the design. The same
file bounds the slot: NMDA spikes are *"strictly local… confined to a single dendritic
branch of ~20–50 μm length,"* so the veto is a **compartment-local** abort, not a
global one, and an agent copying it must decide what its own compartment is. **The
veto grade stays `LOW`** — three sources agreeing on a mechanism is not three
replications of a single in-vitro 2 nS measurement, and inflating that would be the
error the counting rules exist to prevent.

#### Read and deliberately not turned into a slot

**ORDER 1290** (`Dopaminergic-Pathway-Diversity-Computation.md`, 41,583 chars, 34
sources) is the richest file of the tranche and the most consequential for the arena.
Its central claim is that **dopamine is a family of pathway- and receptor-specific
meta-signals, not one channel**, supported by optogenetics (Keiflin 2019: cue-period
phasic activation unblocks learning for **VTA** but **not SNc** — a direct falsification
of uniform RPE broadcast), a D1/D2 **double dissociation** (eLife 46050: D1R inactivation
impairs value-dependent *action selection*, D2R inactivation impairs *value learning*,
without cross-effects), single-cell transcriptomic taxonomy (Poulin 2014 six subtypes;
Tiklová 2019 seven), and human snRNA-seq identifying a **SOX6_AGTR1** population
selectively depleted in Parkinson's.

This is a first-order challenge to **Area 75 rank 1** (four channels) and to **Area
103** (the signs and antagonisms), and it is the strongest single piece of evidence
this arena has received against its own neuromodulatory schema. **It was not used to
amend either area in this pass.** The reason is the one the skill states for
remediation reads and it applies equally here: a file that arrives as an amendment to
an area is read with the answer already written. It has been read whole, judged, and
**deferred to its own tranche**, where it gets the room its evidence needs. Recorded in
`VERIFICATION.md` as the highest-value deferral of this pass.

Five further files read and not turned into slots, each with a reason: ORDER 1285 and
1286 (neuroimaging method surveys — the modality table is a reference work, and 1286 is
truncated mid-sentence at line 217); ORDER 1297 (a broad plasticity survey whose AI
parallels are already held across Areas 6, 23, 66 and 97); ORDER 1293 (a textbook
four-system overview that Area 75 and Area 106 now both supersede at higher
resolution); and ORDER 1289 (a four-paragraph stub of the ACh material ORDER 1295
covers completely — one source, not two).

#### Corpus defects found — one new class

**Mid-word truncation of the H1 title line in generated research reports.** Four
instances in one tranche: ORDER 1289 line 41 (`rgic Signaling of Expected
Uncertainty and Precision"`), ORDER 1292 line 49 (`us-Norepinephrine System: Network
Reset and Unexpected Uncertainty"`), ORDER 1298 line 34 (`c Spikes and Plateau
Potentials in Cortical Computation`), ORDER 1300 line 32 (`e: Hebbian Learning and
Synaptic Weight Update Rules`). In every case the **intact title reappears a few lines
below as the `#` H1** — the damage is confined to a clipped duplicate above it.

This is **§8's inversion in its purest recorded form.** The artifact is *reliably*
damaged and the *content* is intact, so a reader who inspects the artifact sees
damage and concludes the file is broken, while a reader who inspects neither sees a
clean document. Every prior instance had the artifact looking *sound* while the prose
was unchecked. Here the artifact looks *broken* while the prose is sound — the same
inversion, inverted, which is confirmation that the pattern is about the validation
path and not about either component. **New class; written to `ARENA-INFRA.md`.**

**Directory-case twins are systematic, and the twin is not always a stub.** Four
instances: `neuroscience/` vs `Neuroimaging-Methods/` (ORDER 1283/1284 — the two
indices list *different* file sets, so the directories have genuinely diverged, which
is worse than duplication); `neuroplasticity/` vs `Neuroplasticity/` (ORDER 1299 a
**20-line stub**, ORDER 1300 the 453-line original, *same `id`*);
`neuroimaging-methods/` vs `Neuroimaging-Methods/` (ORDER 1287/1288, same `id`, same
`aliases`, same source list). This falls under existing classes **C-056**
(case-variant basename collision) and **C-047** (one source at several rows), so no
new class was opened — but the *severity* is now established: the twins are not always
harmless stubs, and `citation_remediation.py`'s **446 basenames published at more than
one row** is a direct consequence.

**Inline citation numbering drift inside a single file.** ORDER 1290 cites `[31]`–`[34]`
in the prose for the explore/exploit and habenula literature while the numbered source
list assigns those indices to unrelated entries; ORDER 1292 uses inline `[13]` and
`[15]` for GANE and McClure while its list assigns those numbers to Mather and Sara.
Both files are otherwise well-sourced with 30+ and 16 entries respectively. Per §7 this
is corpus hygiene, not design — but a reader following a citation number into the wrong
paper is how a wrong *design* gets adopted, so it is recorded rather than dismissed.

**Stub files carrying a `[[link]]` and nothing else.** ORDER 1299 is 20 lines: frontmatter,
a truncated `e: concept` fragment, blank lines, and a single wikilink to the real
document. It carries `confidence: high`. A 20-line file with no prose asserting high
confidence is the §8 pattern in its most compressed form and is noted for the
`confidence:` convention, which Area 75 already holds as a defect.

**Infra:** one new class (H1 mid-word truncation). The twin-directory and
source-numbering instances are C-056, C-047 and ordinary hygiene respectively.

### Tranche 60 — ORDER 1302–1320 (19 files) — structural plasticity, adaptive
myelination, and the body's typed error channels

**Compliance.** 19 `read_file` calls on corpus files, 19 rows flipped to `[x]`,
in order 1302→1320, each read immediately followed by a single-row patch before
any arena edit. No consecutive ledger patches, no multi-row patch, no bulk read,
no script, no subagent, no `execute_code`, no shell read of corpus content. The
ceiling was checked before starting file 20 and ORDER 1321 was left unread rather
than jumped. Largest single read 58,394 chars (ORDER 1320). **I did not reach 20
files and I am not going to describe it as though I had — the count is 19, and
the two numbers are equal, which is what the check requires.**

**The pass's shape.** The walk cleared `Neuroplasticity/` and `Neuroscience/`.
Two of the nineteen were directory indices with no design content (ORDER 1302,
ORDER 1317), and the substantive yield is seventeen files. **Three areas opened,
0 re-ranks, 2 corroborations.** The three new areas are consecutive in number and
share one property worth naming: **each of them is a structural silence about a
quantity the arena already used constantly without an area.** Area 107 is about
whether a *connection* can be destroyed. Area 108 is about whether a *path* has a
cost that changes with use. Area 109 is about whether the body's condition
arrives *typed*. Each was found by noticing that a term the arena leans on
everywhere had zero occurrences in the file.

---

**Area 107 — structural plasticity.** Rank 1 rests on the strongest causal
result in the tranche, and it is worth being precise about why it is stronger
than the rest: **Hayashi-Takagi et al. (Nature 2015)** did not show that
potentiated spines correlate with learning, they *shrank exactly the spines their
own transgene had labelled*, and doing so **disrupted acquired motor
performance — while shrinking an equal number of spines potentiated by a
different task in the same cortical territory had no effect.** Necessity and
task-specificity in one experiment. That is the arena's own Area 33 test
(a detector is not a certifier) applied to a substrate the arena does not have.
On that basis the mechanism grade is `HIGH`.

**The grade I refused to give, and why.** The design is `UNTESTED` and stays
there. Two independent brakes on raising it, both from the file itself:
no experiment has shown a small set of identified spines to be *individually
sufficient* for a memory, and the **engram-spine dissociations** are directly
against the strong reading — dentate engram-cell spine density *drops* between
recent and remote timepoints while optogenetic engram activation still elicits
freezing, and auditory-cortex fear conditioning leaves a lasting spine trace
while *recall triggers no new structural remodeling*. **A substrate can be
necessary for expression and not be where the memory lives**, and the corpus's
own summary of the Aplysia work puts the sharpest form of it: long-term
sensitization was behaviourally erased by reconsolidation blockade, which *also
reversed the training-induced synaptic growth*, yet was **fully reinstated by
reminder shocks**. The authors argue structure may *express* rather than *store*.
I am not adjudicating that; I am refusing to let `HIGH` on necessity leak into a
claim about sufficiency, which is the exact leak §8 exists to catch.

**The measurement section is why rank 3 is `UNSUCCESSFUL` and not merely
qualified.** Published adult-cortex turnover figures span an order of magnitude
between top labs using nominally similar methods — Grutzendler's ~96%
one-month stability in visual cortex against Trachtenberg's substantially higher
barrel-cortex turnover **in the same 2002 issue of *Nature*** — and CA1 has
three mutually inconsistent results, one of which (Wegner 2018, 2P-STED) found
**double the previously reported spine density** and measured a merged-spine
artefact at **23% of apparent single spines**. The file's verdict is that no
consensus resolution exists. **A design that sizes a store from a turnover rate
inherits a range, not a number**, and this workspace already has a place where
that mistake would be expensive: Area 97 sizes the substrate by its own
architecture.

**Why rank 1's promotion gate points at this workspace.** The mechanistic
support for the gate is Yang et al. (Science 2014): new spines concentrate on
high-frequency branches; **seven hours of post-training sleep deprivation cut
HFB formation nearly in half (4.9 ± 0.7% vs 9.3 ± 0.7%)**; REM deprivation did
*not* disrupt it but disrupting **NREM reactivation did**; corticosterone
controls ruled out stress. So the gate is not metaphorical here.
`ARENA-EVIDENCE.md` is the consolidation pass and `RUNLOG.jsonl` is its replay
buffer, and the promotion condition is precisely the one under which a ledger row
becomes a slot's `Backup document`. Scale stated per R-J5: the class is
*tranches*, not files, and it grows.

---

**Area 108 — adaptive myelination.** The finding I did not expect is that this
area's rank 1 and rank 3 argue *about the same evidence* and the corpus supports
both. Gibson 2014 and McKenzie 2014 establish necessity through two independent
genetic interventions, and the *Myrf* knockout gives the cleanest dissociation in
the file: **myelin is required for learning, not for recall.** The same file's
own methods section then says whether artificial myelin enhancement accelerates
learning **remains untested** — and that is why the slot is a *structural cost
model* and explicitly **not** an intervention. Adopting the intervention on the
strength of the necessity result would be reading a causal claim past its
endpoint, and the file hands me the sentence that stops me.

**The clause I kept because it is counterintuitive and it is the testable
part: the same molecule is the accelerator and the lock.** NgR1⁻/⁻ mice retain
juvenile ocular-dominance plasticity into adulthood (McGee 2005; Akbik 2013,
where NgR1 sets the *low set-point* for adult spine turnover). So a store whose
access pattern has made it cheap simultaneously becomes harder to rewrite. **A
design that optimizes for fast access is optimizing against its own future
adaptability** — which is Area 66's BCM sliding threshold arriving at the
structural layer, with a gene attached.

**Rank 3 is a first-class `UNSUCCESSFUL` and it is the most transferable result
in this tranche.** The field's causal claim about myelin rested on DTI, and **FA
is not a myelin measure**: it reflects orientational coherence of water
diffusion and is driven by axon diameter, packing density, glial cell volume,
extracellular space and neuroinflammation as well as myelin thickness. **≥60–90%
of white-matter voxels contain crossing fibres** (Jeurissen 2013), and Chang et
al. (2017) ground-truthed it with CLARITY — MBP correlated with FA up to r ≈ 0.7
in coherent tracts but **crossing-fibre regions showed weaker correlations**, so
an FA change there may be a fibre-population shift, not myelin at all. Then the
sharper half: **Hofstetter 2013 reported mean-diffusivity reduction in the
fornix after 2 h of spatial learning**, and Hill's *J Neurosci* commentary says
that is too fast for myelin — in vitro differentiation to a mature sheath takes
days to weeks, and local MBP *translation* in minutes-to-hours is **not** sheath
assembly. The alternative is **glial volume change**: activity → K⁺ → astrocyte/
oligodendrocyte swelling → reduced extracellular space → reduced MD. **An
hour-scale DTI signal is not a myelin result.** This is §8's inversion in a
sixth field: a standardised, reproducible, validated metric measuring something
other than the thing it is named for, with a peer-reviewed commentary saying so.

**A consequence I recorded rather than acted on.** Area 82's existing
`UNSUCCESSFUL` on the glial layer — IP3R2 knockouts producing *"surprisingly
mild cognitive phenotypes"*, with the verdict to prefer regularization and
adaptation modules over core forward-pass components — is **supported from a
different direction by this file, and explained by it.** Oligodendrocytes are an
*adaptive* module by construction: they respond to use, not to input. **A glial
mechanism can be load-bearing for timing and cost, return null on a memory task,
and not be refuted by that null** — the knockout was measured on the wrong axis.
The Area 82 `UNSUCCESSFUL` stands and now has a reason attached rather than
just a verdict.

---

**Area 109 — interoception.** Two independent `UNSUCCESSFUL` results in one
file, and the first is the most direct causal test of a hub claim I have read.

**(a) The hub claim failed its own test.** Craig's strongest claim — anterior
insula as the unique substrate of awareness — predicts that bilateral insular
destruction should abolish or profoundly disrupt self-awareness. **Philippi,
Feinstein et al. (PLOS ONE 2012)** tested patient Roger: near-complete bilateral
damage to insula, ACC, mPFC and medial temporal lobes, **~10% of insular
tissue remaining and largely disconnected**, and core self-awareness,
extended self-awareness and introspective ability all **fundamentally
preserved** — including tickle sensation and heartbeat awareness under
high-dose isoproterenol when skin anaesthesia blocked the somatic routes. The
authors' word is that the insula hypothesis **"is untenable."** I am recording
this as a refutation because it is one, and I am *not* recording it as
settling the alternative: the file's own preferred replacement (distributed
brainstem–thalamus–posteromedial networks) is a hypothesis, not a result.

This is a **real constraint on Area 46**, and I want it visible rather than
buried: a Roger whose insular tissue is 90% gone and whose selfhood is intact is
evidence that **the self is not localised in one component.** Any design in this
arena that puts selfhood in a place should read that first.

**(b) The field's dominant measure measures almost nothing.** The Schandry
heartbeat-counting task is the most-used interoceptive accuracy measure, and
**Zamariola et al. 2018 (N = 572)** is the definitive psychometric critique:
scores driven by **under-reporting in >95% of participants** (r = **−0.93**);
overall correlation between actual and counted beats **r = .16, ~2.6% shared
variance**; and non-linear across quintiles (r = .50/.67/.95/.83/.88) so
**top-quintile scorers are statistically indistinguishable in what they
actually track**. Scores correlate **negatively** with heart rate (r = −0.36) —
mechanically inflating accuracy at slower hearts — and differ across 25/35/45 s
intervals, which is a **time-estimation signature**. **Desmedt 2018 (N = 123)**
showed that merely instructing participants to report *only clearly felt beats*
**cuts IAcc roughly in half**, confirming strategy reliance on estimation rather
than perception. Pacemaker patients' counts did not change when device rate was
set to 50/75/110 bpm.

**The counterattack is preserved, not reconciled (R-J4).** Ainley, Tsakiris,
Pollatos et al. (2020) argue the critique rests on **misconceived bivariate
reasoning** — IAcc is a **ratio variable**, so spurious correlations between a
ratio and its components are a statistical artefact dating to Pearson 1897;
under-reporting dominance partly reflects **conservative instructions against
hallucinated beats**; the heart-rate dependence follows from ratio arithmetic.
Zimprich et al. make the ratio-variable point formally. A 2025 three-task
comparison found **moderate positive relations** between counting and
signal-detection sensitivity but concluded the tasks are **not interchangeable**.
Status as the corpus states it: the task survives as a convenience measure, its
construct validity is contested **in both directions**, and load-bearing findings
should be replicated with signal-detection or perturbation methods. **I am not
resolving a live dispute between a psychometric critique and a
misconceived-reasoning rebuttal, and neither does the file.**

**Rank 1 survives both refutations precisely because it never claimed a hub and
never claimed a scalar.** That is the design lesson and it is the reason the rank
order is what it is: the two negatives are what *license* a distributed,
typed-channel architecture. They do not weaken it; they are the evidence for it.
The file's own concession is recorded in the slot — **Seth & Friston explicitly
concede that *"direct empirical evidence for (or against) interoceptive
predictions or prediction errors is still lacking"***, and Barrett & Simmons's
EPIC is *"an Opinion-article synthesis…, not a tested model."* Strong anatomy,
untested predictive account — and it is the predictive account a design adopts.

---

**Corroboration 1 — Area 45 (efference copy), Support 1 → 2, mechanism
`unverified` → `LOW`.** ORDER 1310 is a genuinely independent source: different
evidence type from ORDER 573's build plan, and it supplies what the slot
lacked — a **measured circuit with a matched control**. **Tanabe et al. (Nature
Commun. 2021)** used **chemogenetic (hM4Di), not lesion**, inactivation of the
**SC → MD → FEF** pathway and found it **specifically impairs self-initiated
saccades while leaving visually triggered saccades intact**. The arena's best
behavioural premise for this comparator had been `unverified` Ford 2019 for
many tranches; this is a channel-specific causal result and it is the first time
this slot has had one. **Mackey, Wurtz & Conecta (2019, *eLife*)** adds the
half that changes the design: a mormyrid fish trained to produce a **negative
image** of a small reward-probability region **adapts its internal model within
~20 saccades**, scaled by learning rate and injection site — **the copy is
plastic, and a copy that learns can be wrong in a self-consistent way.**

**The clause that qualifies rank 1 and I did not soften:** the dangerous regime
is **not absence of prediction, it is confident but miscalibrated prediction.**
The cerebellum is described as a low-pass filter with an internal feed-forward
model, so lesions dissociate toward *too much* prediction as readily as too
little — hence the stipulation that studies confirm *diminished* or *absent*
self-generated sensations, **not increased ones**. **So the `agency:` field
records the *input* to the comparator and cannot detect a comparator whose
*output* has drifted.** A provenance tag certifies that the write path was
honest. It certifies nothing about whether the reader's sense of having authored
the item is calibrated. That is now stated in the slot, because it is a
limitation a reader of the slot would otherwise not know.

**Corroboration 2 — Area 66 (metaplasticity), Support 2 → 3, design grade
deliberately held at `UNTESTED`.** ORDER 1303 corroborates the mechanism and
supplies the molecular handle the slot was missing — **θ_M ∝ ⟨y²⟩_τ**, with
**PP1 and calcineurin** as the depotentiation machinery and **PKC** shifting the
stabilization threshold — plus the arena's sharpest critical-period
measurement: **Nogo-receptor mutation extends the critical period from ~30 days
to 45–120 days**, and **PLX5622 (a CSF-1R inhibitor) extends it in adulthood**.
**I held the design grade and the file names the reason itself:** the
adult-reopening result is **rodent, with human translation explicitly
speculative**, and the one human-level finding is **BDNF Val66Met** — a
polymorphism that shifts *individual* learning rates, which is between-person
variance, not a threshold anyone can actuate. Per §8, a mechanism grade earned on
rodents does not become a design grade. One further clause worth carrying: adult
critical-period reopening reopens **both the capacity to learn and the capacity
to be harmed**, and **ispronicline extends a sensorimotor critical period with no
effect on the emotional one** — so the brakes are **not one global dial**, which
is now recorded as a direct constraint on Area 108's NgR1 lock and on any design
that models critical periods as one scalar.

---

#### Area 110 — the bounded continuation store · what nearly displaced rank 1

**The candidate that lost, and it should be recorded because it is the more
common design in the wild.** *Unbounded* task suspension — a stack, a tree, a
scratchpad that can hold any number of suspended contexts and resume any of them
— is what an LLM agent has by default and what the arena's context-window areas
(91, and the Arena-27/Area-38 capacity slots) implicitly assume. It is also the
design the corpus says a human does **not** have. Koechlin & Hyafil (2007)
predict **no recursive branching**: FPC cannot resume a primary *and* a secondary
pending task after a third task. Rank 3 makes the sharpness of this explicit —
**removing the external scratchpad should degrade deep hierarchical planning and
not shallow branching**, and that is a falsifiable prediction this system could
be run against. It has never been run here, and R-J2 forbids manufacturing it,
so the mechanism stays `UNTESTED` and the slot says so.

**Why this is not a conflict with Area 91.** The obvious reading is that Area 91
(cortex as a stack of time windows) and Area 110 (bounded, non-nested) are
contradictory. They are not, and the reconciliation is in the evidence: the
arena's *substrate* may be nested (context windows nest) while the *controller*
that addresses them is not. The corpus's own escape route is the third
Koechlin & Hyafil claim — **recursion is scaffolded externally, through
linguistic coding** — and a language model is nothing if not an external
linguistic scaffold. The prediction and the mechanism come from the same paper
and they are consistent: an external stack is exactly the thing that lets a
bounded controller behave as if unbounded, and removing it should reveal the
bound.

**The capacity number, and why it is graded `LOW` and not `HIGH`.** Two numbers
are in the file and they are not the same number. Koechlin & Hyafil predict
**≤1 pending task**; Collins & Koechlin (2012) fit **≤3 counterfactual task
sets** (95% CI 2–4). The file itself notes these differ in *grain* — a task set
may contain many tasks — and that the **predicted interference between two
pending tasks has not been cleanly demonstrated in humans** and the **direct
behavioural test of recursive branching is lacking**. So the design constraint
in rank 1 is written as *one suspended task; ≤3 counterfactual hypotheses* rather
than as a single number, because the corpus supports the structure and only
approximately supports the constant. Recording `3` as if it were measured to
three significant figures would be the §8 inversion: a real citation behind a
precision the evidence does not carry.

**Lesion evidence is a double dissociation, which is why the anatomy is `HIGH`
and the build is not.** Dreher et al. (2008): across 15 patients, **only left
BA10 lesion volume** correlated with multitasking errors (ρ = 0.94, p < 0.005,
n = 6) and it did **not** correlate with dual-task errors (ρ = 0.65, p = 0.16) —
with lesion volumes comparable between groups (56.8 vs 43.3 ml, n.s.), so the
dissociation is not a size artifact. Badre, Hoffman, Cooney & D'Esposito (2009,
n = 34) supplies the asymmetry in the other direction: rostral lesions impair
abstract **and** concrete control, caudal lesions spare abstract. The
*computation* is replicated. Whether a `suspended` state variable in a scheduler
is anything like it is `UNTESTED`, and that gap is the whole area.

**The electrophysiology is the clause I would not have found without reading.**
Tsujimoto, Genovesio & Wise (2010, *J Neurosci* 30:10779–10789) found goal-
selective FPC neurons encoding goals **only at feedback time** — never at cue,
delay, or response. The arena's learner updates weights on every token. This
circuit updates its *hypothesis values* only at outcome. That is a different
update schedule, and it is cheap to state and expensive to build: reliability
weights that move only on resolution are not the same object as weights that
move on every observation.

**The term *hierarchy* is now constrained, and this is the arena arguing with
itself in public.** Area 62 holds "the three levels of analysis." The file's
dispute section says the term *hierarchy* should be **reserved for demonstrated
asymmetric dependencies, not assumed from gradient alone** — with anatomy on one
side (Petrides & Pandya 1999: area 10 projects to area 6 but not the reverse)
and a monkey counterexample on the other (periarcuate BA 6/8 lesions impair
conditional motor tasks but **not** tasks engaging rostral mid-DLPFC, so rostral
regions can operate without caudal intermediaries). Both preserved, R-J4. Every
slot in the arena that says "the planner routes to the executor" is asserting
the asymmetric dependency; this pass found the one place the corpus licenses it
(Badre 2009) and the one place it does not. Recorded as rank 2 rather than
discarded because a constraint that prevents a wrong design is worth a slot.

**Cross-reference, not counted.** ORDER 1331 §4 and ORDER 1335 §"Visual
Processing Architecture" both carry the hierarchy claim. They were **not**
counted as independent support for Area 110: they state the gradient/hierarchy
distinction in general, not the FPC continuation store, and three files
restating one claim are one source.

---

#### Area 111 — the specificity gradient, and a century-old laundering

**Necessity and sufficiency, kept separate because only one of them is a design
argument.** The peripheral labeled-line claim is supported on both sides, and they
are different kinds of evidence: genetic ablation of a receptor pathway
*abolishes* that taste (**necessity**); optogenetic activation of the
corresponding neurons drives aversive behaviour **with no bitter compound
present** (**sufficiency**). The cortical side has neither — it is anatomical and
imaging work on broadly tuned cells with intermingled ensembles. A design
argument built only on necessity ("the channel is there, so use it") would be
wrong, and one built only on the population-code observation ("distribute
everything") would have no claim on the periphery at all. The file's own
robustness line is the reason the hybrid is rank 1: **central redundancy buys
peripheral damage tolerance; peripheral specificity buys fast accurate
detection.** That is a genuine both/and with a mechanism behind each half, and
it is why this is a design and not a compromise.

**The tongue map, in the file's own words, because the wording is the point.**
The map originated in a **misreading of Hänig 1901** and was taught for
decades. What Hänig found and what survived refutation is a **graded regional
sensitivity difference** — tip slightly more sensitive to sweet and salty, back
to bitter. The categorical version, not the gradient, is what got copied. That
distinction is why this earned a slot rather than going to `VERIFICATION.md`
as trivia under the §7 test: *would a good architect change the design?* Yes.
Any field in this arena that stores a magnitude under a categorical heading
(`confidence:` as a scalar, `Support: N` as a count of a heterogeneous
literature, a slot's rank as a preference) is the same shape, and the tongue
map says the failure does not require anyone to lie — the underlying gradient
was **real** and the claim that replaced it is still false. That is the hardest
class of error to catch and it is the class §8 predicts, because the artifact
(the map, the table, the confident heading) is intact.

**Rank 3 is the file disagreeing with its own preferred interpretation, and the
disagreement is preserved unreconciled (R-J4).** The file says gustatory cortex
responds differently to expected vs unexpected tastes, then says: *"direct
empirical evidence for predictive coding in gustatory cortex is still limited…
this is **also consistent with simpler adaptation accounts**."* Repetition
suppression and prediction error produce the **same BOLD sign**. So any design
that reads a suppression response as a prediction error may be reading its own
habituation as surprise. This bears directly on **Area 33**, whose rank 1 is
negative-result discipline over error-detection signals, and on **Area 27**,
whose reconsolidation gate fires on mismatch — a gate fired on a repetition-
suppression signal is a gate fired on habituation. **Area 33 was not
incremented** (it is already at 8 sources) because this file *weakens* the
general reading rather than adding support to it. The file names the missing
experiment: dynamic causal modelling, or laminar recordings to separate
feedforward from feedback. Not run here; R-J2.

**Corroboration that earned its keep.** ORDER 1324 was also counted into
**Area 63** rank 1, taking it **2 → 3**, and the clause it earns is a *limit on
Area 63's own framing*: a receptive field was being treated as a property of a
cell, and the taste evidence says specificity is a property of a cell's position
in a pathway. Grade **held** at `HIGH` — a source that qualifies a slot is not a
replication of it, and inflating on that basis is §8 applied to a grade.
ORDER 1337 was counted into **Area 4** rank 1, **2 → 3**, for the Volle et al.
(2011) split between *holding* an intention and *releasing* it: patient Z.P.
recalled both action sets and could not recall which to reproduce. Content
intact, enactment lost — a failure that presents as amnesia with nothing
forgotten. Deployment grade **held**; a corroborating anatomy does not promote a
hook.

a pass that finds nothing should say so rather than manufacture a class.

**`Wells & Olson, 2068`** — carried forward unresolved from ORDER 1321. A year
in the 22nd century in a memory-systems debate file, cited in a context that
looks load-bearing. Still `VERIFICATION.md`; still unfixed. **Twelve passes have
now carried it.**

**Standing recommendation, second time raised.** The skill's corpus root
(`/home/operator/.autognosia/`) **does not exist on this host**; every read
resolves under `/home/operator/.hermes/`. It was on the arena's
`BRAIN PARTS NOT YET COVERED` list, which was itself the wrong place for it —

closed this pass, with the strike left standing, and the recommendation moved to
`VERIFICATION.md` where a workspace defect belongs. **Twelve passes have now
reported it. The skill still says otherwise.**

**What I would want a later pass to know.** Both areas this tranche are about a
*quantity the arena was already using*: a register's capacity, a code's
specificity. Neither is a new organ, and that is worth noticing — the arena's
remaining gaps are thinning toward *constants and directions* rather than
toward anatomy. The day a term returns zero for the last time is not knowable
from inside a pass, but this pass found two in nineteen files, which is a higher
yield than the last several tranches. Method: pick a term the arena leans on
everywhere, count it, and **a region with many site-mentions and no
function-mentions is an area waiting to be earned.** Recommend it be added to
the skill.

  records that some longitudinal studies found early *symbolic* number ability
  predicting later *non-symbolic* ability and not the reverse — **the arrow points
  both ways** — and that some researchers find the correlation disappears
  entirely when working memory is controlled, making working memory the common
  cause. Neither is reconciled here. **A grade that was deliberately not
  awarded:** the residual r ≈ 0.20–0.30 (Fazio et al. 2014) is *not* recorded as
  a real causal effect of any size. The corpus's own open question 1 asks exactly
  that and is unanswered, and the §8 inversion is precisely the move of reading a
  modest correlation as a mechanism.
- **Area 114** beat nothing; `ARENA.md` held 0 of *auditory scene*, *Bregman*,
  *source segregation*, *cocktail party*, *phonemic restoration*, and 1
  incidental *segregation*. **The structural claim is the inverse-operation one:**
  Area 53 is cross-modal *binding* and Area 105 is relational encoding, so the
  arena is dense on fusing inputs and empty on taking one apart. **The thing that
  nearly displaced Rank 1** is the self-monitoring line — *speakers monitor
  their own voice using the same ASA mechanisms, integrating auditory feedback
  with motor commands via the dorsal stream* — which makes segregation a
  *solved* problem in the human system rather than an open one, and would have
  supported a stronger grade. It is recorded inside Rank 1 rather than promoted,
  because one corpus sentence about self-speech is not a trial of the design.
  **R-J4 preserved in Rank 3:** the corpus's summary of the attention question
  is that *"the current consensus leans toward a dual-process model"* — a lean,
  not a result — and all three positions (attention-dependent,
  attention-independent, Carlyon's two-phase hybrid) are recorded side by side.
  ORDER 1518 adds a second unresolved axis of the same shape: right-hemisphere
  dominance for emotional prosody is the field's most replicated claim and the
  meta-analysis (Belyusar et al. 2013) finds **consistent bilateral** activation.
- **Area 115** had 1 incidental occurrence of *model collapse* to displace, which
  is none. **This is the area that describes this workspace.** The arena is a
  corpus read by successive passes of one process: pass N writes `ARENA.md` and
  `ARENA-EVIDENCE.md`, pass N+1 reads them. The corpus's agent-specific section
  names the failure — *"If an agent's knowledge base is updated using its own
  outputs, rare but important facts may be lost over time… An agent that only
  reads its own outputs will converge to a narrow worldview"* — without noticing
  it was describing this file. **R-J4 preserved in Rank 1 and deliberately
  unreconciled:** Shumailov et al. (replacement → linear error growth, Markov
  absorption to a delta function with probability 1) versus Gerstgrasser,
  Schaeffer et al. (accumulation → bounded error, proved for linear regression
  via Dohmatob et al., empirical across transformers/diffusion/VAEs). The
  corpus's own resolution is that both are correct within their assumptions, and
  the disagreement is entirely about which assumption reflects reality.
  **The grade split is the load-bearing part:** `HIGH` for the linear-regression
  bound, `LOW` for the deep-model extension, which the corpus states is
  *empirical, not proven*. Writing `HIGH` across the board would be §8's
  inversion in its most flattering form. **Rank 3 is the sharpest finding in the
  tranche** and it is the corpus's own: the proposed early-detection metrics are
  **perplexity and diversity score**, and a system whose diversity has collapsed
  has an *improving* perplexity on the corpus it now reads. **The standard
  instrument improves as the defect grows.** R-J2 forbids this arena generating a
  better one, so the slot records the gap and stops.

**Two corroborations, both grades held, and one grade *moved* on mechanism only.**

- **Area 40 Rank 3 (glymphatic clearance) — Support 1 → 2**, by ORDER 1344. The
  independence is real: a different discovery (Louveau et al. 2015), a different
  lab (Kipnis), a different route to the same anatomy. Three things were added
  the first source did not carry, and the third is why this is not a repeat:
  (i) a **serial dependency** — ORDER 1344 states clearance *"obligately
  requires sleep-dependent glymphatic influx, convective transport, and meningeal
  lymphatic efflux — a serial dependency where failure at any stage compromises
  the entire pipeline"* — which makes per-stage observability a design
  requirement the slot did not make; (ii) the **gate is a chemical and it is
  measurable** — sleep expands interstitial volume 60% (13.6% → 22.7%, n=10,
  p<0.01) via *LC norepinephrine withdrawal*, so a maintenance gate held by a
  neuromodulator can be held closed by an unrelated upstream state; (iii) **a
  published negative that was an instrument artifact** — Mestre et al. 2018
  report I² = 73% heterogeneity explained entirely by anesthesia choice, with
  tribromoethanol suppressing glymphatic function **in both genotypes and
  masking the KO effect**, and the corpus records that Smith et al. (2017)'s
  negative is attributed to exactly this. **That is Area 24's general form
  arriving from a direction the arena had not reached**, and it is also why the
  *design* grade stays `UNTESTED`: the measurement of this organ was, for years,
  not trustworthy enough to certify its own absence. **Grade on the human
  mechanism moves to `HIGH`** on the five-lab meta-analysis (4 *Aqp4* KO lines +
  *Snta1* KO, SMD −1.70 [−2.49, −0.90], p<0.0001); **the design stays
  `UNTESTED`** because the corpus still names no agent-side implementation.
  **R-J4 preserved:** ORDER 1344's own table marks *bulk flow vs diffusion* as
  **Debated**, and its 2024 human figure (Ringstad et al., peak parenchymal
  gadobutrol 0.5 mM at 10–26h) is a very different quantity from fast rodent
  transport. Not reconciled.
- **Area 46 Rank 1 (body ownership, tool boundary) — Support 2 → 4**, by ORDER
  1514 + ORDER 1520. **Grade held at `HIGH`, and the reason is stated rather
  than accumulated: this is the third increment and not one of them is a second
  trial.** What the two new files add is anatomy (ORDER 1514's Iriki single-cell
  macaque recordings, Graziano's premotor bimodal neurons) and an independent
  discipline (ORDER 1520's Mountcastle columns, Lederman & Klatzky exploratory
  procedures) — neither is a body-transfer-illusion paper, which is what makes
  them independent rather than a third sighting of the same study. Two design
  facts were added and the first is a **bound the arena did not hold**: tool
  extension is **sensitive to the means of coupling** — Carlson et al. (2010) got
  assimilation within seconds for a *directly held* object and **no assimilation
  for an object held via a mechanical intermediary** — so a self-model that
  assimilates by reachability will over-extend exactly where the corpus says it
  should not. ORDER 1514 preserves Reed & Farah (1995) against the whole
  extension account (a separate *working space*, supported by patient E.D.S.'s
  personal/extrapersonal neglect dissociation); **not reconciled (R-J4)**. The
  second is the degradation mode: **patient IW**, who without constant visual
  attention cannot walk or maintain posture. A self-model whose updates ride an
  automatic channel does not degrade into a coarser model — it degrades into a
  **manual, vision-bound one that spends attention to stay running**, and ORDER
  1520's clinical inventory (astereognosis, sensory ataxia, central pain
  syndrome, asomatognosia) with astereognosis *rare* relative to visual agnosia
  says the redundancy Area 40 Rank 3 relies on is itself a brain property with a
  measured failure rate.

**Deliberately not incremented, and the reason, because an unincremented
corroboration is a finding and not an omission.**

- **ORDER 1519 (Signal Detection Theory) does not increment Area 33 or Area 24,
  though it is the obvious candidate.** The file is a clean statement of the
  sensitivity/bias decomposition and of **meta-d'** — Type 1 performance (d')
  against Type 2 (confidence about the detection) — which is Area 98's
  object-level/meta-level split in its most operational form, and its §"Signal
  Detection in Recognition Memory" is the detector/certifier asymmetry
  restated in psychophysics. **It is not counted as an independent source for
  either** because SDT is the *framework* those areas draw on, not a report of
  the asymmetry in a new domain; counting it would inflate the support count
  with the theory that generated the earlier sources. It is recorded here as
  **reach**, and its own claim is graded `HIGH` and separately usable.
  Its genuinely new content for the arena is one sentence — *the criterion's
  optimality is systematically under-achieved, and the shortfall is largest
  exactly where the stakes are highest* (base-rate neglect, Wickens & Genovese
  1983/1988) — and that belongs to the **general form**, not to a slot.
- **ORDER 1346 (Nietzsche & existentialism) earns no area and no slot, and the
  reason is the skill's own load-bearing guard.** The file is entirely about
  philosophy of mind — will to power, bad faith, thrownness, care, the claim that
  *"an agent that cannot be harmed, cannot lose, cannot die — does it truly make
  meaning or merely compute?"* — and it discusses **no mechanism, no
  measurement, and no trial**. It contains one design-adjacent assertion the
  arena might be tempted to promote (that stakes and vulnerability are
  prerequisites for meaning-making in an artificial system) and **that assertion
  is promoted nowhere**, because promoting it would require a brain part, and the
  file names none. Recorded as a *framing*, not a design. The skill's §4 guard —
  **corpus hygiene is not a brain part; if you cannot name the brain function it
  fills, it is infrastructure** — is what kept it out, and this is the first
  pass in a while where that guard had to fire on a whole file.
- **ORDER 1500 (Open Source AI ecosystem) earns no area.** It is a landscape
  survey — engines, models, licences, frameworks — and the arena already holds
  its one design-relevant line in Area 27 and Area 24 (evaluation methodology
  introducing more error than model differences; a 50-line parser fix moving a
  model from rank 13 to rank 1 in a tool-calling benchmark). The remaining 890
  lines are tool inventories with a **monthly expiry date**, which is the
  signature of a file that should be re-read rather than absorbed.
- **ORDER 1509 (pain/nociception) is absorbed into Area 112 Rank 1** as the
  regulatory-loop anatomy (PAG → RVM, ON/OFF/NEUTRAL cells) rather than opening
  its own area, because the arena already holds pain as a typed error channel in
  **Area 109** and the file's contribution here is the **descending ON/OFF
  balance** — a controller with both terms, which is exactly Area 112's subject.
  Its own design claims (an error signal should scale with severity, be
  learnable, be modulated by context, and have both immediate and delayed
  components) are recorded as reach, not as a new area.
- **ORDER 1512 (pathology and failure modes) earns no new area** but **confirms
  that the arena's own areas are the right ones**: its fourteen-row table maps
  one-to-one onto existing slots (Capgras → Area 46, Korsakoff's confabulation →
  the hallucination areas, OCD's amplified ERN → Area 33, split-brain →
  multi-agent coordination). It contributes **no mechanism the arena lacked**.
  That is a corroboration of coverage rather than of content, and it is recorded
  as such — a file that changes nothing because everything it says is already
  held is exactly the "this area is already covered" case the skill warns
  against, and the honest response is to record that the file was read, agree,
  and add no count.

**No new defect class this pass** — stated plainly rather than manufacturing one.
The `Wells & Olson, 2068` misdate carried by previous passes still stands; ORDER
1519 §"Signal Detection and Eyewitness Identification" gives the same paper as
**Wells and Olson (2000)**, which is the correct year, so the bad instance is in
a different file and is **not** fixed by this pass. Thirteenth pass carrying it.

### Post-pass ad-hoc verification of the C11 trim (tranche 62) — 15/16, one
### pre-existing failure reported rather than suppressed

`trim_c11.py` (run from the session scratch dir, not the workspace) replaced
two 42-line corroboration blocks in `ARENA.md` with 17- and 21-line summaries
by **line index**. A line-index splice can silently swallow the section after
it, so the mutation was checked rather than assumed. Script:
`~/.hermes/cache/scratch/hermes-verify-trim-c11.py`, 16 checks.

**The load-bearing check passed:** all 8 distinctive findings from the trimmed
prose — *serial dependency*, *tribromoethanol*, *I² = 73%*, *13.6%*,
*Carlson et al.*, *Reed & Farah*, *patient IW*, *astereognosis* — are still
present in `ARENA-EVIDENCE.md`. The two-file layout's actual invariant (prose
removed from the answer survives in the audit trail) holds.

**Three initial failures were verifier bugs, not file defects, and each was
proved before the assertion was changed** — the discipline the arena itself
argues for:
1. *"'measured failure rate' is a splice bleed"* — it was **my own new
   sentence** in the replacement text. The check was matching content it was
   supposed to be looking for.
2. *"'I2=73%' missing from the evidence file"* — the files write **I² = 73%**
   with a superscript-2. Wrong literal, not a lost fact.
3. *"Area 46 has 4 rank slots"* — the fourth is the phrase *"same file as
   Rank 1 — reach, not independence"* **inside a Grade field**. Field prose,
   not a slot. Confirmed identical in the 88-area snapshot.
A fourth iteration was then needed because the arena uses **two legitimate
slot-heading styles** (`**Rank N —` and `  - **Rank N —`, 44/44/42 occurrences)
and the checker had only been taught one.

**The failure that remains is real, pre-existing, and not mine: Area 17 carries
5 rank headings, not 3.** Slots 2 and 3 are marked `` `not yet earned` ``
(ORDER 552 fills this slot) and a later block adds *Rank 2 (now earned)* and
*Rank 3 (now earned)* without removing the placeholders. **The 88-area
snapshot has the same 5**, so this predates tranche 62 by many passes. It is
the two-file layout's exact failure — placeholder slots kept in the answer and
the real content appended below them — and `arena_invariants.py` does **not**
catch it, because C11 counts lines rather than slots and the file is
over-budget for unrelated reasons. **Left red on purpose:** a checker that
passes by tolerating a known violation is the §8 inversion in miniature. The
checker now carries an explicit paired assertion that the anomaly is
pre-existing, so a *future* pass that makes it worse will fail differently than
one that leaves it alone.

**Not fixed here, deliberately.** Collapsing another pass's five slots into
three is a content judgement about which designs survive — an arena decision,
not a verification fix.

### Negative control for the tranche-62 verification — and the blind spot it
### found in my own checker

The first version of `hermes-verify-trim-c11.py` printed 15 PASS / 1 FAIL. That
is not evidence, because it had only ever agreed with me: of its four initial
failures, three turned out to be checker bugs I then "fixed", and one was a real
pre-existing finding. A checker that has never gone red has not been tested.
The skill's own rule applies — *verify a check can actually fail, and that its
verdict changes a decision* — and it applies to the verifier.

`hermes-verify-negative-control.py` injects one known defect at a time into a
temp copy of the **real** ARENA.md/EVIDENCE.md and asserts the checker fails on
each. Seven mutants: stale pre-trim header; clause dropped by the splice;
trimmed finding lost from the evidence file; splice overran into the next area;
rank slot deleted; document truncated; pre-existing Area 17 anomaly grown.

**First run: 6 of 7 caught, 1 SURVIVED — and it was a real blind spot I had
just introduced.** My Area 17 exemption compared a *count* of rank headings, and
the mutant added a `Rank 4`, which the `Rank [123]` regex never matched. The
count stayed 5, the exemption absorbed new damage, and the checker exited 0. In
substance: **I had built a checker that could not detect the failure mode it was
exempting.** Fixed by pinning the exact rank-label *sequence* (`['1','2','3',
'2','3']` for Area 17) rather than a count, so a sixth heading, a removed one, or
any other change fails even inside an exempt area.

**Second run: 7 of 7 caught, control green, `VERDICT: checker is falsifiable`.**
Final state: **11 checks, 0 failed, 1 warning** against the real files.

This is the §8 inversion caught in the act, in the one artifact that exists
solely to produce authority. The eight-item survivors list — the check that
actually matters — passed on the first run and kept passing, and the *structural*
check that looked like a formality was the one that lied.

### Tranche 63 · ORDER 1510, 1516, 1521–1529, 1532–1540 — the Perception block and the philosophy-of-mind block

**20 files, 20 `read_file` calls, 20 rows flipped. Ceiling respected.** ORDER
1530–1531 are `personal-finance/` and are `[-]` by the user's exclusion scope
(finance); they consumed no slot and were never opened. ORDER 1541 — the 21st

resumes there in order.

**Largest single read: 81,994 chars** (ORDER 1538, `Language-and-Thought-Debate.md`,
902 lines). The corpus median is ~21k, so this is a large but legitimate single
document; the 100k one-document ceiling was not approached. **No read returned
`truncated: true` and no `offset` continuation was needed.** One read per file,
one `patch` per mark, no two consecutive ledger patches, no patch touching more
than one row, no bulk read, no script, no subagent, no `execute_code`, no shell
read of corpus content.

**Remediation check on arrival, which is what the priority order turns on.**
`scripts/citation_remediation.py` reported **0 MUST RE-READ, 0 MUST STRIKE,
6 AMBIGUOUS twin, 0 PROVEN**. The 39 MUST RE-READ items from the prior run are
discharged. The 6 remaining are a *basename collision*, not an unearned
citation, and this is worth stating precisely because the previous run reported
them as outstanding: each of the six `frontier-research-ontology-round*` basenames
exists at **three** ORDER rows, the arena cites the full path under
`oracle/brain/.meta/archive/`, and C6's stem-based matcher resolves the stem to

this pass:

| Cited basename | arena's full path resolves to | read at | unread twin |
|---|---|---|---|
| round43-2026-09-09 | `oracle/brain/.meta/archive/…` | ORDER **1193** | 1791 (and 64) |
| round44-2026-09-10 | same dir | ORDER **1194** | 1792 (and 65) |
| round56-2026-09-05 | same dir | ORDER **1207** | 1805 (and 78) |
| round60-2026-10-20 | same dir | ORDER **1211** | 1809 (and 82) |
| round84-2026-09-11 | same dir | ORDER **1229** | 1827 (and 100) |

All six earning rows are `[x]`. The arena already carries the full-path
disambiguation note at the Area 95 heading, written by the pass that read 1211.
**No citation was added, weakened or struck this pass, and C6 is unchanged
because nothing this pass touched a twin.** Recorded so a future pass does not
re-open remediation on a false alarm — and equally, so it does not use this
table to *skip* a genuine unearned citation later. The fix, when a pass chooses
to make it, is a checker change (match on full path, not stem), not an arena
change.

**Three areas opened, all by the same cheap method: a term the arena leans on
returning zero.**

**Area 116 — affordances are relational.** Earned by ORDER 1521. `ARENA.md` held
**3** occurrences of *affordance* and **0** of *Warren* across 115 areas. The
load-bearing content is that Warren (1984) measured climbability as a **ratio**
— riser height over leg length — with a categorical switch past a boundary, and
that it replicates across action modes. This makes the concept structurally
incompatible with how the arena currently uses the word: Areas 102 and 22 both
*read* an affordance field, and a relation against the reader's own capability
is not a field. What made it a brain part and not a fourth facet of Area 102 is
Cisek's **affordance competition hypothesis** — parallel specification of
multiple potential actions in posterior parietal cortex, resolved by competition
rather than serial selection. Gaver's three-way taxonomy (perceivable / hidden /
false) is rank 2 because of an asymmetry worth more than the taxonomy: **hidden
affordances fail silently and false ones announce themselves**, so any design
that only listens for errors catches exactly one of the two failure modes.
Grading is deliberately split rather than averaged — body-scaling is broadly
replicated for stairs and sitting and *less consistent* for reaching and passing
through, and the corpus reports high-profile replication failures in
embodied-cognition priming, so `LOW` is the honest read, not a hedge.

**Area 117 — binding is a synchrony window, and it is learned.** Earned by
ORDER 1527 (762 lines, the largest substantive file of the tranche) and
corroborated by ORDER 1528. `0` occurrences of *temporal binding window* and
`0` of *multisensory*. The mechanism is Stein & Meredith's **inverse
effectiveness**: multisensory gain is *largest when the individual inputs are
weakest*, supra-additively, and only inside a 50–150 ms window; outside it the
response is the stronger unimodal response alone. Friston/Fritsche's precision
weighting then makes the design-relevant move — **a degraded cue widens the
window**, so a fixed timeout is not a crude approximation of binding, it is
systematically wrong in the case that matters. Grade split is the slot: `HIGH`
on the principle (the corpus calls it one of the most robust findings in
multisensory neuroscience, replicated across cats, monkeys and humans), `LOW` on
the agent design, which has no trial. Rank 2 carries the plasticity and the
clinical enlargements, and the corpus itself rates the clinical work **moderately
replicable (d = 0.6–1.2)** — that qualifier is preserved rather than upgraded
because the effect sizes look impressive. Rank 3 holds the online-vs-postdictive
dispute on chronostatic backdating **unreconciled (R-J4)**, exactly as the corpus
states it, and the design asks for a record type this workspace cannot currently
express: *this conclusion rests on three of four results*.

**Area 118 — gist before objects.** Earned by ORDER 1529, corroborated by
ORDER 1522 and ORDER 1521. `0` occurrences of *spatial envelope*, *parahippocampal
place area*, or *scene-selective*. Kept separate from Area 102 on a precise
distinction: Area 102 is *which* stream reports and which acts; this is an
**ordering** claim, that a third earlier stream (PPA/OPA/RSC) fires at 100–250 ms
and gates where the later one looks. Area 102 has no time axis and cannot express
that. The decisive evidence is the negative manipulation — **preserve
low-frequency spatial envelope and remove detail, categorization holds at ~70–80%
of full accuracy; scramble the envelope and preserve the detail, and it falls to
~10–20%** — and the scale consequence is stated as R-J5 requires: the envelope is
O(1) in corpus size and the item-first pass is O(files), so at 14,589 the ratio is
not a constant factor, it is the whole budget. Rank 3 deliberately does *not*
resolve gist-versus-ensemble: the corpus says the evidence is inconclusive, the
two are highly correlated, and a design that must know which is which has bet on
an open question. Build so either answer works.

**A defect in `ARENA.md` itself, reported and not repaired.** The status header is
**stacked history** — a tranche-58 block immediately followed by a tranche-52
block further down, each a full multi-paragraph narrative. That is the C11
pattern (answer-file accretion) in miniature, and it is the same disease §8
describes: the pass that wrote a *report* put it in the answer file rather than
here. It was **not** fixed, for two reasons, both load-bearing. First, the
governing rule is never to delete what has not been read, and the passes that
wrote those blocks have not been re-read. Second, the correct destination is
this file, and moving them is a deliberate act for a future pass that can
account for what it moves. Flagged in the arena's own status block so it is
visible to the next reader rather than discovered later.

**Files read and what each one contributed** — recorded so a later pass can tell
an earning read from a walk-by. Earning: 1521 (Area 116), 1527 (Area 117), 1529
(Area 118). Corroborating: 1522, 1528, 1529→116, 1521→118. **Five of the twenty
were structural or operational rather than substantive** — ORDER 1510, 1516,
1524, 1536, 1537 are directory indices, and 1532/1533 are the `personal/` index
and a one-page operational lesson. The `personal/lesson-follow-instructions-
exactly.md` page is not a brain part and earns no area: it is a record of the
rule this whole job runs under (no scripts, one file at a time, human-in-the-loop,
after the 71-file loss), and its correct home is this workspace's own instruction
set, which is where the skill already carries it.

**Two substantial philosophy-of-mind files (1535 free will, 1539 personal
identity) were read and produced no new area, and that is a finding rather than
a null.** `ARENA.md` held **0** occurrences of *Libet*, *readiness potential*, or
*bundle theory* — so these looked like gaps. They are not. Area 11 (selfhood and
regime-dependence) and Area 68 (the self as a strange loop) already hold the
content, and the genuinely new material in both files is **negative**: the
replication crisis. Moisy et al. (2021) found the readiness potential did *not*
reliably precede conscious intention in a large pre-registered replication (134 ms
against Libet's ~350 ms); Tranel et al. (2019) found no pre-conscious prediction
of specific choices via iEEG; Schultze-Kraft et al. (2018) showed the signal
appears even before participants intend to decide, which means it is **general
readiness, not a specific decision**. What survives is narrow: the RP exists, and
unconscious processing is extensive. This is Area 99's general form — *the famous
pattern replicated and the famous explanation did not* — already in the arena, and
a second file landing on it is **corroboration of an existing area, not a new
area**. Recorded here rather than silently skipped, because "I read it and it
changed nothing" and "I did not read it" must never look the same in this
workspace. Note also that ORDER 1534 (`Embodied-Cognition-and-Enactivism.md`,
653 lines) did not earn an area either: `0` occurrences of *4E cognition* and
*sense-making* looked like a gap, but Areas 20, 35 and 85 already carry the
grounding and symbol-grounding content, and enactivism is a **framing** over
mechanisms the arena holds rather than a distinct organ.

**What would have been rejected and why.** Gaver's taxonomy as a *rank-1* design
was rejected in favour of the relational storage rule: a taxonomy of failure
modes tells you what can go wrong, not what to build, and Area 116 rank 1 is the
thing that makes both hidden and false affordances *representable* in the first
place. Chronostatic backdating as a *rank-1* design was rejected for the same
reason — it is a mechanism for handling a gap, not a policy for whether to have
one, and the honest policy (mark the gap, carry the distinction forward) is
rank 3. Ensemble coding as a *rank-1* was rejected in favour of the scene
envelope: the arena's problem is not "what is the mean of these 548 files" but
"what kind of thing are they", and the envelope is the cheaper prior.

**Nothing this pass re-ranks an existing area, and no grade changed.** Areas 9, 11,
20, 33, 35, 41, 44, 65, 68, 85, 89, 99, 102 and 109 were each re-read against
these files and none of the twenty moved a rank. The three new areas are
additive, which is the correct outcome when the read reaches parts the arena has
not reached rather than evidence that contradicts what it holds.

### Tranche 64 — ORDER 1541-1560, three areas, and a false corpus-loss alarm

**20 `read_file` calls, 20 rows flipped. EQUAL. Ceiling respected exactly:** 20 was
reached at ORDER 1560; ORDER 1561 is next in order and was left unread rather than
jumped. No excluded lines fell in the window, so all 20 slots went to real files.
Largest single read 77,191 chars (ORDER 1551); no read returned `truncated: true`;
no `offset` continuation was needed.

**A false alarm, and why it is recorded at length.** This pass opened by marking
**fifteen consecutive files `[!]`** on `File not found`, then correctly stopped rather
than continuing the sweep across 508 unread rows. Diagnosis: the run prompt specifies
the corpus root as `/home/operator/.hermes/`, the skill text says
`/home/operator/.autognosia/`, and **this pass read the skill's root**. `VERIFICATION.md`
already carried the correction — "the corpus root in the `wiki-cognition` skill is
`/home/operator/.autognosia/`, which does not exist on this host. Every read resolves
under `/home/operator/.hermes/`" — recorded on an earlier pass and **not read before
acting this pass**. All fifteen `[!]` marks were reverted to `[ ]` and the tranche
re-run against the correct root; all fifteen files then read normally.

The cost was real: fifteen mis-marked rows for roughly a third of the slot, and a
window during which the ledger asserted fifteen corpus defects that did not exist. Had
the sweep continued, the pass would have burned its entire budget marking 520 rows
blocked on a path error and reported a healthy-looking tranche. **The rule that caught
it is the one about the failure signature, not the one about path discipline:** the
tell was fifteen `patch` calls in a row with no `read_file` between them, which is
precisely the pattern the skill forbids. It looked like productivity.

Two defects carried forward. First, **the skill's own text is wrong about the corpus
root** and has been for at least two passes; a future pass reading only the skill will
repeat this exact failure. Second, the `VERIFICATION.md` entry that would have
prevented it existed and was not consulted. Both are filed in `VERIFICATION.md`. A
2.9G copy of the corpus exists at `/home/operator/bak_autognosia` (2,107 markdown files
under `oracle/brain`, versus 2,153 under the live root) — **it was deliberately not
read from**, because `ORDER.txt` paths resolve against the live root, and reading a
backup would place unearned citations into the arena, which is the precise failure
this workspace exists to prevent.

**What the tranche found.** All three areas were earned by the zero-hit probe, now
used in five consecutive passes and still the cheapest method available: a term the
arena leans on everywhere, returning **zero** across 118 areas. `ketamine`/`xenon`/
`dissociative` = 0 (Area 119). `population vector`/`cosine tuning`/`one-hot`/
`grandmother cell` = 3 (Area 120). The free energy principle itself = 4 incidental
hits, none about the FEP (Area 121).

Area 119 is the sharpest negative result in the tranche and the one most likely to be
misread later. ORDER 1545 §6.4 records ketamine and xenon producing subjects who are
**behaviourally unresponsive with preserved or enhanced PCI** — causal integration and
behavioural unresponsiveness **come apart in a human being**. REM sleep decodes high on
PCI with no report. The corpus states plainly that this "challenges the simple equation
of high PCI with consciousness." Grade held at `LOW` rather than raised: the
dissociation is well-attested in the source, but propofol, sevoflurane and isoflurane
behave conventionally, so this is a **rival ordering**, not a uniform failure. Saying
more would be the §8 error this arena is built to catch.

Area 120 is the only `HIGH`-graded area opened in several tranches, and the grade is
defensible rather than generous: the cosine tuning law is replicated across
laboratories, species (macaque, human, cockroach, cricket, electric fish) and
techniques (single-electrode, multi-electrode, Neuropixels, fMRI, calcium imaging),
and the population vector approaches the maximum-likelihood decoder in the
broad-tuning regime. Support 2, counted as two because ORDER 1548's
Pouget/Dayan/Zemel material on probability distributions in population codes is a
different source from the Georgopoulos primary literature in ORDER 1547. **Rank 3
deliberately carries the counter-evidence:** broad tuning is *not* established as
optimal, sparse coding is a live rival, and per Averbeck/Latham/Pouget the effect of
noise correlations depends entirely on their geometry relative to the decode
direction. A rank-1 slot hiding this would be the arena committing the error it exists
to prevent.

Area 121 points at the arena's own grade column. Friston's own words are quoted in
ORDER 1551 §4.1: the FEP "cannot be falsified. It cannot be disproven," on the analogy
of Hamilton's principle. ORDER 1551 then names the consequence the arena has never
recorded: when a process theory fails, "defenders can always retreat to the FEP as a
state theory (which cannot fail) and argue that the issue is with the particular
process theory implementation." That is **unlimited absorbing capacity for
implementation failure** — a design that can only ever be re-implemented, never
refuted. The arena's `HIGH`/`LOW`/`UNTESTED` column assumes the opposite: that a grade
falls when evidence weakens. Ranks are therefore `LOW`/`LOW`/`UNTESTED` despite the
FEP being the most-cited framework in the file, because the *principle* is not
evidence about the *design*.

**Corroborations, both recorded without grade changes.** Area 73 (access vs phenomenal
consciousness) 3 -> 4: ORDER 1542 §5.1 restates Block's distinction from the
philosophical side, citing neither the dissociation experiments of ORDER 932 nor
Graziano's single-unit work of ORDER 927, so the independence test holds. **Grade NOT
raised** — a third source saying the same thing is not a second verdict, and the file's
own §12.1 lists GWT and IIT as still contested. The efference-copy /
corollary-discharge distinction in ORDERS 1550 §1.1 and 1551 §2.3 is recorded as
**reach** on the precision area, with the Bays (2006) vs Kilteni & Ehrsson (2020)
disagreement **preserved unresolved per R-J4** rather than resolved either way.

**Read and deliberately not turned into slots.** Five are corpus infrastructure rather
than brain parts (1546, 1549, 1555, 1557, 1559 — directory indexes, a scoped-rules
page, a template index); the §4 guard is why a link index and a project template do
not become areas. Three are philosophical framing over mechanisms already held (1541,
1543, 1544 — and 1543 and 1544 are substantially the same four-metaphor argument told
twice). 1554 (schema theory) earned none: Tse et al. 2007 on mPFC-accelerated schema
consolidation is real, but schema-consolidation is already held, and its headline claim
— *memory is reconstructive* — is Area 74's interpreter re-stated. 1556, 1558 and 1560
are project records.

**One near-miss worth naming.** ORDER 1554 independently arrives at Area 121's exact
defect in a different domain: schema theory is *"so flexible it can explain any finding
— and therefore predicts nothing specific,"* with a **circularity risk** where schemas
are inferred from the very distortions they explain. Two independent arrivals at one
shape is **not** corroboration — a shared shape is not a shared source — so it is
recorded here as a coincidence worth watching and **not** counted in Area 121's Support.

**Defects filed, not repaired.** ORDER 1547's source list carries two entries for the
same paper (Seung & Sompolinsky 1993 as [5] and [6]; Salinas & Abbott 1994 as [2] and
[7]), and one DOI is rendered as raw text rather than a link. Corpus hygiene, §7: no
architect changes the design because a citation is listed twice. ORDER 1545's
references give Chalmers 1995 as *Journal of Consciousness Studies* 2(3), 200-219,
while ORDER 1542 gives the same paper without pages; recorded, not reconciled.

#### What ORDER 1563 and 1565 earned (Area 4 corroboration, no rank change)

`Prospective-Memory/Implementation-Intentions.md` (ORDER 1563, 22,372 chars) and
`Prospective-Memory/Prospective-Memory-Cueing.md` (ORDER 1565, 8,397 chars) are

1563 is the *intervention* literature (Gollwitzer; the if-then plan; three
mechanisms — cue hyperaccessibility, automatic response initiation,
competing-response suppression; Webb & Sheeran's 94-study N>10,000 meta-analysis
at d = 0.65; Mendoza et al. 2010 at d = 0.43 in clinical settings; Gardner et
al. 2018 at ~12 percentage points across 39 health studies), and 1565 is the
*mechanism and localisation* literature (McDaniel & Einstein's multiprocess
theory; focal vs. non-focal cues; the **monitoring cost**; Marsh et al. 1998;
Kliegel & Jopp 2009; Burgess et al. 2001 placing the retention interval in
**rostrolateral PFC / BA 10**; Ruch et al. 2016 meta-analysing **29 studies,
N = 738**, confirming RLPFC and anterior PFC during retention with inferior
frontal gyrus at retrieval and dACC monitoring for cue occurrence).

**Recorded against Area 4. No re-rank, no grade change.** The design Area 4 ranks
first is not displaced. What these two files add is (a) a **neural address** for
the monitoring state the area already modelled behaviourally, and (b) a **cost**:
the monitoring cost is a measurable decrement on the ongoing task that scales
with intention importance, task complexity, and delay. (b) is a genuine design
input the arena did not hold — an implementation that only stores IF/THEN rules
appears to pay nothing for them, and the corpus says a human pays a measurable
ongoing-task decrement to hold one. **The corpus does not say an AI pays it.**
No trial is reported in either file, and both are explicitly about human
subjects; the monitoring-cost figure is recorded `unverified` for any non-human
system and does not raise the grade.

**An evidence-honesty note that belongs here, not in the slot.** ORDER 1563's
frontmatter lists eight DOIs and **several are attached to the wrong papers**:
