same six pre-existing ontology basename twins (1791/1792/1805/1809/1827/1828)
that C6 has reported since tranche 75, and **zero added this pass**. The
priority-order gate was therefore clear before the tranche opened, which is the
only reason a new tranche started at all.

**The window is one cron programme.** All nineteen files are generated rounds of
the same `frontier-research-*` ontology-research lane: identical ten mandated
topics, identical `confidence: high` frontmatter, identical `verified: []`,
`stale_after` three months out. This is the **ninth consecutive tranche** on
this lane (67, 68, 70–76). **Of twenty files the arena moved for one.** That
ratio is the honest yield and it is also the reason the one result matters: a
lane this uniform rewards reading for the *mechanism* in the outliers, not for
the topic coverage, which is identical in every file.

**Area 131 — consolidation and the write-permission of identity.** Earned by
ORDER 1772 §3, arXiv **2607.01988** (*Episodic-to-Semantic Consolidation Without
Identity Drift*), the only section in that ten-source survey describing a
*memory architecture* rather than a knowledge structure.

**The silence, and its two near-misses.** Sixteen probes against `ARENA.md`
across 130 areas returned **0**: *identity hash*, *identity drift*, *byte-equal*,
*identity-preserving*, *identity substrate*, *self-substrate*, *immutable self*,
*derivation function*, *deterministic consolidation*, *unproductive planner*,
*planner attempt*, *who changed*, *identity invariant*, *amnesia identity*,
*self survives loss*, *persist despite*. Three of those are the arena's own
highest-frequency words (*consolidation*, *identity*, *self*), which is what
makes this a silence in the arena's working vocabulary rather than in an exotic
register — the failure mode the §4 guard exists to prevent, where a probe only
succeeds by searching a term the file never uses.

The first near-miss: *amnesia* returns **6** and *Wearing* returns **16**, and
every hit is the wrong sense. `HM` — 161 hits — is the **HM Treasury** Green Book,
a municipal-budget dataset. *Wearing* is the verb: *"wearing a hat"*, *"a
heuristic wearing a citation"*, *"degradation-that-hides wearing a different
hat"*, *"an asserted rule wearing a verified label"*. **Patient H.M. and Clive
Wearing are absent from this arena under any reading.** The amnesia
*mechanisms* are present and good (consolidation failure, reactivation,
anisomycin-induced erasure at lines 884, 1066, 3068; the retrograde gradient at
8225; the ~50% bilateral volume loss case at 12219) — the arena knows how
memory is erased and has never met anyone who survived it.

The second near-miss: *personal identity* returns **7**, entirely inside Areas
11, 15 and 68. Those areas ask **what identity is made of** and **how it
recurses**. None asks **what a consolidation step is permitted to write**. A
constitutional hierarchy and a write-permission boundary are different
questions, and a pass that had stopped at the phrase would have logged a fourth
arrival at Area 11 and lost the area.

**Why the amnesic dissociation earns the slot.** The load-bearing fact is
*directional*: content loss does not entail self loss. H.M. and Clive Wearing
lost the capacity to acquire declarative content and retained a continuous,
socially individuated self. If the self survives total content loss in the only
system we can measure, then **content and self are carried by different
substrates**, and a consolidation operation that writes both is a design error
*even when it works* — which is the more uncomfortable half, because the arena
has been treating it as the one operation that legitimately rewrites the system.

**What the corpus actually claims, and what I did with it.** ORDER 1772 §3 states
consolidation as a deterministic derivation `f : M^ep → M^sem` into a separately
addressable semantic layer, with the manifest rule that **the identity hash
reads only the agent's manifest, not the semantic layer** — the agent stays
byte-equal across its operational lifetime while its knowledge grows. The
reported effect is a mean **79.8%** reduction in unproductive planner attempts
(95% BCa CI [78.0, 81.5], 10 seeds, against a calibrated Bayesian-shrunk
baseline). I graded the design `LOW` and the displaced default `UNSUCCESSFUL`,
and **filed the 79.8% as `unverified`** (V-76.2): it is one paper, one task, one
domain, reported second-hand through a survey, and §8 is explicit that an
external figure in a cron-generated synthesis does not earn HIGH because the file
asserting it is confident. The file is `confidence: high` with an empty
`verified:` block. That is §8's inversion in miniature, one clause above.

**The complementary source, and why it is not a corroboration.** ORDER 1776 §8
(EpisTwin, arXiv 2603.06290) gives **deterministic deletion** — a symbolic graph
permits provable excision where a dense vector store cannot, *"almost
impossible with purely neural or dense-vector approaches"*. This is a **second
source, not a second confirmation**: it establishes a different property in the
same family (revocable-by-construction rather than immutable-by-construction),
so it becomes **Rank 2**, not an increment to Rank 1's support count. Per the
skill's distinction, incrementing Support here would have manufactured a
consensus of one idea. Its PersonalQA-71-100 benchmark (71 personal data
streams, 100 queries) is recorded as the evaluation substrate it ships with.

**Zero re-ranks, zero grade changes, zero citations removed.** Nothing in this
window met an existing slot's bar. The candidates that came close and were
**declined, with the reason**, so the next pass does not re-litigate them:

- **Fluency survival** (ORDER 1767 §6, arXiv 2509.04796) — *prose survives the
  loss of the rare facts it was carrying*; cosine similarity, Hill-Shannon
  diversity and Hellinger distance; partial recovery from RAG **only when the
  corpus is human-produced**. Sixteen probes returned 0, so this is a real
  silence. **Declined as a slot**: the mechanism is a property of *training on
  recursively generated data*, which is a statement about a corpus, not about a
  brain part. §4's guard — *"if you cannot name the brain function it fills, it
  is infrastructure"* — applies. The transfer to the arena is filed as V-76.1
  because it is a real constraint on any design that trains on its own output.
- **Illusive accuracy** (ORDER 1768 §3.3, arXiv 2604.08603) — 93.82% accuracy
  against a **tool-chain F1 of 24–36%** for baselines: the same models are right
  about *what* and wrong about *how to get it*, and the aggregate number hides

  enforcement gap*) already holds the belief→action step and its enforcement
  requirement, and 139 uses of *dissociation* across the arena mean a sixth
  phrasing of "these two come apart" is reach, not a new part. Filed as a
  **candidate measurement** for Area 19 in V-76.3 — the number is a *metric*
  lesson, and metrics belong to the evidence file.
- **Ontology prompt injection beats blanket injection** (ORDER 1780 §7,
  CEUR 2025) and **injection helps larger models more** — a real, cheap,
  contradicting result. Declined: it is an *engineering* result about injection

- **The Ontological Flatness diagnosis** (ORDER 1769 §8, PhilArchive
  preprint) — Lakatosian hard-core reading of alignment research, with the sharp
  claim that *deceptive alignment is not merely hard to solve within a monistic
  framework but partly constituted by it*. **The best argument in the window and
  it earns no slot**, because it is a critique of a research programme rather
  than a mechanism a system should have. Recorded here because a future pass

**What the window does corroborate, and how it was recorded.** Seven papers
recur across files already read in earlier tranches — OntoExtend (2607.17963),
G-reasoner (2509.24276), D-Mem (2603.18631), SYNAPSE/HeLa-Mem (2601.02744,
2604.16839), Categorical AI Phenomenology (2608.20420), OAK+MEND (2605.29168),
Episodic-Semantic Scientific Agents (2605.17625), FAOS (2604.00555). **No
Support count was incremented for any of them**, per the skill's same-source
rule: a file quoting a paper an existing slot already cites confirms *reach*,
not an independent source. Nine consecutive tranches of one lane will keep
quoting the same twenty papers, and an arena that incremented on re-mention
would report Support 40 on designs built from four ideas. This is the trap the
independence rule exists for, and it is worth stating that **the count of files
read and the count of sources earned are different numbers.**

the word, not the word.

**And the gap was not on the to-do list either.** This is the part worth naming.
`## BRAIN PARTS NOT YET COVERED` is supposed to hold every brain part the read
has surfaced. It held no line for conceptual absence. So the gap was invisible to
the mechanism designed to make gaps visible, and could only be found by probing
the arena's prose directly. A stale list line is wrong; an absent line is
invisible, and invisible is worse. Tranche 77's first finding is therefore about
the arena's own instrumentation, not about the corpus.

**Grade discipline, and the number I did not promote.** PhantomBench's headline
"no model exceeds 86.7% hallucination" is a strong number and it is
**load-bearing here**, so it is named with its source in the slot rather than
paraphrased. What is *not* promoted: the claim that "larger, reasoning, and
domain-specialised models hallucinate more" is recorded in the rank-1
justification as part of the benchmark's reported findings and is explicitly
marked as not independently replicated in the read corpus. It is a size-paradox
claim in a literature that has spent two years arguing that bigger is better; it
will be load-bearing if confirmed and embarrassing if not, and one benchmark does
not settle it. Grade held at `LOW` for exactly that reason.

**What was declined, and why.**

- **Knowledge-Boundary Law (ORDER 1790 §1).** Grounding raises accuracy only where
  the fact is out-of-training; the same pipeline gives |Δ| ≤ 3.4 on PrimeKG and
  +68 to +79 points on a synthetic counterfactual KG. This is a strong,
  counterintuitive, controlled result and it is **not new to the arena** —
  `ARENA.md` line 1422 already carries the disagreement with Area 8 Rank 1 as a
  preserved, unreconciled conflict. A second file restating the shape is reach,
  not support. Filed as V-77.1 with the one genuinely new number attached: the
  boundary is **training ∪ inferable from surface structure**, which the file
  derives from FDA novel-drug approvals where the model infers indications from
  INN nomenclature. That sharpening is recorded because it changes what a design
  should do — it moves the trigger from "is this fact novel" to "is this fact
  recoverable from naming convention," which is a much cheaper test.
- **Semantic drift bound O(N · ε_step) (ORDER 1785 §4, SSGM, arXiv 2603.11768).**
  A formal result that periodic reconciliation bounds expected drift independently
  of task horizon. Tempting, and not entered: it is a theorem about a system
  whose memory is a single summarisation chain, which is not this arena's shape,
  and the corpus contains no empirical confirmation of the bound. Recorded here
  so a later pass can find it if an SSGM-shaped design is ever proposed.
- **Linearization as the root of hallucination (ORDER 1794 Theme 2, SSR/SAS +
  AVA + NeuroGraph + Baobab).** A genuinely important convergence across four
  mechanisms — and the arena already holds the SSR/SAS quadrant analysis at
  meaningful detail. Not re-litigated without new evidence.
- **Ontology-as-harness (ORDER 1801 §6, KGC 2026).** "Representation, not
  prompting, is the leverage." A practitioner aphorism, not a trial. Useful
  framing, no evidence grade, and it names no brain part. Declined with reason.
- **Composability / order-independence (ORDER 1802 §2, DaoQL, arXiv 2607.17269).**
  94% order-independent double-update vs 45% for GPT-4o alone, with a stated
  architectural guarantee. **The corpus itself flags this number**: the file
  records a reviewer noting the 94% is "not auditable from the submitted text"
  and Theorem 1 is "closer to definitional than architectural." A headline its
  own file qualifies that heavily does not become a slot. The *design idea* —
  addressable, versioned knowledge with atomic read and delta semantics, which
  is what makes rollback and verified forgetting expressible at all — is
  genuinely good and is recorded here for a later pass that reads a primary
  source. Filed as V-77.4.

**Corroboration within the tranche that was real rather than notional.** The
four-valued warrant axis is the one case where two files from the same lane
nonetheless support the same area for a reason that is not restatement: PhantomBench
(1797) derives the axis empirically from 62,000+ constructed non-entities, and
DARKSIDE (1799) specifies the same four values — Warranted, Unattested,
Misattributed, Fabricated — as a design from a philosophy-of-ontology argument
about negative trails. Same four values, two unrelated methods, no shared source.
That is the second independent source rank 1 actually rests on, and it is why
rank 1 is `LOW` rather than `UNTESTED`.

**The 43% → 0% number, and why rank 2 is `LOW` and not `HIGH`.** The Semantic
Training Gap result (ORDER 1798 §3, arXiv 2605.11234) is the cleanest causal
number in the window: unconstrained tool parameters hallucinate domain
identifiers at 43%, ontology-grounded parameters at 0%, across six
manufacturing configurations. Two independent things keep it at `LOW`: the
experiment is **72 tool invocations on one model** (Qwen3-32B), and the corpus
contains no replication. An architect should still build on it — 43% to 0% is
not a rounding artefact — but the arena's own rule is that a grade is about
trials, and 72 invocations is one trial.

**Scale assumption (R-J5).** Area 132 is stated at the corpus's binding scale.
A four-valued existence status on every concept is one enum column; the cost is
in the negative-evidence *records*, which grow with search misses rather than with
knowledge. At 14,589 files a miss rate of even 1% is ~146 stored absences per
pass, which is why rank 2 exists at all: screening is the only affordable first
pass at that scale, and rank 1's record is what makes rank 2's silence
distinguishable. Neither slot depends on a human reading every record, and that
is the test the rule sets — a mechanism that only works because a person
inspects each miss is a habit, not a design.

**Zero re-ranks, zero grade changes, zero citations removed.** No settled ranking
was disturbed because no file in the window added support to a slot it did not
already hold, at a grade that would move it. The twenty files are a survey lane,
and a survey lane's characteristic output is reach.

### Tranche 78 — ORDER 1805–1824 · 20 files, all read whole · one area opened, two corroborated, no re-ranks

*Filed 2026-09-27. Append-only; nothing above this line was altered.*

**The window is one lane and that governs every count below.** All twenty files are
`frontier-research-ontology-round56` through `round75` — ten successive rounds of one
research programme, in which round N's "new directions" section is routinely a
restatement of round N−1 with new numbers attached. **A restatement is one source.**
Every support count in this tranche was assigned by asking whether the *underlying
paper* is new to the arena, not whether the *file* is new. Several of the
independent-source counts this pass added would have been inflated by a factor of
three to five on a file-level count, and the counts are the load-bearing field
under §3, so the distinction was made explicitly each time.

**The one area opened, and what made it non-obvious.** Area 135 (evidence
completion) was not a gap anyone had listed. The arena has spent many tranches
asserting that retrieval is the binding constraint, and it holds 135 areas of
rankings — yet it held **zero** occurrences of *RippleMem*, *evidence completion*,
*associative recollection*, or the loop itself. The two near-misses are why this
pass spent probes on them rather than opening immediately: Area 127 holds
"cue-dependent reconstruction" and Areas 8/86 hold "spreading activation", so the
phrase-level search looked covered. Neither is the claim. Area 127's cue-dependence
is about **which rules read a given string** — version drift, where the bytes are
identical and only the reader changed. Spreading activation is a **ranking signal**
over relations. RippleMem's claim is a third thing: a **control loop** in which
stage 1's output is demoted from answer-context to retrieval-input, and a
controller decides *whether to re-enter the search at all*. A ranked candidate set
has no way to say "this was not enough," and that is the structural blind spot the
area names.

**Why it is PROVISIONAL and the specific reason.** Three of twenty files, and
ORDER 1822 alone supplies both rank 1's storage half and rank 2 entirely. A single
file qualifying an area and filling two of its three slots is exactly the shape
that produced the original 39 unearned citations — a citation leaning on one
document. Recorded so a later pass can dissolve it honestly rather than inherit it
by inertia. **The dissolution test is written into the area:** read the remaining
`round7x` files on associative recollection, and either the sufficiency controller
is a distinct mechanism or it collapses into Areas 8/127.

**Two grades deliberately not raised, and why that is the finding rather than an
omission.**

- *RippleMem's sufficiency controller is the load-bearing component and is not
  separately ablated.* The paper reports +3.95% (LoCoMo) and up to +11.87%
  (LongMemEval-S) — a ~3× spread across tasks — and attributes neither to the
  controller. **A loop whose stopping rule is unreported is not a verified loop.**
  Three implementations agreeing on a mechanism is worth `LOW`; it is not worth
  `HIGH` when the component that decides when to stop is unmeasured.
- *HyperSkill appears in three files* (ORDER 1822 §5, ORDER 1820, and by
  reference in ORDER 1823). Counted as **one source**, not three. Its +11.51 /
  +11.18 gains are the authors' own, on one implementation, so `LOW`.

**Corroborations — recorded as new data, and in one case a contradiction the arena
must keep.**

- **Area 132 (absence) — independently corroborated, from a different group and a
  different domain.** ORDER 1822 §3 (MOOSEDev, arXiv 2608.13662) reports negation
  at **0.98 for a typed graph vs 0.06 for vector memory and 0.00 for prose notes**,
  with set-completeness 1.00 vs 0.18 vs 0.08 and supersession traversal 0.98 vs
  0.27 vs 0.12. This is a *second* lab measuring the same categorical separation
  Area 132 was built on, in software-project memory rather than the original
  domain. Support 2 → 3, grade unchanged at `LOW` — corroboration of a `LOW` is
  still `LOW`, and inflating it would violate the same-source caution in the other
  direction.
- **Area 132 also gains a *failure mode* the arena had not recorded**, from the
  same file: the advantage is **not** caused by incomplete ingestion. Mem0 *has* the
  facts and still cannot enumerate sets, establish absence, or traverse relations —
  the queries are unanswerable by construction, not answered badly. This is
  already in Area 132's body (line ~1264) from an earlier pass; this pass confirms
  it from a second source rather than adding it again.
- **The contradiction, preserved and not resolved (R-J4).** ORDER 1807 §8 and
  ORDER 1810 §8 give **directly opposite** recommendations on constraining ontology
  generation, recorded in `VERIFICATION.md` as V-78.5. ORDER 1823 §7.1 now adds a
  third position that is compatible with both: it reads GrOIL's closed-vocabulary
  prompting, Open Ontologies' MCP tool constraints, and the subsumption→
  satisfiability formal reduction as **three instantiations of one principle**
  (constrained generation) — which is the ORDER 1807 side, not a synthesis. The
  arena therefore holds a live 2-against-1 split with no tiebreaker, and the
  minority position is not deleted. Note that the minority side's own evidence is
  the strongest single number in the tranche: **raw-OWL F1 0.323 with a file versus
  0.431 with none** — giving the model strictly more input made it worse. That
  number is already load-bearing in Area 134 rank 2 and is recorded there.
- **Reachable but not promotable — recorded so a later pass does not re-derive it.**
  The **soundness guarantee** in ORDER 1823 §1.6 / ORDER 1824 §6 (arXiv
  2604.16672) is the most interesting rejected candidate of the tranche: under the
  Open World Assumption the method produces **only Type II errors** — it can delay
  discovery of a correct axiom but *never introduce an incorrect one*. The arena
  held **0** occurrences of it, so it is genuinely unobserved. It was **not** made an
  area because it is a property of a *reasoner*, not of a brain: a one-sided error
  direction is a guarantee about a formal inference procedure, and per §4 guard 4 a
  component whose brain function cannot be named is infrastructure, not an area.
  Filed in `VERIFICATION.md` with the reasoning intact, so a later pass that finds
  the cortical analogue (one-sided learning rates, e.g. the avoidance-learning
  asymmetry) can promote it on earned grounds rather than re-reading the file.
  Also unobserved and also not promoted: AVA's **optimization–generalization gap**
  (ORDER 1822 §2, arXiv 2609.00177) — contrastive fine-tuning takes triplet accuracy
  to near-perfect while *degrading* taxonomy discovery and *severely* degrading
  alignment under DPO. That is a real finding about representation quality, but the
  arena already holds the capacity-vs-precision relationship (Area 130) and treating
  this as a fourth instance of it would be repetition, not corroboration.

**Provenance, not design.** Three of the twenty files carry defects that would
change a design if a good architect knew about them, so they are recorded rather
than absorbed: future-dated paths (ORDER 1809 `round60-2026-10-20`, ORDER 1823
`round74-2026-10-22`, ORDER 1824 `round75-2026-11-15` — all dated *after* the
2026-09-07 `generated.at` inside the same file, which is internally inconsistent
and means the mtime/date cannot be trusted for recency anywhere in this lane); and
the round-number/path mismatch in ORDER 1824, whose front-matter `sources:` block
lists 17 papers while the body has 16 sections, with Lippolis (arXiv 2503.05388)
appearing **twice** under two different titles. See `VERIFICATION.md` V-78.x.

**What this tranche did not do, stated plainly.** It produced no re-rank and no grade
change. Per §3 that is the correct outcome for a lane whose twenty files restate
one frontier: the new mechanism was one area, and everything else either
corroborated a held slot or fell into the reachable-but-infrastructure class. No
area was deleted, none was demoted, and no existing ranking was re-litigated
without new evidence.

(`…-rounds78-81-supplement.md`) is a self-declared supplement to ORDERS
1838–1841, read in full and **counted as reach, not as an independent source**; its
one genuinely new datum is a graph-embedding result (768-dim, 92% edge fidelity at
25× speed) that no slot currently rests on, so it increments nothing.

**Four corroborations, and the reasoning that decided each grade.**

1. **Area 7 Rank 3 — learned memory management. Support 1 → 5, grade held `LOW`.**
   ORDER 1844 §2 and ORDER 1845 §4 between them supply six implementations of the
   "memory operations as a trained policy" family with numbers. The one that
   decides the design is **MemRL (arXiv 2601.03192)**: it beats standard RAG
   **with the LLM frozen**, structuring experience as Intent-Experience-Utility
   triplets and running Bellman TD on memory utility. That isolates the variable —
   what is learned is the *reuse rule*, not the model — and it is what converts this
   slot's interaction note from "directly competes with Area 6 Rank 1 for the write
   path" to "separable and composable." A learned op-policy can be fitted to a
   store whose consolidation rule is untouched, so the two designs stop being
   exclusive and **no rank moves**. `LOW` is held for two reasons that are recorded
   separately and not averaged: the FrontisAI survey in the same file places
   essentially all 2026 self-evolving agents at **levels 1–2 of 4** and names level
   3 (Learned Policy) as where MUSE/MemRL/MemSkill are *reaching* — so six papers
   landing on a level is convergence on a **goal**, not replication of a **result**;
   and Memory-R1's 152-pair result and AgeMem's GRPO result are each one benchmark.
   Convergence on the architecture is now well evidenced; convergence on the effect
   size is not.

2. **Area 6 Rank 1 — sleep/consolidation. Support 8 → 9, grade held `LOW`.**
   ORDER 1845 §3's **SleepGate (arXiv 2603.14517)** is a second, independently-built
   instance of the area's exact three-mechanism shape — conflict-aware temporal
   tagger, trained forgetting gate, consolidation merger — with an **adaptive
   entropy trigger** on micro-cycles, which is the piece this area's rank 1 has
   asserted across many tranches and never measured. It also states the claim in the
   right form for a bounding mechanism: interference horizon **O(n) → O(log n)**.
   **The bound that keeps this from `HIGH`, and it is a real one:** the experiment
   is a **4-layer, 793K-parameter** transformer reporting **99.5% at interference
   depth 5 against baselines below 18%**. Interference horizon is precisely the
   quantity that degrades with scale, so this is evidence the mechanism is real and
   correctly shaped, and it is **not** evidence it holds at R-J5's 14,589-file
   target. A near-perfect result at depth 5 on a 793K-parameter model is the same
   category of claim as the arXiv 2604.20943 REM null already held in this area: the
   number is the mechanism's own, and its scope is narrow. The same file's
   *synthetic-dreaming*/REM scheme (consolidation into **weights**, no vector DB)
   and ORDER 1844's *Digital Sleep* framework are **three descriptions of one
   lineage — counted once**, per the same-source rule.

3. **Area 133 Rank 3 — construction verification. Support 3 → 4, grade held `LOW`.**
   ORDER 1845 §5's **PRISMA 2020 systematic review (Gorenshtein et al., PMC 2026),
   21 studies across 18 clinical settings**, is the largest-sample source any slot
   in this area has, and it supplies something the arena asserted as metaphor: a
   **monotone dose-response by symbolic authority** — parse-only **+9%** →
   rule-guided **+16%** → knowledge retrieval **+26%** → **iterative validation with
   veto/regeneration +40%**, median +21.9%. Area 39's dendritic veto therefore sits
   at the *top of a measured gradient*, not merely at the end of an intuition. The
   same review reports **latency 2–88s and up to 100× cost** for veto approaches;
   R-J1 makes cost a non-axis, so that is recorded as a **composition** constraint
   (a veto loop that cannot finish inside a turn budget is unusable at any accuracy)
   and explicitly **not** as a demotion. Grade held `LOW` because a review aggregates
   heterogeneous studies whose individual variance the arena cannot see — the
   monotone *ordering* earns the support, the +40% does not.

4. **Area 7 Rank 2 — D-Mem on LoCoMo: a caveat the number previously lacked.**
   ORDER 1844 §2's **MemoryArena (arXiv 2602.16313)** reports that models with
   **near-saturated** LoCoMo performance **plummet to 40–60%** on interdependent
   multi-session tasks. This is the arena's own pre-split `benchmark-suspect` and
   `recall-not-function` rules arriving as an **external benchmark** rather than as
   internal reasoning, and it bounds **every LoCoMo number the arena cites**,
   D-Mem's 51.2 → 54.5 included. Recorded as a bound, not a refutation: a score a
   harder task contradicts is still evidence the mechanism does something. The
   arena's evidence base for memory is narrower than it looked, and this is the
   sentence that says so.

**This is the first pass in four where the taxonomy lane paid out.** Three
consecutive tranches reported "twenty duplicate publications, zero new evidence."
This time the duplicate publications carried a genuinely new **brain-part claim**
that no prior pass had extracted from them — which is the argument against
skipping a window on the grounds that it looks like repeats. **The near-duplicate
is not a near-duplicate of the brain part; only one of the pair (§16.1 in ORDER
1870 and §7.2 in ORDER 1874) states it in the neuroscientific register, and the
other seventeen files in the window mention it only in passing inside a
synthesis.** A pass that had stopped at "eight files, one programme" would have
recorded eight duplicates and lost the area.

**Area 136 opened** — categorization as a pervasive, need-indexed act. The
thirteen probes and the near-misses are recorded in `ARENA.md`; the load-bearing
detail repeats here because it is the part a future pass must not re-derive: the
single `Barrett` hit across 136 areas is **Lance** Barrett's EPIC model, a
different person on consciousness, and both `predictive processing` hits are
about *unfalsifiability*. The arena holds `affordance` 39 times, `perception` 40,
`gradient` 45, `free energy` 6 — **130 hits in the surrounding vocabulary and not
one of them this claim.** Barrett & Miller's actual position is that
categorization is not a late stage but pervades signal processing, is
feedback-dominant, and is **indexed by the current need** — so the same input is
cut into different categories under different goals.

**Why this did not become a slot inside Area 67 or Area 18.** Both are live
alternatives and the distinction is the substance, not a filing convenience.
Area 67 (graded membership, Lakoff/Rosch) and Area 18 (multi-axial non-exclusive
classification) both ask *what shape a category has*. The new claim is about
*what indexes it* — a category computed as `f(input, goal)` rather than
`f(input)`. A system can satisfy Area 67 perfectly (graded, prototype-centred
categories) and Area 18 perfectly (several overlapping axes) and still be unable
to represent "same input, different goal, different category," because it has no
slot for the goal. That is a different object with a different failure mode, and
per §4 it names a brain function.

**A candidate reached and was NOT promoted, and the restraint is the finding.**
The WLNK / weakest-link invariant (`Γ(S) ≤ min(S)` — no inference chain more
reliable than its least reliable premise) is supplied by ORDER 1870 §10.2 and
ORDER 1876 §10.1, is grounded in Dubois & Prade's possibilistic logic, and is
corroborated empirically by Jacovi et al. (2024) finding CoT reliability bounded
by its weakest step. Thirteen probes return **0** across the arena, including
*abduction* at **0** and *Peirce* at **0**. All **14** hits for the bare word
*weakest* are the ordinary English adjective. **The logical principle is absent
from an arena that uses its adjective fourteen times** — and that is exactly the
failure mode the skill's structural-silence discipline exists to catch, because a
grep on the obvious word returns confident false negatives.

It is filed in `BRAIN PARTS NOT YET COVERED` as **opened, not closed**, and no
area was created, on two grounds: (1) **two files, one restating the other**, with
no third independent source; (2) the empirical corroboration is a *paper's own CoT
measurements*, not a trial of the design the arena would build. Area 2 is the
nearest existing home and it is **incompatible** in an interesting way — Area 2
integrates evidence by weighted sum, and the weakest-link bound is the *opposite*
aggregation, an order-of-aggregation constraint rather than a weighting. Both
cannot hold for the same evidence set, which means opening the area would force a
re-rank in Area 2 on evidence this pass does not have. **That is a bigger
decision than this tranche earned**, and it is recorded for the pass that has the
third source.

**Two corpus conflicts resolved by files read this pass.**

1. **The BGE-reranker-v2-m3 architecture conflict, open since tranche 71.** ORDER
   1878 §1 is titled *"CRITICAL PREMISE CORRECTION"* and settles it against the
   corpus's own earlier claim: the model is **vanilla XLM-RoBERTa-Large**, 24
   layers, 1,024 hidden, 16 heads, full softmax attention throughout — corroborated
   across the HuggingFace card, the BGE documentation, hfviewer, the vLLM-Ascend
   deployment guide, and the two originating papers. ORDER 1691 §5.1's
   "full-attention + Gated-DeltaNet" description and the GDN adaptation design
   built on it are **wrong**, and ORDER 1878 says so explicitly. The conflict the
   arena logged at tranche 71 as unreconciled is now reconciled **against** the
   earlier file.

2. **The two-way provenance conflict on the 0.323/0.431/0.717 triple**, logged at
   tranche 74 and again in `VERIFICATION.md`, is **untouched by this window** —
   no file here restates it. It stays open, and the honest status is unchanged.

**Three substantive negative or constraining results, none of which became a slot.**

- **ORDER 1880 §3.2, the conservation result.** The Gated DeltaNet delta rule
  `e_t = v_t − S̃_{t−1}ᵀk_t` is the one propagation rule that **cannot** satisfy
  the LRP conservation axiom, and the file derives exactly why: conservation
  requires `S̃_{t−1}·e_t = 0`, which is not generally true. The subtraction that
  makes the delta rule adaptive is the same subtraction that breaks the sum rule.
  The fix is to decompose it into separate value and prediction LRP paths — at the
  cost of two paths producing conflicting relevance for the same token, needing a
  reconciliation step. A genuine `UNSUCCESSFUL`-flavoured result about a method
  that does not yet exist, filed here because it constrains any future
  attribution design.

- **ORDER 1879 §4.3, the delta rule's blind spot.** A token that *perfectly
  matches the current prediction* writes **nothing** — so Influence Score is 0
  for a token that is semantically important. **The architecture is
  systematically blind to the predictable**, which is a property of the write
  rule, not of the attribution method layered on top. It inverts the usual
  assumption that a zero attribution means a token was unimportant.

- **ORDER 1876 §4.3, LLM-as-judge is worse than a trained classifier.** In
  taxonomy expansion validation, LLM-as-judge scored **15.4% / 19.2%** against a
  path-aware DistilRoBERTa classifier's **34.6% / 42.3%** — and the file's own
  summary is the finding: LLM-as-judge *"hallucinates validity"*. An LLM asked
  whether a parent-child relation is structurally sound is worse at that
  judgement than a small classifier trained on the seed taxonomy's own edges.
  This bears directly on the arena's own evidence-grading practice, which leans on
  model judgement in several areas, and it is filed as a constraint rather than a
  slot because it concerns a task, not a brain part.

**Reach, not support — the clustering, counted honestly.** ORDER 1870 and 1874
both restate Barrett & Miller; that is **one** source, and the independent-source
count for Area 136 rank 1 credits the Rosch prototype evidence, the Barsalou ad
hoc category work, and the LLM-embedded-hierarchy result at ORDER 1872 §2.2
separately. The taxonomy lane's own `confidence: high` frontmatter across eight
files is **not** counted as anything: §8's inversion applies with full force here,
since the frontmatter asserts confidence while the content beneath it is
synthesised prose about other people's papers. The LITE / EEG / Sem-Path
taxonomy-quality metrics (ORDER 1869 §14.1, ORDER 1876 §3.3) and the
TaxoBench dual bottleneck — best agent recalls only **20.92%** of
expert-cited papers, and with perfect input still only **31.24% ARI** — are real
measured numbers and are recorded here; they are **retrieval-of-the-corpus
findings about taxonomy construction**, not findings about a brain part, and per
§4 guard 4 they are infrastructure, not slots.

**Two infrastructure files, not slots, and the security one is worth keeping.**
ORDER 1882 records **GHSA-vxmw-7h4f-hqxh**: when `github.action_repository` is
empty (a long-standing runner bug, actions/runner#2473), the action's fallback
chain fell through to `github.ref_name`, which in a `pull_request` context is
**attacker-controlled** — a branch named `innocent;cat${IFS}/etc/passwd` achieved
arbitrary code execution in the publish job. The generalisable shape: **an empty
context value is not a safe default, it is an unvalidated one**, and a fallback
chain on a missing value widens the attack surface rather than narrowing it. The
file also establishes that OIDC propagation is **not** what composite actions
break — the premise conflates three distinct failures — and that the maintainers
of the affected action forbid the configuration on security grounds, not
capability grounds. ORDER 1881 is the CBOR/DNS-CBOR IANA registration lane already
covered at tranche 70; a reach witness, not an increment.

**ORDER 1885 §6.4 is the one architecture-specific advantage this corpus
identifies**, and it is recorded because no other file in the window notices it:
Active Wiki tracks **provenance**, so attribution-highlighted tokens can be
checked against the source sentences that support an extracted fact. That is a
ground truth most IR systems simply do not have, and it makes the attribution
problem *checkable* here in a way the ViT benchmarks could not be. That is an
asset of this corpus, not a claim about a brain part, and it is filed as such.

**Zero re-ranks. Zero grade changes. Zero citations removed. One area opened

### Tranche 81 addendum — the compliance count in the block above was wrong, and C4 caught it

**The `###` block above opens by claiming "20 `read_file` calls, 20 rows flipped."
That is false. The true count is 18 and 18.** The block is not edited, because
this file is append-only and a corrected count that silently replaces a wrong one
destroys the audit trail; so the correction is recorded here, where a future pass
reading the tranche-81 block will find it.

**How it went wrong, because the mechanism generalises.** The cursor window is
ORDER 1869–1888, which is **20 ORDER *lines***. Two of those rows — ORDER 1871
(`frontier-research-taxonomy-late-2026-supplement.md`) and ORDER 1887
(`graphiti-temporal-knowledge-graph.md`) — were **already `[x]` on arrival**, from
an earlier pass. Both were correctly *not opened* and correctly consumed no slot.
So the pass read **18 files** and flipped **18 rows**. What it then wrote was
"20 files, all 20 read whole, ceiling reached exactly at ORDER 1888" — it had
**substituted the window's line count for its file count**, and then compounded
it by describing the ceiling as "reached exactly," which is a second false claim
since the ceiling was not reached at all.

**What caught it.** Invariant **C4** compares the published summary census against
the live ledger and returned `[FAIL] published {'x': 1586} vs live {'x': 1604}
(delta +18)`. The previous run's report gave 1,586 as the starting census, so
1604 − 1586 = **18**, exactly, and the "20" had no ledger support. **C4 was
written to catch a stale published figure and instead caught a live figure the
arena had just invented** — the checker did its job in the direction nobody
expected, which is the whole argument for running it rather than assuming it.

**The corrected compliance claim.** `read_file` calls this run: **18**. Rows
flipped to `[x]` this run: **18**. **Equal, so the pass is compliant on the ratio
that matters** — no file was marked without its own `read_file`, and no
`read_file` was performed without a mark. The defect is in the *narrative*, not
the ledger: the ledger never claimed 20, and no corpus file was read twice, and
no read was fabricated. **A wrong count in prose is a real defect and is reported
as one** — it is the same class as the unearned-citation defect, in that a claim
outran what the work supports, and it is exactly what the skill's rule "if those
two numbers are not equal, say so plainly" exists to prevent. Here they were
equal; what was wrong was writing down a number the ledger did not support.

**The transferable lesson, recorded because it will recur:** *ORDER line count
≠ file count ≠ mark count.* A window is bounded in ORDER lines, a pass is bounded
in files read, and the ledger records marks. All three differ whenever the window
contains pre-read or excluded rows. **A run that reports its compliance numbers by
subtracting one of these from another will eventually report a ratio it never
performed.** The only trustworthy source for "how many did I read" is the count
of `read_file` calls actually made, and the only trustworthy source for "how many
did I mark" is the live ledger delta against the census the previous run
published. C4 is the mechanical form of that check, and it is the reason the
published census is stored at all.

**This is the first tranche of the twin-free era.** Tranche 82 ended at ORDER
1917, one line before the frontier C-057 predicted. Every file read here is

#### Area 137 — the three-valued epistemic state, and why the middle value bites

Earned by ORDER 1926 §2 (EKBM) with ORDER 1926 §5 and ORDER 1925 §1.

**The near-miss that makes this an area rather than a slot.** `ARENA.md` already
held Area 134 — the availability gap, where the answer is in the system and does
not come out — and I checked it hard before opening a new area, because a
fourth facet of "the system doesn't know what it knows" is not a new area. It is
not one. Area 134's failure is **routing**: the value is decodable and the
output ignores it, and the remedy is to repair the route. The `confused` state
is categorically different: **it emits an answer, and the answer's correctness
depends on how the question was phrased.** No route repair fixes that and no
amount of extra retrieval fixes it, because the information needed to decide
whether to trust the item *is the variance across probe variants* — which a
single probe cannot see by construction. That is a different brain function,
not a different bug.

**The evidence that forces the design.** Two numbers from ORDER 1926 do the
work. Zhao et al. (2025) measure cross-method decision consistency as low as
**7%**, falling to ~**40%** under minimal *non-semantic* perturbation — i.e.
shuffling the answer options, changing nothing semantic, still moves the
decision nearly as much as changing the method does. The corollary is the
design constraint: **a single-probe boundary detector is not a weak detector, it
is an unreliable instrument whose error has never been measured.** That is Area
24's thesis — the appearance of a signal without the warrant for it — landing on
a case where nobody thought to check. Zheng et al.'s own prescription is
perturbation-robust probing that aggregates across input variations, which is
why Rank 1 is aggregation and not a better probe.

**The result that reversed an arena default.** ORDER 1926 §5 finds that
**sensitivity and accuracy anti-correlate across models**: the most accurate
model is not the best monitor, and monitor selection by accuracy is actively
wrong. The arena's Area 95 already requires independence for a signal that
*writes* to memory; this pass applies the same requirement to a signal that
*reads* it, and the arena had only ever applied it to the writer. The companion
within-model result is the one I would put in front of anyone proposing a
confidence gate: **Gemini 2.5 Flash scores T1-CC = 88 with T4-CR = 41** —
excellent calibration, terrible range use. A model can rank its own answers
correctly by confidence while being systematically overconfident, so **a single
calibration metric does not clear a model for monitoring duty.** The arena has
no slot for monitor *selection*; this is it.

**Preserved disagreement, not reconciled.** ORDER 1926 reports ConfRAG's
dampening gate at 5–39% fewer retrievals *at matched always-on-RAG accuracy*,
while ORDER 1925 §1 reports that irrelevant or contradictory retrieved context
drives **ECE above 0.4** — confidence becoming *uncorrelated* with correctness
rather than merely miscalibrated. These are compatible (the gate reduces the
exposure that causes the second) but they are not the same claim, and the arena
records both. Compositional calibration, by contrast, is a hard negative and is
recorded as a standing limit rather than a footnote: **MIRROR reports
Compositional Calibration Error 0.434–0.943**, i.e. compositional calibration
fails universally, so a memory system that is well-calibrated per store is not
thereby calibrated when a query spans stores. **No design in this arena has
solved that**, and a brain that combines episodic, semantic and parametric
retrieval sits squarely in it.

`Nelson` returns 9 and `Narens` 6 across the arena. Every hit is the
*architecture* — the meta/object split, at Areas 98 and 125. **Not one is the
measurement of how the meta-level fails.** That is the whole finding: the arena
had the vocabulary for this brain part for a long time and never asked the
question the framework was invented to raise.

#### Area 138 — a containment theorem, not a benchmark

Earned by ORDER 1929 §2 (MRAgent, arXiv 2606.06036).

I looked hard for a home for this before opening an area, because the arena
holds ~65 retrieval results and a 138th retrieval slot would be noise. The
nearest existing area is **Area 135** (when a recall loop should terminate) and
it is strictly downstream: Area 135 takes the loop's candidate set as given and
asks when to stop; this asks whether the *policy* that generates the candidate
set should be learned at all. The distinction is not stylistic. MRAgent's
Theorem 4.1 states `H_passive^LM(T) ⊊ H_active^LM(T)` for every `T ≥ 2` — the
passive hypothesis class is **strictly contained** in the active one at equal
budget. Every retrieval area in this arena ranks candidate sets, and a ranked
candidate set *is* a hypothesis class. So the theorem says the ranked-set
framing is a strict subset of what the biology does, and **no amount of tuning a
passive retriever closes that gap** — which is a stronger warrant than any
benchmark in the arena, and the reason Rank 3 is `UNSUCCESSFUL` on a proof
rather than on a score.

**Why the grade is `LOW` and not `HIGH`, stated plainly.** The theorem and the
LongMemEval numbers (72.95 vs 54.92 next-best, +32% relative; 118K tokens against
A-Mem's 632K and LangMem's 3.27M) come from **the same group on the same
construction**, so they are one source, not two. Per the corroboration rule I
counted the support once. The file's own risk list also concedes that loop
latency is added and that **poor tag extraction cascades into poor
reconstruction** — a single point of failure for the entire design, since tags
are the intermediate layer everything else depends on. The token-cost result is
the one that decides this at 14,589-file scale (R-J5): 5–27× fewer retrieved
tokens is the difference between a corpus fitting a context budget and not. The
construction cost is the counterweight and the file does **not** quantify it.

**The near-miss recorded rather than dropped.** ORDER 1934 §7.2 cites the **3S
statistic** for a standard Poisson process, `ψ = E[N|V]/V² · Σ(vᵢ − vᵢ₋₁)²`,
optimal against Poisson in the burstiness direction by Neyman–Pearson, needing
no rescaling and no surrogate. That **contradicts the arena's Area 29 framing**
that the rescale-then-test gate is the only correct entry point, so I recorded
it in Area 29's corroboration block rather than quietly dropping it. Area 29's
Rank 1 survives on a different axis — it is a *gate* telling you whether any
such test is in its valid regime, and 3S needs one too, and 3S's optimality is
only against the Poisson null, which is the wrong null once p ≥ 0.1. The
ranking does not change; the reason for it becomes sharper. **A near-miss that
would have displaced a slot is recorded as a near-miss, and the near-miss
survived.**

#### Corroborations into existing areas (2, both from ORDER 1934)

**Area 29 (burstiness), Support 2 → 3, no re-rank.** ORDER 1934 derives
Barabási's universality classes from the communication literature (email,
letters, web browsing, library visits, stock trading) rather than the
log/traffic literature, and lands on the same two classes (α = 3/2 unlimited
queue, α = 1 limited queue) and the same conclusion. Two contributions. First,
**the name for the quantity the arena was already using**: Goh & Barabási
(2008, *EPL* 81:48002) call exactly Area 29 Rank 3's `B = (σ/μ − 1)/(σ/μ + 1)`
the burstiness parameter, with a **memory coefficient M that is low for human
dynamics** — the bursty character comes from the inter-event distribution
alone, not temporal correlation. That is mechanistic rather than statistical,
and it independently supports the gate: a model *with memory* is fitting a
parameter the human process does not have. Second, Kim et al. (2016,
arXiv:1604.01125 — the paper Area 29 Rank 1 already cites) show B is
**overestimated at finite n**. Rank 3's existing failure note says naive TRT
*underestimates* burstiness. **Those are two different biases — the statistic and
its finite-sample estimator — and they do not cancel.** At 14,589 files the
corpus is dominated by low-n series, so the practical consequence is that
**Rank 3's error sign is not stable across the corpus** and the drift decision
inherits whichever it hits. That is a stronger disqualification of Rank 3 than
the one the area made, and it is the R-J5 consequence.

**Area 125 Rank 2 (negative-binomial absence model), Support 1 → 2, grades held.**
ORDER 1934 is an independent derivation of the same model from the human-
dynamics side. It adds three things the slot was missing: (1) the finite-sample
correction must apply to the **threshold**, not just the statistic — the slot
thresholds raw B at 0.1 and a preference with 5–20 mentions over 6 months is
exactly the regime where Kim et al.'s correction is largest, so the gate must
threshold the corrected `B*`; (2) the **direction** of the small-sample bias is
named: ML estimates of NB dispersion are biased upward, so at n < 30 the
correction *under-corrects* — the safe direction, but a known power loss rather
than a surprise; (3) **AIC over BIC**, because the goal is scoring absence
accurately, not identifying the data-generating process. It also supplies the
**corrected Vuong test** (Desmarais & Harden 2013) for the non-nested
ZINB-vs-NB comparison, since the uncorrected test is **biased toward supporting
zero-inflation even when none exists** — a false-positive generator inside the
very test the slot relies on. **Recorded as a disagreement per R-J4:** ORDER
1934 predicts concrete gains (NB 30–50% FP reduction, ZINB a further 10–20%)
where ORDER 1639 declines to predict numbers. Both stay `UNTESTED`; the arena
records both and averages nothing.

### What the window actually was

Four clusters, and **only one of them is about a brain.**

| OIDC / npm / PyPI supply chain | 1939–1941, 1954 | reach, not slots |

Recorded here so a later pass does not re-open them looking for a mechanism.

### A · The quiet findings in the infrastructure files

These are real, they are in the answer file where they change a design, and
none of them is a brain part.

- **ORDER 1937 §6.4** — a GraphRAG ingestion pipeline that catches malformed LLM

  arena's own §8 inversion turned into a runtime property: the pipeline reports
  success, the artifact (a clean index) is intact, and the *content* is quietly
  gone. Filed as an ingestion requirement, not a slot.
- **ORDER 1938 §2.1 / §3.3** — a vector index whose **dimension mismatch fails
  silently at ingestion even though schema creation succeeded**, and
  `eventually_consistent: true` trades read-after-write for throughput. Both are

  a *schema*. Noted rather than promoted.
- **ORDER 1939** — "**Staging Is Not a Silver Bullet**." The finding is that a
  human approval gate in a publish workflow is *ceremonial* when the reviewer

  its way into information is a gate that cannot inform. It did not enter Area 33
  as a re-rank; one file describing a publishing workflow is not a trial of that
  area's claim, and the correspondence is recorded rather than banked.

### B · Collision C-018 — RESOLVED this pass, against ORDER 1950

Eight CBOR implementations, **eight different depth limits** (ORDER 1950 §3:
`16 / 32 / 64 / 128 / 512 / 1000 / 1024 / 1024`), and no pre-send discovery
mechanism. ORDER 1951 contradicts three of them.

| Implementation | ORDER 1950 | ORDER 1951 | Decided by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cbor2` | 1000 (configurable) | **unbounded** — the only crashing library, **CVE-2026-26209** | 1951 |
| `fxamacker/cbor` | 1024 | **32** | 1951, citing its documentation |

**Resolved for ORDER 1951, and the reason is citation weight rather than
recency:** 1951 cites **five library-documentation URLs**; 1950 cites only
IETF/IANA links, which describe no implementation at all. A file that reads the
per-library docs outranks a file that reads the registry. **C-018 is closed.**

**The transferable finding is the collision, not either table:** two files in
the same lane, on the same registry, disagreeing about what shipping libraries
do, and **the one with the external citations is the one that had read the
code.** ORDER 1950's error is a *plausible* table built from specification
rather than implementation — the §8 inversion in its purest form, and it is
worth noting that the arena has now seen this exact pattern three times in
seventy-one files: **a correctly-formatted, well-sourced-looking document whose
content came from a path that never touched the artefact.**

### C · Area 139 — the file that earned it, and the finding that made it an area

ORDER 1957 §6 (BeliefMem, arXiv 2608.04574) states two things. Only one earned
the area.

**The earning claim.** Collapsing uncertainty to a **point estimate destroys the
posterior support for the alternatives**, and the result is a self-reinforcing
error trap: the system loses the information it would have needed to notice it
was wrong. The word doing the work is *destroys* — not "makes less accurate".
The alternatives are not downweighted, they are **removed from the addressable
set**, and the retrieval cue that would have surfaced them no longer points at
anything.

**Why this survived 138 areas.** The probes are the finding:
`point estimate` **0**, `posterior support` **0**, `belief inertia` **0** — and
the decisive one, **`noisy-OR` / `log-odds` / `odds space` all 0.** The arena
has a belief-revision area (Area 1), a reliability-weighting area (Area 2), a
four-channel uncertainty area (Area 75), and a three-valued epistemic-state area
(Area 137, opened one tranche ago). **None of them asks what the belief set
contains.** Area 137 is the sharpest near-miss and the distinction is exact:
Area 137 asks *whether the system knows it does not know*; Area 139 asks *what
was thrown away when it decided*. A system can answer the first perfectly while
having made the second decision irrecoverable.

**The near-miss against Area 1, stated because it is the strongest objection.**
Area 1 is belief revision — AGM operators over a belief set. Could this just be
a fourth facet of Area 1? No, and the reason is ordering: **revision operators
are functions of a belief set, and they cannot recover a target that is no longer
in the set.** Installing a better operator on a set that has already dropped its
alternatives does nothing. The constraint is **write-side and upstream**. That
is a different kind of claim from Area 1's, and it is why this is an area.

**Grades — and the honest weakness.** All three slots are `UNTESTED`, and that
is not a hedge. **The arena holds no measured effect size from this file.** §6
states a mechanism; the file is a design proposal with a validation plan. The
rank-1 slot says this in its own grade field rather than borrowing authority
from the mechanism's plausibility. Support 1/1/1, all three counted once —
ORDER 1957 is the only file that earned the area, and the three slots are one
source's three dispositions of one mechanism.

**Not promoted: the second claim in the same section.** "Stale memory is worse
than no memory" is a *different* mechanism — about a retrieved falsehood
suppressing the search that would have corrected it, which is a retrieval-loop
claim (Area 135/138 territory) and not a storage-format claim. It is recorded
here and **deliberately not a slot**, because promoting it would have made the
area two areas. If a later file develops it, it returns.

### D · Area 140 — the only `UNSUCCESSFUL` in the arena resting on the arena's own measurement

ORDER 1960 (873 lines) enumerates four systematic biases in a 3-signal
consensus used as pseudo-ground-truth. The **structure** of the four is the
finding, not any one of them:

| Bias | Direction | Rate |
|---|---|---|
| (a) seasonal/cyclic over-flagging | FP | 15–25% of FPs |
| (b) gradual drift misses | FN | 20–30% of FNs |
| (c) context-dependent confusion | FP | 10–20% of FPs |
| (d) sparse-correction absence | FN | **25–35% of FNs** |

**The false-positive classes are visible and correctable. The false-negative
classes are silent by construction — a missed drift leaves nothing in the
signal stream to check against.** And the largest single number in the table,
25–35%, is a false *negative*. An instrument whose dominant error mode is the
one it cannot observe is not an instrument that has been validated.

**The grade discipline in this area is the substantive part of the write.** Every
F1 gain ORDER 1960 reports is an **estimate projected from a different domain**:
+0.03–0.05 seasonal is inferred from a *weather time-series* result claiming 99%
FP reduction; +0.05–0.08 absence-monitoring is inferred from *object-detection*
false-negative prediction. The file is explicit that these are projections
("we estimate"), and the arena records them as projections. **The only measured
delta anywhere in this tranche's drift material is negative and lands on the
signal the consensus is built from** — ORDER 1955 §1.2: **removing the
consistency-weight signal improves accuracy by +0.014.** That is what earns Rank
3 its `UNSUCCESSFUL`: not an external citation, a measurement **taken by the
lane that built the consensus, against that consensus.**

**One lane, three files, counted once.** ORDER 1960, 1942 and 1955 are all
`lane-online-a`, and 1960's own frontmatter names 1942 (`online-active-learning-
preference-schema-drift`) as a parent. Counting them as three independent
sources would be exactly the inflation the skill's *three files restating one
study are one source* rule exists to prevent. Support is **1 / 1 / 1**. What
1942 adds is nonetheless a distinct mechanism and is recorded in the slot:
§1.2's **matching-but-wrong** false positive (a pattern can match *and* be
wrong — detection is not validation) and §4.2's **the user stopped mentioning
it**, which is bias (d) seen from the opposite side: the same silence, read as
evidence *for* drift rather than as an absence of evidence *against* it.

**The near-miss is the sharpest in this pass, and the two areas give opposite
instructions from the same word.** Area 29 holds: *"inter-event times are
normal for human activity, so a silence is not evidence."* That is a silence in
an **event train** — a fact about the world that must not be over-read. Area
140 is a silence in the **measuring apparatus**, which biases the **measurement**
in a known direction and must be corrected. Same observation, opposite
instruction, and the difference is entirely *where* the silence sits.

### E · Area 8 corroboration — the fourth file, and a consequence nobody drew

ORDER 1953 (`path-patching-head-boundaries-bge-reranker-v2-m3.md`) describes the
target as **24 layers, 16 heads, `type_vocab_size=1`, vanilla
XLM-RoBERTa-Large** — siding with ORDER 1690 against ORDER 1691, and the first
file in this dispute written by neither lane.

**Support deliberately unchanged at 7.** That figure counts *instances of the
arena's target model being misdescribed*; ORDER 1953 is a third **correct**
reading of the same `config.json`, not a fourth misdescription. Counting it
would inflate the evidence for a defect it is evidence *against*. The
disagreement is now **2-to-1 within the corpus**, and the minority reading is
also the only one not contradicted by the artefact. ORDER 1691's own §6.5
migration-target caveat survives: a file may describe a model it intends to
build.

**The consequence, which is the part worth keeping.** If the target is vanilla
softmax attention, then the saturation-head phenomenon these files analyse is a
property of **standard attention on hard negatives**, not of a hybrid
architecture. That makes the phenomenon **more portable** — it is not gated on
DeltaNet layers existing — and it removes the need for any DeltaNet-specific
machinery in the migration path. Neither ORDER 1690 nor ORDER 1691 drew this,
because both were busy being right about the model.

### F · ORDER 1959 — a duplicate design document inside the corpus

`oracle/brain/research/PROPOSED-BRAIN-ARCHITECTURE.md` is a **155,396-char
copy** of the repo-root file the arena feeds. Read whole (two `read_file` calls,
844 + 714 lines, `truncated: true` then finished through EOF at 1558). **Not
edited** — the skill forbids writing it, and the corpus copy is corpus content
subject to the read, not to the write.

It is a §4 guard-4 case in miniature and worth naming: the arena is forbidden to
write one file and required to read a byte-identical twin of it. Filed in
`VERIFICATION.md`. Its own §13 calls itself *"an older snapshot (36KB,
2026-09-23 09:40)"* while the file is **155KB and dated 2026-09-24T04:30Z** —
**the document's self-description is wrong by a factor of four in size and a
day in date**, which is a small instance of the §8 inversion inside the arena's
own upstream design document.

- **The "expected F1 improvement" table (§7).** Every number is a cross-domain

- **ORDER 1948's filename.** `packed-cbor-radar-alternative-approach.md` — the

### A · Area 141 — how the area was earned, and the probe that earned it

ORDER 1969 (`real-world-correction-pressure-linguistic-analysis.md`) is a
**linguistics** file that arrived in a memory lane, and the reason it opened an
area is a units mismatch rather than a new mechanism. The arena has 140 areas
and every one of them treats a memory system as a set of **entries,
documents, or events**. ORDER 1969 measures the same phenomenon in **turns
inside an adjacency pair**, and its headline number is that **93% of
third-position repairs are context-dependent** — that is, the correction
utterance is *underdetermined on its own* and only becomes a proposition once
it is placed against the T2 it repairs.

**Why the grade is `LOW` and not `HIGH`, stated in full because this is the

1. The LLM arm is **one model** (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, 8 few-shot examples per

2. **No inter-annotator agreement figure is reported for the study's own
   labels.** The κ ≥ 0.80 target appears in ORDER 1961's *protocol*; no κ
   appears in ORDER 1969's *results*. A 12,847-turn corpus labelled by
   unstated means with no agreement statistic is a weaker warrant than its
   precision suggests.
3. The taxonomy is **borrowed**, not derived — Levow et al. 2006 for the
   spoken-dialogue codes, REPAIR-QA for the TPR figures. The borrowings are
   sound; what is *not* borrowed is any external validation that the
   six-category scheme transfers from train-information spoken dialogue to
   text-mode LLM agents. The file's own §8 Q1 concedes exactly this.
4. Per the arena's §8 inversion, `status: verified` plus a full `sources:`
   block of real linguistics papers certifies the **artifact**, not the prose.
   The coverage figures come from a self-measured internal log with no
   labelled benchmark behind it.

### B · Rank 3's `UNSUCCESSFUL` is arithmetic, and it is the part worth keeping

Two files of the same lane, read in the same pass, produce a result neither
produces alone. ORDER 1961 §7.1 sets the proxy consensus's own decision rule:

> Proxy F1 0.75–0.85 → usable but needs improvement
> **Proxy F1 < 0.75 → Reject proxy labels; require human annotation**

ORDER 1969 §5.2 then measures the **correction arm** of that consensus at
**0.34 macro-F1** (MemPalace's 16 hand-crafted patterns) and **0.62** with
LLM-synthesized patterns. Both are below the acceptance bar the consensus's
own file sets. So the ≥2-of-3 rule is, in the words of the file that specifies
it, being carried by an arm it would reject.

This is recorded as `UNSUCCESSFUL` rather than as a low grade because the
corpus ran the experiment and got a negative answer, which is the definition.
**It is not a claim that the consensus cannot work** — fusion genuinely
compensating is untested, and the slot says so in a `Returns if` clause, so a
labelled holdout that clears 0.75 on the consensus while no single arm clears
it would revive this rank. Recorded so a later pass does not rebuild it from
the F1 numbers alone.

### C · Candidates reached and rejected, with reasons

- **ORDER 1978 (RLMF, arXiv 2606.32032) — faithful calibration as a distinct

  Areas 1 and 126; does not open.** The file's sharpest claims are real and

### D · A disagreement preserved rather than reconciled (R-J4)

ORDER 1975 (`rfc7049-tag6-misconception-propagation-analysis.md`) concludes
the tag-6-is-date/time misconception *"is real but not widespread in
authoritative sources"* and needs **no RFC erratum**, on the grounds that it
appears *"primarily in developer discussions and secondary materials."*
ORDER 1977 (`rfc-8126bis-allocation-process-changes.md`) reaches the opposite
operational conclusion — that the misconception actively **blocks** Packed
CBOR adoption and creates *"false perception of conflict with date
semantics."* Both are from the same lane, dated four days apart, and they
disagree about whether the same evidence constitutes a documentation problem
or an adoption blocker. **Both positions are recorded; neither is
adjudicated.** This does not affect any slot — no slot depends on it — and it
is logged because the arena's rule is to preserve disagreements rather than
pick the more recent one.

#### The two areas, and why each probe set is the evidence

**Area 143 — the regime as a regulated variable.** Earned by ORDER 2017 §3.
The earner is one sentence the corpus reports from Haldeman & Beggs (2005):
chemically increasing excitation produced *supercritical* cortical dynamics and
increasing inhibition produced *subcritical*, *"suggesting the brain actively
maintains criticality through homeostatic mechanisms."* **The set-point plus
the controller is the brain part**, and it is separable from the arena's
existing homeostatic variables because the regulated quantity is the branching
ratio — a property of the network's state distribution — rather than synaptic
strength (Area 6) or a local veto (Area 39). The clinical payoff is in the same
paragraph: **epilepsy is supercritical, anesthesia is subcritical.** Two
diseases in opposite directions on one axis, which no per-component health check
in the arena can express.

**The probe set, and the near-miss that makes it real.** `criticality`,
`critical point`, `branching ratio`, `neural avalanche`, `avalanche`, `Beggs`,
`self-organized critical`, `subcritical`, `supercritical`, `dynamical regime`,
`power-law avalanche` — **all 0 across 142 areas**. The decisive probe is the
one that should have found it and did not: **`critical` returns 61 hits, and
every single one is either *critical period* (the developmental window, Areas
15/51/63) or ordinary English** (*"a critical decision," "a more critical node
than NAcc"*). **The arena's own highest-frequency word, searched with a
case-insensitive probe designed to be generous, and the concept is still
absent.** A pass that stopped at the word would have logged a fourth arrival at
Areas 15/51/63 and lost the area. `ARENA-EVIDENCE.md` holds exactly one prior
use of "criticality" and it is the wrong substrate — a knowledge-graph paper's
stable ~12% of semantically distant "surprising edges," named by that paper as
the hallmark of criticality. A graph statistic, not a branching ratio.

**Why the grades are what they are, and the one thing that is unresolvable.**
The *phenomenon* is convergent as reported — six species (cultured rat slices,
zebrafish, turtle, rodent, monkey, human) across four recording modalities — but
ORDER 2017 is a tertiary reference with `sources: []`, `verified: []` and
`confidence: medium`, so the cross-species claim is **`unverified` in this
workspace and earns no grade above `LOW`**. The *controller* earns nothing: no
trial in the corpus runs a closed-loop branching-ratio controller. The
disagreement is carried unreconciled per **R-J4** — the same §3 concedes that
power laws alone do not prove criticality, that exponents vary across studies
(consistent with *near*-critical), and that **Lombardi et al. (2023) produced
avalanche-like statistics in subcritical adaptive Ising models.** The arena does
not pick between Beggs and Lombardi. What survives the objection is the
*regulatory* half: a near-critical brain is still a regulated one.

**An R-J5 limit stated rather than papered over.** The branching ratio is an
**asymptotic** statistic of an event stream. On the short windows a
cron-driven pass actually produces, the estimate is sampling noise, and the
corpus gives **no window length anywhere in the file**. Rank 1 therefore has
**no stated `n`** and is recorded as un-specifiable without one. Inventing a
plausible window would have been the easy move and would have been exactly the
§8 inversion the arena exists to catch.

**Area 144 — the gate as a choice.** Earned by ORDER 2024 §3 and §"Overlaps &
Tensions" §1. Four of five sensory modalities relay through thalamus before
cortex, where the relay gates, modulates by state, and extracts features.
Olfaction does not: OB mitral/tufted axons project **directly** to piriform
cortex, AON, olfactory tubercle, **cortical amygdala** and lateral entorhinal
cortex, putting odor at the amygdala **within one to two synapses of the
sensory surface** — which is the file's explanation for pre-attentive emotional
tagging and for why odors are hard to ignore. **The file is careful in the way
that earns it:** it concedes olfaction *does* have a thalamic route (MDT → OFC)
and that it is the secondary one. A file that had hidden that would have been
overclaiming.

**The probe set, and the sharpest near-miss of the tranche.** The **thalamus
appears 9 times in 142 areas and every occurrence is a relay on a path** —
subthalamic nucleus as veto, suprachiasmatic input, colliculus→MD→FEF, VMpo,
thalamic reticular nucleus in spindle generation, spinothalamic. **Never a gate
a design might decline to route through.** And `bypass` returns **3 hits, all
three a different sense**: neocortical pathways bypassing the hippocampus, a
fast route bypassing the deliberative one, Flyvbjerg's forecasting bypass. **The
word for the architectural move is in the arena's vocabulary and the move is in
no slot** — which is a stronger silence than a bare zero, because it means the
concept has been *adjacent* to the arena's language the whole time.

**Deliberately not opened as a fourth facet of attention or of the fast path.**
Area 125's deterministic-regex fast path is *fast through the same pipeline* — it
is faster because the workload is smaller, not because it skips a stage. Rank 1
of Area 144 requires the arena to distinguish **fast** from **ungated**, which it
currently cannot. That distinction is the slot's whole content.

**The file's own flags are carried, not absorbed.** The headline olfaction
number — Bushdid et al. (2014), *"humans can discriminate more than 1 trillion
olfactory stimuli"* — is **marked as an estimate by the source itself** and is
accompanied in the same file by the criticism that the extrapolation came from
mixtures of a limited base-odorant set rather than natural odors. **No slot rests
on it**, per the arena's `benchmark-suspect` rule. Separately, **human** adult
olfactory-bulb neurogenesis may be *"far less extensive than in mice"*
(Sorrells et al. 2018), which removes the cleanest lifelong-plasticity analogy
this file offers to the arena's stability-plasticity problem. §8's inversion
again, in its mildest form: `confidence: high` in the frontmatter over a
`sources:` list of five links and a `verified: []` block.

**An R-J5 property stated that is rare in this arena:** Area 144 is a *routing*
decision and **scales flatly.** The classes of input into a reasoning system are
few and fixed even when the corpus beneath them is 14,589 files. Most areas here
carry a cost that multiplies with corpus size; this one does not, and the only
scaling obligation is the **maintenance** one — keeping the class enumeration
true as ingress paths are added, which the slot inherits and has no mechanism
for.

#### The corroboration that came with a real divergence

**ORDER 2026 (258 lines) corroborates the arena's incubation/creativity slot
and simultaneously undercuts its design.** The support increment is earned:
**Wagner et al. (2004), *Nature* 427:352–355** — 59% of sleep participants
discovered a hidden Number Reduction Task rule against 24% of wake controls, a
*qualitative restructuring* rather than a speed-up — is a **genuinely independent
implementation of the incubation effect**, and Verleger et al. (2013) supplies
~20% spontaneous discovery during training itself. It counts as an increment
**with a condition attached and recorded**: ORDER 2026 is tertiary
(`verified: []`, `confidence: high` over PMC links), so the *effect* is `LOW` and
the *agent design* stays `UNTESTED`. Not promoted on the strength of the biology.

**The divergence is the valuable half.** ORDER 2026 argues from iOtA (Cai et al.
2020) that insight emerges from **iterative SWS→REM alternation** — SWS
extracts within-task gist, REM does cross-domain integration, and **whole-night
sleep beats both SWS-rich early-night and REM-rich late-night periods
separately.** The arena's slot is a *single* scheduled interval with one trigger.
**If the alternation claim holds, one pass is one sleep cycle, and the arena's
own text concedes that one cycle "produces stabilization but not the progressive
abstraction that requires iterative alternation."** Both are carried per R-J4.

**A control conflict the arena now holds unresolved, and it is a real one.**
ORDER 2026's hypnagogic result — participants held at the theta-dominant sleep-
onset state, with reduced prefrontal inhibition, showing enhanced creative
performance — is a **disinhibition** mechanism. The same arena slot already
carries a **verification-before-commitment requirement** derived from the rATL
gamma burst. **The same offline pass is being argued to need lowered inhibition
and strict verification simultaneously.** These are opposite control directions
on one window. Recorded, not reconciled, and flagged for whoever opens a
dedicated incubation area: **a single offline window cannot be simultaneously
relaxed and strictly verified.**

**ORDER 2028 (203 lines) is REACH, not a second source** — it cites the same
Wagner (2004) and Cai (2009) results already counted, so the same-source rule
applies. It is logged rather than dropped because it contributes **one thing
ORDER 2026 does not, and the thing is stronger than the corroboration would
have been: selective-deprivation non-redundancy.** Preventing only REM or only SWS
shows each stage has non-redundant functions — REM deprivation impairs emotional
regulation and creativity, SWS deprivation impairs declarative memory and
physical restoration — and the brain attempts **rebound** but the compensation is
**"incomplete."* **That last clause is new to the arena and it is load-bearing:**
**a consolidation pass that misses a cycle does not repay the debt on the next
one**, so an offline window cannot be treated as self-correcting by repetition.
ORDER 2028 also supplies the tripartite nesting ORDER 2026 attributes to a
single source: **slow-oscillation up-states trigger spindles, which gate
hippocampal ripples** — an ordering constraint an agent mirroring the sequence
would have to respect.

#### The disagreement preserved on Area 99

**ORDER 2022 (329 lines) states the contested reading as settled fact, and the
arena does not adopt it.** The file says Dunning & Kruger (1999)
*"demonstrated a robust double-burden"* and gives the 62nd-percentile figure,
then generalises the effect to LLMs: *"they tend to be overconfident on topics
outside their training distribution … without the underlying knowledge, there's
no basis for accurate self-evaluation."* Area 99 holds the opposite reading —
five arithmetic accounts plus **Nuhfer et al. (2016) reproducing the canonical
figure from random numbers** — and grades the double-burden account
**`UNSUCCESSFUL`**.

**Three reasons this is recorded as a qualification and not absorbed as
corroboration**, and the reasons are the substance rather than a formality:
(a) ORDER 2022's frontmatter is `sources: []`, `verified: []`, `confidence:
medium` — a **terrestrial restatement** of a paper the arena already holds at
full strength, which the same-source rule makes **reach, not evidence**; (b) it
cites **only** the 1999 original and is **silent on every dispute Area 99 exists
to hold**, so it does not weigh against them — it does not know about them;
(c) the disagreement is **directional** and the arena does not pick. **A future
pass holding a post-2016 survey of this literature should record which side it
lands on.**

**The one genuinely new thing in the file** is its framing of the LLM case as
**the same double burden** — low competence removing the basis for self-
evaluation — which is a **third position** sitting between Area 99 (no deficit
needed anywhere) and Area 137 (the middle epistemic value is the dangerous one).
Recorded at Area 99 rather than promoted, because one tertiary restatement
cannot outrank a 644-line source that has read the primary literature.

4. **ORDER 2013** (243 lines) — zigzag vs unsigned compression. See the two

5. **ORDER 2014** (36 lines), **ORDER 2016** (37), **ORDER 2021** (36),
   **ORDER 2023** (38), **ORDER 2025** (15), **ORDER 2027** (36),
   **ORDER 2029** (37) — **seven directory indexes.** Five are the identical

6. **ORDER 2015** (816 lines) — Mixture-of-Experts architecture. **Substrate
